title: Aging beyond older adults: Transdisciplinary perspectives on demographic change in Japan
title_original: Aging beyond older adults: Transdisciplinary perspectives on demographic change in Japan
summary: Population aging is increasingly recognized not merely as a demographic phenomenon, but as a broader societal transformation reshaping care systems, labor structures, infrastructure, communication, governance, and everyday social relations. Using Japan as an example of an advanced super-aged society, this paper examines how demographic aging and population shrinking interact with social, technological, institutional, and environmental systems across multiple domains of adaptation. Adopting a transdisciplinary narrative and integrative review approach, the study synthesizes literature spanning sustainability science, gerontology, migration studies, urban planning, linguistics, science and technology studies, and environmental governance. The analysis focuses on four interconnected domains: inclusive infrastructure and linguistic accessibility; technological adaptation and robotic care; caregiving, migration, and labor transformation; and nature-based well-being. The review demonstrates that adaptation in aging societies depends on hybrid systems that combine public welfare institutions, technological interventions, migration pathways, community-based support, and family caregiving. While Japan has advanced barrier-free infrastructure, Universal Design legislation, Yasashii Nihongo initiatives, long-term care systems, and assistive technologies, major tensions persist, including labor shortages, unequal caregiving burdens, technological dependence, and barriers to migrant integration. The findings also show that interventions initially designed for older adults frequently generate co-benefits for migrants, disabled persons, children, caregivers, and local communities. The paper argues that demographic aging cannot be effectively addressed by isolated sectoral or disciplinary responses. Instead, aging societies require integrated and adaptive approaches connecting infrastructure, labor systems, migration, communication, technology, environmental design, and caregiving across multiple stakeholder groups. Japan's experience offers insights for societies undergoing similar demographic transitions.

title: French Sports Diplomacy and Soft Power Acquisition
title_original: French Sports Diplomacy and Soft Power Acquisition
summary: This chapter examines the trajectory and future of French sports diplomacy in the wake of the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games. While the Games were widely acclaimed as a success, they also signalled the end of a political and diplomatic cycle in which mega-events served as the cornerstone of France&s;s international influence. This raises a central question: does France possess a coherent and durable sport diplomacy, or has it relied primarily on the opportunistic use of major events to project its image abroad? The chapter traces the institutionalisation of sports diplomacy in France since the early 2010s, through initiatives such as the appointment of a Sport Ambassador and the creation of interministerial structures. It highlights notable achievements—including the Paris 2024 bid, greater French representation in international federations, and the global recognition of organisational expertise—while underscoring enduring structural, political, and conjunctural limitations. The analysis ultimately argues that the future of French sports diplomacy will depend on its ability to move beyond an event-driven approach and to articulate a sustainable, strategically integrated vision of sport as an instrument of foreign policy.

title: Systematic process for design and manufacturing of ergonomic handles for para-table tennis: a case study
title_original: Systematic process for design and manufacturing of ergonomic handles for para-table tennis: a case study
summary: Abstract Wheelchair table tennis serves as an affordable and accessible means of enhancing the physical and psychological well-being of individuals with tetraplegia; however, limited hand mobility and grip strength continue to constrain performance. To address these issues, this study presents a systematic, end-to-end workflow for designing and manufacturing customized, competition-legal table tennis handles tailored to tetraplegic athletes, evaluated through a single-athlete feasibility case study rather than a clinical or sports-performance validation. The process integrates hand geometry capture, computer-aided design (CAD) refinement through iterative additive prototyping, and final fabrication using optimized materials and surface finishing. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a case study was conducted comparing an athlete’s performance using the old and new handles in terms of accuracy, control, and overall playing performance. In this single-athlete case study, successful shots showed roughly $$2.4\times$$ the odds of success with the new handle across drills. As a proof-of-concept evaluation, these findings are preliminary and indicate an association observed in one athlete, not a demonstrated causal effect, and are not intended to generalise to tetraplegic players more broadly. The customized handle was also reported by the athlete to be more comfortable and easier to use.

title: Stable technical profile despite increasing technical diversity across the last three Olympic cycles in elite female extra-lightweight judo
title_original: Stable technical profile despite increasing technical diversity across the last three Olympic cycles in elite female extra-lightweight judo
summary: Objective: To analyze the technical-tactical behavior and scoring effectiveness of techniques in elite female extra-lightweight (≤48 kg) judo across the last three Olympic cycles (2016, 2020, and 2024). Methods: A retrospective observational study which analyzed 159 official International Judo Federation World Circuit contests (53 per cycle) involving athletes ranked among the top 20 in the World Ranking. A total of 107 scoring techniques were identified according to the Kodokan classification and the official IJF rules applicable to each Olympic cycle. Results: No significant differences were observed in the distribution of technical groups across Olympic cycles (χ²=3.109, p=0.927; Cramér's V=0.121). Likewise, the distribution of techniques resulting in Ippon (χ²=3.637, p=0.888) and Waza-ari (χ²=6.383, p=0.604) remained stable. Although the overall technical profile was preserved, the diversity of individual scoring techniques increased from 17 techniques in the 2016 Olympic cycle to 24 in the 2020 cycle, and remained high in 2024 (23 techniques). Sode-tsuri-komi-goshi predominated in 2016, whereas Ouchi-gari became the most frequent scoring technique in 2020 and remained among the leading techniques in 2024. Katame-waza consistently produced most Ippon, whereas Ashi-waza and Te-waza remained the principal sources of Waza-ari. Conclusions: Despite successive IJF rule modifications, the technical profile of elite female extra-lightweight judo remained remarkably stable across the last three Olympic cycles. Elite athletes expanded their technical repertoire while maintaining the effectiveness of the principal scoring strategies, providing coaches with evidence to optimize weight category-specific technical and tactical training.

title: Representasi Gender dalam Konten Body Image di TikTok: Analisis Bibliometrik dan Tinjauan Sistematis (2021-2026)
title_original: Representasi Gender dalam Konten Body Image di TikTok: Analisis Bibliometrik dan Tinjauan Sistematis (2021-2026)
summary: Pesatnya perkembangan TikTok menjadikannya arena krusial bagi negosiasi identitas danpembentukan citra tubuh melalui konten visual. Terdapat kesenjangan sintesis mengenaiinteraksi algoritma dengan stereotip gender tradisional (2021–2026). Penelitian ini memetakanlanskap literatur representasi gender dalam konten citra tubuh melalui metode hibrida: analisisbibliometrik dan tinjauan pustaka sistematis. Mengikuti protokol PRISMA, 223 dokumen dariScopus diproses via VOSviewer untuk memvisualisasikan jaringan kata kunci. Temuanmenunjukkan tren publikasi memuncak pada 2025 dengan 60 dokumen, didominasi bidangIlmu Sosial (140 dokumen) dan Amerika Serikat sebagai kontributor utama. Analisismengungkapkan dikotomi performativitas, di mana algoritma cenderung mempromosikanstandar tubuh tertentu yang melanggengkan seksisme sistemik dan bias gender yang merugikankesehatan mental pengguna. Kesimpulannya, ekosistem TikTok masih terjebak dalam bingkaibudaya yang memojokkan perempuan. Oleh karena itu, direkomendasikan adanya auditalgoritma berkala serta penguatan literasi digital lintas disiplin guna mendekonstruksi standarkecantikan toksik dan menciptakan ruang siber yang lebih inklusif bagi keragaman citra tubuh.

title: Best Practices in Procurement, Contract Management, and Technical Supervision for Electrical Infrastructure Development: A Multi-Country Archival Study of Eight World Bank-Financed Projects
title_original: Best Practices in Procurement, Contract Management, and Technical Supervision for Electrical Infrastructure Development: A Multi-Country Archival Study of Eight World Bank-Financed Projects
summary: Background: Electrical infrastructure projects combine technically interdependent equipment, long-lead supply chains, multi-party interfaces, safety-critical construction, and commissioning obligations. Procurement, contract management, and technical supervision are often managed as separate administrative functions even though delivery failure commonly propagates across their boundaries. Objective: This study identifies best practices across these three functions and tests whether their integrated project-level maturity is associated with stronger delivery outcomes. Methods: A comparative archival study was conducted across eight World Bank-financed electricity projects in Vietnam, Rwanda, Tanzania, Bangladesh, Kenya, Uganda, India, and Pakistan. Official implementation completion reports, Independent Evaluation Group assessments, procurement records, and current procurement and project-governance standards were reviewed through 20 September 2026. An original Procurement-Contract-Supervision Maturity Index (PCSMI) scored eight observable domains from 0 to 2 (total 0-16). World Bank/IEG outcome ratings were independently converted to a six-point ordinal scale. Cross-case pattern matching, Spearman rank correlation, an exact permutation test, leave-one-out analysis, and domain-drop sensitivity analysis were applied. Results: PCSMI totals ranged from 3 to 14. Higher-rated projects more consistently combined market-aware procurement, credible qualification, coherent packaging, clear contract administration, disciplined decision governance, adequately resourced supervision, and formal quality/testing controls. Lower-scoring cases showed recurring combinations of protracted procurement, weak bidder due diligence, payment or site-readiness constraints, fragmented approval structures, poor claims/change records, and late corrective supervision. PCSMI was positively associated with project outcome rating (Spearman rho=0.873; exact two-sided permutation p=0.0071). Leave-one-out correlations ranged from 0.816 to 0.952, and domain-drop correlations from 0.794 to 0.873. Conclusion: In the examined cases, procurement, contract management, and technical supervision functioned as one delivery control system rather than three independent disciplines. The findings support a stage-gated owner model that links market engagement and packaging decisions to executable contract controls, prompt commercial administration, risk-based supervision, inspection/test plans, and commissioning evidence. The small heterogeneous sample supports mechanism-oriented inference rather than causal claims.

title: Self-worth and life meaning: the perceived narrative frames on the identity of people with disabilities
title_original: Self-worth and life meaning: the perceived narrative frames on the identity of people with disabilities
summary: This study investigated the narrative frames of disability and their associations with disability identity in the context of China. Specifically, it explored the sense of Self-worth, Life Meaning, Perceived Discrimination, and Disability Denial in people with disabilities and the complex relationships between media narratives, impairment, and social constraints. Through framing analysis, this study found three tragedy narrative frames ( traditional, medical , and charity ) and three non-tragedy frames ( inspirational, relationship , and rights ) from the traditional media and social media. Additional hierarchical regression analysis of a survey data among people with disabilities revealed that participants who frequently accessed social media platforms were more likely to reject tragic narratives while accepting non-tragic ones. The findings indicate that access to non-tragic narrative resources may help people with disabilities challenge tragedy-based understandings and construct more positive identities. Further analysis, however, indicated that superficial positive valence does not itself constitute affirmative identity acceptance. For example, although the inspirational frame celebrates agency and achievement, it retains a deficit-oriented logic in which impairments must be overcome; accordingly, it reinforces greater disability denial, thereby limiting the formation of a genuine affirmative disability identity.

title: A Review of the Research Methods Used to Determine the Health Effects of Respirable Atmospheric Particles
title_original: A Review of the Research Methods Used to Determine the Health Effects of Respirable Atmospheric Particles
summary: The adverse health effects of air pollution are being increasingly recognized as major causes of disease. Atmospheric particles, as a major component of air pollution, have been extensively studied in terms of their sources, physicochemical characteristics, transport in the atmosphere, and changes in particulate composition during their time in the atmosphere. The relationships between particles and diseases are complex, so research on the health effects and damage mechanisms of particulate matter (PM) is of significant importance. This study reviews the health effects of PM and provides an overview of the hazards of atmospheric PM to various human organs. In addition, this review explores the mechanisms of damage, summarizes the research methods used to determine the health effects, and discusses the influential health factors caused by PM. In combination with current Chinese and global research, the modern technologies and research trends on the health effects of particles are elucidated.

title: Smart technology and multibody simulation for skier safety: a structured narrative review and research roadmap
title_original: Smart technology and multibody simulation for skier safety: a structured narrative review and research roadmap
summary: This structured narrative review examines how smart equipment, wearable and environmental sensing, digital twins, and multibody simulation can contribute to skier safety and prevention of ski-injury. The Scopus® search produced 58,919 aggregate query returns; after excluding two deliberately broad searches, 1,285 targeted-query records were screened and 74 sources were retained. The backward and the forward search for citation searches supported by Google Scholar™ identified another 76 sources, giving 150 included sources. Because the literature is heterogeneous in study design, outcome, and technological maturity, the evidence was synthesised qualitatively rather than by meta-analysis. The review distinguishes technologies that are already useful for measurement or protection from approaches that remain experimental or conceptual. It also identifies validation, calibration, uncertainty quantification, interoperability, false-alarm control, and field robustness as the principal barriers to real-time predictive safety systems. Finally, a non-validated Human-Skills-Equipment-Environment framework and a conceptual Skier Safety Index are presented solely as hypotheses for future research. The resulting roadmap prioritises prospective validation with human-subject data, standardised multimodal data sets, transparent model verification, and controlled evaluation of adaptive safety interventions.

title: SEE THE GOAL OR SEE THE DISABILITY? MEDIACOVERAGE OF THE 2022 FIFA PUSKÁS AWARDAND THE REPRESENTATION OF AMPUTEEFOOTBALL
title_original: SEE THE GOAL OR SEE THE DISABILITY? MEDIACOVERAGE OF THE 2022 FIFA PUSKÁS AWARDAND THE REPRESENTATION OF AMPUTEEFOOTBALL
summary: This study examined the characteristics of media coverage of the 2022 FIFA Puskás Award, the first edition in which an amputee football player received the prize. We analyzed the content of 33 news articles published by mainstream and specialized sports media outlets from Brazil and Poland, as well as institutional publications from sports federations (FIFA, WAFF, UEFA, EAFF, CBF, and CBFA). Analytical categories were established based on prior research on media representation of disability and parasport. Interrater reliability was assessed using Cohen’s unweighted kappa (κ = 0.849; CI = 0.576–1.000). The results indicate that coverage predominantly adopted ableist (18.2%), trivialization (20.5%), sensationalist (19.3%), and disability-focused (12.5%) framings. FIFA and portions of the mainstream media reproduced disability-related stereotypes, whereas WAFF and CBF adopted balanced, performance-centered framings. The absence of coverage by organizations such as UEFA and CBFA raises concerns about institutional responsibility in promoting para-athletes. We conclude that the media narratives surrounding the winning goal emphasized Marcin Oleksy’s disability at the expense of his athletic accomplishments. This study underscores the urgent need for a paradigm shift in media representations of parasport. Received: 2026/02/23 Reformulated: 2026/08/28 Accepted: 2026/08/28

title: ‘He has been the worst coach, but he’s also the one that said “let’s give it a go”’: exploring the promise and potential of inclusive research in disability sport coaching
title_original: ‘He has been the worst coach, but he’s also the one that said “let’s give it a go”’: exploring the promise and potential of inclusive research in disability sport coaching
summary: This paper offers a novel methodological illustration of the fusion of Inclusive Research (IR) and Participatory Action Research (PAR) principles in disability sport coaching in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Using this hybrid methodology, we undertook semi-structured interviews with disabled people, community sport coaches and national coach developers to explore how ‘mainstream’ sports coach development systems can be more inclusive of disabled people. Guided by a Disability Advisory Group, and drawing on reflexive thematic analysis, the research highlighted the strong desire from athletes to participate in mainstream sport, alongside the desire by coaches and coach developers to provide more opportunities for disabled people. Yet, findings indicate that despite the potential for coach education to act as a mechanism for enhancing coaches’ knowledge of inclusion, gaps in support available for both coaches and national coach developers hinder the implementation of inclusive policy. The analysis further illustrated how systemic forms of ableism and structural barriers across mainstream sport, coach education and coaching practices can limit opportunities for inclusion. These findings demonstrate that achieving greater inclusion therefore requires addressing systemic barriers within sport coaching and fostering a culture that supports inclusive practices at all levels. In addition, this paper critically reflects on the participatory research practices employed, examining how these approaches shaped the research findings, and highlights the depth and significance of knowledge generated through such inclusive methods. These reflections offer valuable insights for future sport coaching research seeking to embed participatory and inclusive principles.

title: Correlation between visuomotor abilities and pistol shooting performance in police trainees
title_original: Correlation between visuomotor abilities and pistol shooting performance in police trainees
summary: Precision pistol shooting relies on the integration of visual perception and motor execution, yet the visuomotor abilities associated with marksmanship in police trainees remain poorly defined. Shooting-performance data were collected from 100 police trainees undergoing standardized firearms training using a controlled fixed-distance precision-shooting assessment. Visuomotor assessments were completed by 50 participants selected from the upper and lower quartiles of the shooting-score distribution. The assessment battery included visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, reaction time, target capture speed, depth perception, perception span, multiple object tracking, eye–hand coordination, and go/no-go decision making. Pearson correlations, Welch’s independent-samples t-tests, effect sizes (Cohen’s d), and Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate correction were applied, with Spearman correlations and Mann–Whitney U tests used as sensitivity analyses. After FDR correction across 27 correlations, only faster dominant-hand reaction time remained significantly associated with higher shooting scores ( r = − 0.453, p = 0.0009, q = 0.025). Right-eye visual acuity, binocular visual acuity, and target capture time showed nominal associations at the unadjusted level but did not survive correction. In the group comparisons, right-eye visual acuity and dominant-hand reaction time remained significant after FDR correction (both q = 0.048), whereas target capture time did not (q = 0.326). The dominant-hand reaction-time association remained significant after controlling for right-eye visual acuity (partial r = − 0.510, q = 0.004). An four-variable regression model explained 40.3% of the in-sample variance in shooting score (adjusted R² = 0.350). Dominant-hand reaction time (β = −0.442, p < 0.001) and right-eye visual acuity (β = −0.303, p = 0.015) retained independent inverse associations, whereas binocular visual acuity and target capture time did not. However, no association remained significant when correlations were examined separately within the high- and low-score groups. Dominant-hand reaction time therefore represented the most robust finding, while the visual-acuity and target-capture findings were less consistent across analyses and should be interpreted cautiously in the context of the extreme-group sampling design.

title: Mental, technical, and physical fitness in sports performance: an integrative systematic literature review of their relative and interactive contributions
title_original: Mental, technical, and physical fitness in sports performance: an integrative systematic literature review of their relative and interactive contributions
summary: This systematic review analyzed 50 studies from the Scopus database to determine the relative contributions of psychological, technical, and physical determinants to competitive sports performance, examining how these relationships vary across sport types, competitive levels, age, and sex. Utilizing a narrative synthesis approach in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the review found that no single domain universally dominates; rather, performance relies on an integrated, context-dependent model. Specifically, physical fitness attributes proved most prominent in team and endurance sports, technical proficiency acted as a key mediator in open-skill and precision disciplines, and psychological constructs demonstrated the highest explanatory power in high-pressure, elite individual contexts. However, the validity and generalizability of these findings are constrained by several methodological limitations identified within the literature. These include a predominance of cross-sectional designs that limit causal inference, high outcome measurement heterogeneity that precluded meta-analytic synthesis, single-reviewer screening risks, and a notable demographic bias favoring male, adult, able-bodied team-sport samples over female, youth, and Para-sport populations. To advance the field, future investigations must prioritize longitudinal, multi-domain tracking designs using standardized measurement batteries and actively incorporate underrepresented athletic populations.

title: The Impact of Paralympic and Olympic Broadcasts on Viewer Engagement: The Role of Television in Shaping Staycation Trends in India
title_original: The Impact of Paralympic and Olympic Broadcasts on Viewer Engagement: The Role of Television in Shaping Staycation Trends in India
summary: Sports broadcasting's impact on viewer engagement is a multifaceted topic that encompasses factors such as viewer preferences, audience carryover, social media participation, and the effects of in-the-moment events and nation-related values on viewer attention. The way the Olympic and Paralympic Games are televised shapes attitudes and perceptions of athletes and people with disabilities, with substantial effects on spectator engagement. The 2020 Tokyo Games, as well as the 2024 Paris Games, broke all broadcast viewership records for the number of broadcasters, viewers, and live events. It was hailed as noteworthy for its massive media coverage, which helped promote the disability athletic movement. Through passionate narrative, Paralympic broadcasts run the risk of perpetuating stereotypes, even though they can also encourage empathy and social transformation. Viewers' perceptions of the credibility and athleticism of Paralympic sports compared to Olympic sports are influenced by how these events are portrayed. Distinct categories of sports enthusiasts include information searchers, entertainment seekers, common spectators, and ardent supporters. In contrast to comedies or dramas, sports programs are mostly chosen by ardent fans and have less of an impact on broader audiences. All things considered, the media is extremely important in either supporting or contradicting society norms and prejudices towards disability and sports.

title: Evidence-Based Insights for the Development and Talent Promotion of Young Athletes in a National Sports Context
title_original: Evidence-Based Insights for the Development and Talent Promotion of Young Athletes in a National Sports Context
summary: The development of young athletes continues to be a key concern for sports organizations, coaches and policy makers. In Sweden, the public debate on the balance between early talent promotion programs and more inclusive, long-term athlete development models has recently intensified. This discussion reflects the general global tensions within youth sport systems between high performance ambitions and the goal of lifelong sport, as well as other societal goals related to sport. Taking the Swedish context as a starting point, this perspective article explores the challenges and opportunities in integrating early talent promotion with sustainable athlete development frameworks. While the Swedish case provides the empirical context, the findings and recommendations presented are intended to inform broader international and national debates. We argue that evidence-based youth sport systems can support both elite performance and broader participation goals simultaneously. We propose a nuanced, evidence-based approach that recognizes the complexity of youth athlete development and the importance of aligning scientific evidence with local cultural and organizational contexts. The focus is on creating sport environments that support athlete well-being, intrinsic motivation and diverse opportunities for participation. Rather than prescribing a one-size-fits-all solution, this article highlights principles to help national federations and clubs design systems that promote both elite performance and broad participation. Ultimately, sustainable athlete development requires contextual governance, continuous evaluation and a commitment to promoting both performance goals and the wider benefits of sport.

title: Menstrual Dysfunction is Not a Medal –The Hidden Cost of Overtraining
title_original: Menstrual Dysfunction is Not a Medal –The Hidden Cost of Overtraining
summary: For decades, women in sport have been told that if you work hard enough, something will have to give. That ‘something’ is the menstrual cycle. Missed periods are seen to be a side effect of hard work, discipline, and dedication as a trade-off for success. There is a misconception that losing your period to become an efficient, lean, elite machine, is worth it. Human physiology tells a very different story. Amenorrhea is not a marker of optimum performance and discipline. It is a clinical sign that the body is under physiological stress and conserving energy for essential survival processes. It is a clinical marker of energy deficiency, systemic stress, and hormonal dysregulation. Yet in the sporting world, a blind eye has been turned to this, and it has even been quietly rewarded. This article argues that menstrual dysfunction in athletes should not be normalized as a sign of dedication or elite performance, but recognized as a red flag requiring further education, open discussions without any taboo, medical monitoring, and a cultural change within sport. Although this article refers primarily to athletes assigned female at birth, menstrual dysfunction can also affect transgender men and non-binary athletes who menstruate. The physiological mechanisms discussed therefore apply to anyone who experiences menstrual cycles. The Female Athlete Triad is a spectrum of disorders including low energy availability (LEA), low bone mineral density, and menstrual disorders. Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs) can occur in both female and male athletes when energy intake is insufficient to meet the demands of exercise and basic physiological processes such as the menstrual cycle, resulting in low energy availability. REDs recognises that insufficient energy intake and increased energy output results in disruption in various physiological systems such as the menstrual cycle, basal metabolic rate, bone density, cardiovascular health, and the immune system.

title: The Effect of Soft Tissue Mobilization and Kinesio Taping on Sportive Performance in Athletes: A Randomized Controlled Trial
title_original: The Effect of Soft Tissue Mobilization and Kinesio Taping on Sportive Performance in Athletes: A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: Objective: Instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization (IASTM) and Kinesio tape (KT) applications were suggested in the context of athlete rehabilitation.This study aimed to examine the impact of IASTM and KT on the bilateral hamstring muscles of athletes' balance, agility, and lower extremity explosive power.Methods: A total of 45 athletes who met the inclusion criteria participated in the study.The participants were allocated to the exercise or the control group using simple randomization with a sealed envelope method.The athletes were divided into three groups.All three groups' balance, agility, and jump-lower extremity explosive strength performances were evaluated in a single session using the single foot stance test, agility t-test, and standing long jump test, respectively, before, immediately after, and one month after the intervention.Results: There was a significant difference between the IASTM and KT groups for the agility t-test (p<0.05).In the IASTM group, an important difference was observed in the duration of the single foot stance test (p<0.05).There was no statistically significant difference between the groups in the scores of the single foot stance test, agility t-test, and standing long jump test (p>0.05). Conclusion:The application of IASTM has been demonstrated to enhance balance and agility, while KT has been shown to improve agility in athletes.However, no significant differences were identified between the two methods.IASTM and KT may be useful as complementary methods to existing training programs for athletes, but further research is recommended to determine which is more effective.

title: National Pride vs. Global Unity: Exploring Nationalism-Infused CSR and Stakeholder Perceptions in Global Sports Events
title_original: National Pride vs. Global Unity: Exploring Nationalism-Infused CSR and Stakeholder Perceptions in Global Sports Events
summary: Abstract Global sporting events, such as the Olympics, often highlight a delicate tension between universal ideals of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and nationalistic appeals to local pride. Against this backdrop, the present study investigates how moral foundations (fairness vs. loyalty) and national attachment shape stakeholder perceptions of nationalism-infused CSR motives and CSR authenticity. Building on moral foundation theory and attribution-based CSR research, we tested hypotheses regarding the interplay between these variables. Conducting a survey (N = 755) through Dynata, we found that fairness-oriented individuals attributed egoistic- and strategic-driven motives, while people with in-group/loyalty foundation perceived value-driven motives from the initiatives.

title: Organizational stressors and athlete burnout in elite soccer players: the mediating role of basic psychological need frustration and the moderating role of coach autonomy support
title_original: Organizational stressors and athlete burnout in elite soccer players: the mediating role of basic psychological need frustration and the moderating role of coach autonomy support
summary: Introduction: Athlete burnout is an important psychological state that may affect sustained training engagement, athletic performance, and mental health among elite soccer players. Drawing on basic psychological need theory, this study examined the association between organizational stressors and athlete burnout among Chinese elite soccer players with dual educational and sport-training roles, and tested whether basic psychological need frustration accounted for an indirect association and whether coach autonomy support served as a boundary condition. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 513 Chinese elite soccer student-athletes enrolled in the Football College of Chengdu Sport University. According to the college admission requirements and self-reported athletic-level information, all participants had attained at least the Chinese National First-Class Athlete level before or at university entry. Participants completed measures of organizational stressors, basic psychological need frustration, coach autonomy support, and athlete burnout. Data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis, correlation analysis, bootstrap tests of indirect associations, and a first-stage moderated mediation model. Results: Organizational stressors were positively associated with both athlete burnout and basic psychological need frustration. Basic psychological need frustration was positively associated with athlete burnout and accounted for a significant indirect association between organizational stressors and athlete burnout. Coach autonomy support showed a small but significant buffering effect on the association between organizational stressors and basic psychological need frustration, and the conditional indirect association through basic psychological need frustration was weaker at higher levels of coach autonomy support. Discussion: The findings suggest that athlete burnout among elite soccer players with dual educational and sport-training roles is closely associated with organizational stressors, and that basic psychological need frustration may help explain this statistical association. Coach autonomy support may constitute a contextual boundary condition that modestly reduces the association between organizational stressors and basic psychological need frustration. These results suggest that management of organizational stressors, basic psychological need experiences, and autonomy-supportive coaching behaviors may be relevant targets for future longitudinal and intervention research. Given the cross-sectional and self-reported nature of the data, the findings should be interpreted as theoretically specified statistical associations rather than evidence of strict causality.

title: A Professional Guide to REBT
title_original: A Professional Guide to REBT
summary: A Professional Guide to REBT provides the reader with theoretical and detailed practical information from an experienced and qualified practitioner using and researching Rational Emotive Behaviour Therapy (REBT) day to day. Following a logical flow, each chapter covers a core tenet of REBT aligned with how REBT is practised. The book considers and briefly presents the research evidence to date, grounding this work in evidence-based practice. Each chapter provides a brief but detailed portrayal of REBT, informing readers how the REBT tenet is applied in practice and, importantly, why. A Professional Guide to REBT offers a thorough yet distilled guide on how the fundamentals of REBT are applied and is key reading for students, scholars, and practitioners of psychology, psychotherapy, and REBT.

title: Mathematical and statistical challenges for the surveillance of gastroenteritis
title_original: Mathematical and statistical challenges for the surveillance of gastroenteritis
summary: Gastroenteritis, causing vomiting and diarrhoea, is very common all over the world. Viral causes, such as norovirus and rotavirus, are the most frequent, although some bacteria, parasites and fungi can also lead to gastroenteritis. Many countries operate surveillance systems of diseases, including gastroenteritis or specific gastroenteritis causing pathogens. Typically, statistical methods are used to analyse surveillance data and alert public health authorities of unexpectedly high levels of illness. These methods use historical data to predict the expected value of current data. In this thesis, we address some of the challenges that remain when analysing gastroenteritis surveillance data, with a particular focus on syndromic surveillance data. We work with both mechanistic and statistical modelling approaches in an attempt to bridge the gap between the statistical methods that are used in practice for syndromic surveillance and mechanistic models that are used to model infectious diseases. In particular, we address three challenges. In chapter 2 we present a flexible framework for deriving approximations of stochastic mechanistic models of epidemics for fast inference. In chapter 3 we investigate day of the week and public holiday effects in syndromic indicators of gastroenteritis from syndromic surveillance systems operated by Public Health England in order to improve existing surveillance methodologies. In chapter 4 we identify and analyse additional online datasets for gastroenteritis, and in particular norovirus, surveillance.

title: ‘In search of a new national story’: Issues of cultural diversity in the casting and performance of Shakespeare in Britain 2012–2016
title_original: ‘In search of a new national story’: Issues of cultural diversity in the casting and performance of Shakespeare in Britain 2012–2016
summary: his thesis examines the contribution of British black, South Asian, and East Asian actors, directors and companies to Shakespearean performance in Britain between 2012 and 2016. Stephen Bourne’s Black in the British Frame (2001), British Asian Theatre by Dominic Hingorani (2010), and Colin Chambers’ Black and Asian Theatre in Britain: A History (2011), are three important works that trace the artistic contributions by black, Asian and minority ethnic (BAME) communities in British theatre; yet Shakespearean achievements are underrepresented here as well as in the wider body of published academic writing. This thesis aims to record the artistic achievements and cultural presence of non-white practitioners whose work has been marginalised and poorly documented. It aims to investigate the impact of casting practices and directorial interpretations in the representation of BAME communities in mainstream, non-traditional and educational settings. It also aims to contribute to the development of sustained dialogues about, and understanding of, issues of cultural and ethnic diversity in Shakespearean performance. To do this, several extended analytical case studies of historically significant and culturally important Shakespearean performances are provided. The thesis is divided into four sections. The first examines issues of cultural diversity on Britain’s main stages, particularly in the work of the Royal Shakespeare Company. Section two studies the praxis of BAME theatre companies: Talawa, Tara Arts, Phizzical Productions and Yellow Earth. Section three focuses on educational enterprises in mainstream organisations. Section four concludes with reflection and propositions as to how British Shakespearean production might move towards a more sustainable diverse ecology. The approach of this thesis is ethnographic, and draws on a range of sources of data surrounding these productions including archival resources (such as video recordings, production photographs, reviews and prompt books), interviews with practitioners, observations in rehearsal rooms and reports from funding bodies. This thesis examines important productions in recent history, and assesses major issues, problems and pitfalls, as well as models of best practice, in the casting and performance of culturally diverse Shakespeare in Britain 2012–2016.

title: Esportes paralímpicos e lesão esportiva: uso de tecnologia assistiva – uma pesquisa sistemática integrativa
title_original: Esportes paralímpicos e lesão esportiva: uso de tecnologia assistiva – uma pesquisa sistemática integrativa
summary: As lesões esportivas são práticas constantes em atletas e paratletas que buscam alto rendimento. Atualmente as tecnologias assistivas (TA) são utilizadas em várias modalidades esportivas, a fim de mitigar lesões, escoriações e melhoria de desempenho. Esta pesquisa, busca uma investigação sistemática integrativa, como estudo qualitativo de uso de equipamentos que auxiliem os atletas paralímpicos na melhoria esportiva e na qualidade de vida. Resultados encontrados nas análises e estudos dos autores, demonstram a necessidade de maior aprofundamento nas pesquisas de modo específico ao perfil do atleta e suas condições externas (ambiente) nos quais realizam seus treinos e competições. Em observação as análises de equipamentos digitais ou de tecnologia assistiva, foi encontrado uma lacuna dos quais não apresentam quais são os esquipamentos utilizados e como tais equipamentos influenciam na evolução de desempenho e redução de lesões. Evidenciando uma preocupação em pesquisas empíricas para que estas lacunas possam ser minimizadas com estudos direcionados a biomecânica, tipos de deficiências e equipamentos permitidos e utilizados em modalidades esportivas.

title: Epidemiological Characteristics and Injury Mechanisms of Taekwondo-Related Injuries: A Systematic Review
title_original: Epidemiological Characteristics and Injury Mechanisms of Taekwondo-Related Injuries: A Systematic Review
summary: As a highly-combative Olympic sport, taekwondo has one of the highest injury-incidence rates among Olympic disciplines, yet its epidemiological characteristics and injury patterns remain unclear. This study performed the-first-ever systematic analysis of the epidemiological features and injury mechanisms of taekwondo. A systematic search identified 552 publications published between 2000 and 2024, among which 24 studies covering 15,170 athletes met the inclusion criteria. Results demonstrated that lower-extremity injuries accounted for the largest proportion (54.3%), with the ankle/foot, knee and face being the most-frequently injured sites. Contusions, sprains and strains were the predominant injury types. The injury risk was markedly higher in the third round than in the first two rounds, while the first round carried the lowest risk, a trend associated with fatigue accumulation and aggressive tactics. Major contributing factors to injuries included inattention, unsatisfactory venue facilities, improper use of protective equipment, rule revisions, high-difficulty techniques and insufficient physical conditioning. It is recommended to implement the International Olympic Committee Injury Surveillance System (IOC-ISS) for standardized injury monitoring, together with improvements in protective-gear technology and rule optimization. Future research should prioritize biomechanical analysis of taekwondo movements, long‑term follow-up of chronic injuries, and the establishment of an integrated system combining prevention, surveillance and rehabilitation.

title: Paris and the Seine: An Anthropological Approach
title_original: Paris and the Seine: An Anthropological Approach
summary: Based on urban and political anthropology research centered on Paris, I have developed an approach focusing on the dynamics of “heritagization,” that is, the use of spaces, metropolitan transformations and their relationship with globalization, particularly as seen through the lens of tourism. The Seine, considered as a public space, constitutes a privileged entry point for thinking about the systems that reorganize the relationship between city dwellers and the city. The relationship between Parisians and the river is shaped by historical representations, everyday use and planning policies, which continuously reconfigure this urban space. My analysis focuses on three emblematic projects that reconfigure the relationship between Paris and the Seine in different ways: Paris Plage, Voies sur Berge and the redevelopment of the area around Notre-Dame. These cases reveal the political logics underlying the production of public space, balancing event-based gestures with lasting transformations, “heritagization” with accessibility and urban memory with future experimentation. The analysis highlights the tension between urban planning, political representations of the river and social practices in a city where public space is a stage, a resource and a symbol.

title: Governing a Green Urban Growth Machine: The Case of Kitakyushu Eco-Town, Japan
title_original: Governing a Green Urban Growth Machine: The Case of Kitakyushu Eco-Town, Japan
summary: The restructuring of industrial cities follows various paths depending on local conditions and choices. A novel idea of a local industrial restructuring is to link the industrial park development with the circular economy. The park formations that are based on local government initiatives combine public and private interests, which poses a governance challenge, as they must generate both public value and profits for businesses. In this article, we will focus on the city government’s role and relations with key stakeholders in the building of the green growth coalition around recycling industrial district. Our research is based on single case study methodology. The case is the largest recycling industrial district in Japan, the Kitakyushu Eco-Town. Our interest is in the role of city government as a key player of the green growth coalition. The results show that the city government can effectively build a growth coalition that eventually contributes to the green restructuring. Building a green growth machine is, however, contingent, i.e. the success of the coalition is conditioned by local leadership and endogenous factors as well as their connections with exogenous factors from national governments to global economic and technology trends.

title: Individualization of training load in Paralympic powerlifting based on nosology
title_original: Individualization of training load in Paralympic powerlifting based on nosology
summary: The purpose of the study is to substantiate the necessity of individualizing training loads in Paralympic powerlifting, taking into account the nosological characteristics of athletes. Research methods: theoretical analysis of scientific and methodological literature. Research results and conclusions. Nosological groups were identified taking into account physiological and biomechanical characteristics. The features of planning training loads for each nosological group were determined: control of autonomic reactions, emphasis on the development of the triceps brachii and speed training without the use of fixing belts for athletes with spinal cord injuries; individualization of the "load–velocity" relationship for short-statured athletes and the use of wrist wraps; priority development of the abdominal and back muscles in athletes with amputations; as well as analysis of barbell kinematic characteristics and the predominance of speed training for athletes with manifestations of hypertonia, ataxia, and athetosis. For each nosological group, features were identified that can be taken into account when planning training loads, which can improve the efficiency and safety of the training process in Paralympic powerlifting.

title: ДОСВІД ЗАЛУЧЕННЯ ВЕТЕРАНІВ ВІЙНИ ДО ЗАНЯТЬ АДАПТИВНИМ СПОРТОМ
title_original: ДОСВІД ЗАЛУЧЕННЯ ВЕТЕРАНІВ ВІЙНИ ДО ЗАНЯТЬ АДАПТИВНИМ СПОРТОМ
summary: The large-scale armed aggression of Russia against Ukraine has caused an unprecedented growth in the country’s veteran community in recent history. Such demographic shifts require corresponding changes in state policy aimed at physical recovery, psycho-emotional stabilization, and social adaptation of former military personnel to civilian life conditions. However, there is a lack of comprehensive analysis of the trajectory of Ukrainian veterans’ engagement in adaptive sports: the moment and context of first contact with sports activity, the hierarchy of motivational factors, and the desired organizational model of support. Materials and methods. The empirical basis of the study consists of the results of an online survey of 112 veterans of the Russian-Ukrainian war, conducted by the National University of Physical Education and Sports of Ukraine in 2025–2026. The toolkit included 14 structured questions with closed-ended answers, multiple choice, and elements of open-ended comments. The following methods were used: analysis of scientific literature; the inductive method; synthesis and generalization; methods of mathematical statistics (descriptive statistics – frequencies, percentage distributions). Results. To study the experience of veterans’ engagement in adaptive sports, respondents’ answers were analyzed regarding their understanding of the concept of “adaptive sport”; veterans’ prior sports experience; the periods of engagement in adaptive sports activities; sources of motivation; the choice of sports programs known to veterans and desired for participation; prospective opportunities that open up after engagement in adaptive sports; and the involvement of family members in such activities. Conclusions. The analysis of veterans’ experience of engagement in adaptive sports demonstrated both the significant internal potential of the veteran community – motivational, human-resource, and organizational – and systemic barriers: terminological inconsistency, a gap between medical rehabilitation and sports-based recovery, a shortage of qualified specialists, and limited access to information. Overcoming these barriers requires a targeted state policy built on the “peer-to-peer” model, along with infrastructure supported by human and informational resources. The veteran community represents a unique human capital that the state and civil society must support, including through engagement in adaptive sports

title: Comparison of physical performance tests between male and female spanish national wheelchair basketball players
title_original: Comparison of physical performance tests between male and female spanish national wheelchair basketball players
summary: Introduction Research on physical performance in female wheelchair basketball (WB) players is scarce, and evidence comparing male and female elite players remains limited. The aim of this study was to compare physical performance test between male and female Spanish national WB team players competing at the European Championship medal level. Materials and methods A total of 22 players from the Spanish national WB team participated in the study (male [n = 12]; female [n = 10]). During preparation for the 2025 European Championship, players completed a physical performance test including a rotator cuff test, Initial Maximum Push-Rim Propulsion (IMPRP), sprint tests (5 m and 12 m), and the Repeated Sprint Ability (RSA) test. Results Significant differences between male and female players were observed in maximal force and 1-s average maximal force during the rotator cuff test (p < 0.01; effect size [ES] >0.8), IMPRP test (p < 0.01; ES >0.8), 5 m and 12 m sprint test (p 〈0.01; ES 〉 0.8), and the RSA test (p < 0.01; ES >0.8), with high performance observed in male players. Conclusions Male WB players showed higher performance in selected physical performance test. This study provides reference performance data from European Championship medal-winning national-team WB players.

À l'occasion des Jeux Olympiques et Paralympiques de Paris 2024, cet ouvrage collectif dirigé par Clément Llena et Gildas Loirand propose une contribution ambitieuse : rendre visibles et audibles les apports des sciences humaines et sociales (SHS) du sport dans la compréhension d'un événement sportif globalisé, investi de multiples promesses politiques, sociales et culturelles.Issu d'un congrès organisé à Montpellier en décembre 2022, le projet se distingue d'emblée par sa dimension collective et interdisciplinaire.Plusieurs sociétés savantes en SHS du sport ont été mobilisées, à savoir l'Association Francophone pour la Recherche sur les Activités Physiques et Sportives (AFRAPS), l'Association pour la Recherche sur l'Intervention en Sport (ARIS), la Société Française d'Histoire du Sport (SFHS), la Société Francophone de Philosophie du Sport (SFPS), la Société Savante de Management du Sport (S2MS) et la Société de Sociologie du Sport de Langue Française (3SLF).L'ouvrage témoigne d'une volonté partagée de structurer un espace scientifique capable de dialoguer avec les institutions, tout en conservant une autonomie critique.Le projet s'ouvre sur une série de propos institutionnels émanant de responsables politiques et académiques directement impliqués dans l'organisation ou l'accompagnement des Jeux (T.Estanguet, président du Comité d'organisation des Jeux Olympiques et Paralympiques de Paris 2024 ; A. Oudéa-Castéra, ministre des Sports, des Jeux Olympiques et Paralympiques ; P. Ndiaye, ministre de l'Éducation nationale et de la Jeunesse ; I. Rome, ministre déléguée chargée de l'Égalité entre les femmes et les hommes, de la Diversité et de l'Égalité des chances ; M. Tunon de Lara, président de France Université ; M. Delafosse, maire de Montpellier et président de Montpellier Méditerranée Métropole ; P. Augé, président de l'Université de Montpellier).Ces discours dessinent les contours d'un projet volontariste, où les Jeux sont présentés comme un levier d'éducation, de santé publique, d'égalité, d'inclusion sociale et de transition écologique.Cette entrée en matière met en avant une vision fortement valorisée du sport et de l'olympisme, envisagés comme des instruments quasi naturels de transformation sociale.Toutefois, c'est précisément dans l'écart entre ces discours programmatiques et le contenu scientifique des contributions que réside l'un des principaux intérêts de l'ouvrage.L'introduction, co-signée par les président(e)s des sociétés savantes, insiste sur le leitmotiv du « travailler ensemble », soulignant l'engagement des SHS à penser collectivement le sport dans toute sa complexité.Les vingt chapitres qui composent l'ouvrage sont organisés autour de différents « enjeux » (citoyens, d'innovation, de carrière, sanitaires, de gouvernance, culturels, institutionnels, immatériels, européens et internationaux), offrant une diversité d'approches

À l'occasion des Jeux Olympiques et Paralympiques de Paris 2024, cet ouvrage collectif dirigé par Clément Llena et Gildas Loirand propose une contribution ambitieuse : rendre visibles et audibles les apports des sciences humaines et sociales (SHS) du sport dans la compréhension d'un événement sportif globalisé, investi de multiples promesses politiques, sociales et culturelles.Issu d'un congrès organisé à Montpellier en décembre 2022, le projet se distingue d'emblée par sa dimension collective et interdisciplinaire.Plusieurs sociétés savantes en SHS du sport ont été mobilisées, à savoir l'Association Francophone pour la Recherche sur les Activités Physiques et Sportives (AFRAPS), l'Association pour la Recherche sur l'Intervention en Sport (ARIS), la Société Française d'Histoire du Sport (SFHS), la Société Francophone de Philosophie du Sport (SFPS), la Société Savante de Management du Sport (S2MS) et la Société de Sociologie du Sport de Langue Française (3SLF).L'ouvrage témoigne d'une volonté partagée de structurer un espace scientifique capable de dialoguer avec les institutions, tout en conservant une autonomie critique.Le projet s'ouvre sur une série de propos institutionnels émanant de responsables politiques et académiques directement impliqués dans l'organisation ou l'accompagnement des Jeux (T.Estanguet, président du Comité d'organisation des Jeux Olympiques et Paralympiques de Paris 2024 ; A. Oudéa-Castéra, ministre des Sports, des Jeux Olympiques et Paralympiques ; P. Ndiaye, ministre de l'Éducation nationale et de la Jeunesse ; I. Rome, ministre déléguée chargée de l'Égalité entre les femmes et les hommes, de la Diversité et de l'Égalité des chances ; M. Tunon de Lara, président de France Université ; M. Delafosse, maire de Montpellier et président de Montpellier Méditerranée Métropole ; P. Augé, président de l'Université de Montpellier).Ces discours dessinent les contours d'un projet volontariste, où les Jeux sont présentés comme un levier d'éducation, de santé publique, d'égalité, d'inclusion sociale et de transition écologique.Cette entrée en matière met en avant une vision fortement valorisée du sport et de l'olympisme, envisagés comme des instruments quasi naturels de transformation sociale.Toutefois, c'est précisément dans l'écart entre ces discours programmatiques et le contenu scientifique des contributions que réside l'un des principaux intérêts de l'ouvrage.L'introduction, co-signée par les président(e)s des sociétés savantes, insiste sur le leitmotiv du « travailler ensemble », soulignant l'engagement des SHS à penser collectivement le sport dans toute sa complexité.Les vingt chapitres qui composent l'ouvrage sont organisés autour de différents « enjeux » (citoyens, d'innovation, de carrière, sanitaires, de gouvernance, culturels, institutionnels, immatériels, européens et internationaux), offrant une diversité d'approches

title: Ozone variability and precursor sensitivity in urban Taichung: Insights from observation-based machine learning and chemical mechanism modeling
title_original: Ozone variability and precursor sensitivity in urban Taichung: Insights from observation-based machine learning and chemical mechanism modeling
summary: Ground-level ozone (O 3 ) remains a persistent air-quality challenge in rapidly urbanizing East Asian cities, driven by nonlinear interactions among nitrogen oxides (NO x ), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and meteorology. In this study, we investigated O 3 ​ variability and precursor sensitivity in Taichung, Taiwan – a representative East-Asian urban area – using year-long hourly observations from 2023 combined with a Random Forest (RF) model and chemistry-based simulations with the Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM). The RF model reproduced observed O 3 ​ variability well (R 2 = 0.90, RMSE=5.53 ppbv), and model performance improved substantially when NO and NO 2 ​ were treated as separate predictors rather than as combined NO x ​, highlighting the importance of resolving the O 3 –NO–NO 2 ​ relationship in data-driven prediction. O 3 -NO x -VOCs sensitivity analysis based on the optimal RF model showed that O 3 formation in Taichung was predominantly VOC-limited, although some conditions approached a transitional regime. However, the response of O 3 ​ to changes in total VOC–OH reactivity (TVOCR) was relatively weak, implying that O 3 reductions from VOC controls may occur gradually. MCM simulations provided mechanistic support for these results by showing that daytime O 3 ​ production was dominated by the HO 2 ​ + NO pathway, while alkene ozonolysis contributed significantly to O 3 ​ loss and partly offset VOCs-driven O 3 production. These results indicate that urban ozone pollution in Taichung is governed by coupled effects of VOCs availability, O 3 ​-NO titration and radical termination, and demonstrate that integrating machine learning with explicit chemical mechanism modeling is a useful framework for interpreting urban ozone sensitivity and informing precursor-control strategies.

title: Global epidemiology, clinical burden, and antimicrobial resistance of the WHO priority pathogens: An updated review focusing on understudied non-baumannii Acinetobacter and emerging extensively drug-resistant threats
title_original: Global epidemiology, clinical burden, and antimicrobial resistance of the WHO priority pathogens: An updated review focusing on understudied non-baumannii Acinetobacter and emerging extensively drug-resistant threats
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) priority pathogens list, particularly those classified as "critical" and "high" priority, serves as a pivotal framework guiding global efforts to combat antimicrobial resistance (AMR). This review synthesizes updated evidence on the global epidemiology, clinical burden, and antimicrobial resistance of WHO priority pathogens as of 2026. Despite extensive research on Acinetobacter baumannii, non-baumannii Acinetobacter species remain relatively understudied despite their increasing clinical relevance. This review highlights the significance of these non-baumannii species in healthcare-associated infections and their emerging resistance profiles. Additionally, the review addresses newly identified extensively drug-resistant (XDR) threats that pose significant challenges to current therapeutic options. By synthesizing the latest surveillance data, molecular resistance mechanisms, and treatment hurdles, this review aims to inform clinical management strategies, infection control practices, and public health policy development. Ultimately, this evidence-based synthesis seeks to support targeted interventions and guide future research priorities in the global fight against AMR.

title: Sponsors’ health-related messaging & corporate social responsibility: a multi country analysis of the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games
title_original: Sponsors’ health-related messaging & corporate social responsibility: a multi country analysis of the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games
summary: Research Aim: This paper extends Furtado et al. (2025)’s exploration of health-related messaging before and during the 2024 Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games. Given that the overwhelming majority (95%) of that study’s health-related messages emanated from corporations, this paper aims to explore the confluence of health messaging with sport mega event (SME) sponsorship and corporate social responsibility (CSR). More specifically, this paper aims to categorise the types of health messaging and activations by national and transnational sponsors accredited through individual National Olympic Committees (NOC) and The Olympic Partner (TOP) programme. Our focus on health adds original contributions to the extant literature on leveraging sport sponsorship as a strategic component of CSR (McCullough and Trail, 2023; Uhrich et al., 2014).

title: Public Perceptions of Disability and Para Athletes Before and After the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games: An Exploratory Independent-Samples Study
title_original: Public Perceptions of Disability and Para Athletes Before and After the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games: An Exploratory Independent-Samples Study
summary: The Paralympic Games are frequently promoted as a catalyst for social change, yet evidence regarding their social legacy remains limited and inconclusive. This study examined differences in French public perceptions of disability before and after the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games using an independent-samples pre–post design. Two surveys were administered to French adults one month before the Games (Time 1: n = 948; Mage = 36.43 years, SD = 13.67) and approximately two months after the Games (Time 2: n = 930; Mage = 37.40 years, SD = 11.83). The questionnaire assessed general perceptions of disability, perceptions of Para athletes, perceived sporting and professional capabilities of persons with physical and vision impairments, and perceived improvements in public accessibility. Participants surveyed after the Games reported higher scores on general disability perceptions, perceptions of Para athletes, and perceptions of persons with physical disabilities. In contrast, lower scores were observed on four of five items concerning persons with vision impairments. Participants with a disability and those with a close personal connection to disability also reported more positive perceptions of public accessibility after the Games. These findings suggest that public perceptions differed before and after the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games but varied by disability type. Given the independent-samples design, they should be interpreted cautiously.

title: When the season takes a toll - Severity and stability of anxiety and depression symptoms in German elite and amateur female soccer players
title_original: When the season takes a toll - Severity and stability of anxiety and depression symptoms in German elite and amateur female soccer players
summary: Among elite athletes, female soccer players face unique mental health challenges due to growing public attention and rising performance expectations, but limited support structures. However, research in this area lacks large-scale longitudinal studies, which can reveal symptom trajectories and periods of elevated symptoms. The present study addresses this gap by examining anxiety and depression symptoms in N = 406 female soccer players of different age groups (age: 12-17, n = 206; 18-24, n = 134; ≥ 25, n = 66) from six amateur and five elite clubs in Germany. We used the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Screener to assess symptoms at four time points. Aside from calculating symptom prevalences, we employed latent data analysis to examine symptom stability and change over the course of the season. Considerable proportions of players reported symptoms of anxiety (20-30%) and depression (15-25%) above established thresholds. Latent growth models demonstrated largely stable symptoms, with consistent between-person differences. Still, significant linear and quadratic symptom trends were detected, with symptom levels peaking around mid-season. During this period, players might experience increased performance pressure, academic stress, or accumulated physical strain. Our results underscore the importance of regular mental health screenings and targeted interventions, particularly during periods of elevated symptoms. In sum, this study contributes valuable insights into the mental health trajectories of female soccer players and provides practical implications for coaches and sport psychologists aiming to foster mental health among their players.

title: From outputs to outcomes? Examining the evolution of social impact reporting in UK major sport events [Abstract]
title_original: From outputs to outcomes? Examining the evolution of social impact reporting in UK major sport events [Abstract]
summary: Aim and Research Questions This research examines how social impact claims and reporting practices are constructed, evidenced, and evolved within documentary materials relating to major sport events in the UK across four cycles aligned to the Rio (2013 - 2016), Tokyo (2017 - 2021), Paris (2022 - 2024), and Los Angeles (2025 - present) Olympic and Paralympic Games. It asks: 1. How are social impact claims constructed and evidenced within major sport event reporting across the four cycles? 2. What content trends and changes occur across cycles? The project frames these questions as an opportunity to demonstrate how a Theory of Change (ToC) approach can strengthen evidential claims, support longitudinal assessment, and encourage more policy relevant, equitable reporting.

title: Quality of Life and Psychosocial Impact of Sport on People with Intellectual Disabilities: The Value of First-Person Discourse
title_original: Quality of Life and Psychosocial Impact of Sport on People with Intellectual Disabilities: The Value of First-Person Discourse
summary: Background: The concept of quality of life (QoL) has become a fundamental focus of research involving people with intellectual disabilities (IDs). Numerous studies have explored this concept. Furthermore, incorporating the first-person perspectives of people with disabilities has become essential in contemporary research. However, no studies have rigorously examined how sport participation among people with IDs is reflected across the QoL dimensions proposed by Schalock and Verdugo. The published literature on these aspects also suggests other emerging topics analyzed. Methods: A thematic synthesis was applied, structured around a directed qualitative content analysis of direct quotes from people with intellectual disabilities published in scientific articles, modified according to the dimensions of Quality of Life and identifying emerging categories. Subsequently, the codes were grouped into descriptive themes that were reinterpreted to generate higher-order analytical themes. A total of 390 direct quotes were analyzed from 24 selected articles. Results: The published accounts of the participants associated sports participation with several aspects of Quality of Life that engaging in sports provides them. The opinions of the individuals themselves refer to all areas of quality of life. Statements were also found referring to aspects such as having an occupation or a routine, other experiences (beyond strictly sporting ones), transition to adulthood, and negative statements and barriers. Conclusions: The testimonies of people with intellectual disabilities show that sport transcends the physical domain, impacting various dimensions of their quality of life. They report that sports practice depends on opportunities, support, and environmental barriers.

title: Strengthening Students’ Attitudes Toward Disability Inclusion
title_original: Strengthening Students’ Attitudes Toward Disability Inclusion
summary: The effectiveness of inclusion in physical education (PE) depends also on the willingness of students without disabilities to interact with and include peers with disabilities.We evaluated an inclusive program in 557 students (285 intervention) from ten schools using a pretest-posttest non-equivalent control-group design, with intact PE classes allocated non-randomly.In the intervention environment, students with developmental disabilities from special education schools participated alongside the students without disabilities in four weekly adapted PE sessions.In the control environment there were no students with disabilities.Students without disabilities completed questionnaires assessing attitudes toward disability inclusion and theory of planned behavior constructs.Attitudes increased more in the inclusive than in the control environment (b = 2.13, SE = 0.12, 95%CI [1.85, 2.41], t(7.4) = 17.71, p < .001,d = 2.46, 95%CI [2.14, 2.79]).Improvements occurred across all inclusionrelated constructs.Behavioral intention was mediated through injunctive norms and perceived behavioral control.

title: Three-dimensional inertial measurement unit-based analysis of wheelchair racing propulsion using a Sensor-in-Glove System
title_original: Three-dimensional inertial measurement unit-based analysis of wheelchair racing propulsion using a Sensor-in-Glove System
summary: This study proposes the Sensor‑in‑Glove System (SIGS), a field‑deployable method for measuring wheelchair racing propulsion during outdoor sprinting. SIGS synchronises two inertial measurement units (IMUs)—one embedded in a 3D‑printed glove and one mounted on the wheel—to capture push cycle‑wise hand and wheel kinematics. As a proof‑of‑concept validation, six elite athletes performed maximal‑effort 100‑m sprints. SIGS recorded continuous motion data, achieving a displacement‑estimation error of 0.73 % over a 10‑m interval. Propulsion onset and hand release were objectively identified from IMU signals without visual inspection, enabling the push cycle to be divided into mechanically meaningful phases. Newly defined 3D acceleration‑vector metrics revealed individual push styles, and peak resultant acceleration showed strong correlations with wheelchair velocity (r = 0.82–0.95). Class‑wise comparisons demonstrated significant differences in peak acceleration (F = 10.52, p < 0.001), indicating that SIGS captures impairment‑specific push characteristics. As the first field‑based 3D acceleration‑vector analysis using a glove‑embedded IMU, this study shows that SIGS provides a practical and quantitative approach for evaluating propulsion mechanics, and offers opportunities for technique assessment and athlete‑specific performance analysis in wheelchair racing.

title: Paralympic sport in Central Asia: a scoping review with descriptive analysis of participation, achievement, and medal efficiency (1996–2024)
title_original: Paralympic sport in Central Asia: a scoping review with descriptive analysis of participation, achievement, and medal efficiency (1996–2024)
summary: Published research on Paralympic sport in Central Asia remains limited despite the region's growing presence at the Games. This review focuses on elite, Games-level participation and achievement. We conducted a scoping review reported in line with the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews, alongside an analysis of International Paralympic Committee (IPC) archival data for five Central Asian countries (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan) across Summer (1996–2024) and Winter (1994–2026) Games, framed through the SPLISS model and the constraint-led approach. The scoping review maps international knowledge; the IPC analysis documents regional outcomes, offering complementary evidence. The review identified three domains: income-, gender-, and technology-linked participation gaps (D1); discipline-specific age profiles ranging from a median of 25 years in Para Swimming to 38 years in Para Equestrian (D2); and ten national policy factors linked to Paralympic success (D3). IPC data showed Central Asian participation rising from 15 athletes in 1996 to 113 in 2024, led by Uzbekistan ( n = 64, Paris 2024) and Kazakhstan ( n = 44), concentrated in Para Athletics, Para Judo, and Para Powerlifting, plus a full Kazakhstani sitting volleyball squad and Para Swimming. Female representation rose from 0% in 1996 to 41.6% in 2024, near the ∼43% global benchmark. Medal efficiency was 0% before 2012, spiked to 73.5% at Rio 2016 (95% CI 59.7%–83.8%), driven by Uzbekistan winning more medals than athletes that edition, then settled at 32.9% (Tokyo 2020) and 31.0% (Paris 2024, 95% CI 23.2%–40.0%); the 2016 spike is statistically distinguishable from other editions, while Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 are not. Uzbekistan grew from 0 athletes in 1996 to 64 in 2024, with the sharpest rise from 32 (Rio 2016) to 64 (Paris 2024), coinciding with documented 2019–2024 state Paralympic-development measures-a plausible institutional account alongside classification reform and host-proximity effects. No study identified by our search has examined elite Paralympic sport development in Central Asia specifically. Four research priorities are proposed: epidemiological profiling, adapted policy analysis with regional researchers, longitudinal athlete tracking, and psychological support programs.

title: Sleep Duration and Reaction Time in Athletes: The Impact of Sleep Deprivation and Sleep Quality on Cognitive-Motor Performance – A Narrative Review
title_original: Sleep Duration and Reaction Time in Athletes: The Impact of Sleep Deprivation and Sleep Quality on Cognitive-Motor Performance – A Narrative Review
summary: Background. Rapid perception, response selection and motor execution are the fundament of many sports, yet these processes may be vulnerable to insufficient or disrupted sleep.Aim. To critically synthesize evidence on the relationships between sleep duration, sleep deprivation, sleep quality and reaction-related cognitive-motor performance in athletes.Material and methods. A focused narrative literature search was carried out mainly in PubMed/MEDLINE, with additional sources identified through publisher databases and reference-list screening. Athlete-specific experimental and observational studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses and expert consensus publications were prioritized.Results. Acute total sleep deprivation consistently impairs vigilance and several reaction-time domains, whereas findings after partial sleep restriction are more heterogeneous. Sport-specific accuracy, response inhibition and complex cognitive-motor performance appear particularly susceptible. Sleep extension can improve vigilance and technical performance, but available intervention studies are generally small. Evidence linking habitual sleep quality independently of sleep duration to reaction time remains limited.Conclusions. Adequate sleep appears important for maintaining cognitive-motor performance in athletes, particularly when tasks require sustained attention, rapid response selection and technical precision. Individualized sleep strategies are preferable to a universal duration threshold.
