title: Exertional Heat Stroke — Recognition and Cooling Protocols: A Narrative Review
title_original: Exertional Heat Stroke — Recognition and Cooling Protocols: A Narrative Review
summary: Background. Exertional heat stroke (EHS) is the most severe form of exertional heat illness and one of the leading causes of non-traumatic sudden death in athletes, soldiers and outdoor workers. It is defined by central nervous system dysfunction combined with severe hyperthermia, and its outcome depends almost entirely on how quickly the diagnosis is made and body cooling is begun. With rising global temperatures and growing participation in endurance and team sports, timely recognition and correct cooling have become increasingly relevant to clinical practice. Aim. This narrative review synthesises the current evidence on the recognition of EHS and on cooling protocols, with a focus on medical aspects, and critically compares diagnostic tools and cooling modalities across sporting, military, occupational and community settings. Material and methods. A thematic narrative synthesis was performed of original studies, systematic reviews, case reports and consensus-based reviews addressing the pathophysiology, recognition, cooling and prevention of EHS. Results. EHS diagnosis rests on the combination of neurological dysfunction and elevated core temperature; rectal thermometry is the reference standard, whereas peripheral methods are unreliable and frequently unavailable. Rapid whole-body cold-water immersion is the gold-standard treatment; cooling rates above 0.15 °C·min⁻¹ and the principle of "cool first, transport second" are consistently associated with survival without complications, yet these practices remain incompletely implemented. Alternative field methods differ substantially in efficacy. Conclusions. Recognition and aggressive cooling are the decisive, modifiable determinants of survival in EHS. Persistent gaps in temperature assessment, prehospital protocols and provider knowledge must be closed to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality.

title: Sleep, chronotype, and jet lag in athletic performance: a narrative review
title_original: Sleep, chronotype, and jet lag in athletic performance: a narrative review
summary: Background: The circadian timing system governs near-24-hour rhythms in body temperature, hormone secretion, and neuromuscular function that shape athletes' capacity to train, recover, and compete. Sleep, chronotype, and transmeridian travel are three interrelated circadian domains with direct medical relevance for performance. Aim: To critically appraise current evidence on how sleep quantity and quality, chronotype, and jet lag influence physical and cognitive performance in athletes, and to review countermeasures. Material and methods: Narrative review of experimental studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses addressing sleep, circadian rhythms, chronotype, and travel in athletic populations. Results: Athletes habitually sleep under 8 hours per night with reduced efficiency, and 28–65% screen as poor sleepers. Acute sleep loss degrades physical performance by approximately 7.6%, with afternoon and evening tasks most affected. Chronotype shifts the diurnal performance curve: morning types perform best early and evening types later, while late chronotypes may vary by up to 26% across the day. Time since entrained awakening predicts peak performance more reliably than clock time. Athletes report higher perceived exertion when training against their circadian preference. Social jetlag and eastward transmeridian travel impair strength, power, and aerobic capacity and raise injury risk. Sleep extension, strategic napping, light management, and melatonin partially offset these deficits. Conclusions: Sleep and circadian alignment are modifiable determinants of performance and health. Chronotype-informed scheduling and structured sleep and travel protocols should be integrated into athlete care, though heterogeneous methods limit firm conclusions.

title: The interpersonal and intrapsychic functions of the pride expression
title_original: The interpersonal and intrapsychic functions of the pride expression
summary: A large body of research suggests that pride is associated with a distinct, cross-culturally recognized and spontaneously displayed nonverbal expression. Given its apparent universality, this expression is likely to have evolved as a functional signal, benefitting both receivers and senders. Here, we focus primarily on the intrapsychic benefits received by those who express pride. We review research suggesting that the expression communicates an individual's deservedness of high status to others, and that it does so implicitly and across diverse cultural contexts. We then discuss the expression's function in the context of dual-strategies theory, which suggests that there are two distinct forms of high rank: prestige, based on earned respect, and dominance, based on threat of force. Studies suggest that the pride expression reliably and cross-culturally communicates prestige, but not dominance. Finally, we discuss functions of the pride expression that go beyond the display's signal value. In sum, the pride nonverbal expression appears to be a highly functional display that likely evolved to facilitate humans' adaptive responding to opportunities for social rank attainment. This article is part of the theme issue 'Mechanisms, development, phylogeny and functions of emotional expressions'.

title: Historical and Contemporary Functions of Rituals in the Olympic Games
title_original: Historical and Contemporary Functions of Rituals in the Olympic Games
summary: The Olympic Games represent a multidimensional structure in which rituals, symbols, and ceremonial practices occupy an important place alongside athletic competition. In the Ancient Olympic Games, sacred processions, oaths, offerings, sacrifices, and award practices constituted important elements of the religious and social order. In the Modern Olympic Games, the Olympic rings, the flame and torch relay, the oath, and the opening, closing, and medal ceremonies are among the fundamental components of the symbolic and institutional structure of the Olympic Movement. This study aims to evaluate the rituals associated with the Olympic Games in terms of the functions they perform within the Games, rather than limiting the discussion to their historical development or to formal similarities and differences between the Ancient and Modern Olympics. Designed as a narrative review, the study examines historical and classical sources, academic studies, and institutional documents of the International Olympic Committee. Based on the evaluation of the literature, the functions of Olympic rituals were examined under five interrelated dimensions: the production of sacredness and meaning; regulatory, normative, and institutional functions; the formation of unity and belonging; the ritualization of achievement and honor; and the representation and visibility of Olympic values. The findings indicate that, in the Ancient Olympic Games, rituals contributed to maintaining the sacred order, reinforcing behavioral norms, and publicly honoring athletic achievement, whereas in the Modern Olympic Games they serve to sustain institutional order, symbolically reinforce a shared sense of belonging, ceremonially recognize achievement, and make Olympic values visible. In conclusion, Olympic rituals can be regarded not merely as ceremonial elements accompanying the Olympic Games, but as interrelated and multifunctional practices that contribute to the construction and maintenance of the Games’ worlds of meaning, order, belonging, achievement, and values.

title: Sex Differences in Injury, Stoppage and Concussion Rates in Amateur and Olympic-Style Boxing
title_original: Sex Differences in Injury, Stoppage and Concussion Rates in Amateur and Olympic-Style Boxing
summary: Background. Women have boxed at the Olympic Games since 2012; since 2013 elite men have competed without headguards while women have kept them. Sex differences in injury, stoppage and concussion rates in amateur and Olympic-style boxing have not been systematically reviewed. The review question was: in amateur and Olympic-style boxers, do injury incidence, stoppage rates and concussion rates differ between women and men? Methods. PubMed/MEDLINE and Consensus were searched on 29 September 2026 (English-language reports, no date limit), with backward citation searching. Eligible studies reported at least one outcome (injury, stoppage, diagnosed concussion, laceration, fracture, other craniofacial or regional injury, or acute neurocognitive change) for women and men from the same amateur or Olympic-style boxing population with sex-specific denominators; outcomes were kept separate. Screening and extraction were single-reviewer with verification. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-E and certainty with GRADE. Risk ratios (women versus men) were pooled with a restricted maximum likelihood random-effects model with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Results. From 416 unique database records and 36 citation-search records, four studies were eligible, all International Olympic Committee injury-surveillance cohorts (Olympic Games 2012, 2016 and 2020; Youth Olympic Games 2018). Sex-specific boxing data were available from the published text of two. At London 2012, where both sexes wore headguards, 7 of 36 women (19.4%) and 18 of 247 men (7.3%) sustained a medical-attention injury (risk ratio 2.67, 95% CI 1.20 to 5.94). At Tokyo 2020, where men boxed without headguards and women with them, the reported risk ratio was 0.43 (0.24 to 0.75). The pooled estimate (risk ratio 1.05) was not interpretable (I² = 92%; Hartung-Knapp 95% CI 0.00 to >1000). No eligible study reported stoppages, diagnosed concussion, lacerations, fractures or neurocognitive change by sex. Certainty of evidence was very low. Conclusions. The direction of the sex difference in injury reversed once protective-equipment rules diverged by sex, and no sex-stratified evidence exists for stoppages or concussion. Regulators cannot assume equal or unequal risk by sex. Sex-stratified surveillance with exposure denominators, recording stoppage and concussion by sex, is a prerequisite for evidence-based sex-specific rules. Registration. Not registered.

title: Genomic Surveillance of Anti-Microbial Resistance within the One Health Framework
title_original: Genomic Surveillance of Anti-Microbial Resistance within the One Health Framework
summary: Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat and widely recognised as a ‘silent pandemic’. It occurs when available antibiotics fail to effectively treat infections in humans and animals, leading to increased morbidity, mortality, and healthcare and economic costs. The emergence of AMR extends beyond hospital settings, with healthy communities, animals, and environments serving as reservoirs for transmission. Hence, effective surveillance systems for monitoring the emergence and spread of resistant pathogens across various sectors are very much needed, in line with the One Health framework. In recent years, advances in genomic technologies have transformed AMR research and surveillance by enabling high-resolution characterisation of high-priority pathogens and their resistance determinants. This chapter explores the role of genomic surveillance in detecting, monitoring, and understanding the mechanisms of antibiotic resistance. Key genomic approaches, including metagenomic and whole-genome sequencing (WGS), are discussed in relation to their applications in identifying resistance genes (ARGs), tracking transmission pathways, and investigating outbreaks. The chapter also highlights the comparison and/or integration of culture and genomic techniques to achieve the desired objectives while balancing cost, time, and analytical performance. Finally, future perspectives on the integration of genomics within a One Health framework, particularly for multi-pathogen detection through wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES), are discussed.

title: Isometric trunk strength in seated para-athletes: relationship to manual muscle testing and comparison with non-impaired controls
title_original: Isometric trunk strength in seated para-athletes: relationship to manual muscle testing and comparison with non-impaired controls
summary: Introduction Trunk muscle strength is an important performance indicator in para-athletes competing in seated sports and is commonly assessed in classification systems using manual muscle testing (MMT), together with functional and sport-specific tests. Quantitative isometric strength measures may provide complementary information about force-generating capacity. However, the relationship between isometric trunk strength and MMT-assessed trunk and hip strength is not well described in para-athletes with neuromusculoskeletal impairments. This study aimed to examine isometric trunk strength in seated para-athletes and compare it with 1) MMT scores of the trunk and hips and 2) isometric trunk strength in a reference group without physical impairments. Methods Male para-athletes competing in seated sports ( n = 32, 34.7 ± 13.7 years, 8.7 ± 4.1 exercise h/week) and a reference group without physical impairments of similar age and weekly exercise ( n = 10, 35.0 ± 12.5 years, 9.8 ± 6.4 exercise h/week) participated. Isometric strength was measured seated for flexion, extension, rotation, and lateral flexion using a strength rig. MMT of the trunk and hips was summed to obtain an MMT Trunk–Hip score. Associations with isometric strength were examined using Spearman's rank correlation. Para-athletes were categorized into Very Low, Low, Moderate, and High MMT Trunk–Hip groups. Group differences were analyzed using Kruskal–Wallis tests. Results Higher MMT Trunk–Hip scores were associated with greater maximal isometric trunk strength in all movement directions ( p < 0.001), with large effect sizes. The High group did not differ from the reference group, whereas the Very Low and Low groups consistently demonstrated lower strength across directions. The Moderate group showed greater heterogeneity, with strength varying by movement direction. Conclusion MMT Trunk–Hip scores were strongly associated with isometric trunk strength in seated para-athletes, supporting MMT's ability to capture meaningful differences in trunk and hip muscle strength. However, direction-specific variation indicates that MMT does not fully characterize force-generating capacity. Quantitative isometric strength testing may provide complementary information for evaluating and monitoring trunk strength, particularly for performance enhancement. In para-sport classification, these findings support the construct validity of MMT while highlighting the potential value of quantitative strength measures for developing and validating multidimensional assessment methods.

title: User-Centric Pedestrian Navigation: Transfer Study from Sofia to Tokyo
title_original: User-Centric Pedestrian Navigation: Transfer Study from Sofia to Tokyo
summary: Pedestrian route-finding applications are commonly used for urban navigation. These applications typically focus on finding the shortest or fastest route and rarely consider pedestrian safety or comfort. Such non-utilitarian factors can be accounted for by incorporating a walkability index in the routing algorithm. This study transfers an existing user-centric pedestrian routing approach from Sofia to the Tokyo wards of Shinjuku and Bunkyo. The approach considers the heterogenous needs of different user groups by using an adjustable weighting scheme. Data from OpenStreetMap and local open datasets on streetscape features such as sidewalk width and incline are standardised and walkability scores are calculated using the developed framework. Results indicate that the Sofia routing approach is cleanly transferable to Tokyo. Wasserstein’s, Cliff’s delta, and Kolmogorov-Smirnov’s statistical tests show that calculated walkability scores remain consistent with the intentions of the framework. Calculated routes in Tokyo successfully increase average walkability compared to the shortest path, without excessively increasing length. Walkability scores are unevenly distributed in the study area, with street segments in pedestrianised residential areas with many parks receiving high scores, while major roads that lack dedicated pedestrian infrastructure receive lower scores. The different user profiles lead to spatially distinct walkability patterns. Scores for tourists are high around densely concentrated commercial facilities, while scores for wheelchair users are high along arterial roads with wide sidewalks and low incline. By successfully adapting an existing pedestrian routing method, this study demonstrates that using user-specific walkability scores for route-finding can be a viable approach in different contexts.

title: Facteurs de motivation scolaire des élèves dans la pratique de l’appui tendu renversé (ATR) en classe de terminale D5 au Lycée Moderne 1 de Gagnoa
title_original: Facteurs de motivation scolaire des élèves dans la pratique de l’appui tendu renversé (ATR) en classe de terminale D5 au Lycée Moderne 1 de Gagnoa
summary: Cette étude porte sur les facteurs influençant l’engagement des élèves dans la réalisation de l’Appui Tendu Renversé (ATR) en Éducation Physique et Sportive, à partir du cas des élèves de la TD5 du Lycée Moderne 1 de Gagnoa. Elle vise à analyser la perception des élèves ainsi que leur motivation lors de cette activité gymnique exigeante. La méthodologie adoptée combine une approche quantitative et qualitative, à travers un questionnaire administré à 54 élèves et des entretiens semi-directifs réalisés auprès de 20 élèves. Les données ont fait l’objet d’une analyse thématique descriptive. Les résultats montrent que la plupart des élèves de TD5 ont une connaissance et compréhension de l’ATR, sont motivés à pratiquer l’Appui Tendu Renversé (ATR), mais sont limités dans leur apprentissage de ce mouvement gymnique à cause des difficultés d’articulation des mouvements ainsi que de l’influence de l’environnement. Les résultats révèlent également que la peur de l’échec, les difficultés techniques et le manque de confiance limitent l’implication des élèves, tandis qu’un accompagnement pédagogique adapté et un climat de classe favorable renforcent leur motivation. L’étude souligne ainsi l’importance de satisfaire les besoins d’autonomie, de compétence et de soutien social afin de favoriser un engagement durable des élèves dans l’apprentissage de l’ATR. This study examines the factors influencing student engagement in performing the Handstand (ATR) in Physical Education and Sports, using the case of students in TD5 at Lycée Moderne 1 in Gagnoa. The data were analyzed using a descriptive thematic approach. The results show that most TD5 students have knowledge and understanding of the ATR, are motivated to practice the handstand (ATR), but are limited in their learning of this gymnastic movement due to difficulties in executing the movements as well as the influence of the environment. The results reveal that fear of failure, technical difficulties, and a lack of confidence limit student involvement, while appropriate pedagogical support and a positive classroom environment strengthen their motivation. The study thus highlights the importance of meeting students' needs for autonomy, competence, and social support to foster sustained student engagement in learning the Handstand.

title: Introduction: Rivalry, Recognition, and Soft Power in Sport Diplomacy
title_original: Introduction: Rivalry, Recognition, and Soft Power in Sport Diplomacy
summary: Sport diplomacy scholarship has continued to grow in recent years. This new literature builds on earlier ideas but moves beyond the studies as a battle between superpowers or the hosting of mega-events. Moving beyond these countries to consider regional rivalries, minority or oppressed groups, and middle powers brings greater insight into sport diplomacy and how it has functioned, particularly as a form of soft power. The Olympic movement and football are still important within sport diplomacy, but their examination from states other than the dominant countries provides more nuanced understanding. In addition, newer sport diplomacy scholarship incorporates different countries and sports, and increasingly considers women athletes and teams as important actors within sport diplomacy.

title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research on Crowds and Disasters: A Vosviewer-Based Study Using the Scopus Database
title_original: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research on Crowds and Disasters: A Vosviewer-Based Study Using the Scopus Database
summary: Crowds are defined as situations in which large numbers of individuals congregate in close proximity. These environments can be observed in everyday settings such as shopping malls and metro stations, as well as planned events like football matches and the Olympic Games. In such settings, physical closeness, lack of social distancing and insufficient hygiene may pose significant public health and safety risks. When not properly managed, crowds can harm large numbers of people and exacerbate the impacts of existing disasters. The relationship between crowds and disasters is critical to risk assessment and crisis management. This study aims to conduct a bibliometric analysis of research within the context of crowds and disasters by examining documents indexed in the Scopus database using the keywords “crowd and disaster”. Bibliometric visualizations were generated using VOSviewer software. The analysis revealed that the most frequently used keywords were disaster management, crowd disasters, crowdsourcing, social media, and disaster response. In more recent years, keywords such as metro station, crowd evacuation, emergency evacuation, crowd disasters and stampede have gained prominence. It was also found that studies in this area spanned multiple disciplines, notably computer science, engineering, and the social sciences. Based on the findings, three research recommendations are proposed: fostering interdisciplinary collaboration, enhancing international cooperation and promoting research on crowds and disasters.

title: Age-Related Performance in Taekwondo Athletes with Physical Disabilities: An Analysis of the Paralympic Games
title_original: Age-Related Performance in Taekwondo Athletes with Physical Disabilities: An Analysis of the Paralympic Games
summary: Abstract This study investigated age-related performance in Para taekwondo athletes across two Paralympic Games editions, Tokyo 2020 + 1 and Paris 2024, examining potential differences according to Paralympic edition, sex, and competitive achievement. Data were obtained from the official results books of the Paralympic Games and included 192 Paralympic participation records, comprising 95 female and 97 male records. Age-related performance was analyzed according to Paralympic edition, sex, and competitive achievement, classified as medallist or non-medallist. Mann–Whitney U tests were used to compare age differences between groups, while chi-square (χ²) tests of independence were applied to examine the distribution of athletes across age categories (≤ 20, 21–25, 26–30, and ≥ 31 years). Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Female athletes were younger than male athletes at Paralympic participation (26 vs. 28 years; U = 3765.00, p = 0.028). No significant differences were observed between Paralympic editions (27 years for both; U = 4128.50, p = 0.653) or between medallists and non-medallists (26 vs. 28 years; U = 3395.50, p = 0.053). The distribution of athletes across age groups was similar for both sexes (χ²(3) = 5.71, p = 0.126) and competitive achievement levels (χ²(3) = 4.89, p = 0.180). Age differed by sex, whereas no significant age differences were observed according to competitive achievement or Paralympic edition. Overall, the age profile of Para taekwondo athletes at the Paralympic Games was concentrated in the late twenties, with female athletes showing a younger age profile than males, suggesting a consistent age pattern in this Paralympic combat sport.

title: A retrospective assessment of short-horizon real-time COVID-19 projections in Tokyo
title_original: A retrospective assessment of short-horizon real-time COVID-19 projections in Tokyo
summary: We examine the features of five real-time COVID-19 infection projections in Tokyo. We find that these projections tended to (i) overpredict subsequently reported infections, (ii) be less accurate when issued during the fifth infection wave, and (iii) underpredict subsequently reported infections when issued during the rising phase but overpredict them when issued during the peak and falling phases. If policymakers and the public were to utilize real-time projections in future pandemics, it would be useful for them to be aware of the possibility that real-time projections may have systematic patterns.

title: Frame Running participation in all settings for people with physical disabilities—a systematic scoping review
title_original: Frame Running participation in all settings for people with physical disabilities—a systematic scoping review
summary: Purpose This systematic scoping review aimed to map existing knowledge concerning Frame Running across settings for people with physical disabilities.Methods A three-step search strategy was applied across five databases (MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, APA PsycInfo, and Scopus) through August 2025.Results Twenty studies (2010-2025) were included; quantitative (n = 16), qualitative (n = 1), and mixed-methods (n = 3). Most originated from Sweden (n = 6) and the United Kingdom (n = 6). The majority examined health impacts and physiological responses (n = 12), followed by performance enhancement and classification (n = 7), and participant experiences and perspectives (n = 1). Half of the studies included only participants with cerebral palsy (n = 10). Study designs were predominantly cross-sectional (n = 12), with a smaller number of pre-post study designs (n = 3), two of which assessed feasibility. In total, the studies included 494 Frame Running participants.Conclusions Frame Running is an emerging research field with suggested physiological and psychosocial benefits. Evidence is largely quantitative and cross-sectional, highlighting the need for prospective studies with low risk of bias to clarify its impacts and effectiveness of Frame Running, alongside research on lived experiences. Research should evaluate the classification structure and address accessibility across settings to support equitable access and further development.

title: Feasibility of molecular-based testing strategies for SARS-CoV-2-screening in workplaces: a systematic review and reporting checklist
title_original: Feasibility of molecular-based testing strategies for SARS-CoV-2-screening in workplaces: a systematic review and reporting checklist
summary: Background The COVID-19 pandemic underscored the need for effective workplace screening methods, particularly where remote work is not feasible. While lateral flow tests were common, molecular-based testing methods like PCR offer higher sensitivity and specificity. This review examines the feasibility, methods, barriers and facilitators of implementing molecular testing strategies in workplace settings. Methods We conducted a systematic search in the databases PubMed, Cochrane, Web of Science and medRxiv for publications from 1 January 2020 onwards. The search was conducted twice (last in January 2025) to update results. Studies focused on non-healthcare workplaces, excluding schools, universities and care settings. Quality was assessed using standard reporting guidelines, and data were synthesised narratively due to heterogeneous study designs. Results From 1777 records, 51 studies met inclusion criteria, primarily from industrial, laboratory and office settings across 21 countries, mostly in the Global North. Implementation of molecular-based testing was effective in reducing COVID-19 incidence in workplace settings when combined with quick turnaround times and frequent testing. Many employees felt it was the employer’s responsibility to provide safety measures like testing. Challenges for implementation included logistical issues (sample collection, turnaround and ensuring employee participation). Some studies reported higher participation with saliva-based testing compared with nasopharyngeal swabs. While voluntary PCR testing does not increase on-site work when working from home is possible, regular PCR testing decreases durations of absence due to quarantine or isolation. Although higher sensitivity of tests can improve risk reduction in various scenarios, quick turnaround times of test results appear to be at least as or more important than test sensitivity. Conclusions Molecular-based testing strategies in workplaces are feasible and can contribute to pandemic disease control. However, success depends on consideration of ethical, logistical and financial factors. Core parameters are testing frequency, test sensitivity and turnaround. This review suggests a checklist for reporting on workplace testing strategies in future epidemic or pandemic situations. PROSPERO registration number CRD42023391600.

title: Pathways to the podium: age and technical-tactical factors associated with medalling in Para Judo
title_original: Pathways to the podium: age and technical-tactical factors associated with medalling in Para Judo
summary: This study aimed to explore factors associated with medalling in Para judo at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games, focusing on athlete characteristics and technical-tactical variables. Using published competition results, medalling outcomes for men and women were separately modelled using Bayesian penalised regression. Models included age, body weight, sport class, throws, groundwork techniques, and penalties per match. Results are reported as posterior probabilities that the regression coefficient was greater or less than zero, Pr(β > 0) or Pr(β < 0), according to the direction of the posterior mean. In males, age showed a predominantly negative posterior distribution (Pr[β < 0] = .944), whereas body weight (Pr[β > 0] = .972), throws (Pr[β > 0] >.999), groundwork techniques (Pr[β > 0] >.999), and penalties (Pr[β > 0] = .962) showed predominantly positive posterior distributions. In females, throws and groundwork techniques showed positive associations with medalling (both Pr[β > 0] >.999), whereas age (Pr[β < 0] = .818) and penalties (Pr[β < 0] = .801) showed predominantly negative posterior distributions with greater uncertainty. Overall, throws and groundwork techniques showed the most consistent positive associations with medalling across both sex-specific models. These findings may inform technical-tactical priorities and long-term athlete development in Para judo.

title: Adaptive Sports and Social Reintegration
title_original: Adaptive Sports and Social Reintegration
summary: Purpose: This study aimed to examine the role of participation in adaptive sports in the process of social reintegration among individuals with acquired physical disabilities, with a specific focus on para alpine skiing. Particular attention was given to the development of athletic identity and life satisfaction. Methods: This qualitative study formed part of a broader sequential mixed-method investigation. Following a quantitative phase involving 129 para alpine skiers, semi-structured interviews were conducted with six purposively selected elite para alpine skiers who participated in the Sochi 2014 Winter Paralympic Games to complement and deepen the quantitative findings. Data were analysed using qualitative content analysis informed by grounded theory principles, allowing for the identification of key categories and relationships within the resocialisation process. Results: The findings indicate that participation in adaptive sports, particularly para alpine skiing, plays a central role in social reintegration after disability. Athletes reported significant improvements in life satisfaction, driven by increased independence, structured daily routines, and meaningful goal-oriented activity. The reconstruction of athletic identity emerged as a key mechanism underlying psychological adaptation, contributing to enhanced self-concept and self-efficacy. In addition, participation in adaptive sports facilitated the expansion of social networks and strengthened interpersonal relationships, supporting broader social reintegration. However, the process was influenced by contextual factors, such as financial constraints and access to sports infrastructure. Conclusions: Adaptive sports participation represents a critical pathway for social reintegration, promoting life satisfaction and athletic identity development among individuals with disabilities. These findings highlight the importance of reducing structural barriers and ensuring equitable access to sport as part of comprehensive rehabilitation strategies.

title: Prevalence and patterns of sports supplement use in elite wheelchair basketball players: an analysis based on the AIS framework
title_original: Prevalence and patterns of sports supplement use in elite wheelchair basketball players: an analysis based on the AIS framework
summary: Background Sports supplement use is widespread in elite sport, yet evidence regarding supplementation practices in Paralympic team sports remains limited. Wheelchair basketball players present specific physiological and contextual characteristics that may influence supplement use and its alignment with current scientific evidence. Methods A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted in 66 elite Spanish wheelchair basketball players (57 men and 9 women) from 10 first-division teams. Participants completed a validated questionnaire assessing self-reported sports supplement use, reasons for consumption, and sources of information. Supplements were classified according to the Australian Institute of Sport (AIS) framework based on scientific evidence and safety. Descriptive and exploratory analyses were performed to examine associations between self-reported sports supplement use and athlete characteristics, including sex, functional classification, and training profile. Results Overall, 72.7% of athletes reported current self-reported sports supplement use. Expressed as proportions of the entire sample ( n = 66), Group A products were consumed by 66.7% of athletes, Group B products by 31.8%, while no athletes reported using Group C (0%) or Group D (0%) substances. Protein supplements, creatine monohydrate, and caffeine were the most frequently consumed products. Supplement use patterns were generally similar across sex and functional classifications, although no statistically significant differences were observed. Conclusion Elite wheelchair basketball players show a high prevalence of self-reported sports supplement use, predominantly involving products currently classified within AIS Group A. While the primary use of Group A supplements reflects a high intake of products with established efficacy, actual evidence-based practice requires individualized evaluation, underscoring the importance of professionally guided nutrition strategies in Paralympic team sports.

title: Multidimensional approach to perceptions in football academies about educational, relational, inclusive, safety and social aspects among players, parents and coaches
title_original: Multidimensional approach to perceptions in football academies about educational, relational, inclusive, safety and social aspects among players, parents and coaches
summary: Introduction Youth football represents an important educational and social environment for young people’s development. Previous studies have typically assessed players, coaches, and parents using the same questionnaire to directly compare perceptions. Although methodologically rigorous, this approach may overlook role-specific perspectives. Therefore, this study aimed to analyse and compare the perceptions of players, coaches, and parents regarding the educational and social value of youth football from their respective viewpoints. Methods A multidimensional, multi-stakeholder approach was adopted through a comparative re-analysis of data collected using three role-specific questionnaires administered to players, coaches, and parents. While differing in wording, the questionnaires addressed equivalent concepts across five contextual dimensions: (1) educational value of the football academy, (2) educational and communicative relationships, (3) inclusion and equity, (4) safety and relational climate, and (5) social function of the club. Composite indices were calculated for each dimension and analysed using descriptive statistics and between-group comparisons through Welch’s ANOVA. Results No statistically significant differences emerged among players, coaches, and parents regarding the educational value of football academies, educational relationships, and inclusion-related dimensions. However, significant differences emerged in perceptions of safety and the club’s social function ( p < 0.05). Coaches reported significantly higher perceptions of safety compared with the other stakeholder groups, whereas parents attributed greater social value to football academies than players did. Descriptive analyses further highlighted greater variability in players’ responses, suggesting that young athletes’ experiences are less homogeneous than the representations provided by adults. Discussion These findings emphasize the importance of considering stakeholder-specific perspectives when evaluating the educational and social role of youth football. Greater alignment between organizational practices, educational objectives, and young athletes’ lived experiences may enhance the effectiveness of youth sport environments. Furthermore, the role-specific methodology adopted in this study generated stakeholder-relevant findings while preserving methodological rigor, offering a valuable framework for future research in youth sport settings.

Coaches reported significantly higher perceptions of safety compared with the other stakeholder groups, whereas parents attributed greater social value to football academies than players did. Descriptive analyses further highlighted greater variability in players’ responses, suggesting that young athletes’ experiences are less homogeneous than the representations provided by adults. Discussion These findings emphasize the importance of considering stakeholder-specific perspectives when evaluating the educational and social role of youth football. Greater alignment between organizational practices, educational objectives, and young athletes’ lived experiences may enhance the effectiveness of youth sport environments. Furthermore, the role-specific methodology adopted in this study generated stakeholder-relevant findings while preserving methodological rigor, offering a valuable framework for future research in youth sport settings.

title: Tactical and technical indicators in wheelchair rugby: a preliminary analysis of elite Brazilian teams
title_original: Tactical and technical indicators in wheelchair rugby: a preliminary analysis of elite Brazilian teams
summary: Although ample evidence demonstrates that tactical and technical indicators play a pivotal role in match analysis, a consensus on the most effective predictors of success in wheelchair rugby (WR) remains elusive. Therefore, the aim of this study is to analyze potential tactical-technical indicators of points scored and match outcomes in WR among elite Brazilian teams. Notational analysis was conducted on the semifinals and finals matches of the “II Copa dos Campeões de Rugby em Cadeira de Rodas”, using the Lince 1.4 software. Tactical-technical performance indicators were evaluated by decision-making quality and overall game efficiencies and frequencies. Fisher's exact test evaluated the association between decision-making quality and score outcomes, while an independent t-test compared performance differences between winning and losing teams. Appropriate decision-making for pass, reception, and throw-in was statistically associated with a successful try outcome (P<0.05). Regarding the performance parameter efficiencies between winning and losing teams, large and very large effects in favor of winning were identified for steals/interceptions (d= 1.2) and throw-ins (d= 2.4), respectively. In conclusion, strategic decision-making related to passing, receiving, and the throw-in seems to be essential for scoring tries. Moreover, throw-in efficiency and steals/interceptions emerged as possible performance indicators among elite Brazilian teams.

title: Does Prudential Regulation Improve Solvency? A Structural Break Analysis of Pension Fund Dynamics
title_original: Does Prudential Regulation Improve Solvency? A Structural Break Analysis of Pension Fund Dynamics
summary: This paper examines whether the 2019 prudential regulatory event improved pension-fund solvency dynamics. The analysis relies exclusively on previously estimated results reported in the thesis archive and combines ARIMA intervention models, polynomial time-trend regressions, Chow structural-break tests, and time-series decompositions. ARIMA results show no statistically significant intervention effect for the solvency-related index in either group (Control: xreg = 0.0024, p = 0.7423; Treatment: xreg = 0.0190, p = 0.3090). Time-trend regressions likewise show no differential post-event effect, although the treatment coefficient is negative and significant (-0.0491; p = 0.002). Chow tests, however, detect significant structural breaks in 2019 for both groups, with stronger evidence in treatment (Control: F = 1.710325, p = 0.0114; Treatment: F = 1.985284, p = 0.0015). Decomposition results show mild deterioration in the control trajectory and continued upward trend in treatment. The evidence therefore points to structural adjustment and heterogeneous resilience rather than a clean causal solvency gain attributable to the intervention regressor alone.

title: A Circulatory System Approach to Needs Assessment: A Conceptual Model Integrating Societal, Organizational, and Human Resource Levels
title_original: A Circulatory System Approach to Needs Assessment: A Conceptual Model Integrating Societal, Organizational, and Human Resource Levels
summary: Needs Assessment (NA) is an important process for organizational and educational contexts as they develop plans. However, many of today's predominant needs assessment frameworks conceptualize needs assessments as linear or otherwise level-limited processes, making them less effective in highly complex and rapidly changing environments. This article provides a critical review of five currently influential models of needs assessment and proposes a conceptual framework that looks at needs assessment as an ongoing process through the lens of a systems thinking approach. By using the metaphor of a circulatory system, the proposed model integrates all three levels (social, organizational, and human) into a connected analytical framework. In addition, the proposed model gives specific decision-entry rules for identifying where to start analyzing needs and how to transfer the metaphorical perspective of the proposed framework into a logical series of procedures that will guide the diagnosis and intervention process. The proposed model attempts to address fragmentation in existing models and their inability to represent needs assessment in a dynamic and iterative manner. In essence, the proposed needs assessment framework provides practical guidance to decision makers and practitioners of needs assessments by offering both a flexible and structured approach to conducting needs assessments within a variety of different forms or settings.

title: Reconceptualising Implementation Readiness as a Dynamic System: A Framework for Educational Change
title_original: Reconceptualising Implementation Readiness as a Dynamic System: A Framework for Educational Change
summary: Educational reforms often fall short not only because policies are poorly designed but also because education systems lack the systemic readiness required for effective implementation. Although readiness is widely acknowledged as important, current frameworks tend to treat it as a preliminary stage rather than as a dynamic, multi-level capacity, leaving a significant theoretical gap. This paper extends existing models by developing the Educational Policy Implementation Readiness Framework (EPIRF), which reconceptualises readiness as an evolving configuration of psychological, cultural, structural, and political conditions that shape reform success. Drawing on an integrative review of organisational change theory and educational policy implementation research, the EPIRF identifies four interdependent readiness dimensions: Activation, Alignment, Mobilisation, and Institutionalisation. The framework’s contribution lies less in the labelling of these dimensions than in their relational and political reinterpretation for multi-level educational systems, in which readiness is recursive and continuously renegotiated rather than sequential. The preliminary model was refined through a Delphi-informed expert validation (N = 15) in which all framework components met the a priori consensus threshold. Observable markers and a candidate item pool are proposed for each dimension to support future operationalisation. The EPIRF offers policymakers and system leaders a diagnostic lens for assessing and strengthening the conditions necessary for sustainable reform, and it offers researchers a means of identifying misalignments in reform processes and designing context-responsive implementation strategies.

title: Adaptive Gyroscopic Leadership Model: Integrating Planned and Generative Orientations in Principal Leadership Preparation
title_original: Adaptive Gyroscopic Leadership Model: Integrating Planned and Generative Orientations in Principal Leadership Preparation
summary: School principal leadership increasingly operates within contexts characterized by ambiguity, uncertainty, disruption, accountability pressures, and rapid social and technological change. Traditional approaches to principal leadership often struggle to prepare aspiring leaders for the interpretive, relational, and adaptive demands of contemporary practice. This theoretical paper examines the reconceptualization of principal leadership preparation through the integration of planned and generative orientations in organizational development. Drawing on these perspectives, this paper introduces the Adaptive Gyroscopic Leadership Model (AGLM) as a conceptual framework for understanding how leadership preparation programs can cultivate the capacity to maintain purposeful direction while responding to changing environments. The AGLM conceptualizes leadership preparation through five interdependent components: core commitments, sustained learning momentum, planned learning structures, generative learning structures, and contextual forces. Their continuous interaction provides a framework for creating learning conditions intended to support candidates’ professional judgment and adaptive capacity. This paper presents the redesign of a public university’s Educational Leadership program as an illustrative application of the AGLM. Specifically, program elements related to coursework and clinical practice, assessment, and learning support are mapped onto the framework. The paper contributes to educational leadership scholarship by offering a theoretically grounded framework for designing principal leadership programs that develop adaptive and reflective leaders.

title: Educational Leadership for Social Mobility in Arab Minority Schools: A Comparative Case Study from Israel
title_original: Educational Leadership for Social Mobility in Arab Minority Schools: A Comparative Case Study from Israel
summary: Social mobility refers to the ability of students to progress in society in adulthood. Studies on the school principal’s role in promoting social mobility have predominantly focused on schools with ethnic and cultural diversity and less on schools serving minority communities. The current study addresses the principals’ role, comparing two schools from the same minority group that differ in their organizational and student characteristics. Using a qualitative comparative-case study design, data were collected through 30 semi-structured interviews with school community members, including principals, teachers, parents, and students, as well as four observations. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis, which revealed both similarities and differences between the cases. In both cases, principals emphasized emotional and social aspects, promoted students’ leadership and empowerment, and focused on skills and abilities. Nevertheless, the two schools differed regarding the perceptions of grades and technological skills. Additionally, the principals’ perceptions were related to gender and socioeconomic backgrounds. The study extends the literature on social mobility leadership and culturally responsive leadership by demonstrating how leadership practices are adapted to different organizational, socioeconomic, and cultural contexts within the same minority community. The findings may assist school leaders and policymakers in designing context-sensitive strategies to promote students’ social mobility in minority schools.

title: Role of Strategic Management Accounting In Decent Work And Economic Growth In The Context Of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
title_original: Role of Strategic Management Accounting In Decent Work And Economic Growth In The Context Of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
summary: Purpose: This investigation aims to examine the function of strategic management accounting in supporting the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) number 8, which emphasizes economic progress and good jobs. Methodology: This study employs a literature review methodology from various national and international journals to analyze the connection between sustainable development objectives and strategic management accounting procedures. Results: The results of the analysis show that strategic management accounting has an important contribution in creating an economic system that is transparent, accountable, and free from corruption. The strategic function of accounting is not only limited to financial reporting, but contributes to planning, controlling, and evaluating policies that encourage increased labor productivity and community welfare. Findings: Through the integration of financial, social, and environmental information, strategic management accounting can be a tool for policy formulation and decision-making that is in line with the principles of sustainability. Novelty & Originality: The novelty of this study lies in its systematic synthesis of strategic management accounting practices within the framework of SDG 8, an integration that has received limited attention in prior literature. title: Towards an integrated form of university social responsibility
title_original: Towards an integrated form of university social responsibility
summary: La plupart des universités se sont dotées d’un plan de responsabilité sociétale coordonnant les actions qu’elles mènent pour contribuer au développement durable. L’impact de cet engagement sur leur environnement social et naturel fait toutefois débat. Selon la littérature, l’intensité de cet impact est liée au degré d’intégration des principes du développement durable au fonctionnement des universités, ainsi qu’à leurs missions d’enseignement et de recherche. En mobilisant ces enseignements et le concept de création de valeur partagée, cet article propose une analyse de différentes formes de responsabilité sociétale de l’université (RSU) en France et expose les conditions, ainsi que les leviers d’une intégration en profondeur de la RSU à la stratégie des universités. L’une des cinq universités étudiées exerce une forme de RSU entièrement intégrée. Elle pilote un projet stratégique croisant ses atouts scientifiques avec les problématiques clés de ses parties prenantes. Ce modèle implique une spécialisation des activités de recherche ainsi qu’une reconfiguration organisationnelle afin de faciliter l’interdisciplinarité, tout en préservant la liberté académique.

title: Social representations of quality of life at work among university staff : an exploratory study in a French university
title_original: Social representations of quality of life at work among university staff : an exploratory study in a French university
summary: Préoccupation avérée dans les organisations privées et, plus récemment, dans les organisations publiques, la qualité de vie au travail (QVT) est aujourd’hui un sujet incontournable de la gestion des ressources humaines. Tandis que les études sur ce thème se multiplient, la littérature scientifique fait état d’un manque en ce qui concerne la QVT des personnels – tant administratifs qu’enseignants-chercheurs – des universités publiques. Afin d’évaluer les enjeux de la QVT en université, nous mobilisons la théorie structurale d’Abric. Cette recherche prend la forme d’une étude qualitative avec la réalisation d’entretiens semi-directifs visant à mieux connaître ces représentations sociales. Nos résultats mettent tout d’abord en évidence un « noyau central » d’éléments partagés structuré autour du bien-être, du travail collectif, du climat social et de l’environnement physique de travail. Ensuite, des « éléments périphériques » ressortent : communication, stress, répartition du travail, relation administratif-enseignant. Les résultats font aussi ressortir des disparités dans lesdites représentations en fonction des profils étudiés (enseignants-chercheurs vs administratifs). Ces données nous permettent de mieux appréhender la complexité du concept de QVT dans le contexte de l’université publique. De plus, cette recherche apporte des éléments de connaissance indispensables pour mettre en place des démarches de qualité de vie au travail adéquates au sein des universités publiques.

title: CSR communication and financial performance : the moderating role of public authorities and the rule of law
title_original: CSR communication and financial performance : the moderating role of public authorities and the rule of law
summary: L’article analyse le rôle modérateur des modes de régulation et de gouvernance publique et en particulier l’efficacité des pouvoirs publics et de l’État de droit dans la relation entre la communication RSE et la performance financière des entreprises. En s’appuyant sur les travaux examinant la complémentarité entre hard et soft law , notre étude se propose d’éclairer la manière dont l’implication des pouvoirs publics dans l’encadrement des acteurs privés influence leur perception du rôle instrumental de la communication RSE. À partir de données recueillies auprès d’un échantillon d’entreprises internationales totalisant 11743 observations couvrant 30 pays entre 2007 et 2018, notre analyse empirique montre que la relation entre la communication de l’information RSE et la performance financière des entreprises apparaît plus significative dans les pays caractérisés par une faible efficacité des pouvoirs publics et un État de droit plus fort. Nos résultats indiquent que la perception des acteurs privés d'un faible leadership de la gouvernance publique est de nature à les inciter à davantage considérer la qualité de l'information RSE comme un levier stratégique de performance dans une logique substitutive de la hard law par la soft law .

title: Compromise in a pluralistic project-group : the activities of the broker of Worlds in the elaboration of a compromise convention
title_original: Compromise in a pluralistic project-group : the activities of the broker of Worlds in the elaboration of a compromise convention
summary: Notre recherche examine un groupe-projet d’un établissement de formation en travail social (EFTS), qui se saisit d’une nouvelle démarche d’intervention sociale pour initier des actions novatrices. Le contexte pluraliste de l’EFTS et sa difficulté à embrasser de nouveaux Mondes qui le pénètrent, nous amènent à mobiliser la littérature sur les Économies de la Grandeur. La perspective conventionnaliste développe la notion d’acteur compétent, capable d’élaborer des compromis, mais qui reste encore très peu étudiée par la littérature. Nous entendons répondre à ce « research gap » en nous intéressant aux activités déployées par la pilote du groupe-projet en formulant la question de recherche suivante : « Quelles sont les activités du pilote d’un groupe-projet en contexte pluraliste, enchâssé dans des mondes différents, qui conduisent les acteurs qui le composent à élaborer une convention de compromis pour lancer des initiatives novatrices ? ». Pour appréhender cet acteur, nous mobilisons les travaux sur le courtier de connaissances et les objets frontières. Le dispositif méthodologique s’appuie sur une observation-participante de l’un des auteurs, salariée de l’EFTS étudié. Le matériau ainsi collecté est complété par deux vagues d’entretien, sur la période 2018- 2022. Les données sont codées à partir d’un plan issu du cadre théorique d’analyse et de codes émergents. Nos résultats nous permettent de définir la pilote du groupe-projet comme un « Courtier de Mondes » que nous définissons comme « un courtier de connaissances qui parvient dans un collectif pluraliste à générer une convention de compromis grâce à ses activités de circulation et d’enrichissement de la connaissance, de mise en relation et de socialisation des acteurs, de développement des compétences des acteurs, et par une activité de réflexivité sur les Mondes » (inspiré de Dutrieux, 2021). Nous répondons à notre question de recherche de deux manières. Tout d’abord nous avons mis en évidence les activités constitutives du courtier de Mondes (en complément de la littérature) par l’importance de l’activité de socialisation et de communication entre les membres du groupe-projet en contexte pluraliste ; nous montrons également que le courtier de Mondes adopte une posture de « user push » pour ne pas imposer sa vision, mais encourager, par une activité de soutien à une réflexivité amenant les membres du groupe à faire sens des connaissances et pratiques au regard des différents Mondes, et à reconnaître leur altérité. Notre seconde contribution est d’identifier deux types de conventions de compromis, que nous appelons épistémique et pragmatique, la première offrant les éléments de langage pour soutenir les échanges et la communication nécessaires à la seconde. La formulation des compromis a été soutenue par l’échange autour d’objet-frontière.

title: Public action against air pollution : from the paradoxes of inter-organizational action to a paralyzing vicious cycle
title_original: Public action against air pollution : from the paradoxes of inter-organizational action to a paralyzing vicious cycle
summary: Quels paradoxes de gestion entrent en jeu dans la sphère publique locale et comment sont-ils gérés ? Cette question est posée dans le cadre des politiques publiques d’amélioration de la qualité de l'air. La pollution de l’air est chaque année responsable de 48000 à 100000 décès prématurés en France. Face à cet enjeu majeur de santé publique, l’État oblige les différentes organisations locales à travailler collectivement et dans un cadre de collaboration pour une amélioration effective. Cette injonction de travail collectif se heurte à de nombreux changements, tels que la modification des compétences, la création de métropoles ou encore la fusion d’intercommunalités. Cette obligation interroge d’autant plus que les pratiques de management inter-organisationnel sont propices au développement de tensions paradoxales. Pour déterminer quels sont les paradoxes présents dans le cas de l’amélioration de la qualité de l'air et la manière dont ils sont gérés, l’article mobilise ainsi la littérature sur les paradoxes de gestion (Smith et Lewis, 2011) et s’intéresse particulièrement à une typologie des paradoxes dans un cadre inter-organisationnel (Missonier, 2013), ainsi qu’aux pratiques de gestion des paradoxes (Josserand et Perret, 2003). Les résultats sont issus d’une étude de cas multiples conduite sur trois territoires métropolitains (Métropole du Grand Paris, Grenoble-Alpes Métropole et Eurométropole de Strasbourg). Les données collectées ont été traitées à travers une analyse de contenu thématique faisant suite à un processus de codage dit a prio-steriori (Allard-Poesi, 2003). Il ressort de cette recherche que l’action publique en faveur de la qualité de l'air est entravée par de nombreux freins d’ordre institutionnel, organisationnel, politique ou encore stratégique. Ceux-ci tendent à se cumuler et à former des tensions paradoxales. Huit paradoxes de gestion sont ainsi identifiés sur les territoires étudiés. Bien que certaines pratiques de gestion des paradoxes (Josserand et Perret, 2003) soient mises en œuvre par les acteurs locaux, la gouvernance de l’air demeure ancrée dans un cercle vicieux. Envisager cette dernière en tant que communauté d’enquête et à travers le concept de travail institutionnel (Zietsma et Lawrence, 2010) fournit des éléments de réponse pour concilier certaines tensions paradoxales repérées.

title: Revitalising town centre trade : typologies of organizational approaches in French towns
title_original: Revitalising town centre trade : typologies of organizational approaches in French towns
summary: Depuis quelques années, une nouvelle fonction s’est développée au sein des villes en vue de dynamiser la relation avec les commerçants : celle de manager de centre-ville. Alors qu’elle a fait l’objet de peu de travaux en France, le but de cet article est de caractériser cette nouvelle forme de management public. Pour cela, nous avons réalisé des études de cas auprès d’une trentaine de villes françaises. L’analyse fait ressortir que la dynamisation du commerce de centre-ville s’inscrit dans quatre logiques organisationnelles suivies par les villes qui sont : 1) le développement urbain ; 2) la création d’un guichet commercial unique ; 3) la promotion des commerçants ; 4) la création d’une communauté. La contribution de la recherche est d’introduire une typologie synthétique permettant de caractériser l’action publique initiée par les villes à destination des commerçants. Sur le plan managérial, elle constitue un outil intéressant afin d’aider les villes qui veulent se doter de telles fonctions à la configurer ou bien pour les villes qui en disposent déjà à la faire évoluer.

title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
title_original: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
summary: Se fondant sur 32 entretiens avec des fonctionnaires libanais, pays touché par la corruption et une situation sociale difficile, le but de cet article est de comprendre comment la motivation de service public (MSP) conduit les fonctionnaires à développer une corruption pour une cause noble (CCN). Cette recherche est doublement exploratoire. Premièrement, s’intéresser aux effets négatifs de la MSP, c’est enrichir un champ de recherche essentiellement tourné vers la compréhension des effets positifs de ce concept. Deuxièmement, se focaliser sur la CCN c’est là encore mobiliser un concept qui jusqu’ici a été mobilisé pour le cas de policiers. Mobilisant les travaux sur les deux concepts et ceux sur la justification morale, cette recherche réalise une double contribution théorique. Premièrement, nous montrons que les dimensions de compassion et d’abnégation de la MSP conduisent à une CCN dont nous précisons les contours (soutien supplémentaire et protection contre une sanction). Cette dynamique est source de tensions internes pour le fonctionnaire qui choisit de réaliser une CCN, tant il est affecté par la vulnérabilité des usagers. Deuxièmement, nous dégageons trois facteurs contextuels (échange physique, autonomie spatiale dans le travail et proximité relationnelle) facilitant l'enchaînement MSP-CCN. Nous montrons que ce lien s’inscrit dans la durée au travers du développement d’une justification morale.

title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
title_original: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
summary: Cette recherche, s’inscrivant dans un projet scientifique élaboré en partenariat entre notre Centre de Recherche et le CR ENSP 1 , vise à évaluer les risques émotionnels inhérents aux métiers de la police, et les processus de (dys)régulations des émotions mis en place par les policiers/ières et les collectifs policiers, dans un objectif de Qualité de Vie et Conditions de Travail (QVCT). De nombreuses études abordent la question des émotions dans les organisations ces dernières décennies. Mais la composante émotionnelle au travail, dans les pratiques ayant trait à la Gestion des Ressources Humaines (GRH) et au management publics, est un sujet assez récent au sein de milieux professionnels « extrêmes », à haute fiabilité, comme celui de la Police Nationale. Une étude ethnographique et qualitative a été menée par l’auteure au sein de la Direction Territoriale de la Police Judiciaire (DTPJ) d’une métropole française, au cours du printemps 2021. Plusieurs brigades ont été observées : police technique et scientifique, investigation opérationnelle du numérique, division financière, division criminelle, répression du banditisme, office anti-stupéfiants, groupe anti-terroriste. Cette recherche, fondée sur l’immersion de la chercheuse dans des services policiers pendant 26,5 jours et nuits de mai à juin 2021, ainsi que sur 20 entretiens individuels et collectifs, analyse : les émotions vécues par les policiers, leurs pratiques de (dys)régulations émotionnelles aux niveaux individuel, collectif et organisationnel, et révèle leur rapport au sens au travail. Cette recherche fait apparaître l’importance de deux émotions-clefs constituant des « angles morts » du travail : l’intérêt et la frustration, conduisant les policiers à fournir un travail « invisible », et non discuté, sur les affects relatifs à l’activité dans son ensemble. Cette recherche interdisciplinaire mobilise auteure et praticiens autour d’un double objectif : la prévention des risques psychosociaux (RPS), et la QVCT.
abstract: Cette recherche, s’inscrivant dans un projet scientifique élaboré en partenariat entre notre Centre de Recherche et le CR ENSP 1 , vise à évaluer les risques émotionnels inhérents aux métiers de la police, et les processus de (dys)régulations des émotions mis en place par les policiers/ières et les collectifs policiers, dans un objectif de Qualité de Vie et Conditions de Travail (QVCT). De nombreuses études abordent la question des émotions dans les organisations ces dernières décennies. Mais la composante émotionnelle au travail, dans les pratiques ayant trait à la Gestion des Ressources Humaines (GRH) et au management publics, est un sujet assez récent au sein de milieux professionnels « extrêmes », à haute fiabilité, comme celui de la Police Nationale. Une étude ethnographique et qualitative a été menée par l’auteure au sein de la Direction Territoriale de la Police Judiciaire (DTPJ) d’une métropole française, au cours du printemps 2021. Plusieurs brigades ont été observées : police technique et scientifique, investigation opérationnelle du numérique, division financière, division criminelle, répression du banditisme, office anti-stupéfiants, groupe anti-terroriste. Cette recherche, fondée sur l’immersion de la chercheuse dans des services policiers pendant 26,5 jours et nuits de mai à juin 2021, ainsi que sur 20 entretiens individuels et collectifs, analyse : les émotions vécues par les policiers, leurs pratiques de (dys)régulations émotionnelles aux niveaux individuel, collectif et organisationnel, et révèle leur rapport au sens au travail. Cette recherche fait apparaître l’importance de deux émotions-clefs constituant des « angles morts » du travail : l’intérêt et la frustration, conduisant les policiers à fournir un travail « invisible », et non discuté, sur les affects relatifs à l’activité dans son ensemble. title: Exploration de l’hétérogénéité des entrepreneurs institutionnels en situation de démarche qualité
title_original: Exploration de l’hétérogénéité des entrepreneurs institutionnels en situation de démarche qualité
summary: Dans un contexte de contestation du statu quo institutionnel, cet article vient pour analyser les déterminants différenciés d’adoption de la démarche qualité par profession dans une organisation publique. Le travail institutionnel, récompensé avec cinq certifications ISO 9001, a obligé les adoptants initiaux à migrer vers le statut d’entrepreneur. Cependant, après l’ancrage des pratiques qualité, la justice dans le travail institutionnel se fait attendre. À l’aide d’une méthode séquentielle mixte, l’analyse documentée des pratiques de qualité indique le travail institutionnel en cours. Ce dernier est mis en relation avec une enquête par questionnaire auprès de tous les agents dans un hôpital public. Les relations entre les déterminants de la qualité et les types d’adoptants sont analysées par équation structurelle (SEM-PLS). Les premiers résultats montrent un travail institutionnel d’adoption de la démarche perçu par l’engagement de la direction, la satisfaction des besoins en personnel, les intéressements à distribuer et la célérité dans le traitement des factures. Pour tous les entrepreneurs, la démarche qualité repose en première intention sur la formation des acteurs et leurs relations client. Les professionnels de la santé excluent la planification et l’analyse des données, alors que les professionnels administratifs préfèrent celle-ci pour corriger l’issue de leurs décisions. Les déterminants inscrivent les médicaux dans le profil entrepreneur institutionnel « Affût », les médicaux-techniques comme « Inspiré » et « Influencé » pour les administratifs. Les résultats montrent que les médicaux, disposant de suffisamment de ressources et à la base de l’entrepreneuriat institutionnel, sont dans une situation de regret, traduit par un conflit de valeurs professionnelles, une perte de statut et un conflit d’identité sociale.

title: L’enseignant-chercheur : un manager public durable ?
title_original: L’enseignant-chercheur : un manager public durable ?
summary: Cet article a pour projet de contribuer à la problématique de la durabilité dans un contexte constamment en évolution, où métiers et missions sont en transformation. Transverse à l’ensemble des organisations et à la plupart des métiers, cette question est traitée ici dans un cas exemplaire, celui de l’enseignant-chercheur manager de l’université publique. Ce dernier est en effet en lien direct avec les usagers, les collègues administratifs, enseignants et/ou chercheurs pour l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de réformes incessantes ; il exerce un métier protéiforme, traversé par des légitimités multiples, et dont les missions sont, y compris, heurtées par des injonctions issues d’autres organisations. L’approche est réflexive, qualitative et longitudinale, elle concerne deux études de cas analysés en profondeur sur une période de trois ans. Les résultats puis la discussion montrent la (co) construction concrète des activités mais aussi le sens qu’elles portent et contribuent à générer. Leur analyse, à l’aune de la diversité des légitimités portées dans le temps, suggère des pistes d’action pour le gestionnaire des ressources humaines. Les implications d’une telle recherche sont théoriques : comprendre la longévité, la durabilité, dans un contexte changeant. Elles sont également pratiques : cette analyse permet de proposer des actions au manager public, notamment en termes de GRH.

title: Communication RSE et performance financière : le rôle modérateur des pouvoirs publics et de l’État de droit
title_original: Communication RSE et performance financière : le rôle modérateur des pouvoirs publics et de l’État de droit
summary: L’article analyse le rôle modérateur des modes de régulation et de gouvernance publique et en particulier l’efficacité des pouvoirs publics et de l’État de droit dans la relation entre la communication RSE et la performance financière des entreprises. En s’appuyant sur les travaux examinant la complémentarité entre hard et soft law , notre étude se propose d’éclairer la manière dont l’implication des pouvoirs publics dans l’encadrement des acteurs privés influence leur perception du rôle instrumental de la communication RSE. À partir de données recueillies auprès d’un échantillon d’entreprises internationales totalisant 11743 observations couvrant 30 pays entre 2007 et 2018, notre analyse empirique montre que la relation entre la communication de l’information RSE et la performance financière des entreprises apparaît plus significative dans les pays caractérisés par une faible efficacité des pouvoirs publics et un État de droit plus fort. Nos résultats indiquent que la perception des acteurs privés d'un faible leadership de la gouvernance publique est de nature à les inciter à davantage considérer la qualité de l'information RSE comme un levier stratégique de performance dans une logique substitutive de la hard law par la soft law .

title: Contribution des acteurs de terrain pour une appréhension actualisée des enjeux de l’accès aux soins par la télésanté
title_original: Contribution des acteurs de terrain pour une appréhension actualisée des enjeux de l’accès aux soins par la télésanté
summary: Dans un contexte de désertification médicale, cette recherche analyse les perspectives d’amélioration de l’accès aux soins par la télésanté. Partant du constat que l’amélioration de l’accès aux soins par la télésanté est toujours analysée selon le même prisme que la médecine pratiquée en présentiel, cette recherche pose la question suivante : quelles peuvent être les perspectives d’amélioration de l’accès aux soins par la télésanté ? Elle vise à proposer une compréhension actualisée, à l’ère du numérique, du concept d’accès aux soins. Pour parvenir à cet objectif, la recherche mobilise, au niveau théorique, une grille d’analyse élargie de l’accès aux soins, développée par Saurman (2016). Au niveau empirique, la recherche propose l’étude de 96 projets d’innovation en santé, ces innovations étant, pour la plupart, soit portées par un cœur de projet numérique de télésanté, soit soutenues par les Technologies de l’Information et de la Communication (TIC). Une approche complémentaire de données primaires, 52 entretiens avec les chefs de projet, et secondaires, les documents relatifs à la description du contenu de ces projets, est proposée. Les résultats soulignent le besoin de changer notre regard, à l’ère du numérique, sur le concept d’accès aux soins. Le rôle majeur de dimensions telles que l’acceptabilité technologique et la sensibilisation pour améliorer l’accès aux soins par la télésanté est identifié dans les discours des acteurs, ce qui montre l’importance d’appréhender l’accès aux soins par une approche managériale propre aux sciences de gestion.

title: La diffusion des outils et services e-santé auprès de leurs utilisateurs : l’exemple de « Mon espace santé » en France
title_original: La diffusion des outils et services e-santé auprès de leurs utilisateurs : l’exemple de « Mon espace santé » en France
summary: Les pouvoirs publics souhaitent tirer parti des perspectives offertes par le numérique en santé pour améliorer l’information et la prise en charge des patients tout en luttant contre les inégalités de santé dans les territoires. Cependant, en France, si au cours des quinze dernières années, cette transformation digitale du secteur de la santé s’est particulièrement développée, elle a aussi connu des résultats très variables et parfois encore assez décevants. Pour notamment renforcer et accélérer cette transformation digitale, de nombreux travaux ont décrit en détail les modalités et facteurs favorisant l’adoption et l’appropriation des outils et services numériques en santé. En revanche, beaucoup moins de travaux ont porté leur attention sur la phase de diffusion aux utilisateurs de ces outils et services alors qu’elle détermine significativement leur adoption et appropriation. Pour combler ce manque, à partir de la théorie de la diffusion des innovations, nous proposons d’analyser les modalités de diffusion à ses utilisateurs de l’outil « Mon espace santé » proposé et mis en œuvre par la Caisse nationale d’assurance maladie en France. À partir d’une participation observante au sein des équipes chargées de la diffusion de cet outil, nous décrivons les éléments de diffusion de cette innovation digitale (système social, innovation, canaux de communication, temps). Les résultats de cette analyse nous permettent, dans un premier temps, sur le plan théorique, de proposer un premier cadre d’analyse de la diffusion des innovations digitales en santé. L’application de ce cadre d’analyse nous autorise ensuite une caractérisation des modalités de diffusion de l’innovation digitale en santé « centrée sur l’usager » aux côtés de celles relatives à sa conception déjà très illustrées dans la littérature. Ces modalités sont décrites à travers les principales composantes de la diffusion de « Mon espace santé » (différents rôles de l’usager, canaux de communication utilisés et étapes de diffusion) et trois de ses principes directeurs (usager-acteur, État-plateforme, déploiement incitatif centré sur l’usager). Sur le plan pratique, ces composantes et principes de diffusion représentent autant de pistes d’amélioration de la diffusion des innovations digitales en santé dans le secteur public.
