title: Pool Chlorination By-Products and Airway Hyperresponsiveness in Swimmers: Pathomechanism, Pulmonary Diagnostics and Preventive Management — A Narrative Synthesis of Evidence Published Since 2020
title_original: Pool Chlorination By-Products and Airway Hyperresponsiveness in Swimmers: Pathomechanism, Pulmonary Diagnostics and Preventive Management — A Narrative Synthesis of Evidence Published Since 2020
summary: Background: Competitive swimmers train in indoor facilities where chlorine-based disinfection generates volatile by-products like trichloramine. Aquatic disciplines report the highest prevalence of lower airway dysfunction of any sporting group. The clinical picture, often labelled ‘swimmer’s asthma’, sits between classical exercise-induced bronchoconstriction and chemically mediated airway disorder. Aim: To synthesise evidence (2020 onwards) on mechanisms by which chlorination by-products and sustained hyperpnoea injure airway epithelium in swimmers, appraise diagnostic strategies, and set out preventive and pharmacological options within anti-doping constraints. Material and methods: This narrative synthesis retrieved PubMed/MEDLINE records (Jan 2020–Jul 2026), combining exposure, respiratory, and anti-doping terms. Priority was given to consensus statements, meta-analyses, and clinical trials. Results: Meta-analyses place lower airway dysfunction prevalence at 21.8% across athletes and 39.9% in aquatic disciplines. The dominant mechanism combines osmotic/mechanical stress from hyperpnoea with chemical irritation, disrupting the epithelial barrier. Club cell protein 16 marks this disruption, though interpretation is complicated by acute vs. chronic changes. Symptom-based diagnosis performs poorly; objective bronchoprovocation is required (eucapnic voluntary hyperpnoea shows 46% sensitivity, 74% specificity). Inhaled beta-2 agonists are permitted below daily thresholds, but the therapeutic-to-reportable margin is narrow. Conclusions: Swimmers' airway hyperresponsiveness is an occupational disorder of mixed osmotic and chemical origin, not classical asthma. Objective testing must precede prescription, treatment must align with anti-doping limits, and environmental control of by-products requires greater clinical emphasis.

summary: Il libro è pensato per milioni di persone, potenzialmente per ogni individuo, che desidera essere sano e sentirsi al meglio ogni giorno. title: Difficulties Encountered by Coaches in Teaching Student Athletes
title_original: Difficulties Encountered by Coaches in Teaching Student Athletes
summary: This research determined the level of difficulties encountered by teacher-coaches in teaching student-athletes in a mega-sized public secondary school in a medium-sized division of the Negros Island Region during School Year 2020–2021, as a basis for a strategic intervention plan. A descriptive research design was employed, using a total enumeration of 50 public secondary school teacher-coaches across five sports categories (individual, dual, team, para-games, and combative). Data were gathered using a researcher-made survey questionnaire validated by experts (CVI = 4.50) and tested for internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.813). Data were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, weighted means, and the Mann–Whitney U test. Results revealed that the majority of coaches were older (52.0%), married (58.0%), and non-MAPEH majors (68.0%). Coaches experienced a moderate level of difficulty in Sports Skills Development (M = 2.88) and high levels of difficulty in Sports Support Services (M = 3.63) and Sports Management (M = 4.07). The most prominent challenges were accessing professional development programs (M = 4.84), providing suitable training venues and spaces (M = 4.34), and conducting regular consultations and planning sessions among coaches (M = 4.48). Inferential analysis via the Mann–Whitney U test indicated no significant differences in coaching difficulties when respondents were grouped by age and civil status (p > 0.05). However, significant differences were found in Sports Skills Development (U = 67.50, p = 0.000) and Sports Management (U = 147.00, p = 0.007) according to specialization, with non-MAPEH majors experiencing significantly greater difficulty than MAPEH majors. The study concluded that operational challenges in sports programs stem primarily from resource constraints and a lack of formal sports specialization among teacher-coaches, highlighting the urgent need for structured coaching capacity-building, facility adaptation, and institutionalized communication frameworks.

title: Islamic Teachings as an Internal Discipline System in Athlete Development: A Narrative Review and the Prophetic Athlete Discipline Model
title_original: Islamic Teachings as an Internal Discipline System in Athlete Development: A Narrative Review and the Prophetic Athlete Discipline Model
summary: Discipline underpins high-performance behaviour, and sport psychology has examined it through self-regulation, motivation, resilience, and moral behaviour. Religion has also been studied in athletes, but mainly as a coping resource, an identity marker, or a participation constraint rather than as a self-regulatory system. This narrative review examines how Islamic ethical teachings intersect with established discipline constructs in sport, and proposes the Prophetic Athlete Discipline Model (PADM), which links spiritual, behavioural, moral, and physical dimensions of athlete discipline. Scopus and PubMed were searched purposively in September 2026 using three strings covering religion and sport psychology, Muslim athletes, and Islamic ethical constructs in sport, supplemented by citation tracking from two anchor reviews. Of the (N = 2,286) records screened on title, abstract, and keywords, (n = 70) were retained. Islamic primary sources were handled separately and restricted to Quranic verses, authenticated Prophetic traditions, and established works of Islamic ethics. The retained literature is dominated by cross-sectional and qualitative designs, contains one longitudinal study (n = 1) and three intervention studies (n = 3), and is concentrated in Western settings. Across four domains, Islamic constructs correspond functionally with intention-based motivation, ritual and self-control, moral identity, and recovery behaviour. Qualifying evidence is also present: negative religious coping is associated with adverse pre-competition emotion, the protective component of religiosity appears existential rather than devotional, and Ramadan observance reduces sleep and high-intensity performance. Islamic teachings can be read as a candidate self-regulatory architecture rather than a peripheral cultural variable, but PADM is untested. Its value depends on whether its domains explain variance beyond general religiosity and existing psychological constructs. Instruments now exist to test that.

title: Iron Deficiency in Athletes — Current State of Knowledge
title_original: Iron Deficiency in Athletes — Current State of Knowledge
summary: Introduction and Purpose. Iron deficiency is common among athletes and may occur before anemia develops. Its significance is less clear when iron stores are depleted despite normal hemoglobin. This review summarizes current evidence on iron deficiency in athletes, with particular emphasis on iron deficiency without anemia (IDNA), athletic performance, diagnosis, and management. Materials and Methods. A structured PubMed/MEDLINE search was supplemented by Google Scholar and reference screening. Publications from January 2015 to August 2026 were considered, with earlier studies included when relevant to fundamental aspects of iron metabolism, diagnosis, or treatment. Results. Iron deficiency in athletes results from interacting factors, including increased requirements, inadequate intake, reduced iron availability, and iron losses. Ferritin remains the principal marker of iron stores, although inflammation and inconsistent diagnostic thresholds complicate its interpretation. The functional effects of IDNA are variable. More pronounced depletion appears more likely to impair endurance performance, while increases in ferritin after supplementation do not consistently translate into improved performance. Conclusions. Iron status should be interpreted alongside laboratory findings, symptoms, risk factors, and training demands. Management should focus on correcting documented deficiency and identifying its underlying cause rather than supplementation aimed solely at increasing iron stores or enhancing performance.

title: Analysis of doping control forms in the Republic of Slovenia (2014–2024): the impact of temporal, sport-specific, and demographic factors on the volume and specific gravity of athlete urine samples
title_original: Analysis of doping control forms in the Republic of Slovenia (2014–2024): the impact of temporal, sport-specific, and demographic factors on the volume and specific gravity of athlete urine samples
summary: Učinkovito izvajanje dopinških kontrol je pomemben del protidopinškega sistema. Cilj naloge je bil pridobiti celovit vpogled v izvedbene vidike dopinškega testiranja v Sloveniji v obdobju 2014–2024. Namen je bil z retrospektivno analizo obrazcev za kontrolo dopinga preučiti povezanost demografskih, časovnih in športno specifičnih dejavnikov z volumnom in specifično težo urinskih vzorcev športnikov ter trajanjem dopinške kontrole. Analizirali smo 4615 obrazcev za kontrolo dopinga, ki jih je v navedenem obdobju zbrala Slovenska antidoping organizacija (SLOADO). Anonimizirani podatki so vključevali spol, starost, datum testiranja, šport, športno disciplino, vrsto testiranja (na tekmovanju ali izven tekmovanja), čas prihoda na kontrolo dopinga, čas odvzema vzorca, čas zaključka kontrole in vrsto vzorca. Pri urinskih vzorcih smo analizirali volumen in specifično težo. V glavne analize je bilo vključenih 4442 obrazcev z enojnim ustreznim urinskim vzorcem. Rezultati so pokazali, da so bili volumen in specifična teža urinskih vzorcev ter trajanje dopinške kontrole (razlika med časom prihoda športnika na postajo za kontrolo dopinga in časom zaključka testiranja) povezani z različnimi preučevanimi dejavniki. Pri kontrolah moških športnikov so bili volumni urinskih vzorcev manjši, specifična teža urina pa višja kot pri kontrolah športnic, medtem ko se trajanje med spoloma ni statistično značilno razlikovalo. Starost je bila povezana predvsem z volumnom urina, pri čemer so športniki mlajši od 16 let in starejši od 50 let oddali manjše volumne. Čas izvedbe dopinške kontrole je bil povezan z razlikami, skladnimi s cirkadianim ritmom, saj so imeli jutranji vzorci večji volumen in višjo specifično težo. Letni čas testiranja ni imel vpliva na lastnosti urina in trajanje kontrole. Športniki na tekmovanjih so oddali manjši volumen urina z nižjo specifično težo, dopinške kontrole pa so bile pogosto daljše. V ekipnih športih so športniki oddali urin z manjšim volumnom kot v individualnih športih, kar se je odražalo tudi v daljšem trajanju kontrole. Razlike med športnimi disciplinami so verjetno povezane z intenzivnostjo obremenitve in možnostmi vnosa tekočine med aktivnostjo. Kljub razlikam je bila večina športnikov glede na specifično težo v stanju evhidriranosti. Med dopinško kontrolo je prišlo tudi do oddaje neustreznih urinskih vzorcev, ki niso dosegali zahtevanega volumna (delni vzorci) ali ustrezne specifične teže (razredčeni vzorci). Delni vzorci so bili glede specifične teže primerljivi z enojnimi, medtem ko so imeli razredčeni vzorci nižjo specifično težo. V obeh primerih je bilo trajanje dopinške kontrole daljše. Rezultati raziskave prispevajo k boljšemu razumevanju dejavnikov, povezanih z lastnostmi urinskih vzorcev in trajanjem dopinške kontrole, ter lahko podprejo izboljšanje načrtovanja in izvajanja dopinškega testiranja.

Pri kontrolah moških športnikov so bili volumni urinskih vzorcev manjši, specifična teža urina pa višja kot pri kontrolah športnic, medtem ko se trajanje med spoloma ni statistično značilno razlikovalo. Starost je bila povezana predvsem z volumnom urina, pri čemer so športniki mlajši od 16 let in starejši od 50 let oddali manjše volumne. Čas izvedbe dopinške kontrole je bil povezan z razlikami, skladnimi s cirkadianim ritmom, saj so imeli jutranji vzorci večji volumen in višjo specifično težo. Letni čas testiranja ni imel vpliva na lastnosti urina in trajanje kontrole. Športniki na tekmovanjih so oddali manjši volumen urina z nižjo specifično težo, dopinške kontrole pa so bile pogosto daljše. V ekipnih športih so športniki oddali urin z manjšim volumnom kot v individualnih športih, kar se je odražalo tudi v daljšem trajanju kontrole. Razlike med športnimi disciplinami so verjetno povezane z intenzivnostjo obremenitve in možnostmi vnosa tekočine med aktivnostjo. Kljub razlikam je bila večina športnikov glede na specifično težo v stanju evhidriranosti. Med dopinško kontrolo je prišlo tudi do oddaje neustreznih urinskih vzorcev, ki niso dosegali zahtevanega volumna (delni vzorci) ali ustrezne specifične teže (razredčeni vzorci). Delni vzorci so bili glede specifične teže primerljivi z enojnimi, medtem ko so imeli razredčeni vzorci nižjo specifično težo. V obeh primerih je bilo trajanje dopinške kontrole daljše. Rezultati raziskave prispevajo k boljšemu razumevanju dejavnikov, povezanih z lastnostmi urinskih vzorcev in trajanjem dopinške kontrole, ter lahko podprejo izboljšanje načrtovanja in izvajanja dopinškega testiranja.

title: Coach behaviors, coach–athlete relationships, and competitive psychological processes in elite sport: a temporal narrative synthesis
title_original: Coach behaviors, coach–athlete relationships, and competitive psychological processes in elite sport: a temporal narrative synthesis
summary: Background Research on coach behavior, coach–athlete relationships, and competitive psychological processes has developed in partly separate literatures, limiting understanding of how these domains interact across an elite competitive cycle. Aims This review examined how these domains are represented across foundation building, competitive maintenance, peak competition, and post-competition transition, while distinguishing direct temporal evidence from interpretive phase placement. Methods Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, and Scopus were searched for peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2016 to 22 June 2026. Of 645 records identified, 481 unique records were screened, 205 underwent eligibility assessment, and 30 empirical studies were included. Results Evidence was strongest for competitive maintenance and peak competition. Repeated-measures, diary, prospective, and event-based studies linked coaching behavior and relationship-related judgments with motivation, well-being, perceived justice, burnout, appraisal, coping, affect, confidence, and perceived performance. Evidence for foundation building was limited, while direct evidence on post-season evaluation and cross-cycle carryover was largely absent. Conclusion The proposed temporal framework should be viewed as an evidence-informed research architecture rather than an established causal sequence. It highlights phase-specific hypotheses for future research, coach education, and psychological support.

title: Enhanced but not superior: Performance outcomes from the inaugural enhanced games
title_original: Enhanced but not superior: Performance outcomes from the inaugural enhanced games
summary: The Enhanced Games (TEG) emerged as an athletic event engineered to profit from biotechnological enhancement, such as performance-enhancing drugs (PEDs) utilization, relying on three premises: shattering world records (WR), enabling athletes to surpass their personal bests (PB), and utilizing PEDs to offset age-related physical decline. The effectiveness of TEG's PED protocols in achieving these three premises was evaluated. This is a retrospective analysis from 42 TEG athletes across Track, Swimming, and Weightlifting. TEG's performances were compared to current WR and athletes' PB previous to TEG. The anti-aging PED effects were evaluated by the relationship between the age and performance gaps from PB to TEG competition. Athletes' previous PBs were -5.92% ± 4.68% worse than current WR, which further deteriorated to -8.91% ± 7.52% after TEG, and a single WR was broken. Whereas 19 new PBs were recorded, TEG performances were on average -2.86% ± 7.39% worse than previous PB. Some competitive results were achieved by non-enhanced athletes. Performance decline continued linearly as the time elapsed since the athletes' physical prime (i.e., age at PB). TEG failed to deliver on core promises of widespread WR and broad athletic enhancement, and PED protocol did not attenuate expected age-related performance declines.

title: ASSISTÊNCIA FARMACÊUTICA NO ESPORTE: DESAFIOS PARA SUA IMPLEMENTAÇÃO E IMPLICAÇÕES PARA A SAÚDE DO ATLETA
title_original: ASSISTÊNCIA FARMACÊUTICA NO ESPORTE: DESAFIOS PARA SUA IMPLEMENTAÇÃO E IMPLICAÇÕES PARA A SAÚDE DO ATLETA
summary: A assistência farmacêutica no contexto esportivo tem se destacado pela sua relevância na promoção do uso seguro e racional de medicamentos, suplementos e outras substâncias por atletas. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar os principais desafios relacionados à inserção da assistência farmacêutica no esporte, com ênfase na prevenção de riscos à saúde e na conformidade com as normativas antidopagens. Trata-se de uma pesquisa qualitativa, de natureza descritiva, baseada em revisão bibliográfica. Os resultados evidenciam que, apesar do reconhecimento da importância do farmacêutico na equipe multiprofissional, persistem lacunas na formação específica, na capacitação profissional e na integração desses profissionais ao cenário esportivo. Além disso, o uso indiscriminado de substâncias, muitas vezes sem orientação adequada, representa um risco significativo para a saúde dos atletas. Conclui-se que a ampliação da atuação do farmacêutico no esporte é fundamental para garantir a segurança, a qualidade de vida e o desempenho dos praticantes, sendo necessária maior valorização e inserção desse profissional nesse campo.

title: Regulating technology, enabling participation: evaluating the impact of a new cycling racing class in the UK
title_original: Regulating technology, enabling participation: evaluating the impact of a new cycling racing class in the UK
summary: Purpose/Rationale: This study outlines the introduction of a new racing class in the sport of cycle time-trials in the UK which was implemented to address falling levels of participation. This case study follows up on this policy innovation by conducting a survey of its participants after two full racing seasons and investigates the perceptions of it by its participants.Design/Methodology/Approach: An online survey was administered to cycling time trial participants (n = 801). This survey utilised a traditional thematic analysis approach which was then further validated via an artificial intelligence-based process.Findings: The findings found respondents’ perceptions of the class matched that of its original concept by minimising the resources required to compete, increasing inclusivity and seeing a perceived avoidance or rejection of a technological “arms race”. Respondents were also largely content with the current rules’ content.Practical Implications: Governing bodies should avoid rule changes that increase participant costs or accelerate technological arms races, as these were consistently identified as barriers. They should also actively promote the new racing class as equivalent in status through equal social media coverage, prize structures, and event branding to counter perceptions of it being a “second-class” category. Finally, they should enhance visible rule enforcement to maintain trust.Originality/Value: This is a novel study which contributes to an emerging understanding of how regulatory design can be used to balance performance, accessibility, and participation within technologically evolving sports.

title: Historiographical dimensions of Ukrainian physical culture and sport: a bibliometric analysis of the global scholarly discourse (1991–2025)
title_original: Historiographical dimensions of Ukrainian physical culture and sport: a bibliometric analysis of the global scholarly discourse (1991–2025)
summary: The article analyses the scholarly discourse on the history of the system of physical education, sport and physical activity in Ukraine in contemporary periodicals. Background and aim of the study. The globalisation of science makes it necessary to examine how the Ukrainian past is reflected in international scholarly works, which is essential for overcoming the sense of inferiority and for decolonising national history. Despite the existence of individual reviews, a comprehensive analysis of international publications is still lacking, and researchers have not yet clarified the specific features of how the history of Ukrainian sport and physical culture is being integrated into the global academic space. The aim of the study is to substantiate, on the basis of an analysis of an international body of publications (Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, 1991–2025), the distinctive nature of the Ukrainian history of physical culture and sport as a sociocultural phenomenon and to identify the main thematic areas of its current research. Material and methods. Using bibliometric and comparative analysis methods, a representative body of publications (1991–2025) was examined. The structural and systemic approach made it possible to classify and organise this body of documents according to key thematic clusters. Results. The quantitative analysis revealed a growth in the number of publications (up to 7.6 works per year in 2016–2025), with periodicals (89%) and foreign authors (64%) predominating. Qualitative content analysis made it possible to identify five key thematic areas: physical culture and sport as an ideological and political instrument (using the example of the Soviet system and current sports sanctions); the role of national forms of physical activity and body practices (Sokil, Plast, Fighting Hopak) in shaping identity; the development of sport in the context of modernisation processes and urban history; the evolution of health-enhancing and recreational physical culture, from the therapeutic gymnastics of the early 20th century to the modern fitness industry; and the grassroots self-organisation of physical culture and sports societies. Conclusions. The analysis showed an interdisciplinary and internationally oriented renewal of Ukrainian historiography of physical culture and sport. Overcoming the identified chronological and regional imbalances through methodological modernisation is a promising direction for future global research.

title: ЕФЕКТИВНІСТЬ ТЕОРЕТИЧНОЇ ПІДГОТОВКИ ВЕСЛУВАЛЬНИКІВ НА ЕТАПІ СПЕЦІАЛІЗОВАНОЇ БАЗОВОЇ ПІДГОТОВКИ
title_original: ЕФЕКТИВНІСТЬ ТЕОРЕТИЧНОЇ ПІДГОТОВКИ ВЕСЛУВАЛЬНИКІВ НА ЕТАПІ СПЕЦІАЛІЗОВАНОЇ БАЗОВОЇ ПІДГОТОВКИ
summary: Theoretical training at the stage of specialized basic training should ensure not only the acquisition of specialized knowledge but also its transfer into athletes’ technical, tactical, and organizational decision-making. The aim of the study was to determine the effectiveness of theoretical training of kayakers at the stage of specialized basic training. Research methods: analysis and generalization of scientific and methodological literature, pedagogical testing, pedagogical experiment, and methods of mathematical statistics. The study involved 40 athletes specializing in kayaking who were at the stage of specialized basic training (mean age: 14.25±0.65 years). The participants were divided into two groups of 20 athletes each: the main group and the comparison group. The pedagogical experiment lasted 12 weeks. Results: the developed experimental program was characterized by its comprehensive and systematic nature and by the direct integration of theoretical instruction with practical sports activities. Its content was structured into seven interrelated areas: knowledge of competition rules and regulations; rowing technique and biomechanics; race-distance tactics; training planning and self-monitoring; biomedical foundations and recovery; water safety, first aid, and anti-doping provision; and equipment-related knowledge and digital analysis. The program was implemented over 12 weeks and included 24 theoretical and practical sessions. The greatest relative improvements in the main group were observed in the following components: knowledge of training planning and self-monitoring increased by 74.7%, knowledge of rowing technique and biomechanics by 73.8%, biomedical foundations and recovery by 72.8%, knowledge of competition rules and regulations by 72.3%, and equipment-related knowledge and digital analysis by 71.9%. Tactical preparedness increased by 61.7%, while knowledge of water safety, first aid, and anti-doping provision increased by 54.4%. At the end of the intervention cycle, between-group differences in the integral indicator of theoretical preparedness were statistically significant (p<0.001). Conclusions: the purposeful organization of theoretical training through systematic theoretical and practical micro-modules, problem- and situation-based learning, video analysis, digital tools, self-monitoring, reflection, and the direct transfer of acquired knowledge into training activities has considerably greater potential for developing specialized knowledge among kayakers compared with the traditional approach. The findings confirm the expediency of a purposeful, systematic, and practice-oriented organization of theoretical training for kayakers at the stage of specialized basic training.

title: The utilization of brine for CO2 mineralization – A review
title_original: The utilization of brine for CO2 mineralization – A review
summary: The intensifying demand for freshwater and continued reliance on fossil fuels have accelerated the generation of CO 2 emissions and high-salinity brine waste streams worldwide. Desalination brine and other seawater-derived effluents are enriched in multivalent cations such as Ca 2+ and Mg 2+ , making them promising feedstocks for CO 2 mineralization. This approach enables simultaneous carbon capture and sustainable brine management by converting dissolved inorganic carbon into stable carbonate minerals. This review comprehensively synthesizes recent advances in CO 2 mineralization technologies employing natural seawater, desalination brine, and other industrial brine, focusing on both direct and indirect carbonation pathways. Fundamental mechanisms alongside state-of-the-art technologies are critically examined. Direct carbonation offers low operational costs but remains limited by pH control and kinetic constraints. Indirect methods, on the other hand, can achieve greater conversion efficiency and improved product selectivity. Nonetheless, large-scale deployment still faces obstacles involving high energy consumption, membrane fouling, waste handling, and the purity of the resulting carbonates. By consolidating dispersed knowledge and highlighting key technical challenges, this review elucidates the feasibility and limitations of coupling CO 2 mineralization with brine management. The insights provided aim to support future research directions and facilitate the transition toward industrial-scale implementation of brine-based CO 2 mineralization technologies.

title: Exercise-Induced Bronchoconstriction in Athletes: Pathophysiology, Diagnosis and Management - a literature review
title_original: Exercise-Induced Bronchoconstriction in Athletes: Pathophysiology, Diagnosis and Management - a literature review
summary: Introduction Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB) is a transient lower airway narrowing occurring during or post-vigorous physical activity. Unlike exercise-induced asthma (EIA), characterized by chronic inflammation, EIB affects both asthmatic and non-asthmatic individuals. It is the primary chronic condition in elite athletes, with prevalence reaching 70% in endurance disciplines. Untreated EIB impairs respiratory health, mental well-being, and sports performance. Materials and Methods A systematic literature search was conducted, based on the following databases: Embase, PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar, in reference to PRISMA guidelines. The keyword choice was decided beforehand in relation to the subject of the review. The Stage of Knowledge EIB pathophysiology centers on the hyperosmolar theory. Intense hyperventilation causes evaporative water loss and airway cooling. This osmotic shift and rapid rewarming trigger mast cell degranulation, releasing inflammatory mediators like cysteinyl leukotrienes (CysLTs) that cause smooth muscle contraction. Environmental factors heavily exacerbate this: cold air, low humidity, pollution, toxins, causing the disruption of epithelial barriers Summary EIB is a major health burden for athletes. Accurate diagnosis is vital to differentiate isolated EIB from chronic asthma. Effective management uses pharmacological treatments, like CysLT receptor antagonists, alongside dietary interventions, including Vitamin C, Omega-3, and gut microbiota modulation. These interventions mitigate inflammation, prevent irreversible remodeling, and optimize athletic performance.

title: Modelo de toma de decisiones basada en factores de compra, estrategias de marketing y satisfacción de los establecimientos de alojamiento de la región Puno
title_original: Modelo de toma de decisiones basada en factores de compra, estrategias de marketing y satisfacción de los establecimientos de alojamiento de la región Puno
summary: The profile of the international visitor has evolved into a highly digitalised consumer who plans travel itineraries based on online reviews, ratings, perceived quality, and prior user experiences. Within this context, the present study analysed how foreign visitors' decision-making is influenced by purchase factors, marketing strategies, and service satisfaction in accommodation establishments in the Puno region, Peru. The research adopted a quantitative approach, employing a deductive method, a non-experimental design, and a descriptive–explanatory scope through Structural Equation Modelling (SEM). Data were collected via a 50-item structured questionnaire administered to 200 foreign visitors who selected accommodation services in Puno during 2024. The findings reveal that personal (p = 0.041) and social factors (p = 0.007) significantly influence purchase decisions. Regarding marketing strategies, product (p = 0.026), price (p = 0.031), and promotion (p = 0.003) demonstrated statistically significant effects. Purchase influence (p = 0.004) and preference (p = 0.002) were also significant determinants. It is concluded that foreign visitors' decision-making is primarily explained by economic, social, and strategic service variables, providing empirical evidence to support hospitality management in emerging tourism destinations.

title: Strategic Evaluation and Implementation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Price Volatility in the Steel Commodity Market: A Comparative Study with the Foreign Exchange Market for Commercial Decision-Making
title_original: Strategic Evaluation and Implementation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Price Volatility in the Steel Commodity Market: A Comparative Study with the Foreign Exchange Market for Commercial Decision-Making
summary: This study aimed to implement and strategically compare machine-learning and deep-learning models for predicting price volatility in the Iranian steel commodity market and the EUR/USD foreign-exchange market and to evaluate their usefulness for commercial decision-making. This applied-developmental study used a descriptive-analytical design based on secondary time-series data from January 2019 to January 2024. The foreign-exchange dataset included hourly and daily EUR/USD opening, high, low, closing, and volume data extracted from MetaTrader 5. The steel dataset included daily and weekly prices of steel billets and sheets traded on the Iran Mercantile Exchange, together with the unofficial exchange rate, global 62% iron-ore prices, and seasonal demand indicators. After outlier correction, linear interpolation, logarithmic differencing, and feature engineering, Random Forest, XGBoost, Long Short-Term Memory, and Deep Q-Network models were implemented. Model validation was conducted through walk-forward validation using a three-year training window and a one-year out-of-sample testing window. Predictive and strategic performance were assessed through forecasting errors, directional accuracy, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, win rate, and profit factor. LSTM significantly outperformed Random Forest and XGBoost in both markets, producing the lowest forecasting errors and the highest directional accuracy and explanatory power. In the steel market, LSTM achieved an RMSE of 0.0062, directional accuracy of 70.80%, and R² of 0.77. However, DQN generated the strongest strategic performance, with an annualized return of 28.90%, Sharpe ratio of 1.86, maximum drawdown of 8.70%, and profit factor of 1.84. Bootstrap comparisons confirmed that DQN significantly outperformed LSTM in risk-adjusted trading performance. The steel-market models generally exceeded the EUR/USD models because fundamental variables improved predictability. LSTM was the most accurate forecasting model, whereas DQN was the most effective model for converting market information into profitable and risk-controlled commercial decisions.

title: Designing a Crowdfunding Investment Marketing Model for Enhancing Sustainable Urban Revenues: A Case Study of Tehran Municipality
title_original: Designing a Crowdfunding Investment Marketing Model for Enhancing Sustainable Urban Revenues: A Case Study of Tehran Municipality
summary: This study aimed to design and validate a crowdfunding investment marketing model for enhancing sustainable urban revenues in Tehran Municipality, with emphasis on the role of innovation drivers. This applied study was conducted using a mixed-methods exploratory–confirmatory design. In the qualitative phase, the Delphi technique was used to identify and validate the main dimensions and indicators of the model based on the opinions of 15 experts in urban management, municipal finance, innovation, investment, and crowdfunding. In the quantitative phase, a structured questionnaire was administered to 250 managers and senior experts of Tehran Municipality who were involved in financial, investment, planning, innovation, and public participation domains. Data were analyzed using exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, reliability testing, and structural equation modeling through SPSS and SmartPLS/AMOS. Inferential findings confirmed the adequacy of the measurement model. The KMO values for innovation in urban management, crowdfunding investment marketing, and sustainable urban revenue were 0.874, 0.884, and 0.893, respectively, and Bartlett’s tests were significant at p < 0.001. The extracted factors explained 57.45% of the variance in innovation, 68.30% of the variance in crowdfunding investment marketing, and 72.63% of the variance in sustainable urban revenue. Reliability was also confirmed, with Cronbach’s alpha coefficients of 0.907, 0.931, and 0.923, respectively. Structural equation modeling showed that innovation drivers had a positive and significant effect on crowdfunding investment marketing (β = 0.78, t = 8.45). Crowdfunding investment marketing significantly affected sustainable urban revenue (β = 0.65, t = 6.12). The direct effect of innovation drivers on sustainable urban revenue was also significant (β = 0.32, t = 3.11), and the indirect effect through crowdfunding investment marketing was confirmed (β = 0.51, t = 5.88). The results indicate that innovation drivers provide the institutional, technological, and organizational foundation for effective crowdfunding investment marketing, while crowdfunding marketing functions as a strategic mechanism for converting citizen trust and participation into sustainable municipal revenues.

title: Performing post-Britishness : a quest for independence in the contemporary literature of England
title_original: Performing post-Britishness : a quest for independence in the contemporary literature of England
summary: Since the eighteenth century, the distinctness of the nations of the UK has largely been overshadowed by top-down gestures aiming to unify British identity in everyday-life discourse. Due to the impact of devolution, the debates surrounding the 2014 Scottish independence referendum, and the 2016 EU referendum, the political conflicts between state and nation have been further exposed. Compared with the other three nations, England, in the eyes of many commentators, should be the last to whine about invisibility within an Anglo-British framework. But the fact that an over-stretched England has also led to the absence of the nation can no longer be ignored. An increasing interest in the discovery of England since the 1990s suggests a political and cultural need for renegotiating the boundary between Englishness and Britishness. Nevertheless, many attempts to pinpoint an English identity in the contemporary literature have relapsed into a reconstruction of British conceptions of the nation. In response to the (re-)canonisation of British imaginations, this thesis aims to show that a turn to ‘post-Britishness’ as a reading method suggests not only a desire for the return of England in a range of literature, but also a warning of the risk of expanding the ideas of England into some renewed British ideals. Reading novels by authors including Ian McEwan, Graham Swift, Gillian Slovo, Alecky Blythe, J.G. Ballard, and Tom McCarthy, this research analyses methods pointing towards breaks from idealised imaginations of England. Contextualised in a literary space that canonises a return to imaginary past, post-British critique of this kind can reveal absurdities of using British narratives to conceptualise an English community. By studying the biopoliticalness of British ideals, this thesis argues that a moment of Englishness starting from locating an independent England unavoidably sparks a reconsideration of the organicist strategies of Britishness, and their registration in contemporary literatures. A post-British reading of these literary texts shows that the continuity of an originary (narrative) structure is the major source of the political violence of Britishness. Instead of optimistically assuming a messianic, once-for-all break from such a structure, this thesis argues that awareness of its organicist logic is crucial for understanding the systematic absorption and disciplining of English characters inside British narrative.

In response to the (re-)canonisation of British imaginations, this thesis aims to show that a turn to ‘post-Britishness’ as a reading method suggests not only a desire for the return of England in a range of literature, but also a warning of the risk of expanding the ideas of England into some renewed British ideals. Reading novels by authors including Ian McEwan, Graham Swift, Gillian Slovo, Alecky Blythe, J.G. Ballard, and Tom McCarthy, this research analyses methods pointing towards breaks from idealised imaginations of England. Contextualised in a literary space that canonises a return to imaginary past, post-British critique of this kind can reveal absurdities of using British narratives to conceptualise an English community. By studying the biopoliticalness of British ideals, this thesis argues that a moment of Englishness starting from locating an independent England unavoidably sparks a reconsideration of the organicist strategies of Britishness, and their registration in contemporary literatures. A post-British reading of these literary texts shows that the continuity of an originary (narrative) structure is the major source of the political violence of Britishness. Instead of optimistically assuming a messianic, once-for-all break from such a structure, this thesis argues that awareness of its organicist logic is crucial for understanding the systematic absorption and disciplining of English characters inside British narrative.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding dietary supplements among athletes in Morocco: a national cross-sectional exploratory study
title_original: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding dietary supplements among athletes in Morocco: a national cross-sectional exploratory study
summary: Abstract Dietary supplement (DS) use is widespread in sports but raises important health and ethical concerns, particularly the risk of unintentional doping. In Morocco, data on this topic remain scarce. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of athletes recruited through a convenience sample of 14 Moroccan national sports federations regarding DSs. A descriptive and analytical cross-sectional survey was conducted between December 2023 and October 2024 among 1,094 athletes from 14 national sport federations. Data were collected using an online and face-to-face KAP questionnaire. Descriptive analyses, bivariate tests (χ 2 ), and multivariate analyses (binary logistic regression) were performed using JAMOVI ( p < 0.05). The prevalence of dietary supplement use was 38.1%. No significant difference in supplement use was observed between male and female athletes. Performance enhancement was the main motivation for use (52% of DS users). Nearly half of the athletes were unaware of the potential risks associated with dietary supplements, while 27.3% of DS users reported using supplements under medical or nutritional supervision. An exploratory multivariable logistic regression based on complete-case analysis (N = 366) suggested several factors associated with dietary supplement use. Athletes aged 28–32 years (OR = 2.75; 95% CI 1.34–5.67) and those who had consulted a healthcare professional (OR = 3.38; 95% CI 1.92–5.94) were more likely to report dietary supplement use, whereas athletes training fewer than five hours per week (OR = 0.48; 95% CI 0.25–0.93) and those who did not consider dietary supplements essential for improving performance (OR = 0.43; 95% CI 0.25–0.76) were less likely to use them. The model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC = 0.77) and no evidence of multicollinearity (all VIFs < 2). Among athletes recruited through a convenience sample of 14 Moroccan national sports federations, DS use was common and remained largely unsupervised. These exploratory findings highlight limited knowledge, low engagement with healthcare professionals, and a substantial risk of unintentional doping, providing preliminary evidence supporting the development of educational and regulatory strategies, which should be confirmed by nationally representative studies.

title: The climate responsibility of cultural influencers
title_original: The climate responsibility of cultural influencers
summary: In socially influential fields such as elite sport, music, and film, cultural relevance is often invoked as a special moral status that exempts them from genuine emissions reduction. We argue that visibility and influence should raise, not lower, the bar for climate responsibility, and identify advocacy leverage points to advance action in these sectors.

title: The Performance of Cultural Identity and Race in a Technological Space: Iwa-Akwa Ceremony of Umuezeala Autonomous Community as Prototype
title_original: The Performance of Cultural Identity and Race in a Technological Space: Iwa-Akwa Ceremony of Umuezeala Autonomous Community as Prototype
summary: Ndi Igbo in Nigeria as a race is imbued with different cultures that are celebrated and performed for different reasons. These reasons are either for the appeasement and propitiation to the gods for a wrongful act, as a thanksgiving to Ahiajoku for a bountiful harvest; as a rite of passage to the great beyond; as a mark of honour for achievement and/or an initiation into manhood amongst others. Thus, communities in Igbo land are identifiable with one cultural festivals or the other and this has continued to serve as a clear demarcation between them and their neighbours. Before now, these cultural festivals were performed in their primitive and raw state without much alteration and embellishment but the advancement in technology has altered the way most of these cutural festivals are celebrated and performed. This is the case of Iwa-Akwa ceremony of Umuezeala Autonomous Community in Ehime Mbano Local Government Area of Imo State. This paper therefore, through the use of historical and observational methods, and anchoring on the theory of technological determinism, examines the current technological wavelength in the world and how it has affected the celebration of the event. This is against the backdrop of the fact that technology has revolutionized the world and almost everything man does, including cultural celebrations have been influenced by it. It is the opinion of the writers that modern technology has drastically influenced the festival in terms of its accessibility, communicative nuances, visual appeal and acceptability. The paper therefore concludes that the sustenance of, improvement on and constant modification of these technologies is key to the continued survival of the festival as a cultural identity of Umuezeala people.

title: Mobile Telecommunication Networks and Decent Work in the Cape Coast Metropolis of Ghana
title_original: Mobile Telecommunication Networks and Decent Work in the Cape Coast Metropolis of Ghana
summary: Mobile telecommunication networks are a source of employment for many Ghanaians, especially the teeming youth. It is therefore expected that the employment generated by these telecommunication networks will be decent, as recommended by the International Labour Organization’s provisions on the decent work agenda. This current study investigates the activities of MTN and Vodafone, which are the two leading mobile telecommunication networks in Ghana, and their contribution to decent work in the Cape Coast Metropolis of the Republic of Ghana. Using the mixed-method research design and the International Labour Organization’s framework on the decent work agenda, the study finds that the two telecommunication networks (MTN and Vodafone) have promoted decent work in the Cape Coast Metropolis. The study recommends that management of the telecommunication networks could consider regularizing the activities of the retailers and institute pension and other social protection schemes which will take care of the staff and the retailers in the event of retirement, old age, or invalidity

title: How Consumers Perceive and React to Advertising amid AI Anxiety: Social Media Content Analysis of Apple’s ‘Crush!’ Ad Controversy
title_original: How Consumers Perceive and React to Advertising amid AI Anxiety: Social Media Content Analysis of Apple’s ‘Crush!’ Ad Controversy
summary: While artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted and developed in various fields at an incredible speed, people are experiencing AI anxiety – the fear of disruptive changes that AI may bring in personal or social life. In response to this growing adoption, technology and social media companies have released their advertisements showcasing how their new AI applications can be incorporated into everyday life. However, many of these adverting efforts have faced backlash for being ‘tone-deaf’ to AI concerns and failing to understand how consumers wish to use AI in their life. Drawing on the theoretical framework of controversial advertising (Barnes & Dotson, 1990), we suggest advertising promoting AI may include two controversial components: (1) AI as a controversial product and (2) AI-associated norm violations in the ad execution. Using Apple’s recent and globally publicized “Crush!” ad controversy as a case study, this research conducted a content analysis of social media conversations surrounding the ad to examine the factors contributing to the controversy and identify contemporary consumers’ evaluative norms for advertising in the era of AI. The findings provide practical implications for how brands should or should not represent, promote, or employ AI in their advertising.

title: How Constraints and Preferences Shape Travel Planning: Implications for AI Planning Support
title_original: How Constraints and Preferences Shape Travel Planning: Implications for AI Planning Support
summary: Planning is a common yet complex activity shaped by constraints to satisfy and preferences to balance. Travel planning, as both an everyday activity and a frequent benchmark for evaluating intelligent systems, offers a rich context for examining how constraints and preferences emerge and evolve. While recent AI systems have achieved impressive results in generating personalized itineraries, they often assume that users can articulate stable goals upfront. To understand how real-world planning unfolds, we conducted a two-part interview study: one with eight travelers reflecting on their planning experiences, and one with nine travel agents sharing professional practices. We trace the dynamics of constraints and preferences as they are surfaced, refined, and coordinated throughout the planning process, and identified 11 actions revolving around constraints and preferences, which shaped the planning process. We offer design heuristics for planning tools that better support human-AI collaborative actions to support the fluid, contingent nature of planning.

title: Buyer–Supplier Relationships in the Modern Supply Chain: Exploring Professionals' Perspectives on Power Balance in Pursuit of Decarbonization
title_original: Buyer–Supplier Relationships in the Modern Supply Chain: Exploring Professionals' Perspectives on Power Balance in Pursuit of Decarbonization
summary: ABSTRACT Decarbonization is a contemporary and critical organizational agenda for meeting climate change goals, but little is known about how strategies deployed to meet decarbonization goals interact with employees' agentic capacities and coping strategies, particularly in the context of supply chain pressures and power dynamics. We address this knowledge gap through a qualitative study and collected data through open‐ended essay‐based interviews from 43 supply chain professionals from various countries. The data analyzed through the Gioia method revealed six aggregate dimensions, showing that decarbonization changes what power rests on without changing who holds it: The ability to decarbonize becomes a new, shared basis of dependence that binds partners closer, while the balance of power holds—except where capability is scarce, demand is mature, or one party dominates. Our findings extend power‐dependence theory by indicating a transition in the modern supply chain toward a collaborative dynamic rather than one based purely on power.

title: CHANGES IN AVALANCHE FATALITIES BY ACTIVITY AND ASSOCIATED CHALLENGES IN WINTER OUTDOOR RECREATION IN JAPAN
title_original: CHANGES IN AVALANCHE FATALITIES BY ACTIVITY AND ASSOCIATED CHALLENGES IN WINTER OUTDOOR RECREATION IN JAPAN
summary: In Japan, 214 fatal avalanches have occurred over the past 35 years , resulting in 316 deaths.Of these, 84% (267) of the fatalities belonged to the winter outdoor recreation category.The activities included mountaineering, backcountry skiing or snowboarding, snowshoe hiking, snowmobiling, mountain stream fishing, and skiing at ski resorts.The fatalities included people enjoying these activities as leisure and commercial guided tours.The changes in the number of fatalities for each of these winter outdoor activities were summarized as follows: (1) Mountaineering fatalities, which accounted for about 70% of all fatalities in the 1990s, declined in the 2000s, and have not changed significantly since then; (2) Skier fatalities have increased significantly between 2006 and 2016, but have declined in recent years; (3) Major accidents with more than three fatalities have decreased; (4) Snowboarder fatalities are slightly increasing; (5) Half of the skier fatalities in the last 10 years have been foreign nationals, with many accidents involving expert skiers such as guides or professional skiers.This paper reports on the changes in the number of fatalities by activity, and the effectiveness and challenges of the various safety measures implemented by our organization thus far.At the same time, this paper expresses a strong sense of urgency about the increasing number of fatalities among those who visit Japan in search of "JAPOW" snow, and highlights the need for cooperative relationships with specialized institutions in various countries.

title: Interpreting tourist load: how does sports event tourism intensity impact tourist experience?
title_original: Interpreting tourist load: how does sports event tourism intensity impact tourist experience?
summary: Abstract Sports event tourism has become an important driver of urban competitiveness, yet little is known about how tourists perceive the intensity of their participation and how this shapes their experiences. Existing research conceptualises tourism intensity mainly at the destination level, emphasising issues such as overcrowding and environmental pressure, while neglecting the individual-level loads tourists carry during event travel. This study develops an individual-level conceptualisation of sports event tourism intensity as a multidimensional, tourist-perceived load encompassing temporal, physical, cognitive, social, and sensory demands. Drawing on an interpretivist paradigm, qualitative data were collected from 21 in-depth interviews and 123 online travel posts, and analysed through content analysis and grounded theory to inductively derive the structure and mechanisms of intensity. The findings indicate five interrelated dimensions of sports event tourism intensity—time investment, physical exertion, travel interaction, cognitive engagement, and sensory stimulation—and further reveal two motivational drivers, fear of missing out and maximising travel value, that encourage tourists to voluntarily engage in high-intensity travel experiences. Rather than functioning as a direct determinant of tourist experience, sports event tourism intensity influences emotional outcomes through the development of tourism fatigue, comprising both physical and mental fatigue. Building on these findings and informed by Optimal Stimulation Level Theory, the study develops an interpretive mid-range framework illustrating how motivational drivers, sports event tourism intensity, tourism fatigue, and tourist experience interact throughout sports event tourism. The research contributes theoretically by complementing existing destination-level understandings of tourism intensity with an individual-level perspective, clarifying the distinction between sources of load and their experiential consequences, and extending current theorisation of sports event tourism experience. Practically, it offers insights for organisers and destination managers to design balanced itineraries, optimise infrastructure, and foster emotionally rewarding experiences by aligning stimulation with tourists’ recovery needs.

title: Belirsiz Kriter Ağırlıkları Altında Kurumsal Masaüstü Bilgisayar Tedariki: SMAA-2 Uygulaması
title_original: Belirsiz Kriter Ağırlıkları Altında Kurumsal Masaüstü Bilgisayar Tedariki: SMAA-2 Uygulaması
summary: The renewal of an organization's IT infrastructure requires the simultaneous consideration of multiple, and sometimes conflicting, factors, including cost, performance, technical suitability, and service availability. In such decisions, ambiguity and disagreement regarding the priorities of the various stakeholder groups often restrict the use of conventional multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) methods that rely on deterministic weights.In this paper, the Stochastic Multi-Criteria Acceptability Analysis (SMAA-2) method is applied to a corporate desktop computer procurement problem in which the criteria weights are uncertain. The criterion values of the alternatives were assumed to be deterministic, whereas preference uncertainty was modeled by sampling criterion weights from a uniform distribution over the weight simplex. Eighteen desktop computer models available in Turkish market were evaluated with respect to the main decision dimensions of processor performance, memory and storage characteristics, service accessibility and price, together with their related technical indicators. A total of 10,000 Monte Carlo iterations were performed in the JSMAA software to obtain the Rank Acceptability Index (RAI), the Central Weight Vectors (CWV), and the Confidence Factor (CF) for each alternative.The results indicate that the Pro Tower 290 G9 model has the highest probability of being ranked first (55.5%) and the highest confidence factor (0.71) under the current criterion structure. The CWV results reveal the preference profiles under which each alternative is favorable, while the CF analysis indicates the relative stability of these preferences across varying weight structures. Overall, the study provides a probabilistic evaluation framework that explicitly accounts for preference uncertainty and offers a data-driven, flexible and interpretable decision support approach for corporate hardware procurement.

title: Public Participation, Policy Transparency, and Community Satisfaction: Evidence from Local Tourism Governance in South Sulawesi, Indonesia
title_original: Public Participation, Policy Transparency, and Community Satisfaction: Evidence from Local Tourism Governance in South Sulawesi, Indonesia
summary: This study examines the associations among public participation, policy transparency, public trust, and community satisfaction in local tourism governance in South Sulawesi, Indonesia. The study employed a cross-sectional, one-time, same-respondent self-report survey involving 450 residents recruited through non-probability procedures at purposively selected tourism destinations. The final sample comprised 150 respondents from each of three contextual tourism clusters: natural, marine and island, and cultural tourism destinations. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to estimate the proposed associations. The retained statistical output indicates positive associations between public participation and community satisfaction, policy transparency and community satisfaction, public participation and public trust, policy transparency and public trust, and public trust and community satisfaction. The corrected standardized coefficients were 0.165, 0.414, 0.462, 0.498, and 0.395, respectively. The corresponding indirect associations through public trust were 0.182 for public participation and 0.197 for policy transparency. However, the reported inter-construct correlations ranged from 0.905 to 0.928 and exceeded the corresponding square roots of average variance extracted. The Fornell–Larcker criterion was therefore not satisfied, indicating that the constructs were not demonstrated to be empirically distinct in the available analysis. Because the respondent-level dataset, collection-mode identifiers, data-cleaning log, and complete SmartPLS project could not be recovered, the measurement model could not be re-specified or independently re-estimated. The findings must consequently be interpreted as exploratory associations within the non-probability sample rather than as causal effects or population-level estimates. abstract: This study examines the associations among public participation, policy transparency, public trust, and community satisfaction in local tourism governance in South Sulawesi, Indonesia. The study employed a cross-sectional, one-time, same-respondent self-report survey involving 450 residents recruited through non-probability procedures at purposively selected tourism destinations. The final sample comprised 150 respondents from each of three contextual tourism clusters: natural, marine and island, and cultural tourism destinations. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to estimate the proposed associations. The retained statistical output indicates positive associations between public participation and community satisfaction, policy transparency and community satisfaction, public participation and public trust, policy transparency and public trust, and public trust and community satisfaction. The corrected standardized coefficients were 0.165, 0.414, 0.462, 0.498, and 0.395, respectively. The corresponding indirect associations through public trust were 0.182 for public participation and 0.197 for policy transparency. However, the reported inter-construct correlations ranged from 0.905 to 0.928 and exceeded the corresponding square roots of average variance extracted. The Fornell–Larcker criterion was therefore not satisfied, indicating that the constructs were not demonstrated to be empirically distinct in the available analysis. Because the respondent-level dataset, collection-mode identifiers, data-cleaning log, and complete SmartPLS project could not be recovered, the measurement model could not be re-specified or independently re-estimated. The findings must consequently be interpreted as exploratory associations within the non-probability sample rather than as causal effects or population-level estimates. The study highlights both the potential interrelationship of participatory governance perceptions and the need for future research using independently validated measures, probability-based sampling, and longitudinal or multi-source designs.

title: The Biomechanical and Perceptual Impact of Breast Support during Riding and Running in Female Equestrians
title_original: The Biomechanical and Perceptual Impact of Breast Support during Riding and Running in Female Equestrians
summary: Popular among women, equestrian sport is the only sex-integrated Olympic sport, relying on interspecies communication between horse and rider. Despite extensive breast research in sport, equestrian research is limited. This study investigated the impact of bras on breast movement, comfort, and pain; rider position and asymmetry; and compared breast movement and pain in riding versus running. Participants (n = 21) rode a Racewood™ Equine Simulator (ES) in walk, trot, and canter and ran on a treadmill (TM) in four breast support conditions: everyday (EB), encapsulation sports bra (ESB), combination sports bra (CSB), and bare-breasted (BB). Markers were tracked by a Qualisys motion capture system, and relative breast displacement (RBD) in TM and ES was calculated, along with rider position during ES. Exercise-induced breast pain (EIBP) and bra comfort were measured on 0–100 visual analogue scales, and a survey on bra performance and aesthetics was completed. TM caused the highest EIBP (mm) (x̃ = 67.25, P < 0.001) and RBD (cm) (x̃ = 5.56, P < 0.001) in BB. A moderate positive association (rs(19) = 0.428, P < 0.001) was observed between EIBP and RBD, both of which were reduced by ESB (EIBP P < 0.001; RBD P < 0.002) and CSB (EIBP P < 0.001; RBD P < 0.001) in trot and TM. In trot, torso position improved in ESB (Z = −3.841, P < 0.001) and CSB (Z = −3.806, P < 0.001) compared to EB, and riders were most symmetrical in ESB. Bra comfort and preferences were idiosyncratic. Bra type meaningfully influenced EIBP, rider position, and symmetry. Future larger, longitudinal, field-based studies are warranted.

title: White Deer Award of Excellence: A Strategic Framework for Establishing a Credible Recognition Program for Education and Other Government and Non-Government Sectors
title_original: White Deer Award of Excellence: A Strategic Framework for Establishing a Credible Recognition Program for Education and Other Government and Non-Government Sectors
summary: The White Deer Award of Excellence serves as a strategic initiative to establish credible recognition mechanism that celebrates exceptional achievements and promotes excellence across education, government, and non-government sectors. This study explores the White Deer Award of Excellence as a strategic initiative for establishing credible recognition mechanisms across education, government, and non-government sectors in Region XII. Using an Explanatory-Sequential Mixed Method Research Design, the study investigates how a transparent and strategic awards system can promote excellence and foster a culture of meritocracy. The quantitative phase assesses the relationship between the quality of the White Deer Award and the creation of credible recognition bodies. Data was collected from DepEd districts, municipalities, and NGO offices that recognize outstanding employees annually. Findings revealed that the White Deer Award is perceived as a credible recognition body, with high ratings for transparency, consistency in criteria, and the credibility of the judging panel. The correlation analysis indicates that the award is positively linked with key educational outcomes, such as accreditation and alignment with educational standards. Thematic analysis highlights the importance of community-based validation, direct observation, and thorough evaluation in ensuring credibility. Furthermore, participants suggest strategies to increase awareness, including integrating the award into professional development, utilizing digital toolkits, and promoting it through social media and academic channels. Overall, the study underscores the White Deer Award’s effectiveness in fostering excellence and enhancing the credibility of educational and organizational programs in Region XII.

title: Sportswashing and the Paradoxes of CSR: A critical public relations model of elite sports philanthropy
title_original: Sportswashing and the Paradoxes of CSR: A critical public relations model of elite sports philanthropy
summary: This article revisits a foundational question in critical public relations (CPR): how do we distinguish corporate social responsibility (CSR) grounded in genuine public interests from CSR activities that are strategically mobilized for reputational advantage? It addresses this question by exploring sportswashing, conceptualized here as a reputational outcome of sports philanthropy, particularly the sponsorship of elite athletes. It analyzes this phenomenon through a case study of Australian mining magnate Gina Rinehart and her sponsorships of elite Olympic athletes. It identifies the earned media publicity generated from these sponsorships through qualitative content analysis of Australian newspapers. The findings show that this coverage overwhelmingly framed Rinehart as a benevolent benefactor of Olympic sport, associating her with charismatic athletes and more abstract constructs such as patriotism and national glory. Ultimately, the article develops a critical public relations model of sportswashing (CPRMS) intended as a theoretical disruption of uncritical accounts of CSR. This model demonstrates that sports philanthropy, while clearly beneficial to athletes, can also serve as a tool for image bolstering in the service of private capital.

title: Director Expertise and Compliance to Corporate Social Responsibility Regulations
title_original: Director Expertise and Compliance to Corporate Social Responsibility Regulations
summary: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue This paper investigates whether assigning CSR‐specific expertise to the board committee legally responsible for CSR improves compliance with mandatory CSR law and shapes how firms organize that compliance. Research Findings/Insights Using Indian listed companies subject to mandatory CSR regulation, we find that CSR expertise on CSR committees is associated with higher compliance and more concentrated CSR activities across categories and locations. These associations are stronger among firms facing greater competitive or financial pressures and those without prior CSR engagement. High compliance combined with CSR expertise is also associated with higher firm value, improved creditworthiness, and greater institutional ownership. Theoretical/Academic Implications Our findings highlight how directors with CSR expertise help companies improve legal compliance with mandatory CSR regulations and pursue more focused CSR strategies. This research identifies committee‐level CSR expertise as an important governance mechanism shaping both regulatory compliance and the organization of CSR activities. It demonstrates the benefits of embedding CSR expertise within board structures. Practitioner/Policy Implications We provide evidence that directors with CSR expertise and stronger compliance positively affect firm outcomes. Governments and policymakers could use these findings to promote CSR expertise on corporate boards, incentivize compliance, and promote the convergence of financial and social goals. Our study provides empirical support for recent public policies, including the 2020 EU recommendation to appoint sustainability experts on corporate boards.

title: A stratified ecological model of injury etiology in professional football: a context‑driven “game model” of injury risk constraints management and foresight reasoning under uncertainty
title_original: A stratified ecological model of injury etiology in professional football: a context‑driven “game model” of injury risk constraints management and foresight reasoning under uncertainty
summary: Understanding sports injury etiology, causation, and risk mitigation remains a central focus in sports medicine research.However, current models remain generic, neglecting the sport-specific characteristics and environmental specificities that shape both injury-risk and -resilience.This gap is especially critical in football, where injury risk is inherently intricate and multifactorial.To address this, we propose a novel conceptual approach built around a context-driven "Game Model", specifically tailored to the football's complexity.The core of our model is centred on the principle that a player's injury-risk is directly dependent on the dynamics and context of the team/club rather than being solely determined by a simple causality of prematurely and haphazardly musculoskeletal "intrinsic factors".Our model is structured around five superposed "Ecological Strata", which incorporate the concept of "contextual drivers" mapping the non-linear dynamics of the different constraints within the football environment that influence team and player injury-risk.Through this structure, we bring to light overlooked elements, including player interconnection, non-exposure, response versus adaptation, delayed recursive loop, non-time-loss injuries and foresight-driven clinical reasoning paired with hindsight clinical review, each capturing a dimension of risk that linear models fail to account for.Taken together, our context-driven approach reframes injury-risk recognition as dynamic, contextual, and intuitive, allowing clinicians to navigate, rather than merely react to uncertainty.In doing so, our model offers operational perspectives and windows of opportunities for injury-risk constraints management, enabling more proactive clinical reasoning and transdisciplinary collaborative decision-making, alongside targeted interventions to maintain and develop player health, robustness and performance within the football environment.

title: Financial Challenges and Survival Strategies of Regional Football Clubs: Empirical Evidence from Northern Uganda
title_original: Financial Challenges and Survival Strategies of Regional Football Clubs: Empirical Evidence from Northern Uganda
summary: Regional football clubs in the developing world occupy a peculiar space in the sporting economy: socially indispensable, providing platforms for youth engagement, community identity and post-conflict healing, yet financially precarious in ways that threaten their existence.This study examines the financial challenges and survival strategies facing regional football clubs in Northern Uganda, using a mixed-methods approach that carefully analysed 200 questionnaire responses and 22 Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) with players, coaches, club officials and other football stakeholders across the region.Clubs generally operate within a survival-oriented financial system, leaning heavily on community contributions, owners' support and fundraising, while sponsorship and other commercial revenue remain limited.Key informants identified inadequate government support, unmet player welfare needs, transportation costs and low sponsorship as the major financial problems.These difficulties are not confined to one area of club activity; they spread across player motivation, match attendance, facility development, competition participation and overall club performance.In response, clubs have relied on volunteer support, community contributions and financial assistance from owners or management, while some have begun exploring local income sources such as poultry keeping, farming and small businesses, modest supplements rather than solutions on their own.The findings clearly show the core problem is not simply a lack of money but the absence of regular, diversified income capable of sustaining club activities over time; dependence on sponsorship, government support or occasional contributions leaves clubs financially weak and uncertain.Clubs therefore need genuinely diversified income-generating activities, stronger ties to government and private business, improved facilities and projects suited to the local environment.The study concludes that the central challenge is not simply the absence of money but the absence of predictable, diversified and institutionally supported revenue, a structural fragility demanding deliberate, multi-level intervention, and study proposes evidence-based recommendations for clubs, governing bodies, government and development partners.

title: Sports Finance and Management
title_original: Sports Finance and Management
summary: As the sports business continues to evolve, so does the field of Sport Finance and Management. The first edition of this book provided an in-depth exploration of the dynamic changes within the sports industry, including the interconnected financial relationships between teams and their associated businesses, the influence of fan loyalty, and the impact of sponsorships on team revenues. Building on this foundation, the second edition updates these core elements, introduces new case studies, and examines the effects of changes in facility design, media opportunities, and league and conference policies. These factors are analyzed in relation to their impact on the economic success of teams, the salaries of professional players, and the financial landscape of collegiate athletics. This latest edition goes even further, incorporating discussions on emerging topics such as women's sports and sports betting. It also addresses the significant transformations the industry has experienced in recent years, offering a comprehensive and timely perspective on the evolving world of sports finance and management.

title: Athlete gender visibility, emotional narratives, and audience engagement in CCTV News’s Olympic short-video coverage on Douyin: an empirical analysis
title_original: Athlete gender visibility, emotional narratives, and audience engagement in CCTV News’s Olympic short-video coverage on Douyin: an empirical analysis
summary: Short-form video platforms have become important channels for major sports-event coverage, but empirical evidence remains limited regarding how athletes are presented, how emotions are organized, and how these features relate to audience engagement in specific institutional accounts. This study analyzes 219 short-video posts published by the official China Central Television (CCTV) News account on Douyin during the 2024 Paris Olympic Games. Content analysis, t-tests, and regression analysis were used to examine mention-based athlete gender visibility, emotional narratives, and three platform-displayed engagement indicators: likes, comments, and shares. The results show no statistically significant difference between female and male athletes in mention frequency, indicating relative balance only at the level of being named. Athlete mention frequency was not significantly associated with likes, comments, or shares. Emotional narratives were not directly associated with higher engagement, but posts using emotional narratives contained significantly more athlete mentions. Emotional narrative also positively moderated the relationship between mention frequency and shares, although not the relationships with likes or comments. These findings suggest that, within this single-account and single-platform case, mention frequency is a potential narrative resource rather than an engagement outcome in itself, and its association with content diffusion depends partly on emotional framing. The conclusions should not be generalized to all Chinese mainstream media or interpreted as evidence of complete gender equality in athlete portrayal.

title: Making Sense of Sport Fan Identification and Loyalty: Differentiating First and Second Favorite Teams of Mexico’s NFL Fans
title_original: Making Sense of Sport Fan Identification and Loyalty: Differentiating First and Second Favorite Teams of Mexico’s NFL Fans
summary: In this empirical study, we examined the impact of NFL fanship on team identification and team loyalty. While sport spectators have various motives for watching a game, even when their favorite team is not playing, little to no known research has illuminated how NFL fanship translates to identification with and loyalty for a second favorite team—especially amongst “satellite fans.” Acknowledging ongoing internationalization efforts of the National Football League (NFL), we surveyed 571 Mexico-based NFL fans to better understand this market. Drawing upon literature from identity theory, fanship, and spectatorship, we utilized partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine how Mexico-based NFL fans manifest identification and loyalty to their first and second favorite teams. We found that NFL fanship strongly affects identification for first and second favorite teams, which strongly impacts team loyalty. Our findings demonstrate that Mexico-based NFL fans can be highly identified like local fans, providing expanded insights for scholars and practitioners focused on NFL fanship beyond core domestic markets. Additionally, we found that NFL fanship alone does not significantly influence loyalty to one’s first favorite team; team identification must also be present. However, fanship influences loyalty to one’s second favorite team, offering new perspectives on satellite supporters.
