title: Holocaust Education in the Age of Participatory Culture
title_original: Holocaust Education in the Age of Participatory Culture
summary: Thesis. The study is based on the thesis that Holocaust education in the age of participatory culture is undergoing a profound transformation with both positive and negative impacts. The paper proposes a trauma-informed approach as a framework enabling the responsible mediation of the Holocaust within the environment of participatory culture. Methods. The research is grounded in an interdisciplinary qualitative approach that combines theoretical analysis of the concepts of cultural memory, trauma and participatory culture; content and discourse analysis of selected digital educational platforms and participatory formats; comparative analysis of traditional and digital forms of Holocaust education; and ethical reflection based on trauma-informed principles. Results. Participatory culture strengthens learners’ active engagement, identification and personal connection with the historical subject, supports the development of media literacy and critical thinking. However, without clear ethical and pedagogical frameworks, participatory culture may undermine the dignity of Holocaust memory (possibility for its commercial exploitation, trivialisation or denial, appropriation of trauma etc.). Conclusion. Holocaust education within the conditions of participatory culture represents an irreversible paradigmatic shift that requires new ethical, pedagogical and methodological grounding. The research confirms that a trauma-informed approach, combined with reflection on the media structures of participation, resembles a key prerequisite for the dignified and meaningful mediation of Holocaust memory. Such an approach enables to protect learners from secondary retraumatisation and preserve the ethical integrity of victims’ memory.

title: A fada do skate e o empoderamento do mito: A perspectiva feminista na construção publicitária de Rayssa Leal durante as Olimpíadas de Tóquio 2020
title_original: A fada do skate e o empoderamento do mito: A perspectiva feminista na construção publicitária de Rayssa Leal durante as Olimpíadas de Tóquio 2020
summary: Rayssa Leal was only six years old when she was nicknamed "Fadinha" (Little Fairy), a moniker that bridged the playful world of children's stories with skateboarding and contributed to building her mythic image in the media landscape. Against this backdrop, this study analyzes the representation of the Brazilian athlete in advertising media related to the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games, viewed through the lens of female empowerment. To this end, the study employs the film analysis framework proposed by Vanoye and Goliot-Lété (2006), applying it to keyframes from the "Novas Fadas" (New Fairies) commercial produced by Nike. The theoretical framework integrates concepts of myth, advertising, and gender equity, while also addressing "Femvertising" and its implications for contemporary representations of women. The results indicate that the campaign constructs a mythic, inspirational image of Rayssa Leal through visual elements, animation, and soundtrack, reinforcing values ​​associated with overcoming obstacles and realizing dreams. Concurrently, the narrative mobilizes discourses regarding gender equality and the valuing of women's presence in historically male-dominated spaces, positioning the athlete as a symbolic figure of inspiration, representation, and social transformation.

title: (IM)POSSIBILIDADES DE CARREIRA NO VÔLEI DE PRAIA BRASILEIRO: NARRATIVAS DE JOGADORAS
title_original: (IM)POSSIBILIDADES DE CARREIRA NO VÔLEI DE PRAIA BRASILEIRO: NARRATIVAS DE JOGADORAS
summary: Este artigo tratou da constituição de diferentes carreiras de jogadoras brasileiras de Vôlei de Praia, buscando compreender os desafios e condições que (im)possibilitam o processo de profissionalização, destacando avanços e barreiras implicados nesse processo. Utilizando uma inspiração cartográfica, foram feitas imersões em dois Centros de Treinamento, sendo um localizado na cidade de Fortaleza/CE e outro em Itapema/SC. Nestas imersões, foram produzidos diários de campo, além de oito entrevistas temáticas subsidiadas na história oral, com atletas profissionais ou em processo de profissionalização. Foi possível identificar que as jogadoras associam a profissionalização à classificação no Circuito Brasileiro, à dedicação exclusiva ao esporte e à conquista de títulos expressivos na carreira. Algumas atletas conciliam o treinamento esportivo com o ensino superior, configurando uma dupla carreira como estratégia de segurança profissional. As narrativas das entrevistadas também denunciaram a existência de limitações estruturais e revela que a profissionalização de mulheres no Vôlei de Praia brasileiro ainda ocorre em condições instáveis, exigindo maior institucionalização e investimento.

title: Soft Power, Experience, and Reputation: Drivers of Chinese Travel Intentions to Thailand
title_original: Soft Power, Experience, and Reputation: Drivers of Chinese Travel Intentions to Thailand
summary: Purpose: This study examines how individual experiences, attitudes toward Thai soft power (5F), and perceived country reputation influence Chinese tourists’ intentions to visit Thailand. Research design, data and methodology: A quantitative cross sectional survey of 437 Chinese respondents was analyzed using structural equation modeling to evaluate direct and mediating pathways. Results: Individual experiences significantly enhance perceived country reputation but do not directly predict travel intention. Attitudes toward Thai soft power (5F) show a strong positive effect on perceived reputation and on travel intention. Perceived country reputation neither directly influences intention nor mediates the effects of experience or soft power attitudes on intention. Conclusions: Findings indicate a functional division of roles in travel decision making: reputation operates as a distal evaluative frame, experience serves as a feeder to reputation, and attitudes toward Thai soft power (5F) act as the immediate actuator of intention. Managerial implications recommend prioritizing favorable soft power attitudes through emotionally resonant, culturally immersive communication centered on Thai food, film, festivals, and fashion, delivered through storytelling, digital campaigns, and influencer engagement across key Chinese travel segments. Limitations include the cross sectional, self reported design; future research should employ longitudinal or experimental approaches and include behavioral outcomes to validate causal mechanisms.

title: Study on the Differential Development of Ice-Snow Economy in Shenyang, Harbin and Changchun
title_original: Study on the Differential Development of Ice-Snow Economy in Shenyang, Harbin and Changchun
summary: Against the background that China's ice-snow economy has entered the trillion-yuan track and the three northeastern provinces have become the core leading area of the national ice-snow economy, Harbin takes the lead with an international ice-snow cultural tourism IP + a full industrial chain, and Changchun deeply plows the segmented market with ski training + ice-snow parks. Shenyang is faced with challenges such as resource homogenization, insufficient brand recognition and low industrial collaboration. How to expand the advantages of Shenyang's ice-snow tourism and reshape its past glory is an urgent subject to be studied. In order to conduct a more objective and clear self-evaluation, this paper selects Changchun, a provincial capital city with highly similar geographical location, ice-snow tourism resources and tourist source market to Harbin, and whose ice-snow tourism has made remarkable achievements in recent years, as a reference for a comparative study in the northeast sector with the strongest strength in China's ice-snow tourism. It strives to make the conclusions more convincing and the countermeasures more targeted and operable.

title: A systematic review of event technologies in the context of smart tourism: trends and future directions
title_original: A systematic review of event technologies in the context of smart tourism: trends and future directions
summary: This study presents a systematic review of the integration of emerging digital technologies in smart tourism events, with the purpose of understanding how technological innovation is transforming event design, management and visitor experience. The review examines peer-reviewed journal articles and conference proceedings published between 2014 and 2024 and indexed in the Scopus and Web of Science databases. The analysis was conducted using the Bibliometrix package in the R environment, while descriptive and thematic analyses were performed with the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences. The findings show that several technological domains, including Artificial Intelligence, the Internet Of Things, Big Data analytics and immersive technologies, are driving significant advances in the development of smart tourism events. These technologies support improvements in personalisation, behavioural analysis, sustainability, accessibility and real-time decision making. The review also reveals conceptual fragmentation, methodological diversity and geographical imbalances across the existing literature. Overall, this study contributes to consolidating the theoretical foundations of smart events and identifies promising directions for future research and innovation within technology-enhanced tourism event ecosystems.

title: From interaction to identification: a mixed methods study on the formation mechanism of group identity among Ultimate Frisbee club members
title_original: From interaction to identification: a mixed methods study on the formation mechanism of group identity among Ultimate Frisbee club members
summary: Background Lifestyle sports like Ultimate Frisbee have emerged as important settings for social connection amid urban social atomization. Nevertheless, the voluntary and non-contractual nature of these clubs means they continue to face persistent challenges in sustaining membership. Although prior research has explored group identity in various sporting contexts, the mechanisms through which ritualized interaction and social exchange jointly contribute to members' identification remain insufficiently understood. Objective This study investigates the formation mechanism of group identity among Ultimate Frisbee club members by integrating Interaction Ritual Chain theory and Social Exchange theory, and empirically tests whether emotional energy and relational benefits serve as parallel mediating pathways. Methods A sequential exploratory mixed-methods design was employed. Study 1 adopted a grounded theory approach, using semi-structured interviews with 22 club members across multiple Chinese cities to inductively identify core antecedents and construct a theoretical model. Study 2 employed a cross-sectional survey design, with structural equation modeling applied to a sample of 332 Ultimate Frisbee club members to quantitatively test the hypothesized pathways. Results The grounded theory analysis indicated a dual-pathway mechanism encompassing an affective pathway (interaction rituals → emotional energy → group identity) and a rational pathway (interaction rituals → relational benefits → group identity). The SEM results indicated that both emotional energy and relational benefits significantly mediated the relationship between interaction rituals and group identity. The mediating effect of relational benefits—encompassing trust and social acceptance—was larger (33.58% of total effect) than that of emotional energy (14.97%). Conclusion These findings integrate Interaction Ritual Chain theory and Social Exchange theory into a unified framework, suggesting that rational evaluations of social reciprocity were more strongly associated with identity formation than transient emotional experiences in non-contractual sports clubs. The results point to the central role of relational calculus in voluntary organizations where formal incentives are absent. From a practical standpoint, club managers may consider prioritizing relational rewards and the development of ritualized interaction settings to enhance long-term member retention.

title: Audience Perceptions in the Global South: A Survey-Based Analysis of Beijing’s Multidimensional Image in South Africa
title_original: Audience Perceptions in the Global South: A Survey-Based Analysis of Beijing’s Multidimensional Image in South Africa
summary: Focusing on the under-researched nexus of city image and Global South audiences, this study investigates Beijing’s multidimensional perception in South Africa. Grounded in an integrated framework of soft power and city branding, it employs a stratified survey and regression analysis to reveal a structural City Gap, while Beijing is admired for technological and economic prowess, its image as a political center and inclusive metropolis remains weak, indicating a ceiling for performance-based legitimacy. Regression identifies media exposure and direct visits as key positive predictors. Crucially, a demographic divide emerges: younger cohorts show a significant youth dividend of favorable views, whereas higher education correlates with skepticism. The results confirm the two-step flow of communication, demonstrating the primacy of local media mediation over official narratives. The study concludes by advocating for a strategic pivot from broadcast publicity to city citizen diplomacy, emphasizing glocalized engagement to build genuine soft power.

title: MUITO ALÉM DOS NÚMEROS! QUAL O VALOR DE UM JOGADOR DE FUTEBOL? UM ESTUDO DOS MÉTODOS DE AVALIAÇÃO
title_original: MUITO ALÉM DOS NÚMEROS! QUAL O VALOR DE UM JOGADOR DE FUTEBOL? UM ESTUDO DOS MÉTODOS DE AVALIAÇÃO
summary: Quais os fatores que influenciam os preços de um jogador de futebol? Esta pesquisa teve como objetivo identificar os principais fatores determinantes na avaliação de preço de venda e fazer um comparativo do que está de acordo com o que os clubes de futebol usam. Para tanto, foi realizado uma revisão bibliográfica e documental do tipo descritiva e de abordagem qualitativa, se baseando estudos realizados anteriormente, das demonstrações financeiras do ano de 2023 dos quatro principais clubes de São Paulo e de reportagens encontradas que possam complementar o assunto. O trabalho atingiu seu objetivo ao trazer o entendimento de que os estudos que trazem a abordagem de mensuração do valor do jogador para o mercado podem divergir da forma em que um clube utiliza para tal. Isto leva a compreender que a avaliação do preço de venda de um jogador é complexa devido ao fato de se tratar de avaliações muitas vezes subjetivas, o que impede a criação de fórmulas padronizadas de avaliação.

title: A Study on the Development of Cultural Product Design Centered on the Image of Gamcheon Culture Village
title_original: A Study on the Development of Cultural Product Design Centered on the Image of Gamcheon Culture Village
summary: This study examines the influence of Gamcheon Culture Village's unique cultural image in Busan on cultural product design and investigates the relationship among image elements, brand image, and purchase intention.The research model used image elements (cognitive image, affective image, and behavioral image) as independent variables, brand image as a mediating variable, and purchase intention as a dependent variable.A literature review, field investigation, and case analysis identified key design elements derived from the village's distinctive characteristics, including its terraced residential landscape, colorful visual identity, mural art, and local storytelling resources.The findings indicate that Gamcheon Culture Village's image elements positively influence brand image formation, while an enhanced brand image significantly increases consumers' purchase intention.Furthermore, image elements were found to have a direct positive effect on purchase intention.These results suggest that cultural products reflecting the cultural identity and symbolic characteristics of Gamcheon Culture Village can enhance tourists' perceived value and strengthen the competitiveness of local cultural brands.This study offers practical implications and foundational data for developing cultural product design and regional branding strategies based on local cultural resources.

title: Perception of quality of an international recreational gymnastics event: the case of the GIMNASTRADA 2019
title_original: Perception of quality of an international recreational gymnastics event: the case of the GIMNASTRADA 2019
summary: Introduction The GIMNASTRADA is an annual, non-competitive gymnastics event, held in the city of Cáceres (Extremadura, Spain) since 1996. The 2019 edition was the largest in number of participants with around 3,700 gymnasts and 12,000 spectators. The aim of this study was to determine whether the perception of quality of GIMNASTRADA 2019 was influenced by the type of participation that different groups of attenders developed in this gymnastic event (gymnasts, gymnastics group leaders, family members, audience, organisational staff). Methods To this end, a total of 331 participants completed a short four item-questionnaire created ad hoc for this study in order to evaluate the perceived quality of certain management processes existing in this sporting event (e.g., quality of facilities, planning, organisation and development). The questionnaire, based on single-item measures of previous validated scales as EVENTQUAL and IPA4RE, was answered anonymously by the participants using their own mobile devices via a Google Docs form. Results The results showed differences in questionnaire scores between groups of participants. It is concluded that the type of participation influenced the perception of quality between groups of attenders in GIMNASTRADA 2019. Discussion It would be advisable for sports managers to design sporting events tailored to different participant profiles, including activities adapted to their specific interests, with the aim of providing a positive experience that would promote their participation in future editions.

title: Casting On at the Games: Knitting Through Milano Cortina
title_original: Casting On at the Games: Knitting Through Milano Cortina
summary: This study examined how Olympic athletes shared knitting-themed content on Instagram before, during, and after the Milano Cortina Winter Games in early 2026, with particular attention paid to the themes associated with posts. Instagram has been recognized as a key platform for craft-related content among makers, and it has also served as a central space for athletes’ personal brand building. The research data were collected from athletes’ public Instagram accounts, including images and Reels, up to April 10, 2026, at which point several recurring narratives and themes reached a natural conclusion as the season ended. The findings suggest that athletes utilized social media to curate their personal brands. They framed knitting as a relaxing and enjoyable activity to balance intensive training schedules and traveling. Many emphasized the importance of finalizing knitting projects and described a sense of satisfaction and pleasure upon finishing them. A notable practice involved the “Knitting Club,” where athletes gathered face-to-face during the Olympic Games. Interaction between athletes and their followers was frequent, with numerous comments in the comment sections and shared challenges. Overall, the dialogue was predominantly positive and supportive, highlighting knitting as a means of expressing identity and building community in elite sports contexts.

title: From preferences to narratives: regional preference and semantic structures in Weibo discussions of Beijing’s 5A attractions
title_original: From preferences to narratives: regional preference and semantic structures in Weibo discussions of Beijing’s 5A attractions
summary: Abstract Digital traces from social media increasingly shape how tourist preferences are observed and interpreted, yet attraction-related attention is often treated as a single aggregate indicator, with limited consideration of where this attention comes from and how attractions are discursively framed. Focusing on eight 5A attractions in Beijing, this study uses Sina Weibo posts from 2019 to 2023 to construct a province–attraction–time database and derive two complementary measures: a total preference intensity $$F$$ , capturing emotion-weighted attention, and a preference index $$L$$ , capturing excess or deficit preference relative to an independence benchmark. A lexicon-based sentiment pipeline is used to obtain post-level scores, and temporal patterns are analysed at monthly and seasonal scales. Spatial distributions of $$F$$ and $$L$$ are explored through mapping and clustering, while structural drivers are examined using a gravity-type Poisson model for F and a geographical XGBoost model for $$L$$ interpreted with SHAP values and local importance maps. The results show persistent coastal and Sichuan-centred hotspots of preference, gradual diffusion towards parts of central and south-western China, and mostly positive but event-sensitive sentiment trajectories. Population, income and tourism service supply strongly increase total preference intensity, whereas rich local consumption and accommodation environments are associated with weaker outbound preference; distance exerts only a weak damping effect. Semantic analysis reveals stable clusters of attraction-related discourse and distinct emotional profiles within them. Together, the framework demonstrates how social-media data can be used to characterise uneven regional engagement and divergent semantic constructions of iconic attractions in contemporary China.

title: From Reactivity to Proactivity: The Use of Behavioural Data in Life and Health Insurance
title_original: From Reactivity to Proactivity: The Use of Behavioural Data in Life and Health Insurance
summary: Abstract Traditional life and health insurance compensates after the fact, acting reactively in response to adverse events. Today, the rise of digital technologies enables insurers to intervene proactively, monitoring policyholders’ behaviour and incentivizing lifestyle changes intended to reduce risks before they materialize. This article argues that the shift from reactivity to proactivity marks a profound transformation in the temporal logic and social role of insurance. Based on empirical research, we examine the actuarial, normative, and societal implications of proactivity in life and health insurance. We situate these developments within broader debates on quantification and the quantified self, showing how individual self-tracking practices are embedded into institutional feedback loops that make unprecedented surveillance possible, but also create new forms of personalisation, solidarity, and responsibility. Proactivity, we contend, is not simply prevention by other means, but an innovative reconfiguration of uncertainty management that both disciplines and empowers policyholders through data-driven incentives and recommendations.

title: SILICA FOULING OF ANION-EXCHANGE RESINS IN URANIUM IN-SITU RECOVERY: CURRENT UNDERSTANDING AND REGENERATION APPROACHES
title_original: SILICA FOULING OF ANION-EXCHANGE RESINS IN URANIUM IN-SITU RECOVERY: CURRENT UNDERSTANDING AND REGENERATION APPROACHES
summary: The growing share of in-situ leaching (ISL) in global uranium mining is increasing the demands on the efficiency of ion-exchange processing of pregnant solutions. Strongly basic anion exchange resins that sorb uranyl sulfate or uranyl carbonate complexes are typically used for uranium extraction. Over long periods of operation, their properties deteriorate due to the accumulation of silicon compounds released into the solution during the leaching of silicate rocks. This review examines the mechanisms of silicon fouling of anion exchange resins used in ISL, as well as existing methods for desilication and regeneration. An analysis of scientific publications and technical materials shows that fouling is primarily due to the penetration of silicic acid into the resin pores and its subsequent polymerization. With localized increases in pH, silicate anions can also interact with exchange sites. The formation of oligomeric and polymeric siloxane structures hinders mass transfer, blocks active sites, and reduces the uranium sorption capacity. Alkaline treatment with NaOH and fluoride-containing reagents are used for regeneration. Alkaline solutions are technologically simpler, but less effective against highly polymerized silica phases and, under harsh conditions, can damage the resin. Fluoride systems provide deeper silicon removal but place increased demands on the corrosion resistance of equipment and wastewater treatment. Therefore, the regeneration process must ensure silicon removal without significantly reducing the mechanical strength and sorption properties of the resin.

Strongly basic anion exchange resins that sorb uranyl sulfate or uranyl carbonate complexes are typically used for uranium extraction. Over long periods of operation, their properties deteriorate due to the accumulation of silicon compounds released into the solution during the leaching of silicate rocks. This review examines the mechanisms of silicon fouling of anion exchange resins used in ISL, as well as existing methods for desilication and regeneration. An analysis of scientific publications and technical materials shows that fouling is primarily due to the penetration of silicic acid into the resin pores and its subsequent polymerization. With localized increases in pH, silicate anions can also interact with exchange sites. The formation of oligomeric and polymeric siloxane structures hinders mass transfer, blocks active sites, and reduces the uranium sorption capacity. Alkaline treatment with NaOH and fluoride-containing reagents are used for regeneration. Alkaline solutions are technologically simpler, but less effective against highly polymerized silica phases and, under harsh conditions, can damage the resin. Fluoride systems provide deeper silicon removal but place increased demands on the corrosion resistance of equipment and wastewater treatment. Therefore, the regeneration process must ensure silicon removal without significantly reducing the mechanical strength and sorption properties of the resin.

title: Establishing Netnographic Procedures in Studying Chinese Queer Fandoms: A Critical Reflection
title_original: Establishing Netnographic Procedures in Studying Chinese Queer Fandoms: A Critical Reflection
summary: Online queer fandom is a prevalent and controversial topic that has attracted scholars' attention in recent years across the interdisciplinary fields of media communication, youth communities, and gender expression. Netnography has been widely used in research on online queer fandom and has contributed to a comprehensive understanding of online queer fan cultures. However, the methodological challenges arise when applying netnography to culturally and politically sensitive contexts. Netnography may carry Western-centred assumptions about online visibility, fan identity, and gender expression, and these assumptions may obscure the understanding of the nuances in queer fandom that are shaped by platform censorship, local gender discourse, and fan culture itself. Therefore, a reflexive approach to netnography is needed for studying online queer fandom in nonWestern contexts. Based on previous studies and our own experience of applying netnography in studying Chinese online queer fandom, this study identifies the methodological challenges related to platform governance, coded fan language, internal fan conflicts, and the epistemic authority of scholars. In response to these challenges, we propose four principles for revising netnography: platform literacy, contextual literacy, ethical reflexivity, and discourse-centred, situated interpretation. These principles encourage researchers to approach netnography as a reflexive practice. This study is therefore not only a methodological reflection on the netnographic study of Chinese online queer fandom, but also provides insights for research on other culturally specific, politically sensitive, and platformised digital communities and cultures. Keywords: Netnography, online queer fandom, participatory culture, platform censorship, ethical reflexivity.

title: Atributos que afetam a percepção do cliente na experiência gastronômica em um restaurante à la carte
title_original: Atributos que afetam a percepção do cliente na experiência gastronômica em um restaurante à la carte
summary: A alimentação transcendeu sua função básica de sobrevivência, consolidando-se como um ato de sociabilidade, no qual os restaurantes atuam como ambientes para experiências gastronômicas. Assim sendo, compreender o que mais valoriza e influencia a experiência nesses estabelecimentos torna-se crucial. Nesse sentido, este artigo identificou cinco atributos principais: Ambiente, Atendimento, Cardápio, Comida e Preço, que conectam conceitos do marketing tradicional com o marketing de experiência. A pesquisa, de natureza quantitativa, foi conduzida em um restaurante à la carte na Zona Norte do Rio de Janeiro. Os resultados demonstram que, embora todos os atributos sejam valorizados, o "Atendimento" destaca-se como o mais relevante, enquanto o "Preço" apresenta menor importância relativa. Verificou-se que os atributos subjetivos (Atendimento, Comida e Ambiente), que representam o marketing de experiência, prevaleceram sobre aqueles objetivos (Cardápio e Preço). Adicionalmente, observou-se uma variação na percepção de valor conforme o perfil do consumidor: clientes individuais em dias úteis atribuem menor relevância à experiência, ao passo que casais e grupos, em finais de semana e feriados, consideram a experiência gastronômica como um fator determinante.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Robotics in the Sports Industry: From Qualitative Recommendations to Implementation Gaps
title_original: Artificial Intelligence and Robotics in the Sports Industry: From Qualitative Recommendations to Implementation Gaps
summary: This book review critically examines Ekaterina Glebova's Artificial Intelligence and Robotics in the Sports Industry: Past, Present, and Future (CRC Press, 2026) through the lens of AI implementation management. While the book offers a timely and accessible overview of AI applications across coaching, athlete training, fan engagement, and stadium operations, it suffers from several fundamental limitations that reduce its utility for implementation-focused scholars and practitioners. This review identifies five critical gaps: (1) the absence of a political economy perspective on how AI reinforces existing power asymmetries; (2) neglect of non-elite sports and the digital divide; (3) oversimplification of organizational resistance and human-AI conflict; (4) reliance on non-peer-reviewed sources and lack of empirical evidence; and (5) raising ethical questions without providing actionable answers. The review concludes that the book serves as a valuable starting point for early-stage AI adoption but fails to offer step-by-step implementation frameworks, lessons from failures, or concrete guidance for resource-constrained organizations. For researchers contributing to this special issue on AI implementation, this review highlights critical directions for future inquiry, including maturity models, ROI measurement frameworks, and empirical studies of genuine implementation failures.

title: Beyond Resources? Efficiency and Technology as Explanations for the English Premier League’s Advantage over the Polish Ekstraklasa
title_original: Beyond Resources? Efficiency and Technology as Explanations for the English Premier League’s Advantage over the Polish Ekstraklasa
summary: Badanie porównuje efektywność techniczną i poziom technologiczny profesjonalnych klubów piłkarskich z polskiej Ekstraklasy oraz angielskiej Premier League w sezonach 2021–2023. Wykorzystując model oparty na Slack-Based Model w ramach meta-frontier Data Envelopment Analysis, oceniono dwa rezultaty – wyniki sportowe (ranking Elo) oraz wyniki finansowe (łączny przychód) – w odniesieniu do dwóch nakładów: wydatków na wynagrodzenia zawodników (lub, w alternatywnym modelu, wartości rynkowej kadry) oraz historycznej pozycji w lidze. Wyniki wskazują, że obie ligi charakteryzują się podobną średnią efektywnością techniczną (≈0,8) i funkcjonują na tej samej granicy technologicznej. Różnice w wynikach między ligami wynikają zatem przede wszystkim z różnic w zasobach, a nie z technologicznej lub menedżerskiej niewydolności. Analiza benchmarkingowa wskazuje Brentford jako klub o najbardziej konsekwentnie utrzymywanej efektywności, natomiast Everton, Aston Villa, Śląsk Wrocław i Zagłębie Lubin wykazują utrzymującą się nieskuteczność.

title: WIPO Intellectual Property Standards for Ukraine’s Sustainable Development and European Integration
title_original: WIPO Intellectual Property Standards for Ukraine’s Sustainable Development and European Integration
summary: This study evaluates the international legal standards of the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) as a pivotal framework for advancing Ukraine’s legal and technological infrastructure within the intellectual property area. The methodological basis of the research is a combination of general and specialized methods of scientific inquiry: logical and semantic, historical, structural and functional analysis, grouping, documentary analysis, analytical, modelling, forecasting. The expediency of centralized regulation of the intellectual sphere was retrospectively justified. The meaning of the concepts of intellectual property, IP law, personal property and non-property rights were analyzed. The list of current international treaties on intellectual property administered by the World Intellectual Property Organization, to which Ukraine is a party, was composed. The WIPO agreements (the Patent Cooperation Treaty, the Madrid Agreement, and its Protocol), which facilitate obtaining legal protection for relevant intellectual property objects in foreign countries by Ukrainian inventors were studied. The content of treaties concluded between WIPO and relevant Ukrainian authority was revealed. The measures taken by WIPO along with the Member States aimed at isolating the Russian Federation within the Organization to prevent it from abusing intellectual property mechanisms were highlighted. In the conclusion, the strategic achievements of the cooperation between our country and WIPO were presented, as well as the issues requiring further resolution were identified. Keywords: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), intellectual property, intellectual property rights and interests, UKRNOIVI (IP Office), international treaties, sustainable development.

title: Carnaval de rua na região portuária do Rio de Janeiro: quem pode “virar o mundo” e onde? Uma abordagem crítica do fenômeno festivo no contexto da cidade neoliberal
title_original: Carnaval de rua na região portuária do Rio de Janeiro: quem pode “virar o mundo” e onde? Uma abordagem crítica do fenômeno festivo no contexto da cidade neoliberal
summary: Este artigo tem por objetivo analisar o paradoxo inerente à ocupação festiva de determinados espaços urbanos por grupos sociais privilegiados. Embora o fenômeno festivo seja comumente associado à alegria e à transgressão, sua análise não pode ser dissociada dos contextos sociais e espaciais nos quais se insere. O exemplo do Carnaval de rua na região portuária do Rio de Janeiro evidencia como a festa pode ser instrumentalizada para distinguir simbolicamente o território e atender aos objetivos de gentrificação da operação urbana Porto Maravilha. Assim, propõe-se uma abordagem crítica do fenômeno festivo no contexto urbano contemporâneo, ao considerar a festa na cidade como um espaço-tempo imerso nas lógicas de produção neoliberal do espaço.

title: The Connection Between Emotional Intelligence, the Level of Loneliness and Characteristics of Attitudes towards Parents in Adolescence
title_original: The Connection Between Emotional Intelligence, the Level of Loneliness and Characteristics of Attitudes towards Parents in Adolescence
summary: <p style="text-align: justify;">This article examines the connections between emotional intelligence, the level of loneliness and the characteristics of adolescents&rsquo; relationships with their parents. Adolescence is characterized by significant emotional changes that affect adolescents&rsquo; social relationships and self-esteem. The study is based on theoretical concepts of emotional intelligence, the phenomenon of loneliness and child-parent relationships, developed by both domestic and foreign psychologists. In the empirical part of the work, methods of psychodiagnostic research and correlation analysis were used to identify relationships between the parameters under study. The study involved 76 people aged 12 to 16 years. The results show that high levels of emotional intelligence in adolescents are associated with low levels of loneliness and positive relationships with parents. There is also a positive correlation between subjective feelings of loneliness and the hostility of both parents, and a negative correlation between subjective feelings of loneliness in adolescence and parents&rsquo; positive interest in their children.</p>

title: Psychological Mechanisms of Youth Involvement in Extremist and Terrorist Organizations (Using the Example of Social Networks)
title_original: Psychological Mechanisms of Youth Involvement in Extremist and Terrorist Organizations (Using the Example of Social Networks)
summary: <p style="text-align: justify;">The work describes the signs of recruitment and the psychological mechanisms of youth involvement in extremist and terrorist organizations in the Internet. A structural analysis of materials containing communication aimed at involving youth in extremist or terrorist organizations and/or communities with extremist goals. The object of the study are cases received for a comprehensive psychological and linguistic study at the Moscow State Budgetary Institution &ldquo;Moscow Research Center&rdquo;. The purpose of the work was to describe the signs of recruitment and the basic psychological mechanisms of youth involvement in extremist and terrorist organizations in the Internet. The basis for the methodological substantiation of the identified psychological mechanisms of involvement were the ideas of A.A. Leontiev on the concept of communication; scientific ideas of G.M. Andreeva about social communication. Using the intent analysis method, the psychological mechanisms of youth involvement in the Internet were identified, which are based on the impact on the motivational-need and value spheres of the individual. The described mechanisms allow us to deepen our understanding of the involvement of young people in extremist and terrorist communities.</p>

title: The Effects of Emotional Schema Therapy and Differentiation Training on Emotional Divorce in Women
title_original: The Effects of Emotional Schema Therapy and Differentiation Training on Emotional Divorce in Women
summary: Background: Emotional Divorce (ED) is associated with decreased levels of Emotion Regulation (ER), adaptation, and mental health; subsequently, all such pressures raise stress in various dimensions among the affected individuals. Emotional Schema Therapy (EST), as a socio-cognitive model of ER, may improve marital intimacy and reduce couples’ psychological distress. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of EST and differentiation training on the odds of ED among women. Methods: The mean values of ED significantly decreased in both experimental groups, compared to the control group (P<0.05). A significant difference was also observed between the effects of the two interventions on decreasing the ED rate; thus, the effectiveness of EST was greater than that of differentiation training in this respect (P<0.05).  Results: The mean values of ED significantly decreased in both experimental groups, compared to the control group (P<0.05). A significant difference was also observed between the effects of the two interventions on decreasing the ED rate; thus, the effectiveness of EST was greater than that of differentiation training in this respect (P<0.05). Conclusion: EST and differentiation training reduced ED among the study participants. These approaches can be adopted as an effective intervention to solve the couples’ problems and improve their marital relationship to reduce the odds of emotional divorce.

title: Comparing of the Effects of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and Emotion Regulation Training on Diabetes Empowerment
title_original: Comparing of the Effects of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and Emotion Regulation Training on Diabetes Empowerment
summary: Background: Diabetes mellitus is a widely diffused chronic condition that affects several aspects of patients’ lives. The patient’s life in this condition depends on diabetes management ability. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the effects of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and Emotion Regulation Training (ERT) on the diabetes empowerment of patients with type 2 diabetes.  Methods: This was a quasi-experimental study with a pre-test, post-test-follow-up and a control group design. Of the statistical population of patients referring to the Diabetes Prevention and Control Center of Mashhad Province, Iran, 45 subjects were recruited by convenience sampling method; they were randomly assigned into three groups of ACT, ERT, and control (n=15/group). The study subjects were assessed using the Diabetes Empowerment Scale (F-DES-28) in the pre-test stage, after the intervention, and 3 months later. The obtained data were analyzed by repeated-measures Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) in SPSS V. 22. Results: Both provided interventions presented a significant effect on the empowerment of the research subjects, compared to the controls (P<0.001). The effectiveness of ACT on the diabetes empowerment of patients was significantly higher than that of the ERT group (P=0.04).  Conclusion: It is recommended to use ACT and ERT to empower patients with type 2 diabetes.

title: The Relationship Between Perfectionism, Early Maladaptive Schemas, Attachment Styles, and Body Image Concern by the Mediating Role of Self-esteem in Cosmetic Surgery Applicants
title_original: The Relationship Between Perfectionism, Early Maladaptive Schemas, Attachment Styles, and Body Image Concern by the Mediating Role of Self-esteem in Cosmetic Surgery Applicants
summary: Background: Psychological characteristics could significantly impact applications for cosmetic surgery as well as precognition and satisfaction with surgery. The present study aimed to investigate the relationship between perfectionism, early maladaptive schemas, attachment styles, and body image concern by the mediating role of self-esteem in cosmetic surgery applicants. Methods: This was a predictive correlational study. The statistical population of the study included all female applicants for cosmetic surgery referring to cosmetic surgery centers in Tehran City, Iran, in 2020. A sample size of 400 women was selected based on Klein’s model (2016). The required data were collected by Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES) (1989), Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale (MPS), Young Schema Questionnaire (YSQ-S3), Adult Attachment Scale (AAS), and Body Image Concern Inventory (BICI), and analyzed using Pearson correlation coefficient and structural equations in SPSS and AMOS. Results: The obtained results signified a significant relationship between perfectionism, early maladaptive schemas, attachment styles, self-esteem, and body image concerns (P<0.01). Furthermore, the modified model presented a good fit (The Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA) =0.061, GFI=0.989, IFI=0.987, P<0.05); the indirect paths of perfectionism, early maladaptive schema, and attachment styles through self-esteem were also significant. Conclusion: The evaluated model indicated a good fit; thus, it can play an essential role in recognizing the factors affecting the body image concerns of female cosmetic surgery applicants.

title: Effects of Integrative Behavioral Couple Therapy on Infertility Self-efficacy, Dyadic Adjustment, and Sexual Satisfaction in Infertile Couples
title_original: Effects of Integrative Behavioral Couple Therapy on Infertility Self-efficacy, Dyadic Adjustment, and Sexual Satisfaction in Infertile Couples
summary: Background: Given the rising rate of infertility, the prevalence of mental health disorders in infertile couples is undeniable. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of Integrative Behavioral Couple Therapy (IBCT) on infertility self-efficacy, dyadic adjustment, and sexual satisfaction in infertile couples.  Methods: The present single-case experimental study used a multiple-baseline design. The statistical population of the study included all infertile couples referring to infertility centers in Ahvaz City, Iran, in 2019. The research instruments included the Infertility Self-Efficacy Scale (ISE), the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (DAS), and the Sexual Satisfaction Questionnaire (SSQ). Following a diagnostic interview, 3 couples were selected using the convenience sampling technique. Integrative behavioral couple therapy was conducted in twelve 120-minute sessions for the intervention group. The second couple entered the study in the second session of the first couple; the third couple enrolled the treatment plan in the third session of the first couple and the second session of the second couple. All questionnaires were completed in the first, third, sixth, eighth, and tenth sessions; the study participants were followed up and re-assessed two months later. The collected data were analyzed in SPSS using chart analysis, reliable change index, and significance statistics. Results: The provided IBCT increased infertility self-efficacy (39.04%), dyadic adjustment (25.91%), and sexual satisfaction (55.01%) in infertile couples. Besides, the improvement lasted throughout the follow-up which indicated the effectiveness of IBCT on infertility self-efficiency, dyadic adjustment, and sexual satisfaction in the study subjects. Conclusion: IBCT can be effective in improving personal and marital variables in infertile couples with infertility problems in addition to their marital problems.

title: Bisiklet Sporcularının Tutku ve Bağımlılık Düzeylerinin Kano Modeli Kullanılarak İncelenmesi
title_original: Bisiklet Sporcularının Tutku ve Bağımlılık Düzeylerinin Kano Modeli Kullanılarak İncelenmesi
summary: Alan yazında tutku ve bağımlılığın, özellikle uzun vadeli spora katılımı nasıl etkileyebileceği konusunda az sayıda çalışma bulunmakta ve bu araştırmaların da büyük ölçüde Likert türü ölçüme dayandığı görülmektedir. Bu sebeple bu çalışmanın amacı, bisiklet sporcularının tutku ve bağımlılık düzeylerini araştırmak için farklı bir metodolojik yaklaşım olan Kano modelini kullanmaktır. Kano modeli, bir faaliyetin varlığında veya yokluğunda sporcuların tutum ve davranışlarını nasıl etkilediğini daha iyi anlamamıza yardımcı olabilir. Bunu yaparken de; Likert ölçeklerindeki “kesinlikle katılmıyorum”dan “kesinlikle katılıyorum”a kadar olan tek bir ifadenin açıklanması yerine, işlevsel ve işlevsiz ifadelerle daha derinlemesine bir incelemeye olanak tanır. Araştırma GranFondo Bisiklet etkinliğine katılan, kolayda örnekleme yoluyla seçilmiş, 18 yaşından büyük, çalışmaya gönüllü olarak iştirak etmeyi kabul etmiş 403 bisiklet sporcusu üzerinde gerçekleştirilmiştir. Katılımcılara e-posta ile ulaşılmış ve tutku ile bağımlılığa ilişkin 17 işlevsel-17 işlevsiz anket sorusu yöneltilmiştir. Bulgular tutkunun, ağırlıklı olarak çekici/heyecan verici, beklenen ve kayıtsızlık kategorilerinde; bağımlılığın ise çekici/heyecan verici, beklenen, kayıtsızlık ve zıt/ters kategorilerinde sınıflandığını göstermiştir. Sonuç olarak bu çalışma, bisiklet sporcularının tutku ve bağımlılık düzeylerinin geleneksel Likert türü ölçekler yerine Kano modeli ile incelendiği farklı bir yaklaşım sunarak alana katkı yapmaktadır. Sonuçlar, sporcuların tutku ve bağımlılık düzeylerini, işlevsel ve işlevsiz sorularla daha derinlemesine anlamamıza ve sonuçları incelememize imkan sağlamaktadır. Araştırma, tutku ve bağımlılığın etkilerini, Kano yöntemi kullanılmadan açıklanamayan farklı sonuçlar verdiği için sporcularla ilgili önceki araştırmaları güçlendirebilir. Antrenörlerin ve sporcuların bir faaliyetin varlığının veya yokluğunun sporcu tutumlarını ve dolayısıyla davranışlarını nasıl etkilediğini daha iyi anlamalarına da yardımcı olabilir.

title: Dynamics of the Competitiveness of Russian Male and Female Pole Vaulters During the 2020–2024 Olympic Cycle
title_original: Dynamics of the Competitiveness of Russian Male and Female Pole Vaulters During the 2020–2024 Olympic Cycle
summary: The level of competitiveness in pole vaulting reflects not only athletic performance but also the effectiveness of athlete development within the discipline. This study examines changes in the competitive dynamics of Russian male and female pole vaulters during the 2020–2024 Olympic cycle and identifies factors associated with these changes. The analysis was based on official results from the Russian Indoor and Outdoor Athletics Championships. Competitive dynamics were assessed using a combination of literature review, comparative analysis of competition results, calculation of competitiveness coefficients, statistical analysis, and expert consultations with experienced pole vault specialists. The results indicate a gradual decline in competitiveness in the women’s event, accompanied by lower performance density and a widening gap between leading athletes and the remainder of the field. In contrast, the men’s event demonstrated relatively stable competitive characteristics throughout the study period. These findings provide an empirical assessment of the current state of the discipline and may contribute to improving long-term athlete development, optimizing competition planning, and monitoring the effectiveness of pole vault development programmes.

title: МІЖДИСЦИПЛІНАРНІ ЗВ’ЯЗКИ У ФОРМУВАННІ КУЛЬТУРИ ЗДОРОВ’Я: ІНТЕГРАЦІЯ ФІЗИЧНОЇ КУЛЬТУРИ, РАЦІОНАЛЬНОГО ХАРЧУВАННЯ ТА ФІЛОСОФІЇ ВЕЛНЕСУ
title_original: МІЖДИСЦИПЛІНАРНІ ЗВ’ЯЗКИ У ФОРМУВАННІ КУЛЬТУРИ ЗДОРОВ’Я: ІНТЕГРАЦІЯ ФІЗИЧНОЇ КУЛЬТУРИ, РАЦІОНАЛЬНОГО ХАРЧУВАННЯ ТА ФІЛОСОФІЇ ВЕЛНЕСУ
summary: The article provides a scientific substantiation of the feasibility and efficacy of integrating interdisciplinary links between physical culture and nutrition science as a strategic factor in optimizing, maintaining, and restoring human health. The relevance of the study is driven by declining health indicators, as well as the prevalence of hypokinesia and diet-related diseases. The study aims to substantiate the interdisciplinary connections between physical culture and nutrition science as a factor in optimizing human health, and to integrate nutritional knowledge into the practice of fitness trainers. The following research methods were employed in the study methodology: theoretical analysis and synthesis of data from specialized scientific and methodical literature, as well as Internet resources. Results: The research findings demonstrate that the isolated application of individual academic disciplines fails to provide a holistic approach to human health management and does not ensure the maximum health-improving effect. The study substantiates a synergistic effect (mutually reinforcing action), wherein rational nutrition provides the energetic and plastic basis for physical activity, while physical activity acts as a powerful stimulant for metabolism and nutrient absorption. Furthermore, the mechanisms of mutual influence between physical activity and nutritional status are revealed at the levels of cellular metabolism, as well as the cardiovascular and endocrine systems. As a result of the study, a curriculum for the academic discipline "Fundamentals of Nutrition" was developed. In the process of studying this discipline, the learner will acquire the competence to: provide nutritional support to fitness club clients; offer advisory support to clients with excess or deficient body weight; develop personalized meal plans aimed at optimizing caloric intake and improving dietary habits; provide tailored recommendations to mitigate the negative impact of dietary habits on health status. Conclusions: The implementation of an interdisciplinary approach in the educational process of specialists in the field of physical culture is a fundamental prerequisite for optimizing human health. The materials presented in this article can be utilized to develop personalized wellness programs.

The study substantiates a synergistic effect (mutually reinforcing action), wherein rational nutrition provides the energetic and plastic basis for physical activity, while physical activity acts as a powerful stimulant for metabolism and nutrient absorption. Furthermore, the mechanisms of mutual influence between physical activity and nutritional status are revealed at the levels of cellular metabolism, as well as the cardiovascular and endocrine systems. As a result of the study, a curriculum for the academic discipline "Fundamentals of Nutrition" was developed. In the process of studying this discipline, the learner will acquire the competence to: provide nutritional support to fitness club clients; offer advisory support to clients with excess or deficient body weight; develop personalized meal plans aimed at optimizing caloric intake and improving dietary habits; provide tailored recommendations to mitigate the negative impact of dietary habits on health status. Conclusions: The implementation of an interdisciplinary approach in the educational process of specialists in the field of physical culture is a fundamental prerequisite for optimizing human health. The materials presented in this article can be utilized to develop personalized wellness programs.

title: From “Growth” to “Healing”
title_original: From “Growth” to “Healing”
summary: In 2026, Mango TV aired the fifth season of Dad in Charge under the theme “Dad in Charge: Give Yourself a Hug.” While continuing the narrative of men’s growth through childrearing, the season shifts the focus of emotional communication from validating fathers’ parenting competence toward accepting parental exhaustion and imperfection, marking a turn from a growth narrative to a healing narrative. Taking the documentary footage, observation-studio segments, and danmu comments concerning the season’s four families as its objects of analysis, this study examines the narrative configuration and communication mechanisms underlying this shift. It finds that, through differentiated family samples—dual-income households, a large extended family, and a cross-cultural sojourning family—the program offers viewers four affective positions: guilt, uplift, clumsiness, and ease. Through affective triggering in the documentary footage, mirroring guidance in the observation studio, and social diffusion via danmu comments, the program completes a communication chain that runs from individual emotion to public discussion. The healing turn responds to the emotional needs of childbearing-age families in a low-fertility context and performs a function of sociocultural mediation; media consolation, however, cannot substitute for resolving structural difficulties in childrearing, and the healing narrative also risks the superficialization of emotion.

title: Greco-Roman Wrestling and the Chronology of Physical Culture: Ethnocultural Traditions, Historical Continuity, and Pedagogical Perspectives
title_original: Greco-Roman Wrestling and the Chronology of Physical Culture: Ethnocultural Traditions, Historical Continuity, and Pedagogical Perspectives
summary: Physical culture, as a subcomponent of general culture, reflects the set of constructive manifestations of the human factor in the field of movement, integrating the progress of science, technology, art and medicine (Platonov, Vl., 2006). Within this theoretical framework, the present study aims to show the historical continuity and practical evolution of Greco-Roman wrestling as a specific expression of physical culture, analyzing the connections between socio-cultural development, advances in biomotor sciences and transformations of modern pedagogical paradigms. The paper offers an analytical approach that goes beyond general terminological observations, bringing the following contributions: 1) identifying the historical and socio-cultural stages that shaped the forms and functions of Greco-Roman wrestling; 2) integrating empirical evidence from biomotricity to explain the technical-tactical adaptations and physiological requirements of athletes; 3) formulating contemporary pedagogical directions for optimizing the technical-tactical and physical preparation process within combat training. Thus, the paper argues for the continuity of a specific sports tradition within the broader framework of physical culture and proposes practical and theoretical frameworks for integrating historical knowledge into the design of training and sports education programs.

title: The Ubiquitous Role of the Smartphone in Breaking: An Ethnographic-Informed Study
title_original: The Ubiquitous Role of the Smartphone in Breaking: An Ethnographic-Informed Study
summary: Breaking is a physically demanding street dance, which is highly creative and historically rooted in urban culture. Studies about Breaking are scant, and the role of technology in the modality, e.g., smartphones, while potentially relevant according to a previous technology review, is still unknown. This study is a first step into understanding the role of technology in Breaking. Drawing on observations of 35 training sessions and 15 interviews with Non-Professional to Olympic-level Breakers, we found that smartphones act as digital scaffolds for Breaking. Smartphone use supports training structure, movement arsenal management, performance improvement and creativity, and peer feedback and community engagement. Our contribution is two-fold: we first contribute a detailed understanding of how smartphones mediate Breaking, a form of appropriating the smartphone which has not been previously described; then, we outline design opportunities for future systems aimed at Breaking and other modalities, which are non-hierarchical, heavily rooted in culture, and turn to peer-to-peer expertise exchange to develop complex physical practices.

title: ОБҐРУНТУВАННЯ ЗМІСТУ СПОРТИВНОЇ ПІДГОТОВКИ ПЛАВЦІВ РІЗНОЇ КВАЛІФІКАЦІЇ
title_original: ОБҐРУНТУВАННЯ ЗМІСТУ СПОРТИВНОЇ ПІДГОТОВКИ ПЛАВЦІВ РІЗНОЇ КВАЛІФІКАЦІЇ
summary: The article substantiates the content of sports training for swimmers of different qualifications, taking into account the ratio of its main components, the volume of training load, and the orientation of training sessions. The relevance of the study lies in the fact that athletes at different levels of sports mastery may train within the same educational and training group. They have a common training structure but require different training content according to their qualifications. The aim of the study is to determine the features of the ratio and content of the main components of sports training for swimmers of different qualifications. The study used analysis and generalization of scientific and methodological literature, analysis of regulatory and program documents on swimming, pedagogical observation, comparative analysis, and methods of mathematical statistics. The training activity of 22 male and female athletes of different sports qualifications was analyzed: Second Adult Category, First Adult Category, Candidate for Master of Sports, and Master of Sports of Ukraine. It was found that with the growth of qualification, the weekly and annual volume of training load increases: from 18 hours per week and 936 hours per year among swimmers of the Second Adult Category to 24 hours per week and 1248 hours per year among Candidates for Master of Sports and Masters of Sports of Ukraine. The model distribution of training components showed that swimmers of lower qualification have a larger share of technical training, whereas Candidates for the Master of Sports and Master of Sports of Ukraine show an increased importance of physical, tactical, and psychological components. The analysis of the microcycle revealed differences in training session duration, total workload, and the main orientation of training. It was determined that differentiation of the training load should be reflected not only in an increase in the amount of work but also in changes in the content and orientation of training sessions according to the athletes’ qualification level. The data obtained confirm the need to differentiate the content of sports training for swimmers by qualification level.

title: Perceived Myths and Truths About Women's Participation in Sports and Their Effects on Participation Levels in Sierra Leone
title_original: Perceived Myths and Truths About Women's Participation in Sports and Their Effects on Participation Levels in Sierra Leone
summary: Background: Perceived myths about women's participation in sports remain a significant barrier to gender equity in athletic engagement, particularly in sub-Saharan African contexts. This study investigated the perceived myths and truths about women's participation in sports and assessed their effects on participation levels in Bo and Kenema cities, Sierra Leone. Methods: A descriptive survey research design with mixed-methods approach was adopted. A total sample of 350 respondents was drawn using simple random sampling from female athletes (n = 280), coaches (n = 50), and parents (n = 20) in Bo and Kenema cities. Structured questionnaires and semi-structured interview guides were used for data collection. Quantitative data were analysed using SPSS version 26, employing descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages) and inferential statistics including one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Pearson's product-moment correlation coefficient. Qualitative data were analysed using Thematic Content Analysis. Instrument reliability was established at Pearson's r = 0.82 (test-retest) and Cronbach's α = 0.79. Results: Findings revealed that 88.2% (n = 149) of athlete respondents confirmed the existence of perceived myths about women in sports. The most prevalent myths included the belief that sports cause barrenness (18.6%), loss of femininity/masculinization (17.1%), disruption of the menstrual cycle (17.1%), and loss of virginity (11.4%). One-way ANOVA revealed a significant difference in myth belief across age groups [F(3, 165) = 8.461, p < 0.001], with younger athletes (10-26 years) exhibiting higher myth adherence (92.0%-94.5%) compared to older athletes (26-34 years: 78.6%; 34-42 years: 25.0%). A significant positive correlation was found between myth belief and reduced participation levels (r = 0.226, t = 2.945, p < 0.01). Gender-based discrimination was experienced by 81.7% of respondents. Cultural norms were identified as playing a major role in perpetuating myths by 55.0% of respondents, with cultural norms significantly correlated with media coverage perceptions (r = 0.364, t = 5.051, p < 0.001). Conclusion: Perceived myths significantly hinder women's sports participation in Bo and Kenema cities through reinforcement of gender stereotypes, social stigma, and reduced institutional support. Evidence-based myth-busting campaigns, female role model visibility, and gender-sensitive sports policies are urgently needed to improve participation levels.

title: Women's participation in the Paralympic Games (1960–2024): a longitudinal and bibliometric analysis of global trends and scientific production
title_original: Women's participation in the Paralympic Games (1960–2024): a longitudinal and bibliometric analysis of global trends and scientific production
summary: Background Women's participation in the Paralympic Games has expanded over time, yet this growth has been non-linear and uneven across regions, disciplines, and editions. At the same time, scientific research on women in Paralympic and parasports contexts remains limited and geographically concentrated. Studies that provide a comprehensive, long-term, sex-disaggregated reconstruction of participation across both Summer and Winter editions, together with an examination of its relationship to the geography of scientific production, are scarce. Methods This study reconstructs sex-disaggregated participation in the Summer Paralympic Games (1960–2024) and Winter Paralympic Games (1976–2022) using official data provided by the International Paralympic Committee (IPC), harmonized with National Paralympic Committee data. Longitudinal trends and cross-national patterns are examined through descriptive and comparative analyses. Exploratory non-parametric analyses were used to assess longitudinal trends and macro-regional differences in demographic-normalized participation. As a complementary component, a systematic search of the Web of Science Core Collection (completed 31 October 2025) identified 71 relevant publications, which were analyzed using bibliometric techniques. Results Women's participation in the Summer Paralympics follows a non-linear trajectory, reaching near parity at Paris 2024 (44.4%), whereas participation in the Winter Games remains consistently lower, with only modest long-term growth and no comparable movement toward parity (18%–25%). Two study-specific descriptive indicators, i.e., the Weighted Equity Index and the Normalized Female Participation Index, were used to summarize cross-national differences in internal delegation balance and demographic-normalized participation intensity. The bibliometric analysis documents a small but expanding body of literature that is geographically concentrated. Conclusion These findings suggest a persistent misalignment between the increasing presence of women in the Paralympic Games and the comparatively limited and uneven development of scientific research on this population. The study provides a comprehensive longitudinal mapping of women's participation and offers an empirical basis for future research and policy aimed at improving equity in Paralympic sports.

title: More than movement: a conceptual exploration of the convergence of social-emotional learning and physical literacy
title_original: More than movement: a conceptual exploration of the convergence of social-emotional learning and physical literacy
summary: This paper develops an integrative framework for bringing social-emotional learning (SEL) and physical literacy (PL) into closer conceptual and pedagogical alignment. Rather than treating SEL and PL as separate domains, the paper positions them as mutually reinforcing lenses for understanding how movement experiences can support holistic development across health and physical education, community sport and recreation, outdoor and play-based settings, and lifespan physical activity contexts. Ecological systems theory provides the primary architecture, while socio-constructivist, self-determination, ecological dynamics, and meaningful physical education perspectives explain how embodied learning, motivation, agency, belonging, and adaptive movement competence are cultivated through meaningful activity. Within this integrated view, movement is not limited to fitness, performance, or skill acquisition; it is a relational and culturally situated site through which learners develop empathy, resilience, ethical awareness, confidence, competence, motivation, and understanding. International policy frameworks, including UNESCO's Quality Physical Education guidelines, the OECD's Learning Compass 2,030, and the WHO's Global Action Plan on Physical Activity, further underscore the need for approaches that respond to persistent physical inactivity, widening inequities, and growing concerns about young people's mental health and wellbeing. The framework translates these priorities into design principles that emphasize autonomy, competence, relatedness, equity, cultural relevance, and meaningful engagement. In doing so, the paper proposes SEL–PL integration as an evaluative and conceptual direction for health and physical education and related movement contexts, suggesting that meaningful movement may contribute to identity formation, flourishing, lifelong participation, and more just conditions for wellbeing.

summary: Abstract Gunnar Björnsson, Meghan Griffith, Robyn Waller, and Robert Wallace have addressed aspects of the revisionary account of free will I offer in the second edition of Four Views on Free Will . This is a reply to their comments, focusing on, among other things, basic desert, alternative conceptions of free will, and how to understand what consensus and dissensus remain in theoretical approaches to free will.

title: Unpacking EFL Learner Well-Being in the Chinese Context: A Person-Centered Perspective
title_original: Unpacking EFL Learner Well-Being in the Chinese Context: A Person-Centered Perspective
summary: Language learners’ well-being is crucial for promoting their learning achievement and supporting holistic psychological development. However, the overall level and specific manifestations of well-being among English as a foreign language (EFL) learners remain insufficiently examined. Further, prior research mainly adopted a variable-centered approach to investigate well-being, overlooking the potential individual differences in learners’ experiences. To address these gaps, this study adopted a person-centered perspective and employed latent profile analysis (LPA) combined with follow-up interviews to examine the well-being of 3,995 EFL learners from 16 Chinese universities. The results demonstrated four dimensions of well-being among Chinese EFL learners, namely emotional, cognitive, social, and cultural well-being, with overall levels rated as moderate to high. LPA revealed three distinct profiles of well-being among the learners, which were labeled as the moderate well-being group , the moderately high well-being group , and the high well-being group. Semi-structured interviews indicated that well-being in the three profiles was characterized by external dependence, performance focus, and meaning integration. These findings highlight pronounced heterogeneity in EFL learner well-being, emphasizing the need for differentiated pedagogical approaches to support diverse learner needs.

title: The ımpact of visual attention and visual memory exercises on athletes’ ımagery skills
title_original: The ımpact of visual attention and visual memory exercises on athletes’ ımagery skills
summary: Background and Study Aim. Imagery has increasingly gained attention as a mental training technique in the field of sport psychology. Many Olympic and elite athletes effectively employ imagery training to enhance their performance. Although a substantial body of research has demonstrated the positive effects of imagery training on athletic performance, further research is still needed to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of these interventions. In this context, the present study aims to examine the effects of visual attention and visual memory exercises on athletes’ imagery abilities. Method: A total of 30 athletes participated in this study; 15 were assigned to the experimental group and 15 to the control group. The participants were selected from university team athletes competing in basketball, football, and volleyball. The study was conducted using a quasi-experimental design within the framework of quantitative research methods. Data were collected using the Movement Imagery Questionnaire, the d2 Test of Attention, and the n-back test. A repeated measures ANOVA was conducted to examine time-dependent changes between the experimental and control groups. Results: The findings indicate that the six-week visual attention and visual memory training program did not have a significant effect on athletes’ visual attention skills; however, it led to improvements in their visual memory abilities. Furthermore, analyses conducted in the second phase of the study revealed that, in line with improvements in visual memory, athletes also demonstrated enhanced imagery abilities. Conclusion: The results suggest that the implemented visual memory exercises significantly improved athletes’ visual memory performance, and that this improvement was associated with notable enhancements in both kinesthetic and visual imagery abilities. In contrast, the visual attention exercises did not produce a statistically significant effect on attention performance. Overall, visual memory appears to play a central role in the cognitive foundations of imagery ability.

title: Acting and neuroscience: A systematic review of the relationship between theory and experiment
title_original: Acting and neuroscience: A systematic review of the relationship between theory and experiment
summary: This study is significant in examining the extent to which theoretical explanations of the cognitive and neuroscientific foundations of acting are connected to empirically measurable evidence. The study aims to systematically examine the relationship between theoretical and empirical works, to identify the points of convergence and divergence between these two orientations, and to reveal how knowledge concerning the neural foundations of acting is produced. A systematic review design was adopted in the study. The body of the review consists of academic publications related to acting, stage performance, character portrayal, and actor training. Academic sources published between 1984 and 2026, identified through searches conducted in the ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed databases as well as Google Scholar, were taken into consideration. A total of 295 distinct studies were identified, of which 84 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the analysis. These academic sources were coded as theoretical/non-empirical and empirical/measurement-based, and were compared in terms of shared concepts, findings, points of divergence, and modes of knowledge production. The findings showed that of the 84 units of analysis included in this review, 58 (69%) consisted of theoretical/non-empirical sources and 26 (31%) consisted of experimental/measurement-based sources; this distribution should be evaluated not as a universal bibliometric ratio for the field, but as the source structure that emerged within the selection and coding criteria of this review. The two research orientations converge particularly on the topics of embodied cognition, improvisation and executive functions, and the bodily production of emotion. However, many historical acting techniques that are frequently addressed at the theoretical level do not have a direct empirical correspondence. The findings indicate that the relationship between theory and experiment remains partial and selective. abstract: This study is significant in examining the extent to which theoretical explanations of the cognitive and neuroscientific foundations of acting are connected to empirically measurable evidence. The study aims to systematically examine the relationship between theoretical and empirical works, to identify the points of convergence and divergence between these two orientations, and to reveal how knowledge concerning the neural foundations of acting is produced. A systematic review design was adopted in the study. The body of the review consists of academic publications related to acting, stage performance, character portrayal, and actor training. Academic sources published between 1984 and 2026, identified through searches conducted in the ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed databases as well as Google Scholar, were taken into consideration. A total of 295 distinct studies were identified, of which 84 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the analysis. These academic sources were coded as theoretical/non-empirical and empirical/measurement-based, and were compared in terms of shared concepts, findings, points of divergence, and modes of knowledge production. The findings showed that of the 84 units of analysis included in this review, 58 (69%) consisted of theoretical/non-empirical sources and 26 (31%) consisted of experimental/measurement-based sources; this distribution should be evaluated not as a universal bibliometric ratio for the field, but as the source structure that emerged within the selection and coding criteria of this review. The two research orientations converge particularly on the topics of embodied cognition, improvisation and executive functions, and the bodily production of emotion. However, many historical acting techniques that are frequently addressed at the theoretical level do not have a direct empirical correspondence. The findings indicate that the relationship between theory and experiment remains partial and selective. It is recommended that future research prioritize the empirical testing of acting techniques that are prominent at the theoretical level, increase the number of studies involving professional actors, and strengthen collaboration between actor training institutions and neuroscience laboratories.

title: The insurance of climate-related physical risks: challenges and opportunities for actuaries
title_original: The insurance of climate-related physical risks: challenges and opportunities for actuaries
summary: Abstract We examine the key challenges associated with insuring climate-related risks in the context of a changing climate. Adopting a balance-sheet perspective on insurance company management, we analyze the concept of insurability and how it may be reshaped by climate change. Focussing on non-life perils, we further explore the roles of regulation, risk prevention and mitigation in addressing these issues, and discuss a range of potential solutions – and limitations – that emerge. These challenges also open up interesting opportunities for both academic research and practical innovation within the insurance industry.
