title: Environmental Fate and Biological Effects of Radium-226 in Freshwater Environments: Evidence from Fingernail Clams (Sphaeriidae)
title_original: Environmental Fate and Biological Effects of Radium-226 in Freshwater Environments: Evidence from Fingernail Clams (Sphaeriidae)
summary: Radium-226 (²²⁶Ra) is a naturally occurring radionuclide that is typically present at low concentrations in freshwater environments but can be elevated by industrial activities that disturb or concentrate naturally occurring radioactive materials, including mining, oil and gas extraction, coal production, and wastewater treatment. Despite concerns regarding its mobility, bioaccumulation potential, and radiotoxicity, the ecological effects of ²²⁶Ra remain poorly understood. This knowledge gap has contributed to the absence of a Canadian freshwater quality guideline for the protection of aquatic life. This thesis investigated the occurrence, environmental fate, bioaccumulation and toxicity of 226Ra to a sensitive freshwater species of fingernail clams (Sphaerium striatinum), with a particular focus on the influence of calcium on its behaviour and toxicity. As alkaline earth metals with similar physicochemical properties, calcium and radium are expected to exhibit comparable environmental and biological behaviours, making calcium a potentially important factor influencing 226Ra fate, bioavailability, bioaccumulation, and toxicity. Analysis of Canadian mining effluent data demonstrated that ²²⁶Ra is released from multiple mining sectors and that uranium mines are not uniquely responsible for elevated discharges. Final treated effluent concentrations ranged from 0.2 to 7800 mBq L-1, with average concentrations in several sectors exceeding the regional background upper tolerance limit of 21.7 mBq L-1. To address ecotoxicological data gaps, laboratory methods were developed for the freshwater fingernail clam Sphaerium striatinum, a sensitive bivalve species. Experimental results demonstrated that 226Ra bioaccumulates in both soft tissues and shells, with preferential partitioning to shells. Chronic exposure reduced growth (EC10 = 4.1 Bq L-1) and reproduction (EC10 = 0.37 Bq L-1) at environmentally relevant concentrations, while survival was comparatively less sensitive. Sorption experiments further showed that the environmental fate of 226Ra is strongly controlled by mineralogy and water chemistry, with adsorption to reactive clay minerals rapidly reducing dissolved concentrations. Increasing calcium concentrations reduced sorption and increased the persistence of dissolved 226Ra, whereas organic matter had comparatively little influence. Combined bioaccumulation and toxicity studies demonstrated that calcium exerts competing effects on ²²⁶Ra behaviour. Although calcium can reduce biological uptake through competitive interactions at biological membranes, it also increases ²²⁶Ra dissolved exposure by limiting sorption to mineral phases. Consequently, calcium did not consistently mitigate toxicity and, for some endpoints, resulted in increased organism sensitivity. Dose modelling further indicated that waterborne exposure was the dominant pathway under the conditions tested. Overall, this research demonstrates that the environmental risk of ²²⁶Ra is governed by coupled geochemical and biological processes and that water chemistry can substantially influence both exposure and toxicity. These findings provide critical information for environmental risk assessments and support the future development of science-based freshwater quality guidelines and management strategies for ²²⁶Ra releases.

title: The Price of the Games—Or Whether Mega‐Sporting Events Improve Human Rights in the Host Country
title_original: The Price of the Games—Or Whether Mega‐Sporting Events Improve Human Rights in the Host Country
summary: ABSTRACT Objective The controversy surrounding the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar and the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States has renewed debate over whether hosting mega‐sporting events affects human rights. This article examines whether host governments strategically adjust civil liberties in response to international scrutiny. Methods Using a bidder‐based difference‐in‐differences design, it analyses 74 FIFA World Cups and Olympic Games (1900–2022), comparing successful hosts with unsuccessful bidders across nine civil liberties dimensions from the Varieties of Democracy (V‐Dem) dataset. Results The findings support a selective adjustment thesis. Seven dimensions show no statistically robust effects, suggesting that hosting does not systematically alter most civil liberties. Freedom from forced labor improves before events but deteriorates afterward, consistent with strategic reputation management. A marginal effect on freedom of religion does not survive multiple‐testing correction. Conclusions Host governments, therefore, appear to selectively manage internationally visible rights rather than undertake genuine human rights reform.

title: Aboriginal Australians, Identity and Activism: (Re)Assessing the Impact of Jack Johnson’s Visits to Australia, 1907–1908
title_original: Aboriginal Australians, Identity and Activism: (Re)Assessing the Impact of Jack Johnson’s Visits to Australia, 1907–1908
summary: The African American boxer Jack Johnson visited Australia twice, in 1907 and 1908. Johnson’s time in Australia is best remembered for his defeat of Tommy Burns in 1908 to claim the world heavyweight title and for the racial animus sparked by this victory. Scholars have also analysed these visits from other perspectives, including Johnson’s impact on Australian Aboriginal people, an effect generally interpreted as positive and inspirational. We reassess this claim, balancing new evidence of his positive impacts against negative ones. The relative paucity of Aboriginal voices from the period complicates our ability to understand fully the legacy of this tour for Aboriginal people. However, there exists a range of other sources that indicates Johnson’s impact on Indigenous race relations was more nuanced and multifaceted than has been argued to date. We agree that Johnson’s outsized persona, his Black pride and his athletic victories—especially over Burns and, later, Jim Jeffries in America—had many positive effects on Aboriginal Australians, not only in the cities where Johnson fought but more widely throughout the country. Alongside these impacts, however, Johnson’s victories spiked White racial anxieties that elicited racist commentary and inflamed existing prejudices against Australia’s Indigenous peoples.

title: THE MARKETING POTENTIAL OF CULTURAL AUTHENTICITY: THE WORLD NOMAD GAMES 2024
title_original: THE MARKETING POTENTIAL OF CULTURAL AUTHENTICITY: THE WORLD NOMAD GAMES 2024
summary: The World Nomad Games have emerged as a significant catalyst in the tourism sector, promoting cultural identity and ethno-tourism on a worldwide scale. Cultural tourism destinations are of significant potential as tourists are changing their preferences, focusing on experiencing culture in a more authentic manner. This shift in tourist preferences has proved to be a significant factor in attracting investment. The aim of this research was to examine the role of cultural authenticity in engaging tourists and promoting global marketing of ethnic sports events. The study was based on the World Nomad Games 2024. The methodology adopted in the study was mixed, using both quantitative and qualitative content analysis, as well as EFAS analysis to evaluate the strategic position of the event. The findings indicated that the impact of cultural authenticity was positive on the engagement of tourists in terms of the visual attributes of the event, such as sports, music, and ethnic dishes. On the other hand, the fragmentation in the digital communication and operation was negative in terms of the overall efficiency in the marketing of the event. The present study contributes to the existing body of knowledge by adding the concept of existential authenticity in the analysis of social media and strategic evaluation tools in the context of ethnic sports events. Keywords: cultural authenticity, World Nomad Games, cultural heritage, marketing strategies, national identity.

title: Designing a Policy Framework for Utilizing Sports Capacities in Promoting Social Health and Organizing Leisure Time
title_original: Designing a Policy Framework for Utilizing Sports Capacities in Promoting Social Health and Organizing Leisure Time
summary: Sport może przyczyniać się do rozwoju społecznego poprzez wspieranie jakości życia, uczestnictwa społecznego oraz kapitału społecznego. Celem badania było opracowanie ram polityki wykorzystania potencjału sportu w organizacji czasu wolnego i promowaniu zdrowia społecznego. Badanie miało charakter jakościowy i opierało się na półustrukturyzowanych wywiadach z 13 nauczycielami akademickimi i ekspertami w zakresie zarządzania sportem i polityki społecznej, dobranymi celowo. Dane analizowano z wykorzystaniem podejścia teorii ugruntowanej, obejmującego kodowanie otwarte, osiowe i selektywne. Wiarygodność i spójność analizy wsparto poprzez weryfikację ustaleń przez uczestników, niezależne równoległe kodowanie oraz dokumentowanie decyzji analitycznych. W wyniku analizy opracowano zintegrowane ramy polityki obejmujące uwarunkowania przyczynowe, kontekstowe i interweniujące, proponowane strategie oraz przewidywane konsekwencje. Do kluczowych elementów modelu należały pozycja kulturowa i akceptacja społeczna, uwarunkowania społeczno-kulturowe i zasobowe, czynniki środowiskowe i demograficzne, rozwój infrastruktury oraz strategie społeczne i motywacyjne. Przewidywane konsekwencje obejmowały aspekty ekonomiczne, behawioralne i społeczno-kulturowe. Zaproponowane ramy stanowią koncepcyjną podstawę rozwoju polityki czasu wolnego opartej na sporcie, ukierunkowanej na wspieranie zdrowia społecznego i uczestnictwa społecznego. Konieczne są dalsze badania nad możliwością zastosowania modelu oraz oceną jego przewidywanych efektów w praktyce.

title: Optimal telepresence experience in heritage tourism: A multidimensional scale and its impact on tourist behavior
title_original: Optimal telepresence experience in heritage tourism: A multidimensional scale and its impact on tourist behavior
summary: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly being integrated into on-site heritage tourism, yet little is known about how visitors evaluate hybrid experiences combining physical heritage environments with VR-mediated reconstructions. To address this gap, drawing on telepresence and flow theory, this study conceptualizes and validates Optimal Telepresence Experience (OTE) as a higher-order experiential construct reflecting visitors' overall technology-enhanced heritage experiences. Using a multi-stage scale development process with data collected at a heritage museum in Hue, Vietnam, the study develops and validates the OTE measurement instrument. The findings show that OTE, reflected through emotional, cognitive, and functional dimensions, strengthens visitors’ memory formation and revisit intention. Theoretically, the study advances immersive tourism research by conceptualizing and validating OTE as a higher-order experiential construct for hybrid technology-enhanced heritage experiences. Practically, the validated OTE scale provides a tool for designing and evaluating VR-enhanced heritage experiences that foster deeper visitor engagement and behavioral outcomes.

title: Exploring adapted water polo: a feasibility study on improving psychosocial recovery in women post-breast cancer treatment
title_original: Exploring adapted water polo: a feasibility study on improving psychosocial recovery in women post-breast cancer treatment
summary: Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an adapted water polo programme (Aqua polo) for women following breast cancer treatment. Exploratory secondary objectives were to examine changes in cancer-related fatigue (CRF), quality of life, post-traumatic growth, physical function and participants’ psychosocial experiences. The intervention was conducted in a municipal swimming pool within a renowned local club, as part of a community-based research collaboration between a cancer center and a sport psychology laboratory. Methods A 16-week intervention was implemented, with participants engaging in structured weekly sessions to evaluate both physical and psychosocial outcomes. Fifteen participants took part in weekly 2-hour Aqua polo sessions, supervised by a multidisciplinary team. A mixed-methods approach was used to assess feasibility (session adherence), physical improvements (aerobic capacity, muscle mass), and psychosocial dimensions, including CRF (R-PFS), quality of life (QLQ BR23), post-traumatic growth (PTG-I), and relational dynamics within the sporting environment (through semi-structured interviews). Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and mixed linear models; qualitative interviews were coded inductively using grounded theory principles and NVivo software. Results The programme achieved a high adherence rate, with 87% of participants attending at least 60% of the sessions. Exploratory analyses showed increases in aerobic capacity ( p = 0.009), muscle mass ( p = 0.01) and quality of life ( p = 0.04), whereas no significant changes were observed in cancer-related fatigue. Participants described positive psychosocial experiences, including greater self-confidence, renewed competence and improved body image. Qualitative findings highlighted the importance of social interactions, team cohesion and the coach–athlete relationship in fostering engagement and perceived psychosocial recovery. Conclusion This feasibility study demonstrates that an adapted water polo programme is feasible and well accepted by women following breast cancer treatment. Exploratory findings suggest potential benefits for physical function and psychosocial well-being, while supporting the development of future adequately powered controlled studies evaluating team-based aquatic interventions in cancer rehabilitation. title: The electrical resistivity model of the Australian lithosphere
title_original: The electrical resistivity model of the Australian lithosphere
summary: We present a new 3D electrical resistivity model of the entire Australian subcontinental lithosphere, which we call the Australian Multiscale Model of Electrical Resistivity (AusMMER). The AusMMER is derived from the joint inversion of magnetotelluric (MT) responses from the currently available part of the AusLAMP and state arrays, geomagnetic responses from observatories, and the legacy Australia-Wide Array of Geomagnetic Stations (AWAGS). In total, we invert plane-wave transfer functions from 1,394 MT sites and 60 geomagnetic stations at periods between 10 and 10,000 s. The inversion uses a distributed 3D finite-element electromagnetic solver that operates directly in the spherical frame and supports multiscale, locally refined meshes. This approach allows us to integrate heterogeneous datasets and recover a coherent 3D electrical resistivity model spanning the lithosphere and the uppermost asthenosphere. The imaged anomalies align with major tectonic units and their boundaries, with some prominent features extending into the lithospheric mantle, while others remain confined to the crust. These relationships provide new insights into crust–mantle architecture and the role of deeper mantle processes in shaping Australia’s tectonic domains and continent accretion. We further show that many prominent ore deposits spatially coincide with lithospheric resistivity anomalies, providing new insights into the crust–mantle controls on mineralization. Finally, the AusMMER provides the baseline for quantifying the Geomagnetically Induced Currents during geomagnetic storms.

title: THE 1930 BELGRADE ALL-SOKOL SLET IN THE LIGHT OF TURKISH ARCHIVAL SOURCES AND THE SOKOLSKI GLASNIK NEWSPAPER
title_original: THE 1930 BELGRADE ALL-SOKOL SLET IN THE LIGHT OF TURKISH ARCHIVAL SOURCES AND THE SOKOLSKI GLASNIK NEWSPAPER
summary: The 1930 Belgrade All-Sokol Slet stood out not merely as a gymnastics and sporting event but as a major social manifestation of national unity, Pan-Slav solidarity and the ideological objectives of the Yugoslav state. The event acquired an international dimension through the participation of delegations not only from various regions of Yugoslavia but also from countries such as Czechoslovakia, Poland and Romania. This study examines the Slet in detail, beginning with its preparatory phase and covering its organizational structure, official ceremonies, athletic and cultural performances, as well as its broader impact on public opinion. One of the most striking aspects of the 1930 Belgrade All-Sokol Slet was that it took place shortly after the establishment of the Sokol of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia and under the patronage of King Alexander I. The King’s personal attendance at the ceremonies served as a powerful indication of the state’s support for the event and the political significance attributed to the Sokol movement. This circumstance created an important opportunity to promote the organization nationwide, expand its activities and strengthen its institutional framework. Beyond encouraging the physical development of youth, the Slet conveyed strong messages of discipline, solidarity, social responsibility and the reinforcement of a shared national identity. The program offered a rich combination of parades, mass gymnastic displays, various sports competitions, cultural events and official speeches. Drawing on the archival sources of the Republic of Turkey and Sokolski Glasnik, the official journal of the Sokol of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia (SKY), this study investigates the entire process of the Slet chronologically, from its preparations to its conclusion.

title: Velocity reconstruction from KSZ: measuring f NL with ACT and DESILS
title_original: Velocity reconstruction from KSZ: measuring f NL with ACT and DESILS
summary: Abstract The kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect offers an indirect way to reconstruct large-scale cosmic velocities, by correlating high-resolution CMB temperature maps with galaxy surveys. In this work, we present the first three-dimensional reconstruction of the large-scale velocity field using a photometric galaxy survey, using data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys (DESILS) and the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR5. We detect an 11.7 σ correlation between our velocity reconstruction and the galaxy field, using only DESILS LRGs in the northern Galactic hemisphere. We find that the overall amplitude of the kSZ-induced correlation is low relative to a halo model prediction ( b v = 0.45 +0.06 -0.05 ), in agreement with previous results which find high feedback and smoothed gas profiles near massive galaxies. We use this measurement to place new constraints on local-type primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG), obtaining f NL = -39 +40 -33 . This represents the most stringent f NL constraint from kSZ velocity-based analyses to date. We validate our findings through extensive null tests, including tests for CMB foregrounds based on comparing 90 and 150 GHz CMB data.

title: Replication data and code for “Documenting Sustainability and Legacy in Sport: A Comparative Analysis of VogaShare and Paris 2024”
title_original: Replication data and code for “Documenting Sustainability and Legacy in Sport: A Comparative Analysis of VogaShare and Paris 2024”
summary: This dataset contains derived analytical data, document-level metadata, post hoc dictionary materials, manual coding materials, R code, and output files associated with the article “Documenting Sustainability and Legacy in Sport: A Comparative Analysis of VogaShare and Paris 2024”. The analytical corpus comprises 15 English-language documents: six VogaShare documents and nine Paris 2024/Marseille-related documents. Copyright-protected source documents are not redistributed; stable identifiers and source links are provided in corpus_metadata.csv. The recovered R script reproduces aggregate case-level summaries, Table 1 data, Figure 1 data, Figure 1, and verification checks from the recovered page-level derived output. Primary thematic frequencies represent documentary emphasis and source coverage; they are not direct measures of programme effectiveness, causal impact, implementation quality, social impact, or environmental performance.

title: Constructing languages of intellectual co-operation
title_original: Constructing languages of intellectual co-operation
summary:
Abstract
                  Through an examination of natural languages with allegedly self-evident claims to international status, as well as of constructed languages asserting relative naturalness to achieve international legitimacy, this chapter brings debates on international languages at the League of Nations into wider arenas and into the hands of lesser-known actors and organizations. The chapter argues for a need to methodologically re-evaluate debates on international languages and the League of Nations beyond existing rubrics of official legitimation and of success and failure. These rubrics fail to use an eclectic archive of the League’s internal workings, as viewed here through so-far neglected correspondence received and archived by the League. These letters yield social histories of the League’s consideration of international languages: moments of information collection among communities in the process of imagining themselves.

title: Migration and Tentative Settlement, from 1704 to the 1770s
title_original: Migration and Tentative Settlement, from 1704 to the 1770s
summary:
Abstract
                  Chapter Four covers Gibraltar’s history from 1704 into the 1770s. From the time of the Anglo-Dutch occupation until the end of hostilities in 1713, Gibraltar lost communication with southern Spain. Muslim and Jewish merchants supplied the occupying garrison with provisions from North Africa. In the Treaty of Utrecht, Britain promised Spain that no Jews or Muslims would be allowed to settle in Gibraltar. This agreement exacerbated tensions within Gibraltar, where Protestant settlers sought to forge a collective interest in opposition to the prominence of local Jews. Some of the most influential Jewish merchants were associates of Mulay Ismael, the sultan of Morocco, who in 1721 secured a promise from the British to allow Jewish and Muslim merchants to trade in Gibraltar. During Spain’s failed effort to retake Gibraltar in 1727, the British public rallied in support of Gibraltar, and commentators acknowledged the patriotic service of the Jews residing in the territory. Though Gibraltar was not attacked during the mid-century wars between 1739 and 1763, those conflicts highlighted the garrison’s vulnerability. Military contingencies convinced the local authorities that they needed the loyalty of the territory’s Catholic and Jewish population. Gibraltar thrived economically after 1763. Chapter Four traces the development of distinctive local cultures, with autonomous institutions developing within the Catholic and Jewish communities. Elite Protestant Britons sought to bring their own sophisticated culture to Gibraltar, but few, if any, elite Protestants stayed for long or raised families there. Unlike their Catholic and Jewish counterparts, they did not form a stable community.

title: Why Jewish History Is So Hard to Write
title_original: Why Jewish History Is So Hard to Write
summary:
Abstract
                  Every generation of historians draws a picture of the Jewish past that is bound up with how they think about the Jewish future. And those visions of the future generally turn out to be wrong, because the past two centuries have seen continual, radical upheavals in Jewish life. Today, Jewish historians like Simon Schama and Martin Goodman define Judaism as a pluralistic tradition, emphasizing that Jewishness was never a simple or unitary identity and mistrusting the Bible as a source of historical evidence. The notion that Judaism is about diversity and pluralism reflects the liberal, multicultural values of modern Western Jews. But that liberalism is under several kinds of pressure in an era of rising nationalism and religious extremism, and the lessons of Jewish history might look quite different a century from now.

title: Gibraltar and the British Empire from the 1830s to 1898
title_original: Gibraltar and the British Empire from the 1830s to 1898
summary:
Abstract
                  Chapter Six covers Gibraltar’s history from the 1830s to 1898. There was an ideological shift across the British Empire during this period, as humanitarian activists and imperial officials increasingly believed that British imperial power could benefit not just the people of Britain but also colonized populations and others around the world. In Gibraltar, this outlook inspired new interest in Africa. The chapter recounts the reception given to Ahmad Ibn Tuwayr Al-Jana in 1833, the 1835 trial and punishment of the officers and crew of a slave ship accused of preparing for a voyage from Gibraltar, and the ordeal of Abú Bekr, who after gaining his freedom in Jamaica, came to Gibraltar in 1835 hoping to proceed to his ancestral home in Africa. French power expanded across the western Mediterranean during the 1830s. Shipping became safer and more efficient, and by the 1840s, French steamships were outcompeting the sailing vessels that had traditionally frequented Gibraltar. Gibraltar suffered an economic slump. The territory continued to be wracked by social tension. Between 1842 and 1874, the garrison employed convict labor. During the 1860s, protests against immigration restrictions united local Protestant, Catholic, and Jewish activists in opposition to government policy. Beginning in the 1870s, the garrison and local businesses increasingly relied on day laborers from Spain. The border town La Línea grew, and southern Andalusia was absorbed into Gibraltar’s economic sphere. The region’s dependency on Gibraltar was revealed in 1898 when Spain suffered a downturn following its defeat in the Spanish-American War.

title: Britain’s Overseas Territory in Europe
title_original: Britain’s Overseas Territory in Europe
summary:
Abstract
                  Chapter Nine analyzes Gibraltar’s history since 1986. It begins with a discussion of the purported end of colonial rule in the territory. Though the United Kingdom has not relinquished sovereignty over Gibraltar, the territory, along with several other former colonies, has been granted a large measure of local autonomy, at the cost of losing UK government investment and subsidies. In contrast to other British Overseas Territories, since 1986 Gibraltar has been frequently shaken by shifts in UK government policy. In 2002 local voters almost unanimously supported a referendum protesting the stance of the British government in its negotiations over Gibraltar with Spain. In 2016 the territory voted almost unanimously to remain within the European Union but still had to leave because of the outcome of the referendum in Britain. By 2016, Gibraltar’s economy had been transformed. Internet gambling, smuggling, and offshore banking had become mainstays of the local economy. Gibraltar was one of the richest territories per capita on Earth. There have been several high-profile financial scandals, and during the negotiations over Gibraltar’s future following the Brexit referendum, Spain insisted that Gibraltar introduce financial reforms to combat smuggling, money laundering, and tax evasion. In 2025 the EU, UK, Spain, and Gibraltar reached an agreement effectively ensuring Gibraltar’s continued membership in the EU single market. This agreement ended a long period of heated debate, but the ongoing protests of populist opposition figures in Britain and Spain suggest that arguments over the status of Gibraltar will continue.

title: Slavery, Warfare, and the Sanctification of Spanish Gibraltar, 1492–1704
title_original: Slavery, Warfare, and the Sanctification of Spanish Gibraltar, 1492–1704
summary:
Abstract
                  Chapter Three examines Gibraltar from 1492 until the Anglo-Dutch conquest in 1704. Despite the Spanish conquest of Granada and the expulsion of the Jews, in the decades after 1492 Spain remained religiously diverse. Local religious tensions and violent raids by Muslim and Christian corsairs reached a climax with an assault on Gibraltar in 1540. The chronicle of that event reveals complex patterns of relations between Muslims, Christians, Jews, and conversos in Gibraltar and throughout the region. The chronicle also reveals the prominence of slavery as a feature of daily life in Gibraltar and as a threat facing Muslims, Christians, and Jews alike. After 1540, the Shrine of Our Lady of Europa, which had been sacked by the corsairs, became a widely recognized symbol of defiant Christianity and liberation from slavery. Spanish Gibraltar in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries was a fortified imperial outpost. The townspeople were almost constantly engaged in conflict, negotiation, and trade along the northern coast of Africa. They also celebrated victories against English shipping and Spanish missionary activity in Mexico and Venezuela. After 1607, when Dutch naval forces destroyed a Spanish fleet in the Bay of Gibraltar, the townspeople frequently feared the invasion of rival European imperial powers. Chapter Three concludes with Dutch and English operations within the strait, including the English occupation of Tangier in the 1660s, 1670s, and 1680s, and the Anglo-Dutch conquest of Gibraltar in 1704.

After 1540, the Shrine of Our Lady of Europa, which had been sacked by the corsairs, became a widely recognized symbol of defiant Christianity and liberation from slavery. Spanish Gibraltar in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries was a fortified imperial outpost. The townspeople were almost constantly engaged in conflict, negotiation, and trade along the northern coast of Africa. They also celebrated victories against English shipping and Spanish missionary activity in Mexico and Venezuela. After 1607, when Dutch naval forces destroyed a Spanish fleet in the Bay of Gibraltar, the townspeople frequently feared the invasion of rival European imperial powers. Chapter Three concludes with Dutch and English operations within the strait, including the English occupation of Tangier in the 1660s, 1670s, and 1680s, and the Anglo-Dutch conquest of Gibraltar in 1704.

title: Gibraltar and Its Suburbs, 1898–1936
title_original: Gibraltar and Its Suburbs, 1898–1936
summary:
Abstract
                  Chapter Seven examines Gibraltar’s history from 1898 to 1936. Early in the twentieth century, British railway and shipping companies invested heavily in the Spanish region surrounding Gibraltar. New docks, roads, railway and ferry services, and mansions and luxury hotels conspicuously displayed British investment in several nearby towns, Algeciras in particular. La Línea was home to much of Gibraltar’s day-labor work force and grew dramatically, but in contrast to Algeciras, it remained relatively poor. During a series of labor disputes between 1899 and 1913, many resident Gibraltarians joined protests and strikes alongside Spanish day laborers. This pattern of politics shifted during World War I, when Gibraltarian workers, eager to support the allied war effort, declined to join strikes organized by their Spanish coworkers. After the war, the colonial government cooperated with Gibraltarian labor leaders who promoted a policy of anglicization. The unions, for example, campaigned for better English-language education in the local schools and helped secure the creation of a new city council with four of the nine seats chosen by popular election. Chapter Seven highlights the importance of events across the strait in Morocco for the direction of Spanish politics, from the rise of the Spanish dictator Miguel Primo de Rivera, through his downfall, the collapse of the Spanish monarchy, the creation of the republic, and the outbreak of the civil war in 1936. Francisco Franco first rose to prominence fighting in Morocco during the Rif War 1920s, and he landed troops from Morocco in Algeciras during the first days of the Spanish Civil War.

title: Epilogue: Our Lady of Europa and the Saudi Mosque
title_original: Epilogue: Our Lady of Europa and the Saudi Mosque
summary:
Abstract
                  The epilogue beings with the opening of the Mosque of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques on Europa Point at the southern tip of Gibraltar. The mosque was funded by the Saudi royal family, and its opening was an elaborate pageant. Several speakers reflected on Gibraltar’s history since the Umayyad landing in 711. Many also pointed to the recent renovation of the shrine of Our Lady of Europa a short distance away. They suggested that the two places of worship, almost side by side, signaled that Gibraltar had become an almost uniquely tolerant place. The epilogue cites this moment as part of a long pattern in Gibraltar in which monuments acquire layers of meaning as successive generations build, destroy, reconstruct, and repurpose them.

title: War, Disorder, and Commerce from the 1770s to the 1830s
title_original: War, Disorder, and Commerce from the 1770s to the 1830s
summary:
Abstract
                  Chapter Five examines events in Gibraltar from the great Spanish siege of 1779–1783 to the 1830s. The Great Siege was a defining moment for Gibraltar. The sultan of Morocco’s decision to cut off trade exacerbated the suffering of the garrison and townspeople. Spanish bombardment destroyed most of Gibraltar’s buildings. The siege exacerbated communal tensions within the town. Soldiers rioted. There were attacks on Jews. A large proportion of Gibraltar’s population left. Though Governor George Augustus Eliott was celebrated after the siege as a British national hero, he was criticized in Gibraltar for abusing his powers to enrich himself, restricting trade, and impeding reconstruction. During the 1790s, the commanders of the garrison feared that revolutionary ideology was spreading among the soldiers and townspeople. Early in the nineteenth century, governors launched efforts to instill loyalty among the soldiers and impose discipline on the garrison and town. These projects acquired greater urgency after the yellow fever epidemic of 1804. For the next three decades, successive governors recruited members of the local Jewish and Catholic elite to police their communities and enforce public health regulations. Gibraltar’s trade expanded during the 1820s. Large sailing ships brought goods to Gibraltar from overseas, and smaller vessels carried cargo to and from the nearby Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts. During the early 1830s, the government undertook new efforts to control the movement of people and maintain order. Though civilians were never punished as severely as solders, like the men of the garrison they were under constant surveillance.

title: Franco and Decolonization, 1936–1986
title_original: Franco and Decolonization, 1936–1986
summary:
Abstract
                  Chapter Eight recounts Gibraltar’s history from the outbreak of the Spanish Civil War in 1936 until Spain’s entry into the European Economic Community in 1986. Though the British authorities in Gibraltar remained officially neutral throughout the Spanish Civil War, their actions favored Franco’s right-wing rebellion. Within Gibraltar, many business leaders and conservative Catholics sided with Franco, while many others sympathized with the Spanish Republic. Franco protested British sovereignty over Gibraltar soon after his victory in the civil war, but Spain was impoverished, militarily weak, and remained officially neutral during World War II. After the war, the founders of the United Nations barred Franco’s Spain from joining. Franco responded to his ostracization by posing as a champion of decolonization, despite his intention to hold on to Spain’s protectorate in Morocco. After Spain was admitted to the UN in 1949, Franco invoked UN resolutions on decolonization to renew his protests against British rule in Gibraltar. As the debate over decolonization intensified, Gibraltar’s elected local government acquired greater power and autonomy. In a referendum in 1967, Gibraltarians voted almost unanimously in favor of British sovereignty. Spain’s blockade of the territory from 1969 through 1982 reinforced local opposition to any compromise. After Franco’s death in 1975, Spain petitioned to join the European Economic Community. Britain, a member of the EEC, had a veto over Spain’s membership and insisted that Spain put its claim to Gibraltar aside. After Spain joined the EEC, its border with Gibraltar functioned like other borders within the increasingly integrated European Community.

title: Introduction: The Intersecting Boundaries of Europe, Africa, the Mediterranean, and the Atlantic World
title_original: Introduction: The Intersecting Boundaries of Europe, Africa, the Mediterranean, and the Atlantic World
summary:
Abstract
                  The introduction highlights Gibraltar’s importance as a widely recognized monument marking the intersecting boundaries between Europe and Africa, the Mediterranean and the Atlantic. Shortly after the Castilian conquest of Gibraltar in the fifteenth century, the newly arrived Christian townspeople built a shrine to the Virgin Mary at the southern tip of the peninsula, a place later Spanish writers described as “the last place in Europe.” Since antiquity, Gibraltar’s location had carried mythical significance. Ancient Greeks and Romans recounted how the hero Hercules, sent on a mission to the end of the Earth, discovered an isthmus linking Africa and Europe. He destroyed it, leaving Gibraltar and an adjacent peak in Africa as the only remaining fragments of the demolished land bridge. The introduction explains how adopting a geographical perspective placing Gibraltar at the edge of Europe, the Mediterranean, and the Atlantic helps make sense of the territory’s entire history from antiquity to the present.

title: Antiquity
title_original: Antiquity
summary:
Abstract
                  Chapter One traces Gibraltar’s history from the Palaeolithic era to the end of the reign of the Visigoths. Tens of thousands of years ago, Neanderthals sheltered in Gorham’s Cave on the eastern side of Gibraltar’s mountain. Sea levels were lower than they are today, and the mountain rose from a dry coastal plain. Modern humans, Homo sapiens, had been living across the strait in Africa for hundreds of thousands of years, but there is no compelling evidence of travel, commerce, or communication across the Strait of Gibraltar before the arrival of pastoralists and farmers in Iberia during the Bronze Age. By the ninth century BC, Phoenician and other travelers were routinely crossing and sailing through the strait. In the fourth century BC, a major port was established at Carteia, at the northern end of the Bay of Gibraltar. Carteia thrived under Carthaginian and Roman rule. Chapter One recounts major developments during the period of Roman rule, including the arrival of Judaism and Christianity in southern Iberia. It ends with the Muslim conquest of the kingdom of the Visigoths in 711. According to legend, the invading army landed on or near Gibraltar.

title: Muslims, Christians, Jews, and Five Ports Around the Strait, 711–1492
title_original: Muslims, Christians, Jews, and Five Ports Around the Strait, 711–1492
summary:
Abstract
                  Chapter Two covers Gibraltar’s history from the Umayyad invasion of 711 to 1492. Carteia was already in ruins before the Umayyads arrived, and instead of rebuilding it, they established the new port city of Algeciras on the western shore of the Bay of Gibraltar. During the medieval period, Algeciras, Tarifa, Ceuta, and Tangier competed for dominance of the strait. The town of Gibraltar was founded in 1159 as a ceremonial center. It increased in military importance after the Castilian conquest in 1309. The Castilians strengthened its fortifications and improved its port facilities. After the Marinids ousted the Castilians in 1333, they undertook additional, extensive construction. Gibraltar became one of five rival port cities competing for dominance on the strait, and by the 1370s it was one of four after Algeciras was abandoned. In 1462 Juan Alonso de Guzman, Duke of Medina Sidonia, led the conquering army that permanently placed Gibraltar under Christian rule. The conquest precipitated a period of political instability and frequent, disruptive migration. For a brief period, Gibraltar was occupied by conversos, Spanish people of Jewish ancestry who had converted to Christianity under duress. The Strait of Gibraltar acquired new symbolic significance during the wars of the medieval period. As early as the eleventh century, Iberian Christian kingdoms vowed to make the Strait a border between Christendom and territories ruled by Muslims. By 1492, at least in the eyes of the Spanish, it seemed that this goal had been achieved.

title: Walking through History
title_original: Walking through History
summary:
Abstract
                  Today’s globalized and transnational world encourages interest in migration, migrants, and diasporas as an essential part of human experience. It also rekindles interest in the Jewish diaspora and in the Jewish experience of wandering, exile, and migration. Having their roots in the Bible and the very beginnings of Jewish peoplehood, exodus, wandering, and migration appear as themes in Jewish traditional art and visual culture, such as illuminated Hagadot and decorated sukkah booths. In Christian tradition, these themes are primarily explained through the image of the cursed Wandering Jew. This essay, spanning the second half of the 19th century through the present, surveys a large number of art works created by Jewish artists in response both to these two visual traditions and to their contemporary historical, political, and cultural circumstances. Against the background of emancipation and the search for identity, on the one hand, and poverty, persecution, and wish to better one’s life through immigration, on the other, artists such as Moritz Oppenheim, Maurycy Gottlieb, Shmuel Hirszenberg, Maurycy Minkowski, Marc Chagall, Naftali Bezem, and Zoya Cherkassky-Nnadi created striking works of art that tackle the very essence of Jewish experience of wandering, exile, and migration in modern world.

title: Remembering the Seminole Wars
title_original: Remembering the Seminole Wars
summary:
In Florida, travelers and residents can visit numerous historic sites that inform the public about the Seminole Wars, conflicts fought between the United States and the Seminole during the first half of the nineteenth century. This book focuses on four of these places—Dade Battlefield Historic State Park, Paynes Creek Historic State Park, Okeechobee Battlefield Historic State Park, and Fort King National Historic Landmark—to explore how history has been interpreted at each site over the years.

By comparing the sites, Daniel Murphree identifies shared and different factors shaping their development, including settler colonialism and the extent of Seminole and Miccosukee involvement. He finds that disagreements over who controls and interprets their histories—among officials, local advocates, Indigenous communities, scholars, and visitors—have surrounded the sites from their beginnings and remain important today. Remembering the Seminole Wars helps readers understand how history influenced these sites and how interpretations of the past shape public understanding of the Seminole Wars in modern Florida.

title: Një histori e shkurtër receptimi: vepra e Ismail Kadaresë në Itali
title_original: Një histori e shkurtër receptimi: vepra e Ismail Kadaresë në Itali
summary:
Ismail Kadare, edhe pse një shkrimtar i njohur ndërkombëtarisht, veprat e të cilit janë përkthyer në shumë gjuhë, nuk ka qenë objekt i një vëmendje të madhe nga ana e kritikës italiane. Një lagunë jo pak e rëndësishme nëse konsiderohet jo vetëm rëndësia e këtij autori në vetvete, por mbi të gjitha fakti se vepra e tij është shprehi e një kulture, e cila me Italinë ka pasur një raport thelbësor. Është e veçantë që në Itali, vend i cili në të shkuarën ka qenë një kullë shpëtimi për letërsinë shqiptare, Kadare të jetë përkthyer për një kohë të gjatë nga një gjuhë e dytë dhe jo nga gjuha origjinale e veprave të tij. Vetëm gjatë këtyre viteve të fundit kanë dalë disa botime të librave të shkruar rishtas nga autori, të përkthyer drejtpërdrejt prej shqipes, por përkthimet e vjetra mbesin gjithmonë ato, të dorës së dytë, të cilat rezultojnë të jenë një pengesë për kuptimin e veprës së Kadaresë. Qëllimi ynë në këtë studim është të
bëjmë një histori të shkurtër të procesit editorial të veprës së Kadaresë në Itali.

title: Arab Double-Barreled Surnames: Evidence from Kuwait.
title_original: Arab Double-Barreled Surnames: Evidence from Kuwait.
summary: The indigenous population of Kuwait is composed of a Sunni Arab majority and a Shia minority that is mostly of Persian origin. While some citizens belong to families and others to tribes, most have had surnames for about 300 years. The vast majority of these surnames are single-barreled, i.e., they have one stem that comes etymologically from one of the five components that used to make up medieval Arab names. A small percentage of Kuwaiti surnames come in the form of double-barreled stems such as il-butˤiy buu tˤeebaan or li-xreenij ir-riʃiidiy. This type of surnames combines without overt markers, producing compounds with distinct internal consistency. They index the scope of lineages and family alliances, which reflect complex kinship networks based on naming practices that are shaped by migration histories and evolving concepts of heritage. This article studies the makeup of Kuwaiti double-barreled surnames by examining three corpora: student lists, parliamentary electoral register, for a synchronic perspective, and surname changes for a diachronic perspective. It explores the internal structure and etymological origin of Kuwaiti double-barreled surnames to provide insights into Arab onomastics and Kuwaiti culture. Results reveal an unexpected synchronic density of double-barreled surname types spreading in meme-like fashion diachronically within Kuwaiti society. The article invites policymakers and civil registration authorities to develop clear guidelines for registering double-barreled surnames to ensure consistency in naming patterns. It also encourages interdisciplinary research linking onomastic patterns with sociology and demography, and associating surname structure with social class and urbanization.

title: Comprehensive Health Predictors of Injury, Illness, and Separation From Service After Enrollment in Special Forces Assessment and Selection: A Two‐Year Longitudinal Study
title_original: Comprehensive Health Predictors of Injury, Illness, and Separation From Service After Enrollment in Special Forces Assessment and Selection: A Two‐Year Longitudinal Study
summary: Individuals in physically and cognitively demanding professions face increased risk of injury, illness, and attrition due to repeated exposure to physical and psychological stressors. Identifying modifiable factors associated with these outcomes can guide risk mitigation strategies. This longitudinal study examined the 2-year cumulative incidence of injuries, illnesses, and attrition following enrollment in the United States Army Special Forces Assessment and Selection (SFAS) course (n = 792) and assessed how physical, nutritional, cognitive, sleep, and social support at the time of enrollment were associated with illness, injury, and attrition outcomes. Upon SFAS enrollment, candidates completed psychological, sleep, and nutrition surveys. Anthropometrics and physical performance were assessed, and fasted blood was collected for physiological and nutritional biomarker analyses. Medical encounters and active-duty status were monitored for all candidates, post 2 years enrollment, regardless of SFAS outcome. Logistic regression identified baseline factors associated with 2-year incidence of injury, illness, or attrition. Slower road march times were associated with 25%-66% higher odds of injury, mental or behavioural illness, sleep disorder, and separation from service. Conversely, greater resistance training, better sleep quality, and higher protein intake were associated with 18%-45% lower odds of injury. Elevated morning cortisol at enrollment was associated with 23% lower odds of mental or behavioural illness, whereas negative mood, poorer sleep quality, and less social support were each associated with increased odds of separation by 28%-31%. This study identified modifiable factors that may be targeted to reduce injury and illness and improve resilience and retention in demanding occupations.

title: Designing a Paradigmatic Model for Boxing Development in Iraq: A Grounded Theory Approach and Data-Based Analysis
title_original: Designing a Paradigmatic Model for Boxing Development in Iraq: A Grounded Theory Approach and Data-Based Analysis
summary: This qualitative study designed a paradigmatic model for the development of boxing in Iraq. Boxing has considerable potential to support social cohesion, youth development, economic activity, women’s empowerment, and sport diplomacy, yet its development in Iraq remains constrained by governance weaknesses, resource shortages, infrastructural deficits, socio-cultural barriers, weak planning, and limited monitoring systems. The study used grounded theory based on the Strauss and Corbin approach. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 20 participants, including boxing coaches, Iraqi Boxing Federation officials, university academics, and international boxing referees. Purposive and snowball sampling continued until theoretical saturation was reached. The interview data were coded and analyzed using MAXQDA. The analysis produced 153 open codes, 34 axial codes, and 14 selective categories. The findings showed that boxing development in Iraq is shaped by causal conditions, contextual conditions, intervening conditions, strategies, and consequences. Recommended strategies included infrastructure development, human resource development, strategic governance, international cooperation, digital systems, school-based talent identification, media campaigns, and cultural promotion. title: Escalada indoor na infância: um relato de experiência sobre aprendizagem, desenvolvimento e superação
title_original: Escalada indoor na infância: um relato de experiência sobre aprendizagem, desenvolvimento e superação
summary: BACKGROUND: Childhood is a critical period for human development, during which diverse bodily experiences foster the improvement of motor, cognitive, and socio-emotional skills. In this context, indoor climbing, as an Adventure Physical Activity, has pedagogical potential to promote meaningful learning and expand children's motor repertoire.OBJECTIVE: To report an experience with indoor climbing during a holiday camp, analyzing its contributions to children's development.METHODS: This is a qualitative experience report conducted in January 2025 with 20 children aged 4 to 10 years. The intervention took place in a gym equipped with an indoor climbing wall and was led by five Physical Education professionals. Data analysis was based on the systematic observation of the children's motor and behavioral responses throughout the activities.RESULTS: The intervention made it possible to address aspects such as motor coordination, balance, strength, motor planning, decision-making, and problem-solving. Improvements were also observed in self-confidence, overcoming fear, perseverance, cooperation, and autonomy, supported by pedagogical strategies based on playfulness, progressive task organization, and controlled risk. CONCLUSION: Indoor climbing proved to be a promising pedagogical strategy for different educational contexts, contributing to children's holistic development and expanding the possibilities for intervention in Physical Education. However, further studies in school settings and longer-term interventions are needed.

title_original: กฎหมายควบคมการใชสารตองหามทางการกฬาในฐานะระเบยบกฎหมายโลก : การวเคราะหเชงบรณาการระหวางประมวลกฎการตอตานการใชสารตองหามโลกกบพระราชบญญตควบคมการใชสารตองหามทางการกฬา พ.ศ. 2555 และทแกไขเพมเตม พ.ศ. 2564
summary: The regulation of doping in sport has evolved into a global legal regime characterized by a transnational legal framework that intricately integrates the roles of sporting organizations and states, particularly under the World Anti-Doping Code and the UNESCO’s International Convention against Doping in Sport. This article aims to analyze the international legal framework, examine the legal structure of Thailand under the Anti-Doping Act B.E. 2555 (2012) and its amendment B.E. 2564 (2021), and evaluate the integration between Thai law and the global anti-doping legal order. The study employs a document analysis of relevant legal texts and academic literature using comparative and public law approaches to understand the development, mechanisms, and legal challenges arising from such integration. The findings reveal that the anti-doping legal system constitutes a hybrid regime combining elements of soft law and hard law, wherein the World Anti-Doping Code establishes normative standards while the UNESCO Convention imposes binding obligations on states. Thai law has adapted by adopting an open-ended legislative framework and relying primarily on subordinate legislation as a regulatory mechanism. Nevertheless, the main structural challenge is the tension between state sovereignty and pressures from the global legal order, along with issues of legal certainty, proportionality of measures, and the legitimacy of global governance mechanisms. Accordingly, this study recommends legal reforms to clarify essential principles at the statutory level, strengthen oversight mechanisms in the exercise of administrative powers, and enhance institutional capacity, in order to achieve a sustainable balance between international standards and the rule of law within the domestic legal system.

title: Toward Lifecycle-Ready Digital Twins For Facility Technical Management
title_original: Toward Lifecycle-Ready Digital Twins For Facility Technical Management
summary: Digital twins are increasingly promoted as a means to address persistent challenges in the built environment, yet their role in maintenance-focused facility management (FM) remains underexplored. This article explores the practical integration of digital twins into facility technical management through a real-life case environment involving three operational buildings and a two-year deployment period. Using a mixed-method approach combining surveys, interviews, operational observations, and industry feedback, the study investigates the organizational, technical, and information-management-related factors affecting the implementation and usability of BIM-based digital twins in maintenance operations.The findings identify key requirements related to BIM data structures, information management practices, naming conventions, and the involvement of maintenance stakeholders during the design and handover phases. Based on the case findings, the article outlines a four-step BIM process development framework and a four-step BIM enablement framework for facility technical management.The study further highlights the importance of user-friendly graphical user interfaces (GUIs) in bridging the gap between design-oriented BIM environments and the practical needs of maintenance personnel. The findings suggest that digital twins should be approached as continuously managed lifecycle information assets rather than static handover deliverables. The article contributes practice-oriented insights into how BIM-based digital twins can support information continuity and operational usability in facility technical management contexts.

title: Pulled-up race outcomes as welfare-relevant surveillance indicators in United States Steeplechase horses, 2023–2025
title_original: Pulled-up race outcomes as welfare-relevant surveillance indicators in United States Steeplechase horses, 2023–2025
summary: Introduction Pulled-up race outcomes are routinely recorded but are nonspecific, potentially reflecting fatigue, poor performance, footing, rider judgment, suspected injury, or physiological compromise. We evaluated their association with subsequent participation disruption in United States steeplechase horses. Methods National Steeplechase Association Race Results Reports from 2023 to 2025 were analyzed retrospectively at the horse-start level. Outcomes were time to the next later-date start, ≥60-day interruption, ≥183-day absence, and no recorded later-date start. Cox models were stratified by race type with horse-clustered robust covariance; binary outcomes used horse-clustered generalized estimating equations. Sensitivity analyses excluded November starts because racing is seasonal from March through November. Results Among 3,070 starts by 710 horses, 367 (11.95%) were pulled up, involving 277 horses (39.0%). No later-date start was recorded after 37.6% of pulled-up and 21.2% of non-pulled-up starts. Among returners, median time to the next start was 42 versus 35 days; Kaplan–Meier medians for all starts were 148 versus 45 days. Pulled-up status was associated with a lower recorded return rate (hazard ratio 0.589, 95% confidence interval 0.515–0.675). Race-type-adjusted odds ratios were 2.10 (1.67–2.64) for ≥60-day interruption and 2.36 (1.80–3.10) for ≥183-day absence. Associations persisted after excluding November starts. Discussion Pulled-up outcomes were associated with participation disruption, although clinical reasons were unavailable. They may help prioritize follow-up and longitudinal surveillance but cannot replace veterinary examination or clinical records.

title: Stress echocardiography: from regional wall motion to multiparametric functional testing
title_original: Stress echocardiography: from regional wall motion to multiparametric functional testing
summary: The development of stress echocardiography reflects a diagnostic shift from ima­ging left ventricular wall motion during stress to the simultaneous assessment of multiple cardiovascular responses. This analytical review examines the method evolution through the following practical challenges addressed over time: the acquisition of two-dimensional images under stress, the standardization of physical and pharmacological protocols, the transition from ischemia diagnosis to prognostic assessment, and the integration of coronary, contractile, and chronotropic reserve evaluation, lung ultrasound, and quantitative assessment of left ventricular mechanics. The development of the ABCDE+ protocol is discussed separately, de­monstrating that this approach should be interpreted as a modular integration rather than a replacement for the classical assessment of regional wall motion. The review outlines the stages of the method’s development in Russia, the new Russian clinical guidelines for 2025-2026, the role of contrast enhancement, three-dimensional imaging, and artificial intelligence, as well as the issues currently hindering the full standardization of multiparametric stress echocardiography. The future of stress echocardiography lies in the standardization of quantitative parameters, the clinically justified selection of modules, the external validation of artificial intelligence algorithms, and incremental value of each new parameter.

title: Les affiches des Jeux olympiques d’été ou l’olympisme par lui-même (1896-2024)
title_original: Les affiches des Jeux olympiques d’été ou l’olympisme par lui-même (1896-2024)
summary: L’analyse comparée des affiches des Jeux olympiques permet de déceler dans cet outil de promotion diffusé largement quelques grandes tendances révélatrices de leur temps et des enjeux contemporains à chacun des événements. De fait, à la fin du xix e siècle et au début du xx e siècle, les Jeux olympiques modernes n’étaient pas, et de loin, le méga-événement médiatique qu’ils sont aujourd’hui. Ainsi, si les affiches initiales ont du mal à se dissocier des Expositions universelles, elles mettent ensuite en exergue la référence aux Jeux olympiques antiques par la présence du discobole et la dimension internationale de l’événement. Les plus récentes sont symptomatiques d’une modernité affichée par le biais de symboles et codes iconiques stylisés, rappelant la ville et le pays d’accueil. L’affiche des Jeux olympiques et paralympiques de Paris 2024 introduisant peut-être une nouvelle rupture dans la manière de présenter l’événement.

title: Deformation-enhanced fluid evolution and skarn–IOCG transition in the Paleoproterozoic Elaine Dorothy Cu–Au system, Mount Isa Inlier, Australia
title_original: Deformation-enhanced fluid evolution and skarn–IOCG transition in the Paleoproterozoic Elaine Dorothy Cu–Au system, Mount Isa Inlier, Australia
summary: Abstract The Elaine Dorothy Cu-Au deposit, located in the Mary Kathleen Domain of the Mount Isa Inlier, Australia, records the interaction of Paleoproterozoic skarn metasomatism, fluid evolution, and deformation. The deposit is hosted by carbonate- and calc-silicate-rich rocks of the Corella Formation and comprises diopside–garnet–scapolite–wollastonite ± amphibole assemblages associated with pyrrhotite–chalcopyrite–pyrite mineralisation. Field relationships and mineral textures indicate that sulphide deposition began during or shortly after prograde skarn formation and subsequently evolved from disseminated and vein-controlled to semi-massive, massive, and shear-zone-hosted mineralisation. LA-ICP-MS analyses of pyrite, pyrrhotite, chalcopyrite, and magnetite record systematic variation in trace-element compositions during this evolution. Early Py1 is enriched in Co and Se and displays Co/Sb–Se/As characteristics consistent with a magmatic-hydrothermal contribution. Se-in-pyrite thermometry yields formation temperatures of up to 544 ± 36 °C for the earliest stage, decreasing to approximately 323–417 °C in later Py1 and 342 ± 11 °C for Py2. The transition from Co-rich Py1 to Co-poor, Ni-enriched Py2, together with pyrrhotite-dominated assemblages and cross-cutting chalcopyrite–pyrrhotite textures, records progressive changes in fluid chemistry and conditions of sulphide stability. Variable magnetite trace-element compositions and brecciation further indicate repeated modification during continued fluid circulation. Structural relationships demonstrate that deformation enhanced permeability along the Mary Kathleen structural architecture, promoting fluid focusing, sulphide redistribution, and local concentration within retrograde alteration zones. We interpret Elaine Dorothy as a deformation-enhanced Paleoproterozoic calcic skarn that evolved toward a skarn–IOCG transitional system, rather than as a classic IOCG end member. The deposit demonstrates how deformation, fluid–rock interaction, and evolving redox–sulphur-fugacity conditions progressively modify an early calcic skarn framework, enhancing permeability and fluid focusing, and generating IOCG-affinity characteristics through continued hydrothermal reworking rather than a discrete IOCG-forming event. This provides a process-based framework for recognising structurally reworked skarn systems in Proterozoic mineral provinces.

title: The Deobandi Movement and the Reproduction of Political-Security Power in Pakistan
title_original: The Deobandi Movement and the Reproduction of Political-Security Power in Pakistan
summary: This article examines the role of the Deobandi movement in the reproduction of political-security power in Pakistan by moving beyond reductionist interpretations. The central question is through which institutional, discursive, and network-based mechanisms the Deobandi movement participates in processes of power reproduction. The theoretical framework is grounded in the concept of “power reproduction” and is formulated through the integration of historical institutionalism, symbolic capital theory, and discursive approaches to power. The research adopts a qualitative methodology based on historical-institutional analysis and discourse analysis, encompassing religious-political texts, educational literature, and the discourses of religious and political elites. The findings indicate that the network of religious seminaries, the authority of the ulama, and religious symbolic capital have provided an institutional infrastructure for social and political influence. In dynamic interaction with the state and security institutions, these elements have contributed to the production of legitimacy, the framing of threats, and social mobilization, without being reducible to mere instruments of the state. The internal heterogeneity of the movement further suggests that its connections with politics and jihadism are less inherent than they are products of specific historical and geopolitical contexts. The article concludes that security in Pakistan is not a purely material phenomenon but rather a social and discursive construct shaped through the interaction between the state and religious networks. Therefore, analyses of politics and security in Pakistan remain incomplete without considering the structural role of religious actors. By conceptualizing religion as a source of meaning, legitimacy, and mobilization, this study contributes to the literature on political Islam and security studies in postcolonial societies.

title: The Rise and Decline of the Paduspanians of Ruyan in Relation to the Zaydi Movement of Northern Iran
title_original: The Rise and Decline of the Paduspanians of Ruyan in Relation to the Zaydi Movement of Northern Iran
summary: The Paduspanians were a dynastic lineage whose rulers belonged to families claiming descent from the Sasanian Empire. This dynasty was established in 643 CE by Gil Gavbara and his son Paduspan I in the province of Ruyan, and its rule continued until 1597 CE. In 864 CE, the people of Ruyan and their Paduspanian ruler, Abdullah ibn Wanda Omid, who had become deeply dissatisfied with the oppression imposed by the representatives of the Tahirid governors of the Abbasid Caliphate, namely Muhammad ibn Abdallah al-Tahiri and Muhammad ibn Aws, sought assistance at the suggestion of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Kiya Dabiri from Hasan ibn Zayd, who himself had migrated to the city of Ray due to pressure from the Abbasid administration. The outcome of this request was the uprising and establishment of the Zaydi state in northern Iran in the same year, a polity that endured until 928 CE. The present study addresses the question of how the relations between the Paduspanian dynasty and the Zaydi movement were formed and developed. Based on the hypothesis that the Paduspanians played a significant and constructive role in this relationship, the study aims to examine the early interactions between these two political entities. Employing a descriptive–analytical method and relying on library-based data collection, this research analyzes and interprets the nature of these relations. The findings demonstrate that the Paduspanians played an initial and substantial role in the establishment and continuation of the Zaydi movement.

title: The Formation of the ISIS Takfiri Movement from the Perspective of Governance in Public Law
title_original: The Formation of the ISIS Takfiri Movement from the Perspective of Governance in Public Law
summary: The Middle East region has faced numerous challenges and security crises in recent years, particularly following the events of September 11, 2001, the effects of which have remained directly or indirectly embedded in the collective memory of nations, especially the peoples of the region. The expansionist ambitions of major powers in the region, combined with the ideological rigidity of certain Islamist political and religious factions, constitute one of the most significant factors that have intensified not only political conflicts but also sectarian tensions. The primary concern and research problem of the present study is to identify the central causes of insecurity and to trace its roots within the Middle East. The persistence of insecurity in countries such as Iraq and Syria has, in turn, contributed to the continuation of instability in neighboring states, including Iran, potentially generating adverse security consequences for the political system of the Islamic Republic of Iran. Consequently, determining appropriate approaches to addressing this issue has become a matter of serious intellectual and policy concern. Iraq has long been an influential actor in regional equations, and its critical role in the geopolitical competition among major powers cannot be overlooked, as many regional political transformations over approximately the past four decades have stemmed from developments within Iraq and from the prevailing political and security conditions in that country. This article seeks to analyze the role of regional and global actors in political dynamics and power cycles across different states and ultimately advances the argument that the insecurity observed in the region is the result of prolonged strategic interventions, exploitation of structural vulnerabilities within states, and financial as well as military support provided by powerful countries.

Consequently, determining appropriate approaches to addressing this issue has become a matter of serious intellectual and policy concern. Iraq has long been an influential actor in regional equations, and its critical role in the geopolitical competition among major powers cannot be overlooked, as many regional political transformations over approximately the past four decades have stemmed from developments within Iraq and from the prevailing political and security conditions in that country. This article seeks to analyze the role of regional and global actors in political dynamics and power cycles across different states and ultimately advances the argument that the insecurity observed in the region is the result of prolonged strategic interventions, exploitation of structural vulnerabilities within states, and financial as well as military support provided by powerful countries.

title: “I Am Neither a Criminal nor Am I a Terrorist”
title_original: “I Am Neither a Criminal nor Am I a Terrorist”
summary:
Abstract
                  This chapter examines how the New Sanctuary Movement emerged in post–September 11 America as faith communities responded to intensified immigration enforcement and a growing deportation regime. It traces the political and economic forces of the 1990s, including the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), restrictive legislation, and the rise of crimmigration that expanded border militarization, increased deportations, and deepened public anxiety about undocumented migrants. Through the case of Elvira Arellano, who sought sanctuary in a Chicago church to resist deportation and defend family unity, the chapter shows how religious activism revives sanctuary as moral protest. It analyzes the movement’s national expansion through faith-based coalitions, media advocacy, and family-centered framing while activists challenged mass deportations during the Obama administration. Finally, the chapter evaluates the movement’s continuing role as a faith-based defense against family separation and anticipates renewed sanctuary activism after Donald Trump’s 2016 election reshaped immigration politics.

title: “Guilty of the Gospel”
title_original: “Guilty of the Gospel”
summary:
Abstract
                  This chapter examines the federal prosecution of the Sanctuary Movement between 1985 and 1991, focusing on raids against religious activists such as Sister Darlene Nicgorski and the government’s effort to portray sanctuary as a criminal conspiracy rather than a faith-based defense of Central American refugees fleeing U.S.-supported violence. It traces the counterattack mounted by federal authorities, conservative religious networks, and immigration restrictionists who depict sanctuary activism as unlawful defiance of immigration enforcement. The chapter then examines Operation Sojourner and the Phoenix sanctuary trial, where surveillance, informants, and judicial rulings exclude religious motivations and refugee testimony from the defense. It shows that the convictions unexpectedly expand public sympathy, intensify national media attention, and accelerate the growth of congregational sanctuaries and municipal sanctuary policies. Finally, the chapter traces how sanctuary activism shapes policy outcomes, including Temporary Protected Status provisions and the American Baptist Churches v. Thornburgh asylum settlement.

title: “No Middle Ground Between Collaboration and Resistance”
title_original: “No Middle Ground Between Collaboration and Resistance”
summary:
Abstract
                  This chapter traces the Sanctuary Movement’s emergence in the 1980s, opening with the Sisters of St. Joseph in Concordia, Kansas, who convert their convent into a refuge for Guatemalan refugees and seed a “new underground railroad” carrying asylum seekers to Midwestern sanctuaries. It documents how Bay Area congregations—galvanized by Archbishop Óscar Romero’s assassination and delegations to Central America—form interfaith coalitions that combine legal aid, housing, and public witness. The chapter shows how the Chicago Religious Task Force scales sanctuary nationally by producing training seminars, handbooks, Basta!, and coordinated conduits while debating humanitarian accompaniment versus public pressure. It analyzes internal fractures—Tucson’s border-first, unconditional aid versus Chicago’s strategy of testimony, public pressure, and legal framing as civil disobedience or Jim Corbett’s civil initiative—detailing key actors, numbers, and risks faced by clergy and refugees. Finally, the chapter situates sanctuary as an interfaith movement that amplifies refugee leadership, challenges paternalism, and anticipates federal scrutiny.

title: “La Migra No Profana el Santuario”
title_original: “La Migra No Profana el Santuario”
summary:
Abstract
                  This chapter recounts the July 5, 1980, Sonoran Desert crossing that killed thirteen Salvadorans, follows survivors’ escape from U.S.-backed repression, and shows how Cold War politics and asylum adjudication conspire to deny protection. It locates that crisis within borderland economic shifts—the end of the Bracero Program, maquiladora expansion, and financial dislocation—and ties U.S. intervention in Central America to emerging “crimmigration” frameworks. The chapter chronicles how Tucson organizations, legal advocates, and liberation theology–inspired clergy (Manzo, the Tucson Ecumenical Council, Jim Corbett, John Fife, and others) organized clandestine rescue, shelter, and legal assistance while mounting public campaigns. It describes Southside Presbyterian’s March 24, 1982, sanctuary declaration—banners, public witness, and deliberate publicity—that reframed hospitality as civil disobedience and catalyzed a nationwide sanctuary movement. Finally, the chapter contends that Tucson’s sanctuary converts theological compassion into principled resistance, compels an urgent national reckoning over U.S. foreign and immigration policy, and models faith-based defense of persecuted peoples.

title: The Social Lives of Early Caddo Pottery
title_original: The Social Lives of Early Caddo Pottery
summary:
In this book, Shawn Lambert examines pottery made by the Caddo people on the western fringes of Mississippian culture in North America from 1000 to 1250 CE, revealing a society that was more sophisticated, connected, and influential than previously understood. Lambert traces pottery from its production through exchange, deposition, museum curation, and living Indigenous practice to show that these objects have had dynamic, nonlinear social trajectories across communities, regions, centuries, and cultures.

During this period, Caddo potters developed distinctive new forms, including bottles, beakers, seed jars, and carinated bowls. These finely crafted vessels featured thin walls, polished surfaces, intricate engraved designs, and red and white pigments, and are considered some of the most technically sophisticated ceramics in North America. Lambert discusses new analyses that challenge long-standing assumptions about where Caddo pottery was made and how far potters traveled. He shows these vessels were used in a range of settings and were traded widely among neighboring cultures. The book concludes with a chapter coauthored by contemporary Caddo potter Chase Kahwinhut Earles that explores how traditional pottery-making is being revived and sustained by descendant communities today.

title: Compound interpretation is based on analogy
title_original: Compound interpretation is based on analogy
summary: How compound meanings are best predicted from constituent meanings remains a central question in computational models of lexical semantics. Comparing different computational models provides a way to evaluate alternative accounts of how semantic information is combined during compound comprehension. We propose a new model, the Compound Analogy Model (CAM), that predicts a compound's embedding by adding its constituent embeddings together with the average shift vectors of the two constituents' compound families. The resulting model is parameter-free and exploits local analogical structure in the semantic space. We evaluated CAM against the CAOSS model on Mandarin Chinese compounds. CAM consistently achieved higher prediction accuracy than CAOSS on both training and held-out data, with the exception of three-character compounds, for which analogical generalization is constrained by both small constituent families and a pronounced imbalance in family size between the two constituents. The advantage of CAM remained when evaluation was based on frequency-defined train-test splits that better approximate generalization from familiar to novel compounds. To assess the cognitive plausibility of the two models, we further examined whether model-derived semantic measures predict visual lexical decision latencies for two-character compounds. Predictors derived from CAM provided improved prediction for response latencies compared to predictors derived from the CAOSS model. These findings indicate that compound meaning is better characterized as local analogical generalization than as the application of a learned global linear transformation, and demonstrate that analogical semantic structure provides a cognitively plausible basis for compound comprehension.
