title: Beyond Time Loss: Position-Specific Injury-to-Performance Pathways After Hand Fractures in Elite European Football
title_original: Beyond Time Loss: Position-Specific Injury-to-Performance Pathways After Hand Fractures in Elite European Football
summary: Background: Hand fractures are common sports injuries, but the same diagnosis may carry different performance consequences according to how essential the hand is to a player's role.We investigated whether fracture burden and the broader injury-to-performance pathway differed by playing position, from injury phenotype and acute absence to competitive reintegration and sustained participation.Materials and methods: This retrospective matched cohort study linked manually validated public injury reports with league appearances from the five major leagues, Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga, and Ligue 1 from 2007/08 through 2024/25.Of 35,952 injury records, 329 candidate records with possible hand or wrist injuries (0.9%) were reviewed, from which 148 fracture events (45.0% of candidates) in 142 players were retained.Primary analyses compared incidence, time loss, competitive return, and one-year participation after the publicly reported injury end.Exploratory analyses tested position-specific fracture phenotype and the time period from the public injury-end milestone to first subsequent appearance in one of the five major leagues.Results: Fracture phenotype differed by position (chi-square = 21.48,P < .001;Cramér's V = 0.38): finger/phalangeal fractures accounted for 31 of 63 goalkeeper events (49.2%) versus 15 of 85 outfield events (17.6%) (odds ratio (OR), 4.52; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.15-9.52),whereas metacarpal fractures accounted for 10 of 63 goalkeeper events (15.9%) versus 34 of 85 outfield events (40.0%) (OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.13-0.63).Goalkeepers faced greater time loss than outfielders, even within the same fracture subtype (position-by-subtype interaction, P = .407).Median time loss was 43 days among 63 goalkeeper events versus 18 days among 85 outfield events (adjusted ratio, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.58-2.79).By 90 days, 17 of 45 goalkeepers (37.8%) versus 55 of 68 outfield players (80.9%) had reappeared competitively.Of 103 fracture episodes with an observed appearance after the reported injury end, 14 of 35 goalkeeper episodes (40.0%) versus seven of 68 outfield episodes (10.3%) required more than 90 additional days to reappear (aOR, 6.94; 95% CI, 2.06-23.41;false discovery rate-adjusted q = .005).In the matched cohort, a 30% or greater participation decline occurred in 10 of 18 goalkeeper fracture cases (55.6%) versus 21 of 72 goalkeeper controls (29.2%)(aOR, 3.30; 95% CI, 1.08-10.08),with a fracture-by-goalkeeper interaction OR of 5.74 (95% CI, 1.46-22.66);this interaction estimate was based on a small subgroup of 18 goalkeeper fracture cases.Conclusions: The important positional signal extends beyond the already expected higher fracture incidence in goalkeepers.Playing position was associated with differences in fracture phenotype, acute burden, the transition from the publicly reported injury-end milestone to subsequent competitive selection, and subsequent participation.Return-to-play counseling should therefore distinguish the publicly reported injury-end milestone from subsequent competitive reintegration and incorporate role-specific hand function rather than calendar time alone.

title: دراسة تحليلية لواقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية
title_original: دراسة تحليلية لواقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية
summary: هدف البحث الى بناء وتطبيق مقياس واقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية، والتعرف على واقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية. وانتهج الباحث المنهج الوصفي بالأسلوب المسحي لملاءمته طبيعة المشكلة، وتم اختيار مجتمع البحث من مدرسي التربية الرياضية في مديرية تربية الرصافة الثالثة وعددهم (420) مدرس ومدرسة، اما عينة البحث فتكونت من (200) مدرس ومدرسة التربية الرياضية، اي بنسبة (47.61%) من مجتمع البحث. وتم تقسيم العينة الى ثلاث عينات: عينة التجربة الاستطلاعية، عينة البناء، عينة التطبيق. بعدها قام الباحث ببناء مقياس واقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية على وفق ما يلي :تم صياغة عدد من العبارات الخاصة بمقياس المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية للحصول على النتائج وبما يتلائم وطبيعة عمل مجتمع البحث وعددها (25) عبارة. وبعد الإجراءات التي تم ذكرها، قام الباحث بأجراء التجربة الاستطلاعية على عينة من (15) فرد، في (14/01/2025)، لغرض تهيئة الظروف المناسبة عند تطبيق الاختبار الرئيسي. بعدها تم تطبيق المقياس على عينة البناء البالغ عددها (95) فرداً وذلك للمدة من (21/1/2025) لغاية (2/2/2025) وإن الغرض من إجراء هذه التجربة هو بناء مقياس واقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية. واستقر المقياس بصيغته النهائية على (25) عبارة. وبعد ان تم بناء المقياس قام الباحث بتطبيق صورة المقياس النهائية على عينة البحث والبالغ عددها (90) فرداً، وذلك للمدة من (5/3/2025) ولغاية (2/4/2025). بعدها تم مناقشة النتائج ورفدها بالمصادر العلمية.

title: The association between data-driven training monitoring and athlete burnout: a chain-mediated indirect path between performance anxiety and psychological exhaustion
title_original: The association between data-driven training monitoring and athlete burnout: a chain-mediated indirect path between performance anxiety and psychological exhaustion
summary: Introduction Data-driven training monitoring has enhanced the precision of training-load assessment, fatigue detection, and training regulation in competitive sport. However, continuous data collection, performance metric comparisons, and evaluative feedback may also constitute emerging sources of psychological stress for athletes. Drawing on the Technology Stress Generators Model, the Challenge–Hindrance Stressor Framework, and the Job Demands–Resources Model, this study examined the relationships among data-driven training monitoring stress (DTMS), evaluative anxiety, psychological exhaustion, and athlete burnout, as well as potential differences across gender and sport type. Methods Cross-sectional questionnaire data were collected from 588 active athletes. Confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling, bootstrap tests of indirect effects, and multigroup analysis were conducted to examine the hypothesized relationships and between-group differences. Results DTMS was significantly and positively associated with evaluative anxiety, psychological exhaustion, and athlete burnout. Evaluative anxiety and psychological exhaustion each constituted a significant indirect pathway between DTMS and athlete burnout, and the sequential indirect pathway through evaluative anxiety and psychological exhaustion was also statistically significant. Multigroup analysis further showed significant between-group differences in the association between DTMS and evaluative anxiety. This association was stronger among female athletes than among male athletes and stronger among athletes in physical endurance sports than among those in skill-based sports. Discussion The findings suggest that data-driven training monitoring should extend beyond the technical objectives of data acquisition and assessment accuracy to incorporate psychologically informed practices. Particular attention should be given to the interpretation of monitoring data, the communication of anomalous indicators, and the delivery of evaluative feedback to reduce the psychological burden potentially associated with data-intensive monitoring.

title: Sporda Çocukluk Dönemi Kötü Muamele Ölçeği (ÇDSKMÖ): Geçerlik ve Güvenirlik Çalışması
title_original: Sporda Çocukluk Dönemi Kötü Muamele Ölçeği (ÇDSKMÖ): Geçerlik ve Güvenirlik Çalışması
summary: Bu çalışmanın amacı, bireylerin çocukluk dönemindeki spor yaşantılarında deneyimledikleri kötü muamele davranışlarını retrospektif olarak değerlendirmeye yönelik geçerli ve güvenilir bir ölçme aracı geliştirmek ve geliştirilen Çocukluk Dönemi Sporda Kötü Muamele Ölçeği’nin (ÇDSKMÖ) psikometrik özelliklerini incelemektir. Araştırma metodolojik ölçek geliştirme deseninde yürütülmüştür. Olasılıklı olmayan uygun örnekleme yoluyla, 18 yaşından önce spora katılmış ve spor bilimleri alanında öğrenim gören 400 genç yetişkine ulaşılmıştır. Veri seti açımlayıcı faktör analizi (AFA) ve doğrulayıcı faktör analizi (DFA) için 200’er kişilik iki bağımsız gruba rastgele ayrılmıştır. Alan yazın taramasıyla oluşturulan 56 maddelik havuz, uzman değerlendirmeleri ve ön deneme sonrasında 52 maddeye indirilmiştir. AFA sonucunda duygusal istismar, cinsel istismar, fiziksel istismar, ihmal ve akran zorbalığı alt ölçeklerinin her birinin tek boyutlu yapı gösterdiği ve nihai formun 45 maddeden oluştuğu belirlenmiştir. Faktör yükleri 0,658–0,905, açıklanan varyans oranları %52,371–%72,183 ve Cronbach alfa katsayıları 0,884–0,938 arasında değişmiştir. Bağımsız örneklemde yürütülen DFA, beş alt ölçekli yapıyı ve alt ölçeklerin ortak bir üst yapı altında değerlendirilmesini desteklemiştir (χ²/sd=0,65; RMSEA=0,005; NFI=0,96; CFI=0,99; GFI=0,98). Sonuçlar, ÇDSKMÖ’nün bireylerin çocukluk dönemindeki spor yaşantılarında deneyimledikleri kötü muamele davranışlarını davranış temelli ve çok boyutlu biçimde retrospektif olarak değerlendirmede kullanılabilecek geçerli ve güvenilir bir öz-bildirim aracı olduğunu göstermektedir.

title: International sport policy meets national cultures: reinterpreting qualitative interview data to understand Safe Sport implementation
title_original: International sport policy meets national cultures: reinterpreting qualitative interview data to understand Safe Sport implementation
summary: With challenges related to interpersonal violence in sport as a backdrop, this paper examines how cultural institutions operate across societal contexts and what this means for Safe Sport implementation in six European Mediterranean countries: Cyprus, Greece, Italy, Malta, Portugal and Spain. In an earlier study, interviews with individuals educating and recruiting coaches (n = 60, 10 from each country) and thematic analysis identified three institutions that constrain Safe Sport implementation: patriarchy, a winning (at-all-costs) attitude and an orientation towards blindness and silence. In this paper, we conduct a theory-driven secondary analysis of the same data, understanding institutions as three pillars(regulative, normative and cultural-cognitive) to examine how these institutions are carried and reproduced across three carriers of interrelated contexts: the state, the family and sport. The analysis demonstrates that the states’ weak regulative role allows these institutions to function, families socialise their members into accepting them and in sport they operate largely unchallenged. For Safe Sport implementation to progress, several carriers of institutions must change relatively simultaneously. States must provide not only laws but protection systems for those who report harm; families must socialise children to recognise and speak about unacceptable behaviour; and sport organisations need structures that support rather than penalise disclosure.

title: Governing through narrative: rethinking EDI and Indigeneity in Canadian sport policy
title_original: Governing through narrative: rethinking EDI and Indigeneity in Canadian sport policy
summary: Canadian National Sport Organisations (NSOs) have increasingly adopted equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) policies as markers of ethical governance. Yet little attention has been paid to how these policies understand Indigeneity within a settler colonial context. This study examines 21 publicly available EDI policies from 19 federally funded Canadian NSOs to analyse how Indigenous peoples are represented across 5 dimensions: discourse, knowledge, relationships, political recognition, and governance. Drawing on critical policy analysis informed by settler colonial theory, we show that while Indigenous peoples are routinely acknowledged within organisational commitments to inclusion, they are rarely recognised as rights-bearing peoples with distinct political authority or jurisdiction. Instead, they are incorporated into broad administrative categories that obscure Indigenous histories, governance relationships, and nationhood. Across all 5 dimensions, the policies privilege recognition and participation over the redistribution of authority and shared governance. These findings suggest that EDI policies function less as mechanisms of structural transformation than as organisational narratives that stabilise existing institutional arrangements. The discussion argues that advancing reconciliation in sport will require moving beyond inclusion towards governance approaches grounded in Indigenous rights, jurisdiction, and shared authority, while also developing the critical theoretical capacity needed to interpret competing legal, political, and institutional responsibilities.

title: Freelance dance artists’ experiences of managing career challenges: insights into mental skills training from artists and practitioners
title_original: Freelance dance artists’ experiences of managing career challenges: insights into mental skills training from artists and practitioners
summary: Freelance dance artists (FDAs) need to manage major career challenges that could jeopardise their mental well-being. Even though research in sport implies that psychologically informed practitioners (PIPs) and mental skills training (MST) could offer FDAs valuable support in addressing these demands, little is known on how dancers use mental skills training to manage career challenges, and how practitioners support them to cope with these pressures. To address these gaps, this study explored FDAs’ experiences in managing career challenges, how mental skills development informed their experiences, and how PIPs supported dancers in navigating these challenges. Eight FDAs and eight PIPs were recruited for online semi-structured interviews. Underpinned by a pragmatic stance, data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Three themes were generated: (1) Getting ready to address the challenges: (re)connecting to thoughts and emotions through metacognition, (2) It felt quite empowering: managing career challenges through self-regulation, and (3) Seeing the bigger picture: reaping benefits beyond the dance context. Findings suggest that MST in dance is a personal‑and‑interpersonal practice with potentially life-enhancing benefits increasing dancers’ mental well-being. PIPs played an important role in dancers’ mental skills development, and supported them in enhancing mental qualities that are transferable beyond the dance context. This study and the creative tools used to generate the data advances our understanding of MST in dance and suggests including interpersonal dimensions in future work.

title: Optimizing the Transformation of Lex Sportiva into Local Regulations to Achieve Good Sports Governance in Bekasi City
title_original: Optimizing the Transformation of Lex Sportiva into Local Regulations to Achieve Good Sports Governance in Bekasi City
summary: Lex Sportiva is a transnational normative order produced by sports organizations, federation rules, and arbitral practice. Its norms do not automatically operate as municipal public law. This normative legal study examines how selected Lex Sportiva principles may be received and harmonized within Bekasi City sports regulations without displacing mandatory national law. The study uses statutory and conceptual approaches and qualitatively compares Law No. 11 of 2022 on Sports, Presidential Regulation No. 86 of 2021 on the National Sports Grand Design, Bekasi City Regional Regulation No. 5 of 2019, Bekasi Mayor Regulation No. 50 of 2020, and Bekasi Mayor Regulation No. 6 of 2022 against a consolidated framework covering lawful organizational autonomy, integrity and fair play, accountable governance, athlete protection, and accessible dispute resolution. Interviews and focus-group discussions mentioned in the research record are treated only as contextual expert consultation because participant-level and ethics documentation was not available for reproducible empirical reporting. The analysis finds that Bekasi already has a sectoral regulatory foundation, but the reviewed instruments do not transparently establish a complete, integrated good-sports-governance architecture. Reform should therefore proceed through selective reception: each transnational standard must be screened for municipal competence, compatibility with superior law and public policy, institutional feasibility, and procedural safeguards. The study contributes a non-quantitative, provision-by-provision legal screening model and rejects automatic incorporation, an arbitrary compliance threshold, and an unsupported municipal equivalent of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

title: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN NUTRITIONAL KNOWLEDGE, DIETARY HABITS, AND ATHLETIC PERFORMANCE AMONG UNIVERSITY ATHLETES
title_original: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN NUTRITIONAL KNOWLEDGE, DIETARY HABITS, AND ATHLETIC PERFORMANCE AMONG UNIVERSITY ATHLETES
summary: The nutrition of athletes is an essential component of their preparation, recovery, and performance. The objective of this study was to explore the connection between knowledge of nutrition, diet, and sports performance among university athletes. The selected research design was quantitative cross-sectional, which was conducted on 200 University Athletes. The data were collected with the help of a structured questionnaire and analysed using SPSS. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression were used. Nutritional knowledge was significantly correlated with athletic performance (r = .154, p = .030), and dietary habits were also significantly correlated with athletic performance (r = .209, p = .003). There was a significant correlation between nutritional knowledge and dietary habits (r = .231, p = .001). The overall model was significant (F(2,197) = 5.777, p = .004; R2 = .55%) using regression analysis. There was a significant effect of dietary habits, but not of nutritional knowledge itself, on performance.

title: Evidence for the Effectiveness of the Performance Passport Within an Intelligence‐Based Weightlifting Anti‐Doping Programme
title_original: Evidence for the Effectiveness of the Performance Passport Within an Intelligence‐Based Weightlifting Anti‐Doping Programme
summary: Anti-doping organisations are tasked with detecting, deterring and preventing doping in sport, and because biological testing consumes a large share of budgets, efficient resource allocation is essential. Enhancing effectiveness requires better insight into how well current methods identify athletes at risk. The International Testing Agency (ITA) recently introduced the Athlete Performance Passport (APP), which uses competition performance data to flag at-risk weightlifters for targeted testing. This study evaluates the APP alongside established approaches, including Athlete Passport Management Unit (APMU) recommendations and atypical findings from the steroidal module of the Athlete Biological Passport (ABP). Data from 1960 male and 1583 female athletes were analysed, identifying 175 individuals (109 male and 66 female) who committed an Article 2.1 Anti-Doping Rule Violation (ADRV) between December 2009 and April 2025. The study assessed how effectively each method identified these athletes. Overall, the APP detected 34% of athletes who committed ADRVs during this period. Focusing on data since the steroidal passport's introduction in 2014, the APP identified 30% of ADRVs, outperforming APMU suspicious reports (17%) and atypical ABP steroidal profiles (10%). When combined, these methods identified 38% of ADRVs. These findings indicate that performance-based monitoring can strengthen anti-doping risk assessment and improve targeted testing strategies, particularly in sports with comprehensive competition data.

title: Kano-IPA-based post-occupancy evaluation of an urban sports park for active health: a case study in Mianyang, China
title_original: Kano-IPA-based post-occupancy evaluation of an urban sports park for active health: a case study in Mianyang, China
summary: Against the backdrop of “Healthy China” and urban renewal, urban sports parks are critical public spaces for promoting residents’ active health. Taking Sanjiang Sports Park in Mianyang as a case, this study used a mixed-methods approach integrating Post-Occupancy Evaluation (POE) with the Kano–IPA model to evaluate spatial performance and health service functions. Based on 236 valid questionnaires, the results showed that user-oriented facility planning, safety design, and age-inclusive configuration significantly improved usage willingness and experience satisfaction. Core shortcomings included insufficient access convenience, rest facilities, and age-friendly facilities for the elderly and children. Targeted design and refined management can effectively enhance user perception, and a tiered governance model helps improve the health service capacity of public spaces. This study enriches the POE framework of sports parks and provides a reference for the optimization of health-oriented public spaces.

title: Visualising and Theorising Physical Activity Through Photography and Sociology: Reflections on a Collaborative Interdisciplinary Teaching Initiative
title_original: Visualising and Theorising Physical Activity Through Photography and Sociology: Reflections on a Collaborative Interdisciplinary Teaching Initiative
summary: This article considers interdisciplinary collaboration in higher education. We reflect on a pilot project teaching across the Departments of Kinesiology and Art and Design at California State University Northridge in the United States. Two final-year online courses in sports sociology and photography were combined over a four-week period. Students were combined into one class, and interaction across disciplines was required. Students engaged in new materials from both disciplines. We argue for the need for kinesiology and art to consider cross-disciplinary collaboration and reflect on our experience.

title: An Analysis of University Students’ Attitudes Toward Healthy Eating
title_original: An Analysis of University Students’ Attitudes Toward Healthy Eating
summary: This study aimed to examine the attitudes towards healthy eating among students of the Faculty of Sports Sciences at Mardin Artuklu University. The research was conducted using a survey model, a quantitative research method, and included a total of 315 university students (127 women and 188 men) who voluntarily participated. A personal information form and the Healthy Eating Attitude Scale were used as data collection tools. The data obtained were evaluated using independent samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and Pearson correlation analysis. According to the research findings, female students' scores were found to be higher than male students only in the “Poor Eating (KB)” sub-dimension. Regarding the age variable, it was determined that students aged 26 and over had lower total scores on the Knowledge About Nutrition (BHB), Positive Eating (OB), KB, and Healthy Eating Attitude Scale (SBITO) scales compared to younger groups. Regarding housing status, students living in dormitories had higher total SBITO scores than those living in family homes. Regarding class level, a significant difference was found only in the “BHB” sub-dimension; however, a significant difference was found in the “Feelings About Nutrition (BYD)” sub-dimension in the smoking variable. It was determined that students who did not engage in physical activity had higher “BYD” scores than those who did. abstract: This study aimed to examine the attitudes towards healthy eating among students of the Faculty of Sports Sciences at Mardin Artuklu University. The research was conducted using a survey model, a quantitative research method, and included a total of 315 university students (127 women and 188 men) who voluntarily participated. A personal information form and the Healthy Eating Attitude Scale were used as data collection tools. The data obtained were evaluated using independent samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and Pearson correlation analysis. According to the research findings, female students' scores were found to be higher than male students only in the “Poor Eating (KB)” sub-dimension. title: Effects of low dose caffeinated coffee consumption on energy system contributions and repeated sprint indices in combat sports athletes
title_original: Effects of low dose caffeinated coffee consumption on energy system contributions and repeated sprint indices in combat sports athletes
summary: Caffeine research has mostly examined anhydrous capsules between 3 and 13 mg·kg − 1 , doses of 3 mg·kg − 1 and above generally have ergogenic effects. Little is known about doses of 3 mg·kg − 1 or below given as coffee, the form athletes usually consume. Therefore, the present study compared two low doses within the same form; the acute effects of 1.5 and 3 mg·kg − 1 of caffeine as regular coffee against a decaffeinated coffee as placebo on repeated sprint performance and energy system contributions. No anhydrous caffeine form was included, so this was not a coffee vs. capsule comparison. Fifteen national level male combat sports athletes (age 20.4 ± 1.6 years; height 176.3 ± 4.1 cm; body mass 68.1 ± 5.9 kg) completed three sessions with 48 h interval in a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized crossover design. Repeated sprint test was conducted on a cycle ergometer one hour after supplementation; peak and mean power, fatigue index, perceived exertion, delta lactate, peak heart rate and estimated energy system contributions were measured. No statistically significant differences detected between the conditions in any performance related variable (all p > 0.05) or in estimated energy system contributions. The effect sizes were consistently small (η 2 p ≤ 0.01) for performance metrics; however, effect sizes were medium to large for estimated energy system contributions. However, the results of model-based estimation did not show any statistically significant difference between the conditions. No statistically significant changes were detected between the placebo, 1.5 and 3 mg·kg − 1 conditions for any performance, physiological or energy system variables. Future research should aim to evaluate possible effects with a larger sample, including both male and female athletes across different age groups and training levels. Registration of Clinical Trial : The randomized controlled trial registration with the ID: NCT07596511.

title: Musculoskeletal Injury Incidence Among US Military Academy and Reserve Officer Training Corps Cadets: A Scoping Review
title_original: Musculoskeletal Injury Incidence Among US Military Academy and Reserve Officer Training Corps Cadets: A Scoping Review
summary: CONTEXT: Musculoskeletal injuries (MSKI) are a leading cause of limited-duty days and attrition among United States (US) service members (SMs). Nearly half of SMs sustain a MSKI each year, which has long-term impacts on SM health and wellbeing. Despite their similar physical and operational demands, the epidemiology of MSKI among US Service Academy (SA) and Reserve Officers' Training Corps (ROTC) cadets, a key precommissioning cohort, remains poorly characterized. The objective of this review was to map and synthesize available evidence describing the incidence and distribution of MSKI among US cadets and evaluate the strength of evidence across studies. EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: A scoping review was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Eligible studies included English-language, US-based observational research involving cadets at SAs or ROTC programs. Searches were completed in PubMed, CINAHL, and Scopus through July 2025. Injury type, frequency, body region, and sex-specific incidence were extracted from each paper when available. Injury incidence was standardized per 1000 person-weeks to allow comparison across studies. Quality of evidence was appraised using the GRADE framework. STUDY DESIGN: Scoping review with quantitative incidence standardization and qualitative synthesis; GRADE ratings across included studies. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3. RESULTS: A total of 34 studies met inclusion criteria, representing 27 to 24,501 cadets per cohort. Average MSKI incidence among SA cadets was 53.7 injuries per 1000 person-weeks, and 30.6 injuries per 1000 person-weeks among ROTC cadets. Lower extremity injuries predominated, with higher rates among female cadets. Evidence quality was rated as moderate in 10 studies, low in 16, and very low in 8. CONCLUSION: Cadets experience MSKI at rates similar to active-duty personnel, particularly during initial military training. These findings establish a benchmark for future injury prevention and readiness research and emphasize the importance of clinical injury surveillance protocols.Strength-of-Recommendation Taxonomy (SORT):B. Recommendation based on inconsistent or limited-quality patient-oriented evidence.

title: Professionalization of coaches in performance-oriented sport for athletes with visual impairments: a qualitative study
title_original: Professionalization of coaches in performance-oriented sport for athletes with visual impairments: a qualitative study
summary: Introduction Coaching athletes with visual impairments (VI) involves distinct pedagogical, sport-specific, and organizational demands. However, research on the professionalization of coaches in Paralympic sport remains scarce. This study explores qualifications, experiences, attitudes, and contextual conditions relevant to coaching in this setting. Methods Semi-structured expert interviews were conducted with four experienced coaches working in blind football, goalball, judo, and rowing at a German Paralympic training center. Transcripts were analyzed using structuring qualitative content analysis with an inductive–deductive category-development approach. Results Five interrelated dimensions emerged: pathways and motivations for Paralympic coaching, qualifications and competencies, coaching philosophy, institutional conditions, and sport-specific adaptations. Formal qualifications provide an important basis, but disability-specific expertise was primarily acquired through practical experience and self-directed learning. Empathy, flexible communication, individualized motor-learning strategies, and trust-based yet performance-oriented coach athlete relationships were central to practice. Limited resources, informal entry pathways, and insufficient specialist education constrained professionalization. Conclusions Coaching in performance-oriented sport for athletes with VI requires more than theory-based licenses. Practice-oriented, disability- and sport-specific education, mentoring, and the systematic transfer of experiential knowledge are needed. Stronger institutional support and collaboration among schools, clubs, and federations may promote sustainable coaching structures and equitable athlete development in Paralympic sport.

title: Comparative effects of suspension-based and dynamometer-based isometric training on neuromuscular performance in trained male athletes: a randomized comparative study
title_original: Comparative effects of suspension-based and dynamometer-based isometric training on neuromuscular performance in trained male athletes: a randomized comparative study
summary: Objectives Isometric strength training is widely used to enhance athletic performance and support rehabilitation. However, few studies compare the effects of dynamometer-based and suspension-based isometric training on performance, and the effects of these methods remain unclear. This study compares the effects of dynamometer-based and suspension-based isometric training on muscle asymmetry, balance, estimated maximal strength, anaerobic power, and isokinetic strength in trained male athletes. Methods This study included 16 healthy male athletes aged 18 to 21 years (mean age: 18.81 ± 1.16 years; height: 178.06 ± 4.65 cm; body weight: 74.25 ± 4.32 kg; BMI: 23.43 ± 1.24 kg/m 2 ; body fat: 14.29 ± 1.55%). Participants were randomly assigned to either the TRX-based isometric training group (TRG, n=8) or the dynamometer-based isometric training group (DTG, n=8). Both groups performed isometric strength training based on the principle of progressive overload for eight weeks. The TRG group completed a predetermined series of four exercises three days per week. In contrast, the DTG group performed 6-second isometric contraction series in both flexion and extension positions for each leg three days per week. We assessed data normality using the Shapiro-Wilk test and calculated the mean and standard deviation. The relationship between pre-test and post-test measurements in the TRG and DTG groups was analyzed using a two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA; time × group); the level of statistical significance was set at p <.05. Results A significant main effect of time from the pretest to the posttest was found for the parameters of isokinetic peak torque, OSI, MLI, peak power, average power, and estimated 1RM (p <.05). In contrast, no significant main effect of time was observed for muscle asymmetry, API, and time to reach peak power (p>.05). Furthermore, it was stated that neither the group effect nor the time × group interaction showed a statistically significant effect on any of the performance parameters (p>.05). Conclusion In conclusion, while an eight-week TRX and dynamometer-based isometric training program resulted in significant changes in selected strength, balance, and anaerobic power parameters attributable to the main effect of time, no significant changes were observed in group effects or time × group interactions for any of the measured parameters.

title: EFEKTIVITAS SENAM LANTAI DALAM MENINGKATKAN KESEIMBANGAN DAN KELENTURAN TUBUH SISWA SMAN 1 DEMON PAGONG
title_original: EFEKTIVITAS SENAM LANTAI DALAM MENINGKATKAN KESEIMBANGAN DAN KELENTURAN TUBUH SISWA SMAN 1 DEMON PAGONG
summary: This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of floor gymnastics exercises in improving the balance and flexibility of students at SMAN 1 Demon Pagong. This study employed a quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design. The research sample consisted of 20 tenth-grade students selected based on predefined criteria. The research instruments comprised the stork stand test to assess static balance and the sit-and-reach test to measure lower-body and trunk flexibility. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro-Wilk normality test, the paired sample t-test, and effect size calculation (Cohen's d). The results indicated that the average static balance performance increased from 12.45 seconds to 21.78 seconds (t(19)=18.42; p<0.001; Cohen's d = 4.12), while the average body flexibility improved from 24.10 cm to 32.65 cm (t(19)=16.75; p<0.001; Cohen's d = 3.74). These findings rejected the null hypothesis (H_0) and accepted the alternative hypothesis (H_a). Consequently, structured floor gymnastics training can significantly improve students' balance and flexibility within the evaluated group. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui efektivitas latihan senam lantai dalam meningkatkan keseimbangan dan kelenturan tubuh siswa SMAN 1 Demon Pagong. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain pre-experimental model one-group pretest-posttest design. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 20 siswa kelas X yang dipilih secara terarah sesuai kriteria penelitian. Instrumen yang digunakan adalah stork stand test untuk mengukur keseimbangan statis dan sit-and-reach test untuk mengukur kelenturan tubuh bagian bawah serta punggung. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan statistik deskriptif, uji normalitas Shapiro-Wilk, uji paired sample t-test, serta perhitungan ukuran efek (effect size). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata keseimbangan statis meningkat dari 12,45 detik menjadi 21,78 detik (t(19)=18,42; p<0,001; Cohen’s d = 4,12), sedangkan rata-rata kelenturan tubuh meningkat dari 24,10 cm menjadi 32,65 cm (t(19)=16,75; p<0,001; Cohen’s d = 3,74). Peningkatan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa hipotesis nol (H_0) ditolak dan hipotesis alternatif (H_a) diterima. Dengan demikian, penerapan latihan senam lantai terstruktur dapat meningkatkan keseimbangan dan kelenturan tubuh siswa secara signifikan pada kelompok yang diteliti.

title: Critical Animal Media Studies
title_original: Critical Animal Media Studies
summary: The year 2022 marked the 10th anniversary of the course Critical Animal Studies: Animals in Society, Culture and the Media at the Department of Communication and Media at Lund University. As the first initiative of its kind in Sweden, the course explores the shifting roles and positions of non-human animals in today’s complex societies. It aims to equip students with analytical tools to critically assess norms and structures that organise human-animal relations, along with their ethical, cultural, and social consequences. What started as a one-course offering driven by an idea has evolved into a decade-long project of education and emancipation for non- human animals. This anthology stands as a testament to the course’s impact, aiming to extend the rich discussions, debates, and insights cultivated beyond the classroom walls. This celebratory collection assembles writings from former students, instructors, and guest lecturers, delving into themes ranging from critical media analysis over activist strategies to pedagogical reflections. The anthology’s scope not only reflects the diverse facets of the course but also unveils the myriad, often subtle intersections between human-centered society and the lives of non-human animals.

title: Factors associated with potential doping behavior among Swedish combat sport athletes: a cross-sectional study
title_original: Factors associated with potential doping behavior among Swedish combat sport athletes: a cross-sectional study
summary: Introduction The global growth and commercialism in combat sports have resulted in practitioners using performance-enhancing substances such as androgenic anabolic steroids, diuretics, hormone modulators, or stimulants. To gain a competitive edge, pressure often makes experienced athletes more prone to doping. Despite global trends of doping in combat sports, there is an evident lack of knowledge on protective and risk factors related to doping behavior in combat sports athletes. This study aimed to investigate (i) the prevalence of potential doping behavior (PDB) in Swedish combat sport athletes, (ii) sexbased differences in PDB, and (iii) factors associated with PDB. Methods A crosssectional observational study was conducted using a digital survey approach. The study population consisted of 120 active male (age: 40.6 ± 13.0 years) and 45 female members (age: 40.6 ± 9.2 years) of combat sport clubs in Sweden. Two standardized questionnaires were used: (1) Knowledge of Doping Questionnaire (KD), and (2) Questionnaire on Substance Use (QSU). The data were analyzed using Binomial Logistic Regression analysis and Fisher's Exact Test. Results The prevalence of PDB was 9.7%. The logistic regression analysis showed “Training load” (OR = 1.005) and “Occasional tobacco use” (OR = 7.178) were positively associated with PDB. In other words, occasional tobacco users had over seven times higher odds of PDB compared to non-users. Also, each unit increase in training load slightly elevated the risk for PDB. Additionally, sexbased differences showed males as more prone to PDB compared to their female counterparts ( p = 0.007). All other covariates, including “Doping knowledge ,” “Daily tobacco use ,” “Trust in coach expertise in doping ” and “Competitive results ” were not significantly associated with PDB. Discussion In conclusion, for Swedish combat sport athletes, PDB was associated with higher training load and occasional tobacco use. Consequently, future antidoping interventions should address these identified associations in doping prevention programs.

title: Comparison of cooling methods for drug-induced hyperthermia in a pre-hospital and emergency department setting: a systematic review
title_original: Comparison of cooling methods for drug-induced hyperthermia in a pre-hospital and emergency department setting: a systematic review
summary: INTRODUCTION: Hyperthermia is a medical condition characterized by elevated body temperature above 39.0 °C due to imbalanced heat production and dissipation. Stimulant drugs such as cocaine and amfetamines, as well as intense physical exertion, commonly induce hyperthermia. In severe cases, hyperthermia presents life-threatening complications requiring immediate temperature reduction interventions. Management involves various cooling modalities that differ in efficacy and practicality within pre-hospital and emergency department settings. This systematic review evaluates and compares the efficacy of cooling modalities for managing drug-induced hyperthermia suitable for pre-hospital and emergency department settings. Due to the paucity of data on drug-induced hyperthermia, studies examining exercise-induced hyperthermia were also included to provide additional evidence on cooling efficacy. METHODS: A comprehensive search for cooling efficiency studies across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, CINAHL, APA PsycINFO, and SportDiscus from inception until October 2025, without language restrictions was conducted. Randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and case-based studies were included. Quality assessment utilized the GRADE approach for certainty of evidence, while the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and RoB 2.0 assessed risk of bias. Meta-analysis was performed when feasible. RESULTS: The search identified 6,920 citations, with 71 studies included in this systematic review comprising 1,932 patients treated with 12 different cooling modalities. Analysis demonstrated that an ice water immersion cooling rate of (0.169 ± 0.027 °C/min) and cold water immersion cooling rate of (0.162 ± 0.037 °C/min) achieved the highest cooling rates. Meta-analyses confirmed that cold water and ice water immersion were more effective than passive cooling. Ice water-soaked sheets or towels had a cooling rate of (0.121 ± 0.030 °C/min) and room temperature immersion a cooling rate of (0.089 ± 0.020 °C/min) produced adequate cooling rates, while all other cooling modalities proved inadequate as standalone treatments. DISCUSSION: Due to paucity of data on cooling methods specifically for drug-induced hyperthermia, this study incorporates data from exertional hyperthermia to inform treatment recommendations. Both populations share similar demographics and involve exertion as a primary or contributing factor, supporting the clinical relevance of this approach. However, important pathophysiological differences exist; in case of exertional heat stroke hyperthermia related to exertion improves as physical activity ceases, while stimulant-induced hyperthermia persists despite cessation of activity due to ongoing central drug effects. Although sedation can reduce physical activity in intoxicated patients, these patients often present with concurrent medical complications requiring simultaneous monitoring and treatment. CONCLUSION: When ice or cold water immersion is available, often at large events, and can be applied safely, this represents the preferred cooling method. For emergency and pre-hospital settings, ice water-soaked sheets or towels are a practical cooling method available to most emergency departments and pre-hospital settings to treat hyperthermic intoxicated patients that is less resource intensive than immersion techniques and maintains continuous patient monitoring capabilities. Given the limited data on drug-induced hyperthermia, further research should address these knowledge gaps and investigate combined cooling strategies and their practicality in pre-hospital and emergency department settings.

title_original: Looking Back, to Learn From Activist Histories
summary: The year 2022 marked the 10th anniversary of the course Critical Animal Studies: Animals in Society, Culture and the Media at the Department of Communication and Media at Lund University. title: Psychological characteristics of athletes on the Vietnamese national weightlifting team prior to the 2019 Asian Championships: a cross-sectional descriptive study
title_original: Psychological characteristics of athletes on the Vietnamese national weightlifting team prior to the 2019 Asian Championships: a cross-sectional descriptive study
summary: This cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted to evaluate the psychological characteristics of athletes in the Vietnamese National Weightlifting Team prior to the 2019 Asian Championships. The study participants included 17 elite athletes (9 males and 8 females) from the Vietnamese National Weightlifting Team. Standardized psychometric and specialized assessment instruments—including the Competitive Anxiety Inventory (CAH), Profile of Emotional States (PET), Sport Competition Anxiety Test (SCAT), and Psychological Reliability Assessment tests—were administered to assess health status, emotional states, competitive anxiety, and psychological stability. Given the cross-sectional nature of the dataset, the findings reflect specific pre-competition psychological states during that historical training macrocycle rather than a real-time profile of the current roster. The results indicated that the participants exhibited varying levels of pre-competition psychological activation; while general health status and positive emotional indicators showed stable baseline parameters, specific markers of competitive anxiety and emotional regulation varied among the athletes. Due to the limited sample size ( n = 17 ), sex-specific subgroup analyses yielded no statistically significant differences in primary anxiety and emotional variables ( p > 0.05 ). These insights highlight the necessity of individualized psychological monitoring in elite weightlifting and provide a foundational baseline and methodological reference point for future longitudinal and cross-national investigations in strength sports.

title: Physical education teacher education for intercultural citizenship in a traumatized society
title_original: Physical education teacher education for intercultural citizenship in a traumatized society
summary: In divided and conflict-affected societies, higher education institutions offer opportunities for sustained intergroup encounter. Yet proximity alone does not produce meaningful interaction, trust, or cooperation. This challenge is particularly acute in Israel, where Arab and Jewish students enter higher education after years of segregated schooling, amid tensions and intensified fear, mistrust, and collective trauma following October 7, 2023, and the subsequent war. This perspective article argues that Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) offers an underexplored space for fostering intercultural citizenship. It synthesizes relevant theoretical perspectives and evidence from studies by the authors and others to develop a framework for PETE in divided and traumatized societies. Integrating intergroup contact theory, intercultural citizenship, Sport for Development and Peace, and trauma-sensitive pedagogy, the framework positions PETE as a space for structured contact, embodied cooperation, civic engagement, and resilience. The framework is illustrated through the “Roaming Course,” an experiential, student-led PETE model combining on-campus learning, encounters in diverse communities, shared physical activity, and guided reflection. Drawing on studies involving Arab and Jewish PETE students in Israel, the article shows how structured, discipline-based contact may narrow the gap between willingness to engage and actual intergroup interaction while strengthening students’ capacity to cope with social tension and collective trauma. It demonstrates the value of embedding intercultural citizenship within core curricula rather than relying on extracurricular interventions. It concludes that PETE can prepare future educators to act as agents of social connection, inclusion, and resilience in divided societies.

title: Cross-cultural adaptation of the Athlete Diet Index, a web-based dietary assessment tool for athletes
title_original: Cross-cultural adaptation of the Athlete Diet Index, a web-based dietary assessment tool for athletes
summary: Background The literature suggests that many athletes fail to meet health and sport-specific dietary recommendations which may negatively impact their overall health and performance. Moreover, completing a proper assessment of an athlete's diet is complex; the quality and validity of assessment tools are lacking in this population and resources to conduct these evaluations are limited. The Athlete Diet Index (ADI) is a validated dietary assessment tool that evaluates dietary intake and patterns of Australian athletes. However, the ADI does not consider Canadian nutrition recommendations or country-specific dietary patterns in language relevant to the population.Methods The cross-cultural adaptation initially began with a revision of the ADI by three experienced sport dietitians. This Canadian version was then reviewed using a modified Delphi process involving a panel of eight experienced Canadian sport dietitians. Next, the forward-backward translation method was applied to obtain the French language version. Lastly, as recommended in the COnsensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement Instruments (COSMIN) methodology, a pilot study with a convenience sample of Canadian athletes (n = 49) was conducted.Results The initial revision stage led to the adaptation of 67 of the 112 questions and text elements (i.e. 97 questions and 15 instructional statements) for reasons such as language (65), Canadian dietary context (35), and relevance to Canadian athletes (4). After two rounds of Delphi interspersed with a roundtable meeting, the panelists agreed to modify 56, add five, and delete four questions. The forward-backward translation process resulted in a total of 48 changes to improve terminology (32), syntax errors (9), and align with decisions of the modified Delphi panel (7). The pilot study indicated the tool was relevant/very relevant (n = 44) and easy/very easy to understand (n = 39). English and French versions were judged equivalent by a majority (80%) of the bilingual athlete participants (n = 11).Conclusion The cross-cultural adaptation of the ADI resulted in a 98-question Canadian version of the dietary assessment tool supported by evidence of face and content validity and available in the language of their choice.

title: A study of the “Breakthrough of Localized Influence” in regional sports events: agenda, emotion, and cultural identity
title_original: A study of the “Breakthrough of Localized Influence” in regional sports events: agenda, emotion, and cultural identity
summary: The rapid development of social media has profoundly transformed how cultural and sports events are disseminated, enabling regional sports events to overcome geographical constraints and attract nationwide attention--a phenomenon referred to as “breakout” (chū quān). Such events, rich in local cultural symbols, have become important vehicles for spreading regional culture and fostering local identity. This study explores the dynamics and differentiated pathways underlying this phenomenon. We collected comprehensive data on the “Jiangsu City Football League” (“Su Chao”), a phenomenal regional sports event in China, including 222,027 posts and comments from Weibo and 743,794 video titles and comments from TikTok. Using a mixed-method framework that integrates LDA (Latent Dirichlet Allocation) topic modelling, social network analysis, and sentiment analysis, we examined the agenda networks (i.e., cognitive associative structures formed by co-occurring issue attributes) constructed by official media, opinion leaders, and the public, as well as the structural associations among them. We further propose a triple linkage pathway of “agenda network construction - emotional resonance stimulation - cultural identity reinforcement”: agenda network construction provides the cognitive framework, emotional resonance injects affective energy, and cultural identity reflects deeper social outcomes; the three dimensions co-evolve. The results suggest that: (1) the agenda networks of Weibo and TikTok are oriented around different cores--Weibo focuses on “cultural honour,” while TikTok emphasizes “commercial confrontation-fusion”; (2) transmission pathways diverge across platforms--Weibo exhibits hierarchical collaboration (a top-down, orderly flow pattern from official media to opinion leaders to the public), whereas TikTok suggests competitive public reconstruction (the public’s active deconstruction and re-creation of established agenda frameworks); (3) breakout depends on the triple linkage pathway, manifesting as a gradual pathway on Weibo and a carnival-like pathway on TikTok. This study offers a new theoretical framework for understanding complex communication of regional sports events in social media ecosystems and provides practical guidance for coordinating cross-platform strategies.

title: Ergogenic effects of beetroot juice supplementation on neuromuscular function and simulated combat demands in elite female taekwondo athletes
title_original: Ergogenic effects of beetroot juice supplementation on neuromuscular function and simulated combat demands in elite female taekwondo athletes
summary: Beetroot juice supplementation has been widely examined across various sport disciplines due to its potential ergogenic effects. However, evidence regarding its impact on combat sports particularly in female athletes remains limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the acute effects of beetroot juice supplementation on simulated taekwondo combat performance and neuromuscular function in elite female taekwondo athletes. Seven elite female Olympic taekwondo athletes (age: 20.3 ± 3.7 years), participated in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study consisting of two experimental trials). Each trial involved the consumption of either 140 mL of beetroot juice (which contains 12.8 mmol NO₃⁻) or 140 mL of a placebo (with 0.08 mmol NO₃⁻) followed by a simulated taekwondo combat session and assessments of neuro-muscular function (i.e., vertical jump and visual cognitive performance). In addition, metabolic (i.e., blood lactate), and perceptual responses (i.e., rate of perceived exertion) were measured before, after, and 3 minutes post-combat. No significant differences during the simulated taekwondo combat (e.g., attack time; p = 0.531–0.989; ηp² = 0.01–0.05), neuromuscular function battery (p = 0.302-0.700; ηp² = 0.02-0.04), blood lactate concentrations (p = 0.705; ηp² = 0.13), or rate of perceived exertion values (RPE) (p = 0.717; ηp² = 0.12) were obtained between beetroot juice and placebo conditions. Acute ingestion of beetroot juice (140 mL) did not enhance simulated combat performance or neuromuscular function in female Olympic taekwondo athletes.

title: Feature Engineering for Virtual Currency Price Prediction in Online Games Using a Multiple Linear Regression Approach
title_original: Feature Engineering for Virtual Currency Price Prediction in Online Games Using a Multiple Linear Regression Approach
summary: Changes in the price of Growtopia's virtual currency can influence players' decisions when buying, selling, or storing items, while price information circulating in the community is often inconsistent. This condition confirms the need for transparent, data-driven predictions. This study aims to predict the prices of World Lock (WL), Diamond Lock (DL), and Blue Gem Lock (BGL) using multiple linear regression. The novelty of the study lies in the application of three separate models with a combination of lag features and cyclic time features, accompanied by chronological data sharing to avoid information leakage. The initial dataset contained 925 daily observations from 2024–2026, while the modeling was limited to 194 data points from 2026 that had a consistent scale. After the formation of Lag_1, Lag_2, Lag_7, Day_Sin, and Day_Cos, 187 complete lines are available, divided into 150 training data and 37 test data. The models were evaluated using MSE, RMSE, MAPE, and R². All three models yield an R² of 0.9318, a MAPE of 2.3191%, as well as a MAPE-based accuracy of 97.6809%. The RMSE is 0.1400 for WL, 14.0017 for DL, and 1,400.1705 for BGL, respectively. As of July 13, 2026, the actual and predicted differences are 0.1743 WL, 17.4286 DL, and 1,742.8648 BGL, respectively. The 123-day recursive prediction yields a final value of 2.8357 WL, 283.5670 DL, and 28,356.6979 BGL. The results show the model follows a general pattern, but its response weakens when price changes occur suddenly. The findings can be used as companion information to transactions, rather than as price certainty or investment recommendations.

title: पर-एथलटस क समजक-आरथक सथत एव खल सहभगत: चयनत खल परशकषण कनदर क एक समजशसतरय अधययन
title_original: पर-एथलटस क समजक-आरथक सथत एव खल सहभगत: चयनत खल परशकषण कनदर क एक समजशसतरय अधययन
summary: प्रस्तुत अध्ययन का उद्देश्य चयनित खेल प्रशिक्षण केन्द्रों में प्रशिक्षण प्राप्त कर रहे पैरा-एथलीट्स की सामाजिक-आर्थिक स्थिति, खेल सहभागिता, प्रशिक्षण सुविधाओं, पारिवारिक एवं सामाजिक सहयोग तथा उनके सामने उपस्थित सामाजिक, आर्थिक और संस्थागत चुनौतियों का समाजशास्त्रीय अध्ययन करना है। अध्ययन इस धारणा पर आधारित है कि पैरा-एथलीट्स की स्थिति को केवल उनकी शारीरिक क्षमता या खेल प्रदर्शन के आधार पर नहीं समझा जा सकता, बल्कि उनकी सामाजिक स्थिति परिवार, आर्थिक संसाधनों, सामाजिक दृष्टिकोण, संस्थागत सुविधाओं, प्रशिक्षण व्यवस्था, रोजगार के अवसरों तथा सामाजिक मान्यता जैसे विभिन्न कारकों से निर्मित होती है। अध्ययन में प्राथमिक एवं द्वितीयक दोनों प्रकार के आँकड़ों का प्रयोग किया गया है। प्राथमिक आँकड़े चयनित खेल प्रशिक्षण केन्द्रों में पैरा-एथलीट्स से प्रत्यक्ष संपर्क, साक्षात्कार तथा क्षेत्रीय अवलोकन के माध्यम से संकलित किए गए। प्रारम्भिक पायलट अध्ययन में 15 पैरा-एथलीट्स को सम्मिलित किया गया, जिनमें 10 पुरुष तथा 5 महिलाएँ थीं और सभी उत्तरदाता 20-30 वर्ष की आयु-वर्ग से संबंधित थे। चयनित अध्ययन केन्द्रों में लखनऊ तथा ग्वालियर स्थित संस्थानों को सम्मिलित किया गया। अध्ययन के लिए साक्षात्कार अनुसूची का प्रयोग किया गया तथा क्षेत्रीय अनुभवों को समझने के लिए प्रत्यक्ष अवलोकन किया गया। प्रारम्भिक क्षेत्रीय अध्ययन से संकेत मिलता है कि पैरा-एथलीट्स को आर्थिक संसाधनों की कमी, सीमित पारिवारिक सहयोग, सामाजिक भेदभाव, आधुनिक खेल उपकरणों की कमी, उन्नत प्रशिक्षण सुविधाओं की सीमित उपलब्धता तथा प्रशिक्षण के बाद रोजगार और जीवन-वृत्ति संबंधी अनिश्चितताओं जैसी समस्याओं का सामना करना पड़ता है। साथ ही, कुछ प्रशिक्षण केन्द्रों में नियमित प्रशिक्षण तथा आवासीय सुविधाएँ उपलब्ध होने से खिलाड़ियों को खेल प्रतिभा विकसित करने का अवसर भी प्राप्त होता है। अध्ययन पैरा-एथलीट्स की खेल सहभागिता को सामाजिक पहचान, सामाजिक सम्मान और सशक्तीकरण की प्रक्रिया से जोड़कर देखता है। अध्ययन का निष्कर्ष है कि पैरा-एथलीट्स के समग्र विकास के लिए केवल खेल प्रशिक्षण पर्याप्त नहीं हैय इसके साथ आधुनिक खेल सुविधाएँ, प्रशिक्षित मानव संसाधन, स्वास्थ्य एवं पुनर्वास सहायता, पारिवारिक एवं सामाजिक सहयोग, रोजगार के अवसर तथा दीर्घकालीन संस्थागत समर्थन आवश्यक हैं। इस प्रकार पैरा-स्पोर्ट्स को केवल खेल उपलब्धि के क्षेत्र के रूप में नहीं, बल्कि सामाजिक समावेशन और सशक्तीकरण के महत्वपूर्ण माध्यम के रूप में समझना आवश्यक है।

title: “The gym became a bit of a lab”: International Olympic Weightlifting coaches’ situated knowledges of training women athletes
title_original: “The gym became a bit of a lab”: International Olympic Weightlifting coaches’ situated knowledges of training women athletes
summary: In this paper, we extend gender-responsive coaching literature by examining how coaches’ learning processes influence their knowledges about sex, gender and athleticism. Our analysis draws upon semi-structured interviews with 10 coaches of elite women Olympic Weightlifters from eight countries: Aotearoa New Zealand, Botswana, Canada, China, Colombia, Denmark, the Philippines and the United States. Using Haraway’s concept of “situated knowledge”, we discuss how coaches’ knowledges were shaped by their national sport systems, gender norms within their national contexts, and their bodily experiences of Olympic Weightlifting. Exploring the contradictory understandings of women’s bodies, minds and motivations that these coaches relayed, we discuss whether any of these knowledges can be considered “better” than the others. We conclude that while coaches’ contradictory knowledges may be constructed in response to the diverse gendered bodies and identities that they encounter, they may still be critiqued based on the futures they imply for women athletes.

title: Multivariate analysis of physical preparedness indicators in qualified Greco-Roman wrestlers
title_original: Multivariate analysis of physical preparedness indicators in qualified Greco-Roman wrestlers
summary: Background and Purpose. Modern competitive activity in Greco-Roman wrestling is characterized by high-intensity bouts and increased demands on athletes’ physical preparedness levels. Despite the considerable number of studies in wrestling, the issues related to the comprehensive analysis of interrelationships between wrestlers’ physical preparednessindicators using multivariate statistical methods remain insufficiently explored. This determines the necessity of identifying the most informative components of physical preparedness in order to improve the systems of monitoring and managing the training process. The purpose of the study was to conduct a multivariate analysis of physical preparedness indicators in Greco-Roman wrestlers and to identify the most informative components characterizing the structure of their athletic performance. Materials and Methods. The study involved 32 sub-elite Greco-Roman wrestlers (mean age: 22.03±1.76 years; height: 176.66±4.61 cm; body mass: 74.47±7.90 kg) with 10-12 years of training experience, who regularly participated in national competitions and trained at least six times per week. Physical preparedness assessment was carried out using a battery of tests evaluating speed abilities, speed-strength abilities, coordination abilities, strength endurance, general endurance, and wrestlers’ special work capacity. Descriptive statistics, correlation, factor, cluster, and discriminant analyses were applied using IBM SPSS Statistics software. Results. Physical preparedness indicators of sub-elite Greco-Roman wrestlers were tested and subsequently used in the multivariate analysis. Correlation analysis revealed numerous statistically significant relationships between the wrestlers’ physical preparednessindicators. Strong relationships were identified between speed abilities and speed-strength fitness, strength endurance, and coordination abilities. The largest number of interrelationships was observed for indicators of speed-strength qualities and strength endurance, indicating their leading role in the structure of wrestlers’ special work capacity. The obtained results confirm the complex nature of physical preparedness and the necessity of integrated development of physical qualities within the training process. Factor analysis identified several latent factors explaining the major part of the total variance of the sample. The first factor predominantly characterized the level of athletes’ speed-strength fitness. The second factor was associated with the functional capabilities of the body, including strength, general, and special endurance. The third factor reflected wrestlers’ coordination abilities. The obtained factor structure confirms the multidimensional nature of physical preparedness in wrestling. Cluster analysis identified three typological groups of athletes differing in the structure of physical and functional preparedness. Wrestlers in the first group demonstrated high levels of strength, general, and special endurance; athletes in the second group were characterized by higher levels of speed and speed-strength abilities; whereas wrestlers in the third group had the most balanced structure of physical fitness. This indicates the existence of different individual models for achieving high athletic performance in Greco-Roman wrestling. Discriminant analysis demonstrated high effectiveness in classifying athletes into the three groups. The greatest contribution to group differentiation was made by the following tests: “2×800 m run”, “Hanging Leg Raises Test”, “Forward bends with a partner of equal weight”, “Swing-overs on the wrestling bridge”, “Running around the head on the wrestling bridge”, and “10 forward rolls”. Conclusions. The results of the study demonstrated that the physical preparedness of sub-elite Greco-Roman wrestlers has a complex and multidimensional structure. Correlation analysis revealed numerous statistically significant relationships among indicators of speed, speed-strength, coordination abilities, strength endurance, and special endurance, indicating a high level of integration of physical qualities within the athletes’ fitness structure. Factor analysis identified three leading factors: speed-strength fitness, special strength endurance, and coordination abilities, which together explained 70.82% of the total variance of the indicators. Cluster analysis confirmed the existence of three wrestler types characterized by different orientations in the development of physical qualities and special work capacity. Discriminant analysis demonstrated high classification accuracy and confirmed the informativeness of the applied tests for differentiating wrestlers according to their preparedness levels. The obtained results may be used for the individualization of the training process and optimization of physical preparednessprograms for sub-elite Greco-Roman wrestlers.

title: Football and symbols: a Bayesian analysis of symbolic consumption in sports club brands
title_original: Football and symbols: a Bayesian analysis of symbolic consumption in sports club brands
summary: Introduction Contemporary football operates as a cultural system in which club brands function as symbolic resources through which fans construct identity, lifestyle, and social belonging. However, existing research has largely relied on linear analytical approaches, limiting the understanding of how real social identity, ideal social identity, and lifestyle interact as an integrated symbolic system. Aims This study aims to analyze how football club brands generate a sense of belonging through symbolic consumption, considering the interrelationships among real social identity, ideal social identity, and lifestyle. Methods A quantitative, cross-sectional, non-experimental design was employed using a non-probabilistic sample of 786 Colombian football fans. Data were collected through validated symbolic consumption scales measuring real social identity, ideal social identity, and lifestyle as perceptions of brand–self congruence; the sense of belonging was not directly measured but theoretically inferred. A Bayesian network analysis was conducted using a Gaussian graphical model to estimate conditional dependencies among items and identify the most central nodes of the symbolic consumption network. Results The results reveal a cohesive yet differentiated symbolic network composed of nine nodes and 21 significant conditional relationships. Items measuring ideal social identity showed the greatest relational prominence in the network, exhibiting the highest levels of closeness, betweenness, and expected influence. Real social identity items occupied a more peripheral position, while lifestyle items showed a moderate integrative role, linking identity perceptions to self-reported lifestyle congruence. These findings suggest that the perceived symbolic connection with football brands is, in this sample, more strongly associated with aspirational self-projection than with congruence with the current self-image. Conclusions Within the scope of the nine items analyzed, the sample studied, and the cross-sectional design, symbolic consumption in football appears to be predominantly aspirational. The results suggest that football club brands may operate as narrative and cultural devices through which fans project desired identities. Methodologically, the study illustrates the value of Bayesian network analysis for exploring the relational structure of symbolic consumption in sport.

title: Contemporary athletic nutrition: Principles, nutrient timing, and applied ergogenics
title_original: Contemporary athletic nutrition: Principles, nutrient timing, and applied ergogenics
summary: Modern athletic nutrition has undergone a paradigm shift from static caloric balancing and empiric dietary observations to a complex, molecularly driven field based on cellular bioenergetics, nutrient-gene interactions, and circadian chronobiology. This comprehensive review covers the history of sports nutrition from the early classical respiratory studies to the modern era of precision metabolomics. It details the inner workings of the phosphagen pool, anaerobic glycolysis, and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. It introduces the thermodynamic and molecular bases of skeletal muscle contraction. The review addresses exercise as a physiological stressor through molecular signaling cascades, glycogen regulation, and the crossover concept. It therefore ends with a description of the modern paradigm of dietary periodization, including substrate management, acute nutrient timing, and individualized use of ergogenic supplements, to maximize athletic performance while also maintaining systemic metabolic health and skeletal muscle remodeling.

title: Built to fall: ruin value from romanticist ideal to materials design philosophy
title_original: Built to fall: ruin value from romanticist ideal to materials design philosophy
summary: Abstract Ruin value is an architectural principle endorsing the use of designs and materials that would allow buildings to age beautifully and retain their aesthetics even when transformed into ruins. Here, the principle is extracted from the political context in which its proponent, Albert Speer, proposed it and discussed as a continuation of a longer Romanticist tradition of appreciation of weathering and the melancholy beauty of things in decline. Noting its reach well beyond architecture and across other artistic genres, the principle is brought here into the context of natural sciences and the following question is analyzed: Is there room for ruin value in today’s materials science and engineering? The ensuing analysis charts the chronological appearance of a number of categories of materials where intrinsic degradation represents the key aspect of their functionality. These include biodegradable tissue engineering constructs, metallic implants designed to corrode, self-healing polymers, stimuli-responsive drug and gene delivery carriers, and intelligent, bioinspired and “living” materials whose dissipative character extends beyond energy loss to encompass their material structure as well. Common to all these materials is the embodiment of the principle that order, in some, if not all, aspects of their structure, must be ruined, and symmetries broken for matter to be brought closer to functioning as an animate, intrinsically smart, environmentally responsive system. The expositions of the ruin value doctrine articulated by Walter Benjamin, Albert Speer, and Speer’s teacher and intellectual predecessor, Heinrich Tessenow are juxtaposed throughout the discussion with the physicochemical principles underlying the structural transformations documented across each category of materials surveyed. It is concluded that the continued pursuit of viewing materials not as static objects whose properties are to be optimized at a single point in time, but as temporal processes whose value is inseparable from their aging and dissolution, will prove fruitful in the effort to endow inert matter with the adaptive, responsive and self-regulating features characteristic of living systems.

title: Coaching effectiveness, resource allocation, and athlete readiness in collegiate basketball programs
title_original: Coaching effectiveness, resource allocation, and athlete readiness in collegiate basketball programs
summary: Collegiate basketball programs are pivotal for athlete development, yet readiness depends on the synergy between individual ability, coaching quality, and institutional support. This study investigated the levels of coaching effectiveness, resource allocation, and athlete readiness, while examining the significant relationships among these variables. The research was anchored on Self-Determination Theory, Transformational Leadership Theory, and Deliberate Practice Theory, explaining the psychological and environmental factors influencing performance. Utilizing a descriptive-correlational research design, the study surveyed collegiate basketball athletes from the City College of Tagaytay via total enumeration. Data gathered through a researcher-made questionnaire were analyzed using weighted mean, standard deviation, and Pearson’s Product-Moment Correlation Coefficient. Findings revealed that coaching effectiveness, resource allocation, and athlete readiness were all High. Specifically, feedback quality and communication were the strongest coaching dimensions, equipment was the primary resource asset, and basketball skills performance was the highest readiness indicator. Correlation analysis showed that both coaching effectiveness and resource allocation had selective relationships with readiness. Communication and feedback quality, alongside equipment and conditioning services, emerged as the most consistent predictors of athlete preparedness. The study concludes that specific dimensions of coaching and institutional support significantly influence athlete readiness. It is recommended that coaches prioritize instructional responsiveness and motivation, while administrators enhance facilities and training support through the proposed structured basketball training program to sustain high-level athletic development.

title: Legal Aspects of Transgender Individuals' Participation in Sports Competitions
title_original: Legal Aspects of Transgender Individuals' Participation in Sports Competitions
summary: Ureditev sodelovanja transspolnih oseb na športnih tekmovanjih predstavlja kompleksno vprašanje na presečišču prava, športa in študij spola. Gre za področje, na katerem se prepletajo pravice ter pravni interesi različnih družbenih skupin in kjer meja med avtonomijo športnih organizacij in državnim ter mednarodnim pravom ni povsem jasna. Predmetna magistrska naloga obravnava trenje med načelom prepovedi diskriminacije ter načelom avtonomnosti športnih organizacij, kot zgolj dvema možnima pravnima vidikoma glede sodelovanja transspolnih oseb na športnih tekmovanjih, pri čemer predstavi pravila športnih organizacij, relevantno državno ter mednarodno pravo, sodno prakso in vidik varstva človekovih pravic. S pregledom pravil športnih organizacij o razvrščanju vrhunskih športnikov v kategorije glede na spol predmetna magistrska naloga oriše aktualni pravni položaj transspolnih športnikov v vrhunskem športu. S tehtanjem relevantnih človekovih pravic pa predmetna magistrska naloga problematizira tudi, ali so trenutno veljavne ureditve razvrščanja transspolnih oseb v kategorije glede na spol skladne z načelom prepovedi diskriminacije, in izpostavi zahtevnost iskanja ravnotežja med biološkimi značilnostmi, spolno identiteto ter pravili avtonomnih športnih organizacij.

title: Perspectives in women's football (part 1) “we currently do not have a coach, we train ourselves”- experiences of women & girls playing football in Australia, a mixed methods
title_original: Perspectives in women's football (part 1) “we currently do not have a coach, we train ourselves”- experiences of women & girls playing football in Australia, a mixed methods
summary: Objective To explore the characteristics and lived experiences of women and girls across all levels of football in Australia. Design Cross-sectional survey. Method Participants included women and girls aged ≥12 years registered to play competitive club football during the 2023/2024 season. . A convenience sample was recruited through targeted emails, social media, and physical fliers. The questionnaire, developed with input from players, coaches, and administrators, had a mix of open and closed-ended questions exploring the characteristics and experiences of playing football in Australia. Data were collected between May–September 2024, with data from closed-ended questions analysed using descriptive statistics, while data derived from open-ended questions were analysed using conventional content analysis. Responses were mapped to the Socio-Ecological Model (SEM). Results 211 players were included, mean age 28.5 (SD = 13.7) years, 112 (53%) with tertiary education, and 158 (74%) with a family member who also played football. Key findings spanned the SEM with players reporting varied access to training, medical support, and facilities, with 21% indicating unequal access to resources compared to men's teams. Most players had men as coaches, with mixed preferences for coach gender. Factors preventing players from reaching their full potential included; competing priorities, family responsibilities, health issues, financial burden, coaching quality, and environmental factors. Conclusions Our study highlights ongoing challenges and inequities faced by some women and girls footballers. Addressing issues including unequal access to resources, coaching, and facilities is crucial to foster a more inclusive and supportive environment that enables women and girls to reach their full-playing potential.
