title: DIPL 6104 NA The Art and Science of International Negotiations
title_original: DIPL 6104 NA The Art and Science of International Negotiations
summary: This course provides an overview of academic theory and diplomatic practice on the art and science of international negotiations. The Fall 2026 semester unfolds against the backdrop of the election of the next UN Secretary-General, with negotiations from UN Member States, the Security Council, and the General Assembly actively taking place. Students will analyze this process in real time and consider how various actors negotiate and come to agreements on processes leading to inter-governmental elections and negotiated agreements. In addition, a study of selected international negotiators, negotiation techniques, practices, and standards will complement an analysis of internationally agreed documents such as those leading to the creation of the UN Sustainable Development Goals, the Pact of the Future, and the Declaration on Future Generations. By the end of the course, students will have an understanding of how negotiations take place; will engage in conversation with diplomatic negotiators to enhance their practical knowledge; will learn skills that assist in the analysis of international processes; and will apply negotiation techniques to their lives and professional pursuits. Key Questions Explored Students will answer the questions of how negotiations are conducted and what the key qualities of successful negotiators are; what the best techniques are to bring to discussions; and how to identify different positions and draw from examples of milestone international negotiations. title: Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
title_original: Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: When training large language models with reinforcement learning, terminal rewards provide little guidance about which steps matter. Common methods for assigning step credit overlook that work built on uncorrected mistakes is wasted while independent work remains valid. With only a final success/failure reward, every step in a failed episode has zero total future reward, even when it made progress. We propose Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping (DARS), which represents task progress as predicates linked by prerequisite relations and assigns step-level credit over the dependency graph. An annotator marks which predicates each step verifies, invalidates, or repairs. Verified predicates are discounted according to graph distance from the nearest broken prerequisite, while independent predicates are unaffected. Repairs update these weights based on any errors that remain; invalidated predicates need re-verification to regain credit. A fixed potential converts these annotations into signed per-step rewards. A common reward and annotation interface allows DARS to integrate with a range of reasoning and agentic training methods, such as GiGPO and ARPO/AEPO, without changing their rollout strategies or optimizers. Across five task families and models from 1.5B to 8B, DARS improves success by up to 10 points over GiGPO trained with the same budget and harness (ALFWorld), raises the WebShop task score and Search-R1 QA accuracy, complements AEPO's entropy-based training on AIME24/25 with a Python interpreter, and exceeds OmniOPD in controlled tool-free reasoning comparisons at 1.7B and 4B. Ablations show that step-level credit, dependency attenuation, and graph topology each contribute. On ALFWorld, a distilled 8B annotator matches the API annotator, enabling DARS to run efficiently without a frontier judge. Code is available at https://github.com/JianhuiWei7/DARS.

title: Editorial: Exploring the multidisciplinary roles of sports events
title_original: Editorial: Exploring the multidisciplinary roles of sports events
summary: The five core pillars of this topic, drawing on original empirical research and systematic reviews, illustrate the multidisciplinary complexity of the sporting landscape, namely:  The success of major sports events is fundamentally dependent on the volunteer workforce, a vital human resource that facilitates long-term social legacies. Empirical evidence from the Special Olympics World Games 2023 (SOWG 23) reveals that volunteer motivations in inclusive settings are primarily intrinsic, driven by a desire to express personal values and establish interpersonal contacts.Notably, the research identifies a parental history of volunteering as a key predictor of sustained engagement, suggesting that values instilled during childhood continue to influence active commitment well into adulthood. For sports organisations, these findings underscore the importance of shifting the recruitment focus away from extrinsic rewards toward strategies that emphasise community building and value alignment. To ensure a sustainable volunteering legacy, managers must implement di erentiated communication channels, such as digital platforms tailored to younger generations, to foster lasting engagement across diverse demographic groups. The multidisciplinary nature of sports events is also evident in how di erent stakeholders perceive quality. The case of GIMNASTRADA 2019, an international recreational gymnastics event, uses Service Quality Theory and Role Theory to demonstrate that "success" is highly subjective. The study found that the type of participation significantly influences quality ratings: while organisers and group leaders reported the highest levels of satisfaction, active gymnasts tended to have lower perceptions of service quality. This discrepancy is attributed to the "expectation-performance gap," in which active participants face greater performance pressure and have more stringent requirements for facilities and logistics. These findings suggest that sports management must move toward a tailored experience design, ensuring that the specific needs of athletes, families, and spectators are addressed separately to promote long-term loyalty and repeat participation. Sports events also serve as a "cultural battlefield" where national identity is constructed and contested. An analysis of Indonesian media narratives regarding the naturalisation of football players illustrates the tension between pragmatic nationalism and cultural essentialism. Media outlets often frame naturalised players as "national assets" who enhance international competitiveness, yet they simultaneously express scepticism about the athletes' "authenticity" and emotional ties to the nation. Drawing on the distinction between "thin citizenship" (legal recognition) and "thick citizenship" (cultural intimacy), the research shows how the media acts as a mediator of public perception. While some naturalised athletes successfully integrate by embracing local language and social initiatives, the discourse remains divided. This highlights the role of sporting events as critical sites for defining the symbolic boundaries of an "imagined community" in the era of globalised labour migration. From an economic and marketing perspective, the success of sports events is often linked to the "fit" or congruity between the event and its sponsoring brands. A metaanalytic review of 31 studies confirms that high levels of sports event-brand fit lead to positive cognitive, emotional, and behavioural responses from consumers. However, the e ectiveness of this fit is moderated by cultural contexts. In Eastern cultures, brand-event alignment is more e ective at generating emotional responses, reflecting a preference for harmony and collectivism. Conversely, in Western cultures, the fit has a stronger impact on behavioural intentions, such as purchase probability. Furthermore, the research suggests that symbolic brand responses-such as brand loyalty-are not instantaneous but require long-term sponsorship commitment and repeated interaction to bridge the "expectation gap" in consumers' minds. The final multidisciplinary lens focuses on the impact and legacy of sports events on the Quality of Life (QOL) of host communities. A scoping review of the literature indicates a significant shift from evaluating purely economic outcomes to measuring subjective well-being. While mega-events like the Olympics dominate the research, the review identifies an underexplored potential in small and mediumsized events to foster social capital and community cohesion. The findings suggest that the positive "feel-good" e ect of one-o mega-events is often temporary. In contrast, recurring participatory events (such as marathons) may o er more sustainable benefits for resident attachment and behavioural change. To advance this field, researchers advocate integrating objective measures, such as Heart Rate Variability (HRV), to complement subjective surveys and better understand the physiological mechanisms linking sports experiences to societal happiness.In conclusion, the articles in Exploring the Multidisciplinary Roles of Sports Events o er a profound and critical perspective on the role of sport in contemporary society. Collectively, they provide academics, event managers, and policymakers with practical insights and actionable tools to maximise the social legacies of sports events by understanding the intergenerational dynamics of volunteer motivation, improve service delivery through greater recognition of the role-specific expectations of diverse event participants, navigate the complex identity politics surrounding sports journalism and national team recruitment, optimise sponsorship strategies by acknowledging cultural di erences in consumer behaviour, and promote long-term societal well-being by moving beyond short-term economic metrics towards more holistic quality-of-life indicators. Taken together, the findings presented in this volume constitute a significant contribution to the ongoing dialogue on how sports events can be strategically leveraged to foster more inclusive, prosperous, and happier societies.

title: Relação entre força relativa dos flexores dos dedos e desempenho em escaladores recreacionais: homens e mulheres
title_original: Relação entre força relativa dos flexores dos dedos e desempenho em escaladores recreacionais: homens e mulheres
summary: BACKGROUND: Finger flexor strength is considered determinant of sport climbing performance. However, evidence suggests that strength relative to body mass may be a more relevant indicator of climbing ability than absolute strength, particularly when comparing male and female climbers.OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between relative finger flexor strength and climbing performance in recreational climbers of both sexes.METHODS: Twenty-eight climbers (16 women and 12 men) participated in the study. Climbing performance was determined using the International Rock Climbing Research Association (IRCRA) scale, based on the highest redpoint grade successfully climbed during the previous three months. Body mass was measured using a digital scale, and maximal finger flexor strength was assessed using a Tindeq® load cell attached to an adjustable testing platform developed by the researchers. Comparisons between sexes were performed using one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), while the association between relative finger strength and climbing performance was examined using Spearman’s rank correlation, with 95% confidence intervals estimated from 5,000 bootstrap resamples (p<0.05).RESULTS: Men demonstrated greater absolute finger flexor strength in both the right hand (30.0±7.0 vs. 22.9±4.2 kg; F(1,26)=10.86; p=0.003; η²=0.295) and the left hand (29.8±7.4 vs. 22.0±3.6 kg; F(1,26)=13.32; p=0.001; η²=0.339), as well as greater body mass (p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed between sexes for relative finger strength (F(1,26)=0.043; p=0.838), climbing performance (p=0.112), or weekly training frequency (p=0.322). Relative finger strength was positively correlated with climbing performance in women (r=0.55; p=0.027), whereas no significant correlation was observed in men (r=0.45; p=0.137).CONCLUSION: Bilateral relative strength did not differ between sexes and showed moderate, non-significant associations with performance. It may be used as a complementary measure when assessing recreational climbers.

title: THE URBANISM OF EXCEPTION : Scalar Rivalry and Political Loyalty in the Making of the Panorama Tbilisi Megaproject
title_original: THE URBANISM OF EXCEPTION : Scalar Rivalry and Political Loyalty in the Making of the Panorama Tbilisi Megaproject
summary: Abstract In flawed democracies, such as the Republic of Georgia, legal exceptions for urban megaprojects are becoming a standard mode of governance. While frequently analyzed as singular, top‐down sovereign acts, I argue that the imposition of such exceptions is a complex and dispersed process. Drawing on the case of the Panorama Tbilisi megaproject introduced in 2014 in Tbilisi, Georgia, this article reconceptualizes the urbanism of exception as a governance strategy engineered through intergovernmental rivalry and institutionalized political loyalty. Through a qualitative analysis, I show how rivalry between national and local governments controlled by opposing political parties led to the strategic rewriting of national law to bypass local opposition. Furthermore, I demonstrate how political loyalty functions as a governance tool, blurring public‐private boundaries and ultimately culminating in the promotion of project executives to high‐level state positions. The article contributes to critical urban theory by revealing the contested nature of state power in megaproject implementation and proposes the concept of the commodification of exception: the centralization of the right to bypass rules as a tradable asset available exclusively to political and economic elites.

title: Adesão e aderência de mulheres na corrida de aventura
title_original: Adesão e aderência de mulheres na corrida de aventura
summary: INTRODUÇÃO: A Corrida de Aventura (CA) caracteriza-se como uma modalidade esportiva desenvolvida em ambientes naturais, que integra múltiplas disciplinas. Sua prática requer elevado condicionamento físico, elaboração de estratégias e cooperação entre os membros da equipe. OBJETIVO: Investigar a adesão e a aderência de mulheres nas edições do evento “Corrida de Aventura da Mulher”, realizadas no estado do Paraná, entre 2022 e 2025. MÉTODOS: Participaram 215 atletas inscritas nas quatro edições da CA da Mulher. As variáveis referentes ao perfil esportivo foram coletadas por meio de formulário eletrônico aplicado via plataforma Google Forms® e apresentadas mediante estatística descritiva. RESULTADOS: Em 2022, foram registradas 64 inscrições, com 30 participantes experientes. Em 2023, houve 52 inscrições, sendo 24 de atletas experientes. Em 2024, constatou-se aumento expressivo para 164 inscrições, das quais 61 eram de iniciantes. Em 2025, identificaram-se 152 inscrições, com 22 iniciantes. Os achados evidenciam crescimento do evento e tendência de equilíbrio entre os perfis. CONCLUSÃO: Conclui-se que o evento promove tanto a adesão de novas praticantes quanto a aderência e a continuidade do público feminino na CA, contribuindo para a consolidação da participação feminina na modalidade. Sugere-se que mais parcerias sejam realizadas entre associações, projetos e instituições que possam oportunizar mais eventos com estas características, aumentando as possibilidades de mais ambientes que fomentem a participação feminina em esportes de aventura.

title: Street Carnival in the Port District of Rio de Janeiro: Who Can “Turn the World Upside Down” and Where? A Critical Approach to the Festive Phenomenon in the Context of the Neoliberal City
title_original: Street Carnival in the Port District of Rio de Janeiro: Who Can “Turn the World Upside Down” and Where? A Critical Approach to the Festive Phenomenon in the Context of the Neoliberal City
summary: This article aims to analyze the paradox inherent in the festive use of certain urban spaces by privileged social groups. Although the festive phenomenon is commonly associated with joy and transgression, its analysis cannot be understood apart from the social and spatial contexts in which it takes place. The example of street Carnival in the port district of Rio de Janeiro demonstrates how this festivity can be instrumentalized to symbolically distinguish the territory and advance the gentrification objectives of the Porto Maravilha urban operation. Thus, the article proposes a critical approach to the festive phenomenon in the contemporary urban context by considering festivities in the city as a space-time embedded in the neoliberal logics of the production of space.

title: The Influence of Sleep and Autonomic Recovery on Performance in World-Class Swimmers at Major Competitions: The Qualifying Trials, World Championships, and Olympic Games
title_original: The Influence of Sleep and Autonomic Recovery on Performance in World-Class Swimmers at Major Competitions: The Qualifying Trials, World Championships, and Olympic Games
summary: Sleep deprivation is one of the main risk factors for impaired performance in elite athletes, but the changes in sleep and autonomic regulation in response to competitions of varying levels within the same Olympic year remain unknown. In this prospective, longitudinal, observational study, we monitored parameters related to sleep quality and quantity, as well as heart rate variability and resting heart rate, in a cohort of eight Olympic swimmers (n = 8) during the World Championships in Doha, the qualifying trials, and the 2024 Paris Olympic Games, using the Oura Ring Gen3 under real-world conditions throughout the pre-competition, competition, and post-competition phases of each event. The Olympic Games were the only event where sleep efficiency fell below the commonly used reference threshold of 85% during the competition phase accompanied by a reduction in the total sleep score and an increase in resting heart rate. The Olympic setting was accompanied by temporary changes in sleep and autonomic markers, but no sleep parameter or autonomic marker showed a statistically significant association with intra-individual competitive performance, although the limited sample size constrains the power to detect such relationships.

title: Language-mediated abstraction: conceptual concreteness and categorical specificity in language processing
title_original: Language-mediated abstraction: conceptual concreteness and categorical specificity in language processing
summary: The present work investigates the relationship between conceptual concreteness and categorical specificity in accounting for language-mediated abstraction, advancing the claim that these variables constitute distinct semantic dimensions and examining their role in shaping language processing, conversational dynamics, and communicative strategies across three experimental studies. A key contribution of this work lies in adopting a methodology characterized by progressively increasing ecological validity, moving from traditional psycholinguistic paradigms to more interactive and communicative settings. The first study examines the effects of conceptual concreteness and categorical specificity on word processing, both independently and in interaction, across lexical and semantic decision tasks. In addition to replicating the well-established processing advantage of concrete words over abstract words, the study reports a specificity effect: a behavioral advantage of specific words, which instantiate high-resolution representations, over general words in an abstract/concrete semantic decision task. The second study extends the investigation to the perceived plausibility of simulated conversational excerpts. The study examines the role of concreteness and specificity in conversational dynamics, focusing on two linguistic constructs: uncertainty and curiosity (i.e., the need for clarification). The results show that abstract sentences were more likely to elicit expressions of uncertainty and curiosity. However, expressions signaling the need for clarification were also judged as plausible following concrete-general sentences, suggesting their referential indeterminacy. The third study analyzes semi-naturalistic interactions in which interlocutors describe objects under varying conditions of referential availability (present vs. absent) and shared knowledge (known vs. unknown). The study assesses whether interlocutors systematically modulate the concreteness and specificity of their language under these experimental conditions. The main findings indicate that specificity functions as a linguistic cue for maximizing pragmatic informativeness. Together, these studies support the perspective that categorical specificity plays a central role in understanding how language-mediated abstraction shapes both language processing and communicative behavior.
abstract: The present work investigates the relationship between conceptual concreteness and categorical specificity in accounting for language-mediated abstraction, advancing the claim that these variables constitute distinct semantic dimensions and examining their role in shaping language processing, conversational dynamics, and communicative strategies across three experimental studies. A key contribution of this work lies in adopting a methodology characterized by progressively increasing ecological validity, moving from traditional psycholinguistic paradigms to more interactive and communicative settings. The first study examines the effects of conceptual concreteness and categorical specificity on word processing, both independently and in interaction, across lexical and semantic decision tasks. In addition to replicating the well-established processing advantage of concrete words over abstract words, the study reports a specificity effect: a behavioral advantage of specific words, which instantiate high-resolution representations, over general words in an abstract/concrete semantic decision task. The second study extends the investigation to the perceived plausibility of simulated conversational excerpts. The study examines the role of concreteness and specificity in conversational dynamics, focusing on two linguistic constructs: uncertainty and curiosity (i.e., the need for clarification). The results show that abstract sentences were more likely to elicit expressions of uncertainty and curiosity. However, expressions signaling the need for clarification were also judged as plausible following concrete-general sentences, suggesting their referential indeterminacy. The third study analyzes semi-naturalistic interactions in which interlocutors describe objects under varying conditions of referential availability (present vs. absent) and shared knowledge (known vs. unknown). The study assesses whether interlocutors systematically modulate the concreteness and specificity of their language under these experimental conditions. The main findings indicate that specificity functions as a linguistic cue for maximizing pragmatic informativeness. Together, these studies support the perspective that categorical specificity plays a central role in understanding how language-mediated abstraction shapes both language processing and communicative behavior.

title: Social media harassment and psychological distress among collegiate student-athletes: a moderated mediation model of psychological resilience and perceived social support
title_original: Social media harassment and psychological distress among collegiate student-athletes: a moderated mediation model of psychological resilience and perceived social support
summary: Introduction Social media harassment is a sport-relevant digital stressor that may be associated with psychological distress among collegiate student-athletes. This study examined whether psychological resilience statistically accounted for part of this association and whether perceived social support showed both direct protective associations and a buffering role. Methods A cross-sectional multi-site convenience sample of 426 collegiate student-athletes from university sport programs in China, the Republic of Korea, and the United States completed measures of social media harassment, psychological resilience, perceived social support, and psychological distress. Analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, country and gender comparisons, hierarchical regression, bootstrap mediation, conditional process analysis, and robustness checks. Results The four-factor measurement model showed good fit and the focal scales showed acceptable reliability and convergent validity. Social media harassment was positively associated with psychological distress and negatively associated with psychological resilience. Perceived social support was associated with higher resilience, lower distress, and lower reported harassment. The indirect association through resilience was 0.133 (95% CI [0.088, 0.185]). Perceived social support moderated the harassment-resilience association (interaction = 0.12, p = 0.003). Conditional indirect associations decreased from 0.151 at low support to 0.067 at high support, with an index of moderated mediation of −0.042 (95% CI [−0.078, −0.012]). Country- and gender-based differences were small, and the focal pattern remained stable in sensitivity analyses. Discussion The findings support a conditional association model in which resilience is an explanatory psychological resource and perceived social support has complementary direct and buffering roles. Because the data are cross-sectional, the results should not be interpreted as evidence of temporal causality.

title: Influences of joint dynamics on take-off velocity in elite male 110-m hurdlers
title_original: Influences of joint dynamics on take-off velocity in elite male 110-m hurdlers
summary: Objective To study the relationship between lower limb joint moments, joint stiffness, and take-off velocity in high-level hurdlers. Methods This study employed a Qualisys three-dimensional infrared motion-capture system synchronized with a force plate. Based on inverse dynamics principles, kinematic and kinetic data were collected during the clearance phase over the fourth hurdle in 16 elite male 110-m hurdlers. Results During the landing phase, Group B had significantly higher peak joint moments at the hip, knee, and ankle compared to Group A ( P < 0.01). During the propulsive phase, Group B had significantly higher peak joint moments at the hip, knee, and ankle compared to Group A( P < 0.01). Group B had significantly higher joint stiffness at the hip, knee, and ankle compared to Group A ( P < 0.01). During the landing phase, the relative peak joint moments at the hip, knee, and ankle were positively correlated with landing velocity, with correlation coefficients ( r ) ranging from 0.51 to 0.61. During the propulsive phase, the relative peak moments at these joints were highly positively correlated with take-off velocity, with r values between 0.82 and 0.89. Hip, knee, and ankle joint stiffness was highly positively correlated with clearance velocity ( r : 0.80–0.90) but highly negatively correlated with the rate of change in velocity ( r : −0.88 to −0.95). Conclusions During the take-off phase, Group B exhibited greater relative peak joint moments and joint stiffness at the hip, knee, and ankle compared to Group A. These measures were strongly correlated with clearance velocity, indicating that increasing joint moments and stiffness contributes to faster hurdle clearance. Among the lower-limb joints, hip and ankle performance had the most significant influence on clearance mechanics. Additionally, the fitted functional equations enable prediction of clearance velocity from joint moment data. Therefore, incorporating stretch-shortening cycle exercises in training to enhance lower-limb strength, increase joint moments, and improve joint stiffness should effectively enhance performance and competitive outcomes.

title: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN ADAPTIVE PHYSICAL CULTURE AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF SOCIAL INCLUSION OF STUDENTS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
title_original: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN ADAPTIVE PHYSICAL CULTURE AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF SOCIAL INCLUSION OF STUDENTS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
summary: The article provides a theoretical substantiation of the relationship between adaptive physical culture and the development of social inclusion of students with hearing impairment. The relevance of the topic is determined by the reform of Ukraine's education system on the principles of inclusive learning and the need to reconsider the role of physical education not only as a means of correcting the motor sphere, but also as an instrument for the social integration of a child with sensory impairments. The goal of the study is to theoretically substantiate the aforementioned relationship and to develop a generalized model of its mechanisms. The theoretical foundation is provided by N. A. Bernstein's concept of the level-based construction of movements and P. K. Anokhin's theory of functional systems. The research methods include theoretical analysis and synthesis of sources, comparative analysis, generalization and systematization, and theoretical modeling. Based on an analysis of domestic (Yu. Briskin, A. Perederii, N. Dedeliuk, O. Taranchenko) and international (L. Reich, B. Lavay, C. Barboza, M. Tanure Alves, et al.) sources, a structural-functional model has been developed, encompassing the sensorimotor, personal, and social levels of the relationship. The key barriers to social inclusion – communicative, organizational, and attitudinal – have been identified, along with pedagogical technologies that facilitate its realization: visual and gestural support of instructions, peer tutoring, differentiated assessment, and engagement in extracurricular competitive activity. Practical guidelines have been formulated for physical education teachers in inclusive classrooms. Prospects for further research relate to the empirical testing of the model in general secondary education institutions in Ukraine.

title: A Multimodal Framework of Pedagogical Practices in Space
title_original: A Multimodal Framework of Pedagogical Practices in Space
summary: This book outlines a framework for spatial pedagogy, exploring how the dynamics of multimodality work in the interaction of human bodies and classroom spaces in pedagogic practices. Wu extends Spatial Discourse Analysis to establish a framework for analyzing the multimodal nature of embodied practice in space. The volume features four case studies from a range of tertiary classrooms and their material settings in Australian and Chinese higher education, each offering unique insights into teaching and learning practices and how such practices interface with movement, writing, rhythm, and blocking across different contexts. Taken together, the book provides a greater understanding of space in social life and multimodal communication as it plays out in the classroom, charting new directions for future research at the intersection of multimodality and higher education. This volume will be of interest to students and researchers in multimodality, semiotics, educational research, and communication studies.

title: Finnish press and the societal issues of mega-sport events: a discourse analysis of Helsingin Sanomat’s coverage of the Barcelona 1992 and Paris 2024 Summer Olympics
title_original: Finnish press and the societal issues of mega-sport events: a discourse analysis of Helsingin Sanomat’s coverage of the Barcelona 1992 and Paris 2024 Summer Olympics
summary: Sports journalism has been criticized for ignoring sport’s social dimensions, but research suggests that those days of pure enthusiasm are over. This study inves­tigates how the Finnish press has covered societal issues in Olympic reporting and how this coverage has evolved over time. The data consist of Helsingin Sanomat’s coverage of the Barcelona 1992 and Paris 2024 Olympics. Societal issues were addressed in both cases, but the proportion of such articles was higher in 2024. Applying critical discourse analysis, the study examines the discourses through which the Olympics are rep­resented in these articles. Through discourse analysis, four discourses that both question and reinforce the legitimacy of the Olympics were identified. Coverage also includes highly critical reporting of the Olympic Movement. However, the comparison demonstrates a shift toward more critical, multi-voiced, and socially reflective sports journalism. Yet, national loyalty and the pursuit of Olympic success continue to temper its critical depth.

title: Sport facility planning and development in the eyes of local residents
title_original: Sport facility planning and development in the eyes of local residents
summary: Major international sport events are often accompanied by facility development that is expected to generate benefits beyond the event period. This study examines residents’ perceptions of facility development related to the 2023 World Athletics Championships in Budapest, focusing on the National Athletics Centre. Using a questionnaire survey of 1,001 Budapest residents aged 18–89, representative of this population by gender and age, the study analyses perceived positive and negative impacts of the development and examines differences according to sociodemographic characteristics and forms of sport involvement. The analysis identified two dimensions of perceived impacts. Positive impacts referred to urban infrastructure, sport and leisure functions, and future sport participation opportunities, whereas negative impacts referred to expected underuse, preparation costs, and the perceived necessity of the investment. Sociodemographic characteristics were not associated with significant differences in perceptions. In contrast, following the event, being an athletics fan, and sport participation were associated with more favourable evaluations of positive impacts. The findings suggest that residents’ connection to sport and to the event-related discipline may be relevant for understanding how local communities evaluate event-related sport facility development and how benefits related to future use should be communicated.

title: More Police, No New Taxes: Proposition 13 and the Fiscal Limits of Law and Order
title_original: More Police, No New Taxes: Proposition 13 and the Fiscal Limits of Law and Order
summary: Abstract In 1980, Chief Daryl Gates of the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) unveiled the “8500 Plan”: his proposal to increase the number of sworn officers in the city by roughly 25 percent. Two years earlier, the passage of Proposition 13 in California placed strict constitutional limits on local property taxes and required that any new tax be approved by a two-thirds majority of voters. In the following years, Angelenos proceeded to reject a “special police tax” on two separate ballots—even as opinion polls and letters to city officials revealed that most tax revolters also preferred a larger and more responsive LAPD. Yet, as this article demonstrates, what at first seems like a contradiction or case of magical thinking turns out to have been—like the tax revolt—a distributional struggle over public resources and recognition. Tracing the interrelated histories of police expansion and antitax activism reveals a more conflictual relationship between “neoliberal” austerity and carceral state-building than historians have typically assumed.

title: A Scoping Review of Physiological and Behavioural Pain Responses of Ultramarathon Runners
title_original: A Scoping Review of Physiological and Behavioural Pain Responses of Ultramarathon Runners
summary: Pain during ultramarathon races is almost inevitable. Effective pain responses are associated with enhanced race performance. This scoping review synthesises the existing literature on physiological and behavioural pain responses during ultramarathon races and explores the association of these responses with performance. Following the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), we included 31 studies. We organised the extracted data into five overarching categories: neurophysiological mechanisms, running mechanics, medication use, physical therapies, and performance outcomes. Our results show that some ultramarathon runners exhibit exercise-induced analgesia, whereas others exhibit inflammation-driven pain sensitisation. Changes in running mechanics during races may be a response to present or anticipated pain. In addition, many ultramarathon runners take pain medication during the race, mainly to prevent or reduce pain. During ultramarathon races, massage interventions may relieve pain. Finally, ultramarathon runners’ performance may decline in the presence of pain. Among ultramarathon runners, a variety of pain responses are associated with race performance. Because effective pain responses may lead to better performance outcomes, future research should investigate the causal mechanisms linking pain experiences, pain responses, and race performance.

title: Offensive tactical changes from the regular season to the playoffs in the NBA: Analysis of pace, playtype, ball movement, and tracking data
title_original: Offensive tactical changes from the regular season to the playoffs in the NBA: Analysis of pace, playtype, ball movement, and tracking data
summary: This study examined how NBA teams’ offensive tactical structure change from the regular season (RS) to the playoffs (PO), and whether these within-team differences are associated with playoff performance. The raw dataset covered 6422 unique NBA games, and inferential sample of 80 matched RS-PO team-season pairs across five seasons. Phase effects were calculated as RS - PO change scores (Δ) and analysed using paired comparisons, fixed-effects models, multiple regression, possession adjusted sensitivity analyses, alternative playoff outcomes, clutch adjusted models, last 10 game baseline comparisons, and series level sensitivity analyses. Playoff competition was characterized by lower possessions (Δ = 3.34, p _ FDR < .001), transition possessions (Δ = 1.75, p _ FDR < .001), pick and roll ball handler possessions (Δ = 7.74, p _ FDR < .001), total passes (Δ = 16.33, p _ FDR < .001), assists (Δ = 3.41, p _ FDR < .001), touches (Δ = 19.71, p _ FDR < .001), and average offensive speed (Δ = 0.17 km/h, p _ FDR < .001). Isolation possessions increased (Δ = −1.82, p _ FDR < .001), as did average seconds per touch (Δ = −0.19, p _ FDR < .001). Playoff win percentage was primarily associated with regular season win percentage, with an additional positive association for Δ Avg_Speed_Off in the primary multivariable model (B = 0.455, p = .015). This association remained positive in sensitivity analyses but was attenuated in the games played weighted model and was not uniformly significant across advancement based team-season outcomes. Findings indicate that playoff offensive structure becomes slower, less distributed, and more constrained and should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Antik Yunan Spor Tarihi Araştırmalarında Güncel Eğilimler (2000–2026): Sistematik Derleme ve Tematik İçerik Analizi
title_original: Antik Yunan Spor Tarihi Araştırmalarında Güncel Eğilimler (2000–2026): Sistematik Derleme ve Tematik İçerik Analizi
summary: Bu araştırmanın amacı, 2000–2026 yılları arasında Antik Yunan spor tarihi alanında yayımlanan çalışmaların güncel araştırma eğilimlerini sistematik olarak incelemektir. Araştırma PRISMA 2020 rehberi doğrultusunda yürütülmüş ve nihai analize dahil edilen 62 çalışma tematik içerik analiziyle değerlendirilmiştir. Literatür taraması Scopus ve Web of Science Core Collection veri tabanlarında gerçekleştirilmiş ve dil sınırlaması uygulanmamıştır. Veri tabanı taramalarında 403 kayıt belirlenmiş, tekrarların çıkarılmasının ardından 297 benzersiz kayıt taranmış ve uygunluk değerlendirmesi sonucunda 62 çalışma nihai analize dahil edilmiştir. Çalışmaların %45,2’si 2020–2026 döneminde yayımlanmıştır. En sık araştırılan temalar atletik performans, antrenman ve teknik (%24,2) ile etik, değerler, rekabet, eğitim ve felsefe (%22,6) olmuştur. Araştırma yaklaşımlarında tarihsel ve karşılaştırmalı incelemeler (%30,6) ilk sırada yer alırken, incelenen spor dalları ve etkinlikler içinde genel atletizm ve beden eğitimi (%54,8) ile mücadele sporları (%27,4) öne çıkmıştır. Bulgular, Antik Yunan spor tarihi çalışmalarının klasik tarihsel ve filolojik temellerini korurken sosyal bilimler, beşerî bilimler ve spor bilimlerinin farklı yaklaşımlarıyla genişlediğini göstermektedir. Anahtar Kelimeler: Antik Yunan, Spor tarihi, Atletizm, Olimpiyat Oyunları, Sistematik derleme

Araştırma PRISMA 2020 rehberi doğrultusunda yürütülmüş ve nihai analize dahil edilen 62 çalışma tematik içerik analiziyle değerlendirilmiştir. Literatür taraması Scopus ve Web of Science Core Collection veri tabanlarında gerçekleştirilmiş ve dil sınırlaması uygulanmamıştır. Veri tabanı taramalarında 403 kayıt belirlenmiş, tekrarların çıkarılmasının ardından 297 benzersiz kayıt taranmış ve uygunluk değerlendirmesi sonucunda 62 çalışma nihai analize dahil edilmiştir. Çalışmaların %45,2’si 2020–2026 döneminde yayımlanmıştır. En sık araştırılan temalar atletik performans, antrenman ve teknik (%24,2) ile etik, değerler, rekabet, eğitim ve felsefe (%22,6) olmuştur. Araştırma yaklaşımlarında tarihsel ve karşılaştırmalı incelemeler (%30,6) ilk sırada yer alırken, incelenen spor dalları ve etkinlikler içinde genel atletizm ve beden eğitimi (%54,8) ile mücadele sporları (%27,4) öne çıkmıştır. Bulgular, Antik Yunan spor tarihi çalışmalarının klasik tarihsel ve filolojik temellerini korurken sosyal bilimler, beşerî bilimler ve spor bilimlerinin farklı yaklaşımlarıyla genişlediğini göstermektedir. title: Standardized Post-Bout Ringside Concussion Screening in Combat Sports
title_original: Standardized Post-Bout Ringside Concussion Screening in Combat Sports
summary: Context. The objective was a standardized post-bout ringside concussion protocol for combat sports regardless of rule set: professional boxing, mixed martial arts (MMA), bare-knuckle boxing, kickboxing, Toughman contests, amateur MMA and amateur boxing. Amateur boxing was the model for its stricter rules (mandatory post-bout examination, Sport Concussion Assessment Tool after a knockout or head-blow stoppage, tiered restrictions). Evidence Acquisition. PubMed/MEDLINE, Consensus, Scholar Gateway, Wiley Scholar Gateway, SciSpace, alphaXiv and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched on September 30, 2026, without limits, plus citation searching. One reviewer screened and extracted; the author verified a 10% sample. Synthesis followed the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis guideline. Study Design. Clinical review (systematic search with synthesis without meta-analysis) and instrument description. Level of Evidence. Level 3. Results. Of 2,250 records, 2,063 were screened and 214 core records were included (53 amateur); 137 rested on the abstract. Of 33 primary studies judged on full text, 16 were at high risk of bias. No amateur study measured the accuracy or reliability of any ringside item; nothing was pooled. Diagnosed concussion was recorded infrequently with incompatible denominators, stoppage could not substitute for diagnosis, and an abstract reported evolving cognitive slowing after 2 of 160 bouts in boxers not suspected at ringside. In other sports, single components were mostly specific, with limited sensitivity. Amateur evidence for every screening item was SORT Level 3. RACE1 is an 18-card post-bout screen, compared with a pre-bout baseline where possible, scored out of 20, with 3 provisional dispositions. Conclusions. A multidomain post-bout screen can standardize ringside findings, but a normal screen cannot exclude concussion. RACE1 is used only after the bout and never clears an athlete or permits same-day return. Evidence is mainly from amateur boxing; RACE1 has not been evaluated in any sport. Strength-of-Recommendation Taxonomy (SORT). After the bout, any sign, symptom or examination deficit precludes a "no deficit detected" result; absence of signs does not exclude concussion (B). Use brief items from several domains, never one domain alone (B). Transport any boxer with a red flag to a pre-identified trauma center with computed tomography and neurosurgical cover (C). A normal screen is not clearance (C).

title: Understanding athlete experiences in 3×3 basketball: a latent class analysis of service quality and satisfaction profiles
title_original: Understanding athlete experiences in 3×3 basketball: a latent class analysis of service quality and satisfaction profiles
summary: Introduction: The rapid global expansion of 3×3 basketball has transformed the sport into one of the most accessible and socially engaging forms of urban recreation. Despite its increasing popularity and inclusion in the Olympic Games, limited research has examined how participants evaluate their experiences in organized 3×3 basketball tournaments and whether distinct groups of athletes can be identified according to their perceptions of service quality and satisfaction. Objective: The purpose of this study was to identify latent athlete profiles based on perceptions of satisfaction, facilities, personnel, responsiveness, reliability, and participation outcomes in 3×3 basketball tournaments. Additionally, the study examined whether demographic and experiential characteristics, including age, years of team participation, coaching experience, and years of involvement in basketball, predicted membership in the identified profiles. Methodology: A total of 300 athletes participating in official 3×3 basketball tournaments across Greece completed validated questionnaires assessing service quality and satisfaction dimensions. Latent Class Analysis (LCA) was employed to identify homogeneous participant profiles, while demographic and experiential variables were incorporated as covariates. Results: The findings revealed three distinct athlete profiles. The first profile, labelled Low Evaluation of 3×3 (44.97%), was characterized by low levels of satisfaction and unfavorable evaluations across all service quality dimensions. The second profile, Moderate Evaluation of 3×3 (31.44%), demonstrated moderate perceptions across all variables. The third profile, High Evaluation of 3×3 (23.59%), reported consistently high levels of satisfaction, service quality perceptions, and participation outcomes. Among the examined covariates, only coaching experience significantly predicted profile membership, whereas age, years of team participation, and years of involvement in basketball were not significant predictors. Discussion: The study provides novel evidence regarding the heterogeneous nature of athlete experiences in 3×3 basketball and highlights the usefulness of person-centered analytical approaches in sport management research. Conclusion: The findings offer practical implications for event organizers, sport federations, and local authorities seeking to enhance participant experiences, increase satisfaction, and strengthen long-term engagement in urban sport events.

title: 詩讚姚明與他的「明朝」Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty"
title_original: 詩讚姚明與他的「明朝」Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty"
summary: 王抗曝、曹恆平(2026)《詩讚姚明與他的「明朝」》,《科學、技術、工程、藝術與數學之前瞻進展》, 8(10A),2026年10月,102頁,蘭諾出版社,美國麻省。Wang, Lawrence K. and Tsao, Hung-ping (2026). Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty." Evolutionary Progress in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics, 8(10A), October 2026, 102 pp. Lenox Institute Press, Massachusetts, USA. ABSTRACT: 姚明被世界公認為中國所培育出的最傑出籃球運動員之一;然而,他長遠的歷史意義,早已超越其非凡身高與運動成就。姚明於1980年出生於上海,從上海大鯊魚隊走向國際,並於2002年成為美國國家籃球協會選秀大會的第一順位球員。在效力休士頓火箭隊期間,他八次入選NBA全明星賽,五次入選NBA最佳陣容。他曾代表中國參加三屆奧林匹克運動會,於2016年入選奈史密斯籃球名人堂,並於2023年入選國際籃球總會名人堂。本文並非一篇普通的體育人物傳記,而是一篇跨領域的生命書寫。其創作緣起,是兩位作者王抗曝博士與曹恆平博士多年來共同對姚明所懷抱的欣賞與敬意。數學家曹恆平現居加州,人道環境工程師王抗曝現居紐約;兩人曾同為臺北國立臺灣師範大學附屬高級中學同學,並各自取得四個學位,一生重視教育。他們特別敬佩姚明在傷病結束籃球生涯後,仍努力取得經濟學學士學位。受到姚明充滿意義的「第二人生」啟發,曹、王二人亦於晚年走進詩歌,成為「半路出家」的詩歌學徒。本文探討姚明從上海走向休士頓的人生旅程、籃球成就、傷痛與退役、教育、慈善、兒童體育、野生動物保育、中國籃球領導工作,以及他作為中美文化橋樑的意義。本文主張:姚明的身高使他引人注目,球技使他享譽世界,而他的堅韌、謙遜、求知、慈愛與公共服務,才使他成為真正的巨人。本文透過個人回憶、人道環境反思與三語詩章,將姚明描繪為一位第二人生遠遠超越籃球場的楷模。本書繁體中文版並非已出版英文版的單純翻譯,而是一部經過實質擴充的增訂版本。除第3.2節外,全書各章原由王抗曝博士撰寫,並已以英文版出版。曹恆平博士閱讀該英文版後,將其於2002至2008年間隨姚明NBA生涯發展而撰寫的二十六篇球評與札記交予王抗曝。這些同時代文字記錄了一位海外華人資深球迷對姚明球技、人格、傷病、國家責任及北京奧運的即時觀察、預測與憂慮。兩位作者其後共同整理、擴充及修訂這批歷史資料,使當年的現場聲音與今日的生命回望,在本增訂中文版中彼此相遇。本書結合傳記敘事、同時代球評、個人回憶、人道環境反思與三語詩章,呈現姚明從上海走向休士頓、從「大明元年」走向北京奧運,以及從籃球巨星走向教育、慈善、保育與公共服務第二人生的完整歷程。本書所稱姚明的「明朝」,並非指中國歷史上的明王朝,而是曹恆平巧妙借用姚明姓名中的「明」字,將姚明於2002年進入NBA稱為「大明元年」,並以「大明王朝」象徵海外華人球迷對其籃球生涯所寄予的期待。ABSTRACT: Yao Ming is remembered internationally as one of the greatest basketball players to emerge from China, but his enduring significance reaches far beyond his extraordinary height and athletic accomplishments. Born in Shanghai in 1980, Yao rose from the Shanghai Sharks to become the first overall selection in the 2002 National Basketball Association Draft. During his career with the Houston Rockets, he became an eight-time NBA All-Star and five-time All-NBA selection. He represented China at three Olympic Games, entered the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2016, and was inducted into the NBA Hall of Fame in 2023. This article is not a conventional sports biography. It is an interdisciplinary work of life writing inspired by the longtime admiration shared by the two coauthors, Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and Dr. Hung-ping Tsao, who are lifelong friends and former high-school classmates. It examines Yao's journey from Shanghai to Houston, his basketball accomplishments, physical suffering and retirement, education, philanthropy, youth programs, wildlife conservation, leadership of Chinese basketball, and role as a cultural bridge between China and the United States. Personal recollection, humanitarian environmental reflection, and trilingual poetry present Yao Ming as a role model whose second life reached far beyond the basketball court. The traditional Chinese edition of this book is not a mere translation of the already published English version; rather, it is a substantively expanded and revised edition. Except for Section 3.2, all chapters were originally written by Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and published its English edition. After reading the English edition, Dr. Hung ping Tsao entrusted Wang with twenty six commentaries and notes he had written between 2002 and 2008 during the unfolding of Yao Ming's NBA career. These contemporaneous writings document a seasoned overseas Chinese basketball fan's real time observations, predictions, and concerns regarding Yao Ming's skills, character, injuries, sense of national responsibility, and the Beijing Olympics. The two authors subsequently organized, expanded, and revised this historical corpus, allowing the voices of that era and today's reflective perspectives to meet within this enriched Chinese edition. This book weaves together biographical narrative, contemporaneous basketball commentary, personal recollection, humanitarian and environmental reflection, and trilingual poetic chapters. It presents Yao Ming's full journey—from Shanghai to Houston, from the "First Year of the Ming Era" to the Beijing Olympics, and from basketball superstar to a second life devoted to education, philanthropy, conservation, and public service. The term "Ming Dynasty" in this book does not refer to the historical Chinese dynasty; rather, Dr. Tsao ingeniously borrows the character "Ming" from Yao Ming's name, designating his entry into the NBA in 2002 as the "First Year of the Ming Era," with the "Ming Dynasty" symbolizing the hopes placed upon his basketball career by overseas Chinese fans.

title: How do we teach English under the waves of innovation?: discovering perceptions of English learning and teaching in China and the UK
title_original: How do we teach English under the waves of innovation?: discovering perceptions of English learning and teaching in China and the UK
summary: In response to a growing amount of Chinese students pursuing higher education abroad influenced by the rapid economic, social and cultural development in China, this study explores Chinese Second Language (L2) learners and teachers’ perceptions of English Language Teaching (ELT) from secondary school level through tertiary level. English language education has experienced extensive reforms and development, however, Chinese students’ voices reflecting their English learning experience are not positioned as key consideration throughout these learning stages. In this case, this study discusses L2 learners and teachers’ experience of transitions in ELT throughout different learning stages and perceptions of intercultural knowledge embedded within ELT, uncovering English learning difficulties via self-assessment, digging deeply about L2 learners and teachers’ feedback about group work, learner autonomy, exams and interaction between students and teachers. By prioritizing learners and teachers’ feedback and hearing their voices, this study draws upon large-scale data derived from semi-structured individual and group interviews, surveys and focus groups collected over a period of 20 months’ data fieldwork in China and the UK. Responses were gathered from 500 high school students and qualitative interviews with 80 Chinese undergraduates, postgraduates and teachers in Chinese and UK universities in order to build the bridge between learning and teaching perspectives. In this study, survey and interview data is analysed to examine more specifically, Chinese undergraduates and postgraduates who are currently studying in UK universities, with particular reference to international students’ psychological and sociocultural adaptation within their visited country education systems. Specifically, key findings of this research reveal the unbalanced and unequal distribution of ELT education resources between developed and less developed regions, which closely related to students’ attitudes and awareness of output (writing and speaking) practices and access to intercultural knowledge. The influences of Confucianism and traditional Chinese learning culture on Chinese students’ English language learning, which lead to students’ fear of making mistakes and losing face. The directional and leading role of exams throughout Chinese students’ English learning journey and students’ highlights of exam strategies and memorization. The findings from this study help to shed light on how English language policies directly and indirectly influence ELT development in China.

By prioritizing learners and teachers’ feedback and hearing their voices, this study draws upon large-scale data derived from semi-structured individual and group interviews, surveys and focus groups collected over a period of 20 months’ data fieldwork in China and the UK. Responses were gathered from 500 high school students and qualitative interviews with 80 Chinese undergraduates, postgraduates and teachers in Chinese and UK universities in order to build the bridge between learning and teaching perspectives. In this study, survey and interview data is analysed to examine more specifically, Chinese undergraduates and postgraduates who are currently studying in UK universities, with particular reference to international students’ psychological and sociocultural adaptation within their visited country education systems. Specifically, key findings of this research reveal the unbalanced and unequal distribution of ELT education resources between developed and less developed regions, which closely related to students’ attitudes and awareness of output (writing and speaking) practices and access to intercultural knowledge. The influences of Confucianism and traditional Chinese learning culture on Chinese students’ English language learning, which lead to students’ fear of making mistakes and losing face. The directional and leading role of exams throughout Chinese students’ English learning journey and students’ highlights of exam strategies and memorization. The findings from this study help to shed light on how English language policies directly and indirectly influence ELT development in China.

title: Quasi-Constitutionality and Indigenous-State Treaties in Australia
title_original: Quasi-Constitutionality and Indigenous-State Treaties in Australia
summary: The Statewide Treaty negotiated between the First Peoples Assembly of Victoria and the Victorian government is momentous. However, the Statewide Treaty Bill 2025 (Vic), which implements the agreement, is an ordinary piece of legislation subject to the ordinary rules of statutory interpretation and implied repeal. Drawing on jurisprudence from Canada, the United Kingdom and scholarship from the United States, we argue that the anticipated Statewide Treaty Act should properly be understood as ‘quasi-constitutional’ because it: (i) shapes the character of Victoria in moral and legal ways, (ii) is understood within the broader community as a statute of great importance, and (iii) regulates the institutions and powers of the state. This designation has important legal and expressive implications which supports the status and prominence of Indigenous-State treaties.

title: Government Communication and Terrorist Organizations: Towards a Concept of “Crisis Communication” in reaction to 21st Century Islamic Terrorist Attacks for Western Governments
title_original: Government Communication and Terrorist Organizations: Towards a Concept of “Crisis Communication” in reaction to 21st Century Islamic Terrorist Attacks for Western Governments
summary: This thesis addresses the following question: how do and how should Western governments communicate the threat of terrorism, the nature of terrorist activities and their impact on their populations? The main goal behind answering this question is to find out how statements after the most significant Islamic terrorist threats and attacks were influenced by and did influence the socio-political narratives in the UK, France and Germany. This is important as political reactions to terrorist attacks often lead to longer lasting changes than the actual attacks themselves. Political statements are usually the first publicly noticeable action taken and can help to fill a vacuum developed through the uncertainty after unfamiliar events. This systematic comparative analysis of statements from political leaders from the three most influential European states contributes to the existing academic literature in the fields of political communication and counterterrorism as it shows how different cultural norms, political changes and demographic developments affect the content of political statements in reaction to Islamic terrorist threats and attacks. In this thesis, a profound foundation for the systematic analysis of these statements is laid by reconstructing the broader socio-political contexts that existed around the times the statements analysed were first given and then breaking the communication processes down to the different aspects involved in disseminating the message. These aspects are based on Lasswell’s Communication Model and include sender, message, medium, receiver and feedback. The core aspect is the message, which is analysed by using Narrative Analysis focusing on content, terminology and Social Actors. The central argument is that even though different political structures, socio-political contexts and cultural norms influence the basic settings of statements given by the political leaders of the UK, France and Germany and reactions to them by members of the public, demographic changes and an ever faster globalisation have a strong and similar effect on all three countries. Thus, demographic changes and globalisation at an unprecedented pace have contributed to changes in broader political narratives that made it more difficult for leaders of centrist governments to find a political balance that prevents movements of supporters to the right in the political spectrum. This challenge in political communication strongly affected the content of the statements analysed. The systematic analysis conducted in the thesis shows that, as long as they are communicated in a way that fits inside current socio-political frames with consideration of the broader normative contexts that define what is appropriate in times of threat and uncertainty, aspects such as awareness of counterterror and domestic political intentions, timing, credibility in the broader political context, content related aspects such as root causes of Islamic terrorist threats and attacks, the consideration of demographic changes and the length of statements can have direct impacts on the efficacy of statements in reactions to Islamic terrorist threats or attacks.

title: The market potential of local sponsorships in the UEFA Champions League
title_original: The market potential of local sponsorships in the UEFA Champions League
summary: This Master's thesis examines the market potential of local sponsorships within the UEFA Champions League, a competition traditionally structured around global and standardized sponsorship agreements.While the Champions League offers extensive international exposure, its audience is distributed across heterogeneous markets that differ in economic size, purchasing power, and levels of engagement with football.The thesis is grounded in the concept of glocalization and investigates whether these market differences translate into systematic variation in the perceived value of local sponsorships.The research adopts a mixed-methods approach.The quantitative component is based on three independent expert evaluations of local sponsorship value across multiple markets, two of which were provided by specialists presented as Interviewee A (Company A) and Interviewee B (Company B) and the third one was provided by exclusive analytical knowhow developed by Company D. These evaluations reflect professional market assessments grounded in applied sponsorship practice and are examined in relation to objective economic and media-related indicators, including market economic size, UEFA Champions League viewership and purchasing power parity, through Pearson correlation analysis.In addition to their quantitative assessments, both experts participated in in-depth interviews that provided contextual insight into valuation logic, governance constraints, and structural characteristics of the current global sponsorship model.The qualitative component is further complemented by a case study based on an expert interview with Company C, a company specializing in virtual advertising and immersive broadcast solutions, examining the operational feasibility of localized sponsorship activation within a globally standardized competition structure.The results of the quantitative analysis show that the perceived value of local sponsorships is strongly and consistently associated with objective market characteristics.Market economic size and media exposure emerge as the key correlates of local sponsorship value, indicating that sponsorship potential varies systematically across markets.Importantly, the findings suggest that smaller markets can achieve significant sponsorship value when high levels of audience interest in the UEFA Champions League are present.The qualitative findings deepen this interpretation: the interviews with representatives of Company A and Company B confirm that industry practice recognizes structural differences between markets and increasingly demands geographically aligned sponsorship solutions, while the Company C case study demonstrates that technological solutions such as virtual advertising enable market-specific sponsorship activation without undermining existing global sponsorship agreements.Overall, the findings confirm that localized sponsorships represent a feasible and economically meaningful complement to the existing global sponsorship model of the UEFA Champions League.

title: Categories and Ideas Informing Critical Thought in Brazilian Urban Studies: Trajectories and Tensions
title_original: Categories and Ideas Informing Critical Thought in Brazilian Urban Studies: Trajectories and Tensions
summary: This article analyzes trajectories of the categories “periphery,” “favela” and “urban social movements” in Brazilian urban studies, from the developmentalism of the 1950s to the recent neoliberal period, focusing on intellectual production from the Rio-São Paulo axis. It examines the tension between the influence of Eurocentric theoretical frameworks and conceptualizations developed from the Brazilian context. It discusses the role of institutions such as ISEB, CEBRAP and CEDEC in shaping the field, as well as the limitations of the interpretations they produced, which have frequently overlooked race and gender as structuring dimensions of urban experience. Finally, it proposes bringing together urban political economy and decolonial perspectives through the analytical triad of the coloniality, imperiality and nationality of power. This approach seeks to reinterpret the production of urban space in Brazil, highlighting how epistemic and racial hierarchies shape socio-spatial inequalities while also pointing to the emancipatory potential of knowledge and struggles emerging from the peripheries themselves.

title: Orphaned by an Evidentiary Standard: How Efficacy Review Emptied the Anabolic‐Androgenic Steroid Market, and What Doping Control Inherited
title_original: Orphaned by an Evidentiary Standard: How Efficacy Review Emptied the Anabolic‐Androgenic Steroid Market, and What Doping Control Inherited
summary: The anabolic-androgenic steroids have largely left clinical medicine while remaining in wide non-medical use. This review documents how that happened from the supply side, using the US Federal Register from 1970 to 2026, approval and patent records, statutes, treaty texts, and the peer-reviewed analytical literature. Three European firms created the class in 1935, their research contracted to university laboratories, and seven firms in five countries built it out by 1962, into a market where branded androgen preparations were already sold. The FDA's Drug Efficacy Study Implementation 7630 then condemned the tissue-building claims in 1970, retained an osteoporosis claim only while no alternative existed, and closed in 1985 after no sponsor completed the studies. A parallel proceeding on the estrogen-androgen combinations, opened in 1972, was resolved only in 2026. No safety finding drove any of it. Only one product in the class, oxandrolone, was ever determined withdrawn for reasons of safety or effectiveness, and 21 CFR 216.24 contains no anabolic-androgenic steroid. Most applications lapsed. The two jurisdictions then diverged. The US moved these substances into narcotics law in 1990 while European states did not make that move, with consequences for the public health work possible in each. Three of the first designer steroids identified in sport had never been sold as medicines, and for two of them the laboratories had to synthesize reference material before any assay existed. Section S0 of the WADA Prohibited List now names discontinued drugs. The pattern has since repeated with the selective androgen receptor modulators.

title: Disrupting the state: mega-events, bureaucratic displacement and institutional change in Chilean sport
title_original: Disrupting the state: mega-events, bureaucratic displacement and institutional change in Chilean sport
summary: Sport mega-events are frequently justified by political authorities on the basis of their expected benefits and legacies, yet delivering them depends on complex administrative arrangements in which bureaucrats from diverse institutions must translate competing political and administrative ambitions into concrete outcomes. Notably, despite extensive research on sport mega-events, little is known about how hosting – understood as a potential critical juncture capable of triggering institutional change – affects the structures, routines and institutional arrangements of government bureaucrats. Drawing on a historical institutionalist lens, this study addresses this issue through interviews with sport bureaucrats from Chile’s two main sport institutions: the Ministry of Sport and the National Institute of Sport. The main research question is: How did the hosting of the 2023 Pan American Games in Santiago impact the structures, institutional arrangements and routines of Chilean sport bureaucrats? While associated with several positive legacies, the findings reveal that the Games introduced significant uncertainty and instability into bureaucratic arrangements, generating intense operational pressures and prompting new rules and organisational structures. These findings demonstrate that sport mega-events can reorganise administrative attention and produce lasting institutional change, offering insight into why event-led development strategies persist in Chile and other Global South contexts.

title: 诗赞姚明与他的"明朝" Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty"
title_original: 诗赞姚明与他的"明朝" Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty"
summary: 王抗曝、曹恒平(2026)《诗赞姚明与他的"明朝"》,《科学、技术、工程、艺术与数学之前瞻进展》, 8(10B),2026年10月,102页,兰诺出版社,美国麻省。Wang, Lawrence K. and Tsao, Hung-ping (2026). Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty." Evolutionary Progress in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics, 8(10B), October 2026, 102 pp. Lenox Institute Press, Massachusetts, USA. 摘要: 《诗赞姚明与他的"明朝"》姚明被世界公认为中国所培养出的最杰出篮球运动员之一;然而,他长远的历史意义,早已超越其非凡身高与运动成就。姚明于1980年出生于上海,从上海大鲨鱼队走向国际,并于2002年成为美国国家篮球协会选秀大会的第一顺位球员。在效力休斯敦火箭队期间,他八次入选NBA全明星赛,五次入选NBA最佳阵容。他曾代表中国参加三届奥林匹克运动会,于2016年入选奈史密斯篮球名人堂,并于2023年入选国际篮球联合会名人堂。本文并非一篇普通的体育人物传记,而是一篇跨领域的生命书写。其创作缘起,是两位作者王抗曝博士与曹恒平博士多年来共同对姚明所怀抱的欣赏与敬意。数学家曹恒平现居加州,人道环境工程师王抗曝现居纽约;两人曾同为台北国立台湾师范大学附属高级中学同学,并各自取得四个学位,一生重视教育。他们特别敬佩姚明在伤病结束篮球生涯后,仍努力取得经济学学士学位。受到姚明充满意义的"第二人生"启发,曹、王二人亦于晚年走进诗歌,成为"半路出家"的诗歌学徒。本文探讨姚明从上海走向休斯敦的人生旅程、篮球成就、伤痛与退役、教育、慈善、儿童体育、野生动物保护、中国篮球领导工作,以及他作为中美文化桥梁的意义。本文主张:姚明的身高使他引人注目,球技使他享誉世界,而他的坚韧、谦逊、求知、慈爱与公共服务,才使他成为真正的巨人。本文通过个人回忆、人道环境反思与三语诗章,将姚明描绘为一位第二人生远远超越篮球场的楷模。本书简体中文版以增订繁体中文版为依据,并非已出版英文版的单纯翻译,而是一部经过实质扩充的增订版本。除第3.2节外,全书各章原由王抗曝博士撰写,并已出版。曹恒平博士阅读该英文版后,将其于2002至2008年间随姚明NBA生涯发展而撰写的二十六篇球评与札记交予王抗曝。这些同时代文字记录了一位海外华人资深球迷对姚明球技、人格、伤病、国家责任及北京奥运的即时观察、预测与忧虑。两位作者其后共同整理、扩充及修订这批历史资料,使当年的现场声音与今日的生命回望,在本增订中文版中彼此相遇。本书结合传记叙事、同时代球评、个人回忆、人道环境反思与三语诗章,呈现姚明从上海走向休斯敦、从"大明元年"走向北京奥运,以及从篮球巨星走向教育、慈善、保育与公共服务第二人生的完整历程。本书所称姚明的"明朝",并非指中国历史上的明王朝,而是曹恒平巧妙借用姚明姓名中的"明"字,将姚明于2002年进入NBA称为"大明元年",并以"大明王朝"象征海外华人球迷对其篮球生涯所寄予的期待。ABSTRACT: Yao Ming is remembered internationally as one of the greatest basketball players to emerge from China, but his enduring significance reaches far beyond his extraordinary height and athletic accomplishments. Born in Shanghai in 1980, Yao rose from the Shanghai Sharks to become the first overall selection in the 2002 National Basketball Association Draft. During his career with the Houston Rockets, he became an eight-time NBA All-Star and five-time All-NBA selection. He represented China at three Olympic Games, entered the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2016, and was inducted into the NBA Hall of Fame in 2023. This article is not a conventional sports biography. It is an interdisciplinary work of life writing inspired by the longtime admiration shared by the two coauthors, Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and Dr. Hung-ping Tsao, who are lifelong friends and former high-school classmates. It examines Yao's journey from Shanghai to Houston, his basketball accomplishments, physical suffering and retirement, education, philanthropy, youth programs, wildlife conservation, leadership of Chinese basketball, and role as a cultural bridge between China and the United States. Personal recollection, humanitarian environmental reflection, and trilingual poetry present Yao Ming as a role model whose second life reached far beyond the basketball court. This Simplified Chinese edition is based on the expanded Traditional Chinese edition and is not a mere translation of the already published English version; rather, it is a substantively expanded and revised edition. Except for Section 3.2, all chapters were originally written by Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and published as the English edition. After reading the English edition, Dr. Hung ping Tsao entrusted Wang with twenty six commentaries and notes he had written between 2002 and 2008 during the unfolding of Yao Ming's NBA career. These contemporaneous writings document a seasoned overseas Chinese basketball fan's real time observations, predictions, and concerns regarding Yao Ming's skills, character, injuries, sense of national responsibility, and the Beijing Olympics. The two authors subsequently organized, expanded, and revised this historical corpus, allowing the voices of that era and today's reflective perspectives to meet within this enriched Chinese edition. This book weaves together biographical narrative, contemporaneous basketball commentary, personal recollection, humanitarian and environmental reflection, and trilingual poetic chapters. It presents Yao Ming's full journey—from Shanghai to Houston, from the "First Year of the Ming Era" to the Beijing Olympics, and from basketball superstar to a second life devoted to education, philanthropy, conservation, and public service. The term "Ming Dynasty" in this book does not refer to the historical Chinese dynasty; rather, Dr. Tsao ingeniously borrows the character "Ming" from Yao Ming's name, designating his entry into the NBA in 2002 as the "First Year of the Ming Era," with the "Ming Dynasty" symbolizing the hopes placed upon his basketball career by overseas Chinese fans.

Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty." Evolutionary Progress in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics, 8(10B), October 2026, 102 pp. Lenox Institute Press, Massachusetts, USA. 摘要: 《诗赞姚明与他的"明朝"》姚明被世界公认为中国所培养出的最杰出篮球运动员之一;然而,他长远的历史意义,早已超越其非凡身高与运动成就。姚明于1980年出生于上海,从上海大鲨鱼队走向国际,并于2002年成为美国国家篮球协会选秀大会的第一顺位球员。在效力休斯敦火箭队期间,他八次入选NBA全明星赛,五次入选NBA最佳阵容。他曾代表中国参加三届奥林匹克运动会,于2016年入选奈史密斯篮球名人堂,并于2023年入选国际篮球联合会名人堂。本文并非一篇普通的体育人物传记,而是一篇跨领域的生命书写。其创作缘起,是两位作者王抗曝博士与曹恒平博士多年来共同对姚明所怀抱的欣赏与敬意。数学家曹恒平现居加州,人道环境工程师王抗曝现居纽约;两人曾同为台北国立台湾师范大学附属高级中学同学,并各自取得四个学位,一生重视教育。他们特别敬佩姚明在伤病结束篮球生涯后,仍努力取得经济学学士学位。受到姚明充满意义的"第二人生"启发,曹、王二人亦于晚年走进诗歌,成为"半路出家"的诗歌学徒。本文探讨姚明从上海走向休斯敦的人生旅程、篮球成就、伤痛与退役、教育、慈善、儿童体育、野生动物保护、中国篮球领导工作,以及他作为中美文化桥梁的意义。本文主张:姚明的身高使他引人注目,球技使他享誉世界,而他的坚韧、谦逊、求知、慈爱与公共服务,才使他成为真正的巨人。本文通过个人回忆、人道环境反思与三语诗章,将姚明描绘为一位第二人生远远超越篮球场的楷模。本书简体中文版以增订繁体中文版为依据,并非已出版英文版的单纯翻译,而是一部经过实质扩充的增订版本。除第3.2节外,全书各章原由王抗曝博士撰写,并已出版。曹恒平博士阅读该英文版后,将其于2002至2008年间随姚明NBA生涯发展而撰写的二十六篇球评与札记交予王抗曝。这些同时代文字记录了一位海外华人资深球迷对姚明球技、人格、伤病、国家责任及北京奥运的即时观察、预测与忧虑。两位作者其后共同整理、扩充及修订这批历史资料,使当年的现场声音与今日的生命回望,在本增订中文版中彼此相遇。本书结合传记叙事、同时代球评、个人回忆、人道环境反思与三语诗章,呈现姚明从上海走向休斯敦、从"大明元年"走向北京奥运,以及从篮球巨星走向教育、慈善、保育与公共服务第二人生的完整历程。本书所称姚明的"明朝",并非指中国历史上的明王朝,而是曹恒平巧妙借用姚明姓名中的"明"字,将姚明于2002年进入NBA称为"大明元年",并以"大明王朝"象征海外华人球迷对其篮球生涯所寄予的期待。ABSTRACT: Yao Ming is remembered internationally as one of the greatest basketball players to emerge from China, but his enduring significance reaches far beyond his extraordinary height and athletic accomplishments. Born in Shanghai in 1980, Yao rose from the Shanghai Sharks to become the first overall selection in the 2002 National Basketball Association Draft. During his career with the Houston Rockets, he became an eight-time NBA All-Star and five-time All-NBA selection. He represented China at three Olympic Games, entered the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2016, and was inducted into the NBA Hall of Fame in 2023. This article is not a conventional sports biography. It is an interdisciplinary work of life writing inspired by the longtime admiration shared by the two coauthors, Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and Dr. Hung-ping Tsao, who are lifelong friends and former high-school classmates. It examines Yao's journey from Shanghai to Houston, his basketball accomplishments, physical suffering and retirement, education, philanthropy, youth programs, wildlife conservation, leadership of Chinese basketball, and role as a cultural bridge between China and the United States. Personal recollection, humanitarian environmental reflection, and trilingual poetry present Yao Ming as a role model whose second life reached far beyond the basketball court. This Simplified Chinese edition is based on the expanded Traditional Chinese edition and is not a mere translation of the already published English version; rather, it is a substantively expanded and revised edition. Except for Section 3.2, all chapters were originally written by Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and published as the English edition. After reading the English edition, Dr. Hung ping Tsao entrusted Wang with twenty six commentaries and notes he had written between 2002 and 2008 during the unfolding of Yao Ming's NBA career. These contemporaneous writings document a seasoned overseas Chinese basketball fan's real time observations, predictions, and concerns regarding Yao Ming's skills, character, injuries, sense of national responsibility, and the Beijing Olympics. The two authors subsequently organized, expanded, and revised this historical corpus, allowing the voices of that era and today's reflective perspectives to meet within this enriched Chinese edition. This book weaves together biographical narrative, contemporaneous basketball commentary, personal recollection, humanitarian and environmental reflection, and trilingual poetic chapters. It presents Yao Ming's full journey—from Shanghai to Houston, from the "First Year of the Ming Era" to the Beijing Olympics, and from basketball superstar to a second life devoted to education, philanthropy, conservation, and public service. The term "Ming Dynasty" in this book does not refer to the historical Chinese dynasty; rather, Dr. Tsao ingeniously borrows the character "Ming" from Yao Ming's name, designating his entry into the NBA in 2002 as the "First Year of the Ming Era," with the "Ming Dynasty" symbolizing the hopes placed upon his basketball career by overseas Chinese fans.

title: Identifiability, Sequentiality and Infinity (--Remarks--)
title_original: Identifiability, Sequentiality and Infinity (--Remarks--)
summary: Two sections are added to my previous article with similar title, in relation to the so-called dynamic logic-error, other complications with modern mathematics and some details on the philosophy behind scene. These remarks could be seen as more details on the axioms of math-arguments and the actual basis-inspiration of the meta-math previously developed. In other words, this `continuation' gives the connection between (meta-)mathematics and the science of the creation-energy.
