title: A fadinha do skate na publicidade: : a representação mítica da atleta Rayssa Leal no comercial “Novas fadas”
title_original: A fadinha do skate na publicidade: : a representação mítica da atleta Rayssa Leal no comercial “Novas fadas”
summary: O presente estudo objetiva analisar a representação mítica da atleta brasileira Rayssa Leal em mídias publicitárias veiculadas nos Jogos Olímpicos de Tóquio 2020, atendo-se, particularmente, ao comercial “Novas Fadas”, da marca Nike. A pesquisa caracterizou-se como Básica, de abordagem Qualitativa, com finalidade Exploratório-Descritiva, utilizando-se de estudo de caso e análise fílmica da peça publicitária selecionada. A técnica permitiu observar elementos narrativos, simbólicos e audiovisuais que sustentam a representação da atleta, obtendo resultados que demonstram que a publicidade não apenas reforçou a imagem da atleta como ícone juvenil e esportivo, mas, também, operou como um meio de mitificação, transformando a figura pública de Rayssa em símbolo de empoderamento, superação e inspiração coletiva. Constatou-se, ainda, que os elementos audiovisuais e narrativos presentes na peça ressignificam a história pessoal da atleta, conectando-se a arquétipos culturais e afetivos já reconhecidos socialmente. Conclui-se, então, que esse tipo de construção midiática tem implicações diretas na forma como a sociedade vê figuras públicas e consome narrativas simbólic

title: Technical and Operational Assessment of a Large-Scale Hydrogen Mobility System Under Extreme Winter Conditions: Evidence from the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics
title_original: Technical and Operational Assessment of a Large-Scale Hydrogen Mobility System Under Extreme Winter Conditions: Evidence from the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics
summary: As the decarbonisation of transport continues, hydrogen fuel cell vehicles (HFCVs) are attracting increasing attention, particularly in heavy-duty and high-utilisation applications where long operating ranges and rapid refuelling are required. Transferring HFCVs from individual demonstrations to large-scale fleet operation, however, depends on the joint performance of vehicles, hydrogen supply, refuelling infrastructure and operational management. Our study examines the technical and operational feasibility of large-scale hydrogen mobility using the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games as a case study. The analysis covers vehicle deployment and scenario matching, hydrogen production and road distribution, refuelling infrastructure, digital monitoring, fleet coordination, and operational performance under extreme winter and mountainous conditions. More than 1200 HFCVs operated for 52 days across over 80 routes and accumulated more than 3.5 million vehicle-kilometres, supported by 11 hydrogen refuelling stations and approximately 20 t d−1 of hydrogen production capacity. The case study shows that successful fleet operation depended on matching vehicle configurations to transport tasks, coordinating hydrogen supply with refuelling demand, maintaining redundancy across the supply network - and integrating real time monitoring with fleet dispatch. These findings help to identify the main technical and operational conditions for large-scale hydrogen mobility and provide practical guidance for centralised applications, such as public transport, shuttle services and logistics fleets.

title: Infrastructure-Superstructure Contradictions in Vietnamese Elite Sports: An Analysis from the Perspective of Historical Materialism
title_original: Infrastructure-Superstructure Contradictions in Vietnamese Elite Sports: An Analysis from the Perspective of Historical Materialism
summary: Applying the historical materialist principle of the dialectical relationship between infrastructure and superstructure, this study examines the development of Vietnamese elite sports from 2011 to 2026. Using historical-logical analysis and an empirical survey of managers, coaches, and athletes, the study identifies a performance paradox: Vietnam has maintained strong results at the SEA Games while achieving more limited outcomes at the ASIAD and Olympic levels. The analysis associates this pattern with institutional desynchronization between changing economic and material conditions and slower administrative and regulatory adaptation. Key issues include barriers to public-private partnerships, limited autonomy of sports federations, shortcomings in athlete remuneration and occupational insurance, and insufficient investment in advanced training technologies. In relation to Decision No. 1189/QD-TTg and national sports development objectives to 2030 with a vision to 2045, the study proposes coordinated institutional reforms, improved resource mobilization, and greater application of artificial intelligence, biosensors, and sports biomedicine to support sustainable elite sports development.

title: 33rd SEA Games Takeaways: Balancing Sport and Southeast Asia’s Complex Environment
title_original: 33rd SEA Games Takeaways: Balancing Sport and Southeast Asia’s Complex Environment
summary: The SEA Games this year took place in Thailand, marking the seventh time that the country has hosted Southeast Asia's biggest sporting event. Thailand comes out on top of the table, achieving an all-time record of 233 out of 573 possible Gold Medals, overtaking Vietnam's 2022 record of 205 Gold Medals. Another interesting fact regarding this year's event is that several countries sent their largest-ever delegations to the 33rd SEA Games as Singapore sent 930, the Philippines with 1,168, and Malaysia with 1,166 athletes, positively reflecting the expanded 50-sport program and Olympic-aligned events in this year's SEA Games. Despite the positive updates from the 33rd SEA Games, the event also saw Cambodia withdraw 1,515 athletes due to the intensifying Cambodian-Thai border conflict, leaving only 10 countries participating. In this sense, the event mirrored broader ASEAN challenges in managing intra-regional disputes while upholding the principle of regional harmony. A setback also occurred during the preparation, as cyclone Senyar hit and caused flooding in the Songkhla province, forcing 10 sports to relocate from the Southern venue just a week before the opening on 9th December 2025. Some technical issues by the organiser also coloured this year's event, including flag and national anthem errors, which raised questions about the host's preparedness. In Southeast Asia, where national identity and sovereignty remain deeply salient, such incidents risk diplomatic friction and public backlash, emphasizing the political sensitivity embedded in regional sporting events.Our adjunct researcher, Dr Muhammad Rum, delivered his point of view in accordance with the 33rd SEA Games and what lessons learned can be taken for Malaysia as the next host in 2027.

title: Promoting fair play in university sports in Zimbabwe
title_original: Promoting fair play in university sports in Zimbabwe
summary: This study explores the perceptions and lived experiences of university sports administrators in Zimbabwe regarding fair play violations, focusing on perceived causes, impacts, and mitigation strategies within university sport. Guided by a qualitative phenomenological design, data were generated through semi-structured interviews conducted in English with 35 administrators from 16 universities affiliated with the Zimbabwe Universities Sports Association (ZUSA). Of the participants, 23 formed the final sample, selected through stratified purposive sampling, with data saturation determining the endpoint. Ethical approval was granted by the ZUSA Executive, and all participants provided informed consent. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed using iterative thematic analysis. Trustworthiness was strengthened through methodological transparency, reflexive engagement, and consistent application of the coding framework. Findings indicate that fair play violations, including the use of non-student athletes, doping, violence, and gamesmanship, are perceived as widespread and structurally embedded within university sport. Participants linked these practices to a “win-at-all-costs” culture driven by recognition, material incentives, and the emulation of professional athletes who normalise unethical conduct. Such violations undermine competitive integrity, compromise athlete safety, and damage institutional reputation, limiting sponsorship and development opportunities. The analysis also informed the inductively derived Fair Play Restoration Model (FPRM), explaining how governance reform, ethical reorientation, and institutional accountability can restore fair play in university sport.

title: JISMONIY TARBIYA VA SPORT TA’LIMIDA BO‘LAJAK MURABBIYLARNING DEONTOLOGIK KOMPETENTLIGINI RIVOJLANTIRISH TEXNOLOGIYALARI
title_original: JISMONIY TARBIYA VA SPORT TA’LIMIDA BO‘LAJAK MURABBIYLARNING DEONTOLOGIK KOMPETENTLIGINI RIVOJLANTIRISH TEXNOLOGIYALARI
summary: This article analyzes the pedagogical possibilities, content, and effective technologies for developing the deontological competence of future coaches within the physical education and sports training system. A modern sports coach acts not only as a specialist organizing the physical and technical-tactical preparation of athletes but also as an educator, a source of psychological support, a teacher, and a moral role model. Therefore, fostering qualities such as professional duty, responsibility, fairness, honesty, respect for the athlete's honor and dignity, pedagogical tact, confidentiality, professional ethics, and skills for the constructive resolution of conflict situations in future coaches is a crucial pedagogical task. The article identifies the structural components of deontological competence and substantiates the potential of technologies such as problem-based learning, case studies, role-playing games, training sessions, the reflective approach, mentoring, and pedagogical practice in its development. Additionally, criteria and levels for assessing the deontological competence of future coaches are proposed.

title: Sport Motivation Among Young Fencers Training in a Ukrainian Olympic Reserve School During Wartime: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
title_original: Sport Motivation Among Young Fencers Training in a Ukrainian Olympic Reserve School During Wartime: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
summary: Background and purpose Young athletes in Ukraine continue to train during the war, which may disrupt training routines and affect their motivation. However, evidence on sport motivation among young athletes training in Olympic reserve systems during wartime remains limited. This study examined motivation among young fencers training in a Ukrainian Olympic reserve school during wartime and its associations with perceived coach support and war-related disruption of training. Material and methods This exploratory cross-sectional study involved 64 young fencers from a Specialized Youth Sports School of Olympic Reserve in Mykolaiv, Ukraine. Participants ranged in age from 10 to 19 years (M = 14.81, SD = 2.05). Sport motivation was assessed using the Sport Motivation Scale-II, which measures intrinsic motivation, integrated regulation, identified regulation, introjected regulation, external regulation, and amotivation. Additional study-specific items assessed war-related disruption of training and perceived coach support. Descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha coefficients, Pearson correlation analysis, independent samples t-tests, and one-way analysis of variance were used. Results The highest mean scores were observed for identified regulation, intrinsic motivation, and integrated regulation, whereas external regulation and amotivation showed lower values. These three dimensions showed acceptable-to-good internal consistency and moderate-to-strong positive correlations with each other. No statistically significant associations were found between motivational dimensions and perceived war-related disruption or coach support. Female athletes reported significantly higher intrinsic motivation than male athletes (p = 0.010), while no other gender differences were observed. Competition participation level was significantly associated only with introjected regulation (F(2, 61) = 3.45, p = 0.038, η² = 0.10), with athletes without competition experience reporting higher scores than those competing at national or international levels. Conclusions More self-determined forms of motivation predominated among young fencers training in a Ukrainian Olympic reserve school during wartime. Identified regulation, intrinsic motivation, and integrated regulation were also the most closely related motivational dimensions. Perceived war-related disruption and coach support were not significantly associated with motivational dimensions. The small single-school sample limits the generalizability of these findings, and larger studies are needed to confirm them.

title: International rankings and the reproduction of inequality in higher education
title_original: International rankings and the reproduction of inequality in higher education
summary: Digitalization is reshaping global ranking systems for universities which influences their evaluation governance and equity. However this transformation is not only technological it is also linked to deeper structural historical and institutional dynamics that influence equity and visibility in global higher education. This study offers a review of literature based on a discourse analysis of international ranking frame-works, like particularly QS, Times Higher Education, and Webometrics. It examines how digital indicators, algorithmic processes and standardized evaluation models interact with structural disparities between institutions in the global North and South. The research offers original contributions by identifying new forms of digital paternalism in ranking mechanisms and proposing a policy shift toward multidimensional and participatory evaluation models. These results have implications for considering equity, transparency, and institutional agency in the governance of the global systems of higher education.

title: Sportwashing: a growing international concern in sport-for-development
title_original: Sportwashing: a growing international concern in sport-for-development
summary: With organisations today required to operate in more ethically and socially responsible ways, different types of ‘washing’ in sport are emerging, while instances of illiberal practices, such as human rights issues, are becoming a growing concern worldwide. Thus, to situate sportwashing as a global issue, the research draws on four international case studies from England (Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games), Taiwan (2022 Workers’ World Cup), Zambia (Response Network) and Scotland (Scottish basketball). Through this global lens, the research offers insights into structural incentives for sportwashing amongst efforts to leverage sport for social development. Collectively, the cases highlight how organisations operate under banners of social impact; albeit underpinned by broader economic, political, and performance-based objectives. Within the individual cases, nine themes: commercialisation, participation and talent development; institutional legitimacy and reputation building; funding and power beneath democratic prestige; and social exclusion and legacy framing. Furthermore, it is argued that sportwashing manifests by over-exaggerating social impact through and from sport. While the extent of sportwashing varies across ecosystems, such altruistic public-facing notions of social impact actively obfuscate lived realities and go unnoticed, subsequently constraining people’s development. A key issue entails that sportwashing is largely unchallenged until it is too late to proactively address, with the main ramifications experienced by the people and communities that programmes were meant to support. The research thus advances SFD for understanding the negative impact of washing in social impact‑driven environments. It also highlights the need to document sportwashing cases individually, as considering sportwashing broadly conceals individual contextual nuances.

title: Decarbonisation under cap-and-trade: an integrated network Data Envelopment Analysis model with a second-scoring auction mechanism
title_original: Decarbonisation under cap-and-trade: an integrated network Data Envelopment Analysis model with a second-scoring auction mechanism
summary: This study develops a centralised Network Data Envelopment Analysis (NDEA) model within a Directional Distance Function (DDF) framework and integrates it with a second-scoring auction mechanism for carbon permit reallocation under a cap-and-trade system. The model evaluates the performance of Decision-Making Units (DMUs) within a two-stage network structure and determines surplus and deficit volumes of CO2 permits. An endogenous scarcity-based pricing framework is then introduced to link carbon permit prices to the permit shortages and surpluses derived from the model. Subsequently, a second-scoring auction mechanism determines endogenous transaction prices and trading volumes through bilateral permit exchanges. The proposed framework is applied to the European bioenergy supply chain to investigate whether the mechanism can facilitate permit reallocation and reduce the inefficiency of participating DMUs.

title: Editorial: Sport governance: challenges, developments and future pathways
title_original: Editorial: Sport governance: challenges, developments and future pathways
summary: Emerging challenges, including corruption scandals in sport and debates surrounding gender transition, have renewed attention on the importance of effective sport governance-the central theme of this special issue of Frontiers in Sports and Active Living. The issue consists of 13 papers that deal with a wide range of important topics across several countries, including Australia, the USA, Germany, China, Korea, Tunisia and Portugal. Although the various articles may overlap or intertwine, given the broad scope of sport governance, they can possibly be classified or categorized around six major themes based on their particular focus. These include: state involvement in sport, the Olympics, athlete development, corporate Governance, intellectual property rights and sport for development.The state-oriented articles deal with the issues of public subsidies for professional soccer in Germany, sport policy development in Australia, state intervention in US College Sports and local government in China and Portugal. In their study entitled "Public Subsidies for Professional Football Clubs: A Conceptual Political Economy Analysis," Baumeister et al. provided a more integrated conceptual framework to better understand the critical importance of state subsidies in professional football based on a study of Germany's Bundesliga. In making a case for such public subsidies, they strongly suggest that they should not be narrowly conceived as just a strategy to rescue clubs in crisis but as part of a broader sustainable developmental strategy or catalyst to promote urban development, economic growth, social cohesion, and community identity or identity formation as a whole (McCree, 2008).With respect to the USA, Hawkins interrogates the socio-political significance or fallout of one of Donald Trump's many Executive Orders (EO), in his article entitled, "Donald Trump's Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) Executive Order: A Neo-Jacksonianism Tradition." While the EO was seen as impacting all athletes in the major revenue-generating sports of American football and basketball, it was seen as having a disproportionate impact on black students who dominate participation in these two sports, which serves to reinforce the broader racialized status quo.Theoretically, the paper makes an important contribution to the study of populism in sport and populism in general and methodologically, to the use of qualitative research in sport through the application of contextual analysis. In the paper, "Australian Sport Policy and Advocacy: An Historical Account of Policy Evolution, Government Involvement, and the Advent of Lobbying," Mountifield examines the Australian state's transition from a limited role in sport to a more active and interventionist one through the creation of formal sport policies, government sport bureaucracies, ministries and ministers responsible for sport, and dedicated funding for both elite and mass sport. The paper makes an important contribution to the literature on sport policy as well as the role of advocacy or lobbying in the policy process. Three of the papers examined dealt with the Olympic Games as they relate particularly to the IOC, Olympic values and the impact of Olympic hosting on athlete performance. In their unprecedented historical examination of "The evolution of IOC membership and governance" from 1894 to 2023, Xu and Shi show how both internal and external factors of an economic, political, ideological, social and organizational nature combined to bring about substantive changes in the composition and operations of the IOC. As a consequence, the IOC has become much less Eurocentric, more meritocratic and representative, in relation to the presence of women, developing nations and athletes, although the authors question whether some of these changes, particularly the involvement of athletes, are more symbolic or cosmetic than real. In the article, "Beyond excellence, friendship and respect: Olympic education stakeholders' priorities for values in a changing world," Theodorakis et al. examine how Olympic education stakeholders recognise and seek to further contemporary values including peace, social inclusion, environmental sustainability, and gender equality, in addition to the traditional Olympic values of excellence, friendship, and respect. This study is highly relevant to sports governance as it helps to see how shifts in society shape attitudes within the major sports movement, similar to the paper by Xu and Shi.In their paper entitled "Beyond the Podium: The Long-Term Impact of Hosting the Olympic Games on National Sporting Performance," Schoettl and Kainz shift from issues of values and representation to the relationship between hosting and medal outcomes. In this regard, they argue that Olympic hosting should be understood not merely as a short-term home advantage but as a strategic instrument of sports policy. The study contributes to the literature by showing that Olympic hosting can work as a policy lever whose benefits are shaped by governance capacity, strategic prioritization, and sustained investment rather than by the event itself. The article by Guidotti et al entitled "Sustainability of top-performance athletes' mental health and career retirement support services: European major sports organizations' perspective" examines much broader and important issues related to the (non)provision of formal support mechanisms, both financially and emotionally, to athletes in order to help them deal with life after sports. They argue that the available services in Europe are directed primarily towards the medal winners, which leaves a significant number of athletes outside the purview of support. This study signals an emerging trend of recognition for mental health support for elite athletes. Kwon's paper entitled "Athlete Data Sovereignty" examines the equally important issue of who owns and controls the performance data produced by athletes during training or competition (e.g., heart rate output, reaction times). Reminiscent of Marx's notion of the alienation of workers from their own labour, it is argued that since such data are an extension of the athletes' identity and not some impersonal external output, they should be allowed to exercise greater sovereignty over them.The paper assumes great relevance in the age of AI and complements the issue of athlete representation raised by Xu and Chi in their paper on the IOC. In their paper entitled "Whose game is it anyway? Palworld and the new frontier of intellectual property in eSports," Vargas-Chaves et al also deal with the issue of property rights but in the particular context of e-sports or digital sports. Through the Palworld case, especially its perceived similarities with Pokémon, the article examined the tension between creative inspiration and infringement, while distinguishing between copyright, patent protection, trademarks, and Trade Dress. This article elucidates that legal regulation, platform governance, and intellectual property management are now central to the sustainability and integrity of the eSports industry.In the only paper that focuses on national sport organizations, Ghodhbani and Souissi explore different governance models in the context of non-profit sports Federations in Tunisia in their article, "Governance of Tunisian sports organizations: what is the matter?" They argue that these Federations work within the oversight of both supranational and national regulatory systems that allow for both possibilities and constrictions. Majorly, they show how different governance models such as the strong presidential model, the couple's presidential model, the exploded presidential model, and the managerial presidential model influence the functioning of the Federations.The paper by Westerbeek et al. can be situated more in the context of sport for development due to its focus on "The costs of participation in and delivery of community sport in Australia." Based on a rigorous scoping or narrative review, the authors identify the economic and non-economic barriers to participation in community sport in Australia, critically examine existing strategies to deal with them and make several important policy recommendations to facilitate more participation. The paper should make an important contribution to the literature on sport policy as well as the growing field of sport for development.

title: Natural aerosol variability can reverse the apparent air-quality response to abrupt emission reductions
title_original: Natural aerosol variability can reverse the apparent air-quality response to abrupt emission reductions
summary: Abrupt societal disruptions, including economic shocks, pandemic lockdowns, and armed conflicts, are widely used as natural experiments for attributing changes in air quality to changes in emissions. Such attribution commonly rests on observed concentrations: combustion tracers fall, and the resulting improvement is credited to reduced emissions. Here we show that coincident natural aerosol variability can mask, and in this case reverse, the expected concentration response, so that observation-only attribution can recover the wrong sign. We demonstrate this with the 2026 Iran conflict (28 February to 31 March 2026), combining satellite columns, Tehran ground stations, two aerosol reanalyses, back-trajectory analysis, and GEOS-Chem factor-separation simulations. TROPOMI columns and ground stations confirm substantial reductions in SO2, NO2, and CO, the signature ordinarily read as an air-quality improvement. Over the same period and domain, surface PM2.5 instead rose by 67.7 μg m−3. Factor separation attributes the increase to mineral dust (+74.8 μg m−3, exceeding the net anomaly itself), which overwhelms the emission-driven reduction (−2.7 μg m−3) and a small meteorological term (−0.8 μg m−3). Friction-velocity diagnostics place the driver in the tail of the wind distribution rather than in the mean: extreme wind-stress events over the Iraq–Kuwait source region became roughly three times more frequent, a signal that cancels in region-mean statistics but is amplified by the nonlinear threshold response of dust emission. The inferred sign is also scale-dependent, since urban stations in Tehran record cleaner air while the surrounding region deteriorates. We conclude that attribution during abrupt disruptions requires explicit separation of natural and anthropogenic aerosol contributions, and that combustion-tracer columns alone are not sufficient evidence of an air-quality benefit.

title: La télévision au service des Jeux olympiques ?
title_original: La télévision au service des Jeux olympiques ?
summary: Comment la télévision vend-elle les Jeux olympiques ? Cet article se propose de répondre à cette question à travers une étude de cas : l’analyse des interprogrammes de Canal+ au moment des Jeux olympiques de Rio en 2016. Reprise par l’industriel Vincent Bolloré, la chaîne cryptée cherche, en reprenant la diffusion des Jeux qu’elle avait abandonnée en 2012, à revenir à ce qui a fait sa marque de fabrique : le sport. Genre autopromotionnel, les interprogrammes sont un lieu d’observation pertinent pour comprendre comment Canal+ promeut l’événement olympique pour se promouvoir elle-même et défendre son image de chaîne du sport premium .

title: Major League Cricket’s Blueprint for Growth in the U.S.
title_original: Major League Cricket’s Blueprint for Growth in the U.S.
summary: This paper will examine the franchise economics of the Indian Premier League (IPL), as well as several other emerging franchise leagues based in the U.S. to determine if implementing a hybrid framework can help scale the Major League Cricket (MLC) in the U.S. Through analyzing existing research papers, statistics, and first-hand interviews with professional players, this paper will investigate significant differences between the two cricket leagues, roadblocks to cricket’s success in America, and how to overcome them to expand the game’s exposure. Player interviews, existing research papers and statistics analysis outlined repeatable tactics such as revenue sharing, media rights, star-player signings and grassroots and community developments. Despite notable setbacks, such as the lack of support for the league from the nation’s governing body of cricket, limited existing exposure for the sport, and slow entry into a saturated market, cricket certainly has the potential for growth in America through the MLC and by combining what made leagues like the IPL work with researching how niche sports leagues began to break into the American market.

title: Spectacularisation, images et olympisme
title_original: Spectacularisation, images et olympisme
summary: L’augmentation du nombre de salariés combinant activité professionnelle et responsabilités d’aide constitue un phénomène marquant des sociétés contemporaines. Si les tensions travail-famille ont été largement étudiées, les mécanismes de régulation des tensions entre aidance et travail restent encore peu explorés. Cet article analyse comment des parents d’enfants en situation de handicap gèrent ces tensions, en s’intéressant aux ressources mobilisées, aux styles de gestion des frontières et aux conditions contextuelles. À partir de 38 entretiens, les résultats mettent en évidence de multiples tensions inter-rôles (temporelles, émotionnelles, comportementales, financières, de carrière et institutionnelles). Leur régulation s’appuie sur une écologie de ressources disponibles et mobilise trois styles de gestion des frontières. L’étude identifie ainsi quatre stratégies de régulation des tensions aidance-travail : congruente, compensée, conflictuelle et dégradée, reflétant différents équilibres entre tensions, ressources et gestion des frontières. Ces stratégies dépendent notamment de la visibilité du statut d’aidant et des contraintes structurelles. L’article propose ainsi un modèle dynamique de régulation des tensions aidance-travail, montrant comment, sous l’effet de chocs structurels latents, les aidants ajustent en continu leurs ressources et leurs styles de gestion des frontières afin de maintenir un équilibre temporaire entre leurs rôles. Cette recherche enrichit la littérature sur les tensions inter-rôles en offrant une approche dynamique de la régulation des tensions aidance-travail.

title: « Impressions des Vainqueurs »
title_original: « Impressions des Vainqueurs »
summary: Ancrés dans le prolongement du bilan de la Première Guerre mondiale, les Jeux olympiques d’Anvers se révèlent être un levier géopolitique d’assise de la domination des « Vainqueurs ». En France, la médiatisation des compétitions olympiques revêt la nécessité d’assurer la conservation de son « image » victorieuse. Cet article explore la couverture des Jeux de 1920 à travers l’analyse de quatre périodiques ( L’Auto , Excelsior , Le Miroir des Sports , La Vie au Grand Air ) pour comprendre le rôle des récits et des images dans la « fabrique » médiatique des Jeux olympiques d’Anvers.

title: De force et de beauté ? Les Jeux olympiques dans la presse du premier xx e siècle
title_original: De force et de beauté ? Les Jeux olympiques dans la presse du premier xx e siècle
summary: Depuis 1979, le Lacanau Pro est la plus ancienne compétition internationale de surf professionnel en France. Entre 1979 et 2019, les 40 affiches qui la portent à la connaissance du public, en reflètent l’évolution. Si pour Roland Barthes un objet « parle », les affiches du Lacanau Pro racontent l’histoire et la légende de cette épreuve. Quelles sont leurs charges symboliques, idéologiques et culturelles ? Une étude sémio-historique permet de comprendre comment le Lacanau Pro parvient à construire sa propre légende, telle une épopée dont les affiches seraient la révélation graphique.

title: “Las sirenas mexicanas” and “Las guerreras del agua”: Metaphors used in digital news from Mexican and Spanish sports newspapers
title_original: “Las sirenas mexicanas” and “Las guerreras del agua”: Metaphors used in digital news from Mexican and Spanish sports newspapers
summary: This article aims to identify the most frequently employed conceptual metaphors in digital newspapers sports articles that are used to conceptualize sports and sportswomen during the 2024 Olympic Games. The corpus consists of 1,411 news written in Spanish extracted from four newspapers: Récord and ESTO from Mexico, and Marca and Mundo Deportivo from Spain. We first identify the conceptual metaphors used in the news and then classify them into metaphorical fields. The discourse-linguistic analysis based on the qualitative data shows that sports and sportswomen are conceptualized through various source domains. With regard to sports, they are mostly conceptualized in terms of SPORTS ARE WAR and SPORTS ARE STORYTELLING in both the Spanish and Mexican corpus. Regarding the representation of women athletes, in both contexts SPORTSWOMEN ARE CHAMPIONS and LEGENDS; however, in Mexico the conceptual metaphor SPORTSWOMEN ARE CHAMPIONS predominates, whereas in Spain SPORTSWOMEN ARE WARRIORS, QUEENS, STARS, MACHINES, or ANIMALS.

title: La promotion de l’olympienne dans la presse magazine en France
title_original: La promotion de l’olympienne dans la presse magazine en France
summary: Si la médiatisation des jeux Olympiques passe par la presse spécialisée, la presse magazine permet de dépasser l’horizon sportif et lui donner une audience considérable. L’analyse des Unes consacrées aux médaillées olympiques françaises entre 1900 et 2004 permet de dessiner les conditions de leur médiatisation. Tardivement mises en scène, elles vont apparaître sporadiquement selon certaines conditions. Si la production d’un exploit sportif inédit s’avère indispensable, il est loin d’être suffisant et ne permet pas d’accéder à la célébrité médiatique. Il doit aussi inscrire la sportive dans les imaginaires liées à sa position sociale. Un tri s’opère ainsi afin de choisir celles dignes d’attention.

title: Naissance et affirmation du radioreportage sportif : les Jeux olympiques de Paris (1924) et Berlin (1936)
title_original: Naissance et affirmation du radioreportage sportif : les Jeux olympiques de Paris (1924) et Berlin (1936)
summary: Cet article explore les relations entre la radiodiffusion et les Jeux olympiques de 1924 à 1936 à travers l’analyse des pratiques journalistiques. En s’appuyant sur des sources écrites, il met en lumière la sportivisation progressive de la radio au contact des Jeux olympiques, lesquels ont connu une affirmation notable grâce à l’émergence de ce nouveau média. En introduisant des éléments tels que la diffusion en direct et l’immersion sonore, cet article démontre comment la radio a redéfini les normes médiatiques du spectacle sportif au cours de la période de l’entre-deux-guerres.

title: The changing returns to physical exercise in China (2010–2023): a nine-wave repeated cross-sectional study
title_original: The changing returns to physical exercise in China (2010–2023): a nine-wave repeated cross-sectional study
summary: Background Since 2008, when China began to implement its strategy of building a sports power, the institutional context of physical exercise has changed substantially. Yet the temporal dynamics of the socioeconomic correlates of exercise remain underexplored. Objectives To examine whether and how physical exercise participation and its associations with income, self-rated health, and social trust changed over the 2010–2023 study period. Methods Using nine waves of the Chinese General Social Survey (CGSS 2010–2023, N = 78,467), we estimate annual marginal effects of exercise through ordinary least squares regression with exercise-by-year interactions. Three policy periods corresponding to phases of the Sports Power strategy are compared. Results Exercise participation rose from 31.68% in 2010 to 51.26% in 2023. The exercise–income association increased from 0.301 (Period 1, 2010–2012) to 0.367 (Period 3, 2018–2023, +21.9%), although formal cross-period tests did not reach statistical significance; the upward trend is therefore only weakly consistent with Hypothesis 1. The exercise–health association was negative and appeared to deepen across periods, but the cross-period differences lost statistical significance once the non-comparable 2011 wave was excluded, so this apparent change is interpreted cautiously. The exercise–trust association moved from a non-significant −0.013 to −0.101 (SE = 0.014). Subgroup analyses showed larger income associations for men than women (0.420 versus 0.279) and for rural than urban residents (0.449 versus 0.180). Conclusion Exercise participation rose markedly over the study period, and the exercise–trust association turned increasingly negative, but the exercise–income association did not strengthen to a statistically significant degree, and the health-selection pattern was sensitive to the exclusion of the 2011 wave. The observed changes are read as population-level associations rather than causal effects of the Sports Power strategy.

title: Signal detection of substance-related emergency department visits during UEFA EURO 2024 in Germany: enhancing public health surveillance for future mass gatherings
title_original: Signal detection of substance-related emergency department visits during UEFA EURO 2024 in Germany: enhancing public health surveillance for future mass gatherings
summary: Introduction Germany hosted the men's UEFA European Championship (EURO 2024) in summer 2024, attracting millions of visitors across multiple cities. Mass gathering events (MGEs) can rapidly alter social environments which impact substance use behaviors, potentially increasing demand on local healthcare systems. In response, the German national public health institute (Robert Koch Institute, RKI) piloted substance-related indicators using routine emergency department (ED) data from the Emergency Department Data Registry throughout the tournament to explore their applicability for real-time emergency department surveillance. Methods We aimed to monitor substance use patterns in ED visits during EURO 2024 by developing an umbrella syndrome definition for psychotropic substance intoxication (SATX) and two more specific syndrome definitions for acute alcohol intoxication (ATX) and substance intoxication other than alcohol (STX), based on diagnoses, chief complaints, and age criteria. Descriptive analyses compared identified cases during the tournament period (14 June−14 July 2024) with a reference period. Analyses were stratified by sex, age group, and triage level. A quasi-Poisson regression model was used to estimate expected values and 95% prediction intervals (95% PI) for each indicator during the tournament period. Signals were detected when observed case counts exceeded the upper threshold of the 95% PI. Results Between 1 January 2018 and 9 September 2024, 5,602,933 visits from 39 EDs were included. Across both the tournament and reference periods, SATX, ATX, and STX cases were more common among males, particularly for ATX. Most SATX and ATX cases occurred among individuals aged 30–59 years, whereas STX cases were most frequent among those aged 20–39 years. Relative increases in triage level 4 cases were observed during the tournament period. During EURO 2024, signals exceeding the upper threshold of the 95% PI were detected for all indicators, including 16 SATX, three ATX, and 13 STX signals. The largest deviation was observed for SATX on 29 June 2024, with 127 observed cases compared to 74 expected cases. Conclusion This study demonstrated that rapid changes in substance-related ED utilization during MGEs can be effectively monitored using the syndrome definitions and signal detection methods, whose application can support public health surveillance during future events.

title: [Survey on the establishment of smoking areas in city halls in National Association of Directors of Health Departments of Designated Cities, West Block Conference].
title_original: [Survey on the establishment of smoking areas in city halls in National Association of Directors of Health Departments of Designated Cities, West Block Conference].
summary: Objectives In Tokyo, preventing passive smoking progressed during the 32nd Olympic Games. However, smoking areas remain in many local city halls, and tobacco product companies donate smoking areas in front of stations and near parks. A questionnaire survey was conducted at the Western Block Conference of the National Association of Directors of Health Departments of Designated Cities to accurately assess the status of smoking areas established and managed by designated cities.Methods Questionnaires were distributed to the relevant departments in 30 designated cities. Smoking rates in the prefectures in which each designated city is located and tobacco tax revenues by city were collected from comprehensive information provided by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications. The Mann-Whitney U test compared smoking rates. Fisher's exact test examined for correlations, with P<0.05 considered significant. Because this study was an analysis of a questionnaire survey conducted among government agencies and open data, an ethics review was deemed unnecessary.Results Fifteen designated cities (50%) had smoking areas in their city halls. The reasons provided were "staff preference" in five cities and "citizen preference" in three. Twenty-four designated cities (80%) had smoking areas donated by tobacco companies. The WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) guidelines were recognized in 18 designated cities (60%). There was no significant difference in smoking prevalence between designated cities with and without smoking areas in their city halls (P = 0.933). FCTC awareness was not significantly related to the presence of smoking areas donated by tobacco companies (P = 1). The presence of smoking areas in city halls and presence of smoking areas donated by tobacco companies had no significant relation (P = 0.651). Drawing a line of 2 billion yen in tobacco tax revenue, designated cities exceeding this threshold were significantly may have smoking areas in their city halls (P = 0.025).Conclusion Smoking areas remain in city halls of designated cities in Western Japan. Although the presence or absence of smoking areas in city halls and smoking rate or donation of smoking areas had no significant relationship, there was a significant relationship with the tobacco tax. Local governments should not install smoking areas to prevent passive smoking.

title: From temporary event spaces to permanent urban communities: A physical-relational-legacy framework for Olympic Village transformation
title_original: From temporary event spaces to permanent urban communities: A physical-relational-legacy framework for Olympic Village transformation
summary: The Olympic Village has evolved over time to become a full-fledged urban system that encompasses not just the temporary housing needs of athletes participating in the Olympic Games but also infrastructure development, governance coordination, sustainability planning, and long-term community transformation. Although there are many studies of Olympic Villages, they typically focus on a single aspect of them such as the physical redevelopment of an area, the way that it was governed during the Olympics, and what happened to the Village after the Games ended. Existing studies have examined various dimensions separately, but fewer studies integrate these dimensions into a unified lifecycle framework. To fill this gap, this study proposed the Physical-Relational-Legacy (P-R-L) framework to help explain the changes in form that occur in Olympic Villages over their lifecycle. Using a Straussian grounded theory approach and comparative case study methodology, the study investigated six Olympic events: the Summer Olympics of 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024, and the Winter Olympics of 2022. The data collected for this study included official Olympic reports, operational manuals, planning documents, and other types of published materials related to legacy. Using systematic open, axial, and selective coding supported by constant comparison, the study inductively developed the three interrelated dimensions: Physical, Relational, and Legacy. The results of this study indicated that the transformation of an Olympic Village is not simply a matter of developing some areas after the games end. Rather, it involves a series of interactions between changing infrastructure systems, governance mechanisms, and ongoing legacy development processes. Moreover, each of these dimensions interacts with one another at all stages of an Olympic Village's lifecycle instead of occurring sequentially. The study contributes by providing an integrated analytical framework explaining how physical adaptation, governance coordination, and legacy formation interact throughout the Olympic Village lifecycle.

title: Digitalization and participation in democratic governance in a voluntary sport club
title_original: Digitalization and participation in democratic governance in a voluntary sport club
summary: Research question The purpose of this paper is to examine how digitalization interacts with governance to (re)shape participation in sport clubs’ democratic governance. Two research questions are addressed for this purpose: First, how do sport club stakeholders experience and justify digitalization? Second, drawing on the concept of democratic organizing and a broadened understanding of sport governance, what are the implications of digitalization on democratic governance in terms of what constitutes governance issues, who participates in governance, and how governance is carried out in a voluntary sport club?Research methods We employed a single instrumental case study design based on 16 interviews with various stakeholders of a sport club. The empirical setting is one voluntary sport club in Sweden with over 500 members, paid staff, and a broad activity profile that includes both mass and elite sports provided for children, youth, and adults of all genders.Results and findings Digitalization in voluntary sport clubs primarily enhances administrative efficiency while only modestly reshaping participation in democratic governance. Even though digital tools broaden low-threshold and everyday engagement, they largely reproduce existing top-down communication patterns and risk reinforcing passive membership roles. Democratic participation depends on digital competence, organizational routines, and the motives guiding tool adoption. These findings show that digitalization introduces potential new logics of participation but remains constrained by institutional arrangements.Implications We contribute by highlighting how everyday digital practices, not formal structures alone, shape democratic governance, emphasizing the need for inclusive strategies to ensure digital tools genuinely support member voice and organizational sustainability.

title: Personality Rights: New Emergence and Relation with the Sports Industry
title_original: Personality Rights: New Emergence and Relation with the Sports Industry
summary: The right to manage or oversee the exploitation of one’s name, image, likeness or any other aspect of one’s personality is generally known as a personality right. Individual athletes’ rights of publicity also significantly enhance the value of the sports organisations or teams with which they are affiliated. Celebrity opens up opportunities to earn money by promoting brands, creating images or using notoriety as leverage. To prevent their names or likenesses from being exploited by others without their permission, athletes now frequently register them as trademarks; Sachin Tendulkar and David Beckham are among the well-known examples. The goal is to clarify the present legal environment and to offer suggestions for striking a balance between the interests of athletes and OFS operators by examining relevant national and international case law. Furthermore, an examination of international frameworks, especially those of the US and the EU, offers guidance for creating a strong legal framework in India that recognises personality rights. The legal underpinnings and contemporary development of personality rights are examined in this study, with particular attention to their emergence and special uses in the sports sector. The case studies shed light on changing interpretations and safeguards, especially where athletes are involved.

title: Neural oscillatory activity during guided and self-generated motor imagery: a comparative case study of a six-time World Cup skateboarder champion and an experienced recreational surfer
title_original: Neural oscillatory activity during guided and self-generated motor imagery: a comparative case study of a six-time World Cup skateboarder champion and an experienced recreational surfer
summary: This study aimed to examine and compare neural oscillatory activity during guided and self-generated motor imagery in two individuals with contrasting levels of competitive expertise: a six-time World Cup skateboarder champion and an experienced recreational surfer. Following baseline recording, continuous electroencephalographic (EEG) activity (Brain Products GmbH, Gilching, Germany) was acquired during three motor imagery conditions: verbally guided training imagery, verbally guided competition imagery, and self-generated competition imagery. Analyses of frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA), frontal beta asymmetry (FBA), and frontal midline theta (fmθ) showed distinct patterns of frontal oscillatory activity across imagery conditions and between the two athletes. FAA and FBA values were consistently lower in the skateboarder than in the surfer during the imagery conditions, although between-case differences were already evident at baseline. In contrast, fmθ showed a condition-dependent pattern, with higher values in the skateboarder during verbally guided training imagery but lower values during verbally guided and self-generated competition imagery. These case-level observations suggest that frontal oscillatory activity during motor imagery may vary according to imagery condition and individual characteristics. However, because the two participants differed not only in competitive expertise but also in sport discipline, prior imagery training, and trait imagery ability, the observed EEG differences cannot be attributed specifically to motor expertise. Accordingly, these findings should be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating, providing a basis for future studies examining the relationships among motor expertise, imagery modality, and neural oscillatory activity in larger and more homogeneous samples.

title: World-record envelopes: The speed-distance trade-off in racing events
title_original: World-record envelopes: The speed-distance trade-off in racing events
summary: The concept of a mathematical envelope, which is widely used in economics, can be applied to the relationship between world-record racing speeds and event distances. This paper derives and estimates world-record envelopes for running, freestyle swimming, and speed skating and shows how these envelopes are related to the underlying family of individual performance curves. It also compares world-record envelopes for men and women and shows that the world-record envelope in men's running has shifted upward over time but has not changed shape in 120 years. Finally, this paper shows that the speed-distance envelope reflects not only the trade-off between speed and distance for individual athletes but also the change in this trade-off as one moves from one athlete to another. The failure of existing studies to recognize the second effect leads to a misinterpretation of the observed link between world-record performances and human physiology. The paper also shows how this problem can be avoided by estimating individual performance curves using the personal best times of elite athletes.

title: Inducing and measuring identity levels in professional rugby players during immersion in an interactive virtual environment
title_original: Inducing and measuring identity levels in professional rugby players during immersion in an interactive virtual environment
summary: During a game, players experience substantial affective fluctuations, particularly through cognitive appraisal processes, which notably involves self-categorisation process. However, designing a mental training programme using the contextual elements of a game is still a challenge. Moreover, social contexts can be recreated in virtual reality and it has been demonstrated that people tend to have realistic affective and behavioural reactions to it. In this study, we recreated, in virtual reality, one of the key contexts that players can encounter during a rugby game, a try. After an embodiment phase, participants were standing on the field with other avatars representing the other players, surrounded by an audience of virtual supporters. We used different visual and auditory parameters creating two different kinds of social feedback. In the first condition the social feedback was aimed at inducing social identity, in the second condition the social feedback received in the virtual environment was aimed at inducing personal identity. We measured participants' identity level before and after each condition, using interactive visual analogue scales inside the virtual environment. We also measured levels of presence and embodiment using the same method. Affective states were measured using an interactive adaptation of Russel's affect grid, inside the virtual environment as well. Our experiment presents an innovative method aimed at inducing and measuring different identity levels in virtual reality.

title: From partner synchrony to corner support: interpersonal co-regulation and performance recovery in DanceSport and boxing
title_original: From partner synchrony to corner support: interpersonal co-regulation and performance recovery in DanceSport and boxing
summary: Sport psychology has often treated performance regulation as predominantly intrapersonal, yet competitive recovery can also be shaped by relational information. This Conceptual Analysis introduces the Relational Co-Regulation and Performance Recovery (RCPR) Model, a perturbation-centered framework for explaining how partner- and coach-generated inputs may alter recovery after within-competition disruption. Crucially, relational regulatory input is defined independently of success: an observable signal is a regulatory attempt because of its timing, content, and plausible task function, not because recovery follows. A co-regulatory transaction occurs when that input enters a temporally linked interaction loop of detection, appraisal, response, and possible updating; its outcome may be beneficial, null, or dysregulatory. The model also separates psychological state restoration, functional task restoration, and subsequent performance recovery rather than treating them as a single outcome. DanceSport and boxing are used as maximum-contrast theoretical exemplars rather than empirically established sport categories. DanceSport foregrounds predominantly continuous, reciprocal, embodied partner regulation during joint action, whereas boxing foregrounds predominantly intermittent and relatively asymmetrical coach-athlete regulation between rounds. Ecological dynamics, joint action, interpersonal emotion regulation, social support, communal coping, and coach-athlete relationship perspectives are integrated while their distinct explanatory roles are retained. Six core falsifiable propositions address incremental validity, regulatory architecture, matching and uptake, dyadic transmission and co-dysregulation, non-linear dosage constraints, and relational-training specificity. The model generates a research agenda based on perturbation-centered time series, representative simulations, quasi-experimental designs, and converging within-person evidence.

title: Songs about Boys: Black Girl Groups, Pleasure Cultures, and the Race of Romance
title_original: Songs about Boys: Black Girl Groups, Pleasure Cultures, and the Race of Romance
summary: Abstract In the decades after World War II, Black teenage girls cultivated a musical pleasure culture grounded in the tropes of heteronormative romance. Although most scholarship on the “girl group sound” focuses on the impact of the most famous groups on their (white) girl listeners, I center Black girl singers themselves to ask: what did girl group songs mean for the Black girls who created them? I assess documentary evidence from local newspapers, yearbooks, popular magazines, and sound recordings of girls’ original songs alongside interviews with former girl group members to argue that Black girls’ often-dismissed interest in romance in fact constitutes an important stronghold of homosociality and joy. Furthermore, I suggest that Black girl groups’ highly feminine music, entanglement with white-owned production machines, and white, suburban girl audience tend to obscure them in conventional histories of Black American music. By expanding my analysis beyond the most famous groups, focusing on original songs, and resituating them as part of a larger culture created by and for Black girls, I show that girls’ love songs remain crucial records of Black life even when they are not aesthetically innovative or legibly “political.” When one considers Black girls’ songs without only positioning them in relation to a white ear, a record of Black girls’ joy becomes audible.

title: Phygital and e-sports as new forms of sports socialization in the modern digital society
title_original: Phygital and e-sports as new forms of sports socialization in the modern digital society
summary: Introduction . Phygital sports and esports as hybrid tools of socialization that combine the advantages of traditional sports with digital technologies have been analyzed. Phygital sports and esports blur the boundaries between the real and the virtual, altering the role of sport as a social institution. The materials and methods . Empirical data from surveys of individuals participating in esports and phygital sports, as well as materials from focus groups and in-depth expert interviews were analyzed. The research results. The findings demonstrate that esports and phygital sports are not merely digital leisure activities but represent fully fledged, qualitatively new modes of sports-based socialization within digital society, particularly for young people aged 14–30. Compared to esports, phygital sports show higher levels of social adaptation among participants, approaching traditional sports in terms of fostering communication skills and teamwork. Based on age-related trends (a rise in preference for phygital sports from 25% to 60% with increasing age) and data indicating a high willingness to substitute traditional fitness activities with phygital ones (67%), a shift in the dominant recreational paradigm can be predicted within the next 5–7 years. Discussion and Conclusion . The future development of phygital sports and esports will depend on the ability of the state and society to integrate these phenomena into the existing system of social institutions while preserving their unique socialization potential-particularly regarding identity formation, the promotion of social inclusion, and the transformation of perceptions of sport in the digital age. A promising avenue for future research is the study of the long-term effects of socialization through esports.

title: GAMIFIED EFL CLASSROOM: 50 GAMES AND PLAY-BASED STRATEGIES FOR YOUNG LEARNERS ENGLISH TEACHERS
title_original: GAMIFIED EFL CLASSROOM: 50 GAMES AND PLAY-BASED STRATEGIES FOR YOUNG LEARNERS ENGLISH TEACHERS
summary: This book brings together fifty games and play-based strategies organized into five chapters, designed for secondary school teachers of English as a foreign language. The opening chapter lays out the theoretical foundations of gamification, distinguishing it from game-based learning and serious games, and introduces an original five-phase model (Diagnose, Design, Deploy, Deliver, Debrief) that structures the lesson planning used throughout the volume. The following chapters present banks of games applied to the four language skills: fifteen vocabulary and grammar activities, fifteen speaking and listening activities, ten reading and writing activities, and ten activities incorporating digital tools and artificial intelligence. Each game includes objectives, materials, procedure, and adaptation suggestions for different CEFR levels (A1 to B2). The approach draws on Self-Determination Theory and flow research, adapted to the real conditions of public secondary classrooms, such as large groups and limited technology access. The volume thus offers a practical, evidence-based resource for strengthening motivation and language performance among adolescent learners.

title: Athlete-Level Dynamics in Elite Swimming Across Nine Global Championships (2016–2025): Age Structure, Podium Tenure, and Competitive Turnover
title_original: Athlete-Level Dynamics in Elite Swimming Across Nine Global Championships (2016–2025): Age Structure, Podium Tenure, and Competitive Turnover
summary: The elite swimming calendar became substantially denser after 2020. We examined how the individual-event medalist population at the nine global championships of 2016–2025 changed in age structure, podium tenure, medal accumulation, and turnover. All 865 individual-event medals (277 athletes) at three Olympic Games and six World Championships were organized as an athlete-by-edition panel and analyzed with athlete-clustered and wild cluster bootstrap inference, exploratory Bayesian partial pooling, discrete-time hazard models, negative binomial regression, and bootstrap measures of concentration. Mean medalist age ranged from 22.86 to 24.46 years across editions. None of the 34 sex-by-event era contrasts survived false-discovery-rate adjustment; the two with the smallest p-values (men’s 200 m breaststroke, +2.79 years; women’s 400 m individual medley, −5.19 years; both q = 0.062) are exploratory, and both were accompanied by near-complete turnover of the event’s medalists. Median podium tenure was two editions. Each additional year of age at the first observed medal was associated with a higher hazard of a last observed medal (HR 1.106, 95% CI 1.063–1.151) and lower subsequent accumulation (IRR 0.863, 95% CI 0.823–0.904), whereas winning two or more medals at the first observed championship was associated with about half the hazard (HR 0.564, 95% CI 0.364–0.874) and twice the accumulation rate (IRR 2.066, 95% CI 1.410–3.027). The title-defense rate was 58.8% across 2017 → 2019 and 15.4% across the later World Championship transitions (OR 0.128, 95% CI 0.040–0.409), while the Gini coefficient of medal counts ranged from 0.205 to 0.248. Medal concentration remained descriptively similar, while the identities of the winners changed more frequently.

title: Research in the “Games Bubble”: leveraging outreach-embedded data collection at the 2025 Harbin Asian Winter Games
title_original: Research in the “Games Bubble”: leveraging outreach-embedded data collection at the 2025 Harbin Asian Winter Games
summary: Introduction Anti-doping social science has been shaped largely by Western and Eurocentric evidence, with limited research capturing athlete perspectives from geographically heterogeneous and potentially culturally diverse contexts. Major multisport events provide an opportunity to address this gap, especially when research is embedded within athlete outreach. This study examined the feasibility and value of outreach-embedded research aligned with values-based anti-doping outside traditional research settings. Methods Data were collected during athlete outreach activities at the 2025 Asian Winter Games (Harbin, China) using a brief online questionnaire completed by athletes ( n = 293), coaches ( n = 27), team officials ( n = 39), medical personnel ( n = 22), other athlete support personnel ( n = 18), and athlete ambassadors/engagement personnel ( n = 3), representing 28 countries and regions. Survey items assessed motivations for engaging with outreach, satisfaction and perceived impact, and “values in action,” including meanings and importance of clean sport, moral evaluations of performance-enhancement practices, and perceptions of anti-doping legitimacy. Results A total of 402 participants from 28 countries completed the outreach-embedded survey. Engagement with the Athlete Engagement and Education Centre was highly positive: satisfaction scores across content, activity format, and engagement averaged 4.74–4.78/5, 87% of respondents reported being very satisfied, and the program received a mean overall rating of 9.26/10. More than 72% strongly agreed that the outreach increased anti-doping awareness and knowledge and contributed positively to their Games experience, with no significant differences across athletes, athlete support personnel, and officials. Participants also reported high importance of clean sport and strong support for the legitimacy of the current anti-doping system. At the same time, responses showed moral nuance: 69.2% viewed deliberate use of prohibited substances as morally unacceptable under any circumstances, whereas others endorsed conditional acceptance, and legally permissible or medically justified enhancement practices were more widely accepted. Conclusion Outreach and survey content created a productive synergy, generating both positive participant experience and valuable data. Integrating outreach and research at regional multinational multisport events can offer a practical route to diversify the anti-doping evidence base while helping to catalyze deeper, locally grounded research agendas over time.

title: Prerequisites for Nietzsche’s Perspectivism
title_original: Prerequisites for Nietzsche’s Perspectivism
summary: The article examines the philosophical suppositions of the development of Friedrich Nietzsche’s concept of perspectivism and analyzes its relationship to relativism, pluralism, and skepticism. The aim of the study is to identify the intellectual origins of perspectivism and to demonstrate its distinctive nature in relation to foregoing philosophical traditions. The methodology of the work is based on the historical-philosophical reconstruction, comparative analysis, and the hermeneutic interpretation of philosophical texts. The author explores the influ-ence of ancient relativism and skepticism, medieval nominalism, the philosophy of the French Enlightenment, Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz’s pluralism, and Schopenhauer’s transformation of Kantian philosophy on the for-mation of Nietzsche’s conception of perspectival knowledge. It is argued that Nietzsche’s perspectivism cannot be a variety of either strong or weak relativism since it is grounded on the pluralistic ontology of the will to pow-er and presupposes a hierarchy of interpretations rather than their equivalence. Tally the results, perspectivism constitutes an independent philosophical conception, in which the problem of truth is transferred from the do-main of epistemology to that of ontology and living practice.

title: Post-Philosophy and the Need for a New Type of Anthropological Reflection
title_original: Post-Philosophy and the Need for a New Type of Anthropological Reflection
summary: The article is devoted to the study of the phenomenon of postmodernity within the framework of the concept of post-philosophy as an independent scientific field with a new unique methodology for analyzing many aspects of human beingness. This makes it possible to identify the anthropological systems evolution factors, which differ from those in positivism, structuralism, and classical philosophy. The purpose of this study is to indicate a departure from traditional structural, hierarchical concepts and principles, from abstract metaphysical construc-tions and to propose a post-philosophical reflection to study modern forms of appearances previously consid-ered peripheral, pluralistic, fragmentary. The methods of poststructuralism, hermeneutics, and phenomenology helped to consider post-philosophy as a special type of worldview centered on man with his earthly affairs and daily achievements. The use of this “toolkit” contributed to the analysis of multistructurality, rhizomaticity, simu-lativeness, hyperreality as philosophical ideological attitudes. As a result, the author comes to the following conclusions: post-philosophy is a continuation of the issue of the “death of meta-narratives”, an interdisciplinary reflection of neuroscience, artificial intelligence, and linguistics; “rational man” gives way to “hybrid-simulation man” who faces the question of preserving freedom and dignity in the space of innovative algorithms. There is a growing need to return to genuine ethics and morality. It is necessary to form a new anthropological reflection that predominantly explores no rational sphere, but offers survival tools that allow a person to show compas-sion and exercise his talent despite eclecticism, rhizomacy, and chaos.

title: Socio-Cultural Context as a Determinant of the Actualization of the “Us vs. Them” Opposition
title_original: Socio-Cultural Context as a Determinant of the Actualization of the “Us vs. Them” Opposition
summary: This article presents the results of a comprehensive study of the socio-cultural context as a key factor determin-ing the forms and intensity of the actualization of the fundamental “Us vs. Them” opposition. Amid the intensifi-cation of globalization processes, the transformation of migration flows, and the total digitalization of the com-municative space, the socio-cultural context ceases to be a static background, turning into a powerful dynamic determinant of the logic governing the formation of collective identities and the orientation of cultural dynamics. The central focus of the study is the development and theoretical substantiation of an integral analytical model that reveals the systemic connections between specific context parameters-such as the level of social hetero-geneity, the dominant type of social solidarity, the degree of economic stability, and the nature of media dis-course – and the prevailing criteria of socio-cultural differentiation. These criteria can range from rigid ethnic and confessional markers to flexible behavioral and value-based characteristics. Particular attention is paid to the conflict-generating potential of this opposition, which becomes maximally actualized in situations of cultural appropriation, giving rise to a cognitive conflict of interpretations and an axiological clash of value systems.

title: City Inhabitant Lists of Tyumen  in the Late 18th and the First Half of the 19th Century:  Structure, Informational Value, and Representativeness
title_original: City Inhabitant Lists of Tyumen  in the Late 18th and the First Half of the 19th Century:  Structure, Informational Value, and Representativeness
summary: A comparative analysis of Tyumen’s city inhabitant lists and books from the late 18th to the first half of the 19th century reveals their functional nature as prescribed by the 1785 Charter to the Towns and criteria for their dif-ferentiation. Drawing on 12 lists and 18 books from Tyumen archives for 1789–1851, the article characterizes the register form, the evolution of its internal organization, and its informativeness as an independent source. The authors conclude that the list and the book are not draft and final versions of one document, but two distinct sources: the list records the “city-territory” in the full range of its population, while the book constructs the nar-rower circle of “city-corporation,” and compiling it involves systematic estate-based filtering of data. If the inter-nal verification shows that over 40 % of the population – chiefly the city’s “non-core” estates – loses its detailed demographic record when a list becomes a book, then external verification against an 1807 police ward ledger demonstrates the list’s representativeness matching it at 94.6 % city-wide. Clarifying the source’s nature re-solves contradictions in the readings by predecessors and establishes the promising mass personified source for historical demography, microhistory, and prosopography of the pre-reform town.
abstract: A comparative analysis of Tyumen’s city inhabitant lists and books from the late 18th to the first half of the 19th century reveals their functional nature as prescribed by the 1785 Charter to the Towns and criteria for their dif-ferentiation. Drawing on 12 lists and 18 books from Tyumen archives for 1789–1851, the article characterizes the register form, the evolution of its internal organization, and its informativeness as an independent source. The authors conclude that the list and the book are not draft and final versions of one document, but two distinct sources: the list records the “city-territory” in the full range of its population, while the book constructs the nar-rower circle of “city-corporation,” and compiling it involves systematic estate-based filtering of data. If the inter-nal verification shows that over 40 % of the population – chiefly the city’s “non-core” estates – loses its detailed demographic record when a list becomes a book, then external verification against an 1807 police ward ledger demonstrates the list’s representativeness matching it at 94.6 % city-wide. Clarifying the source’s nature re-solves contradictions in the readings by predecessors and establishes the promising mass personified source for historical demography, microhistory, and prosopography of the pre-reform town.

title: The Culture of Native Minorities of Siberia as an Object of Cultural Policy:  An Ecosystem Model
title_original: The Culture of Native Minorities of Siberia as an Object of Cultural Policy:  An Ecosystem Model
summary: The article proposes a conceptual model of the culture of the native minorities of Siberia as an object of cultural policy based on a systems analysis of the interaction among four interconnected components: the bearer, play-ful mechanisms of transmission, oral narratives (legends and sagas), and arts and crafts. It demonstrates that the dominant paradigm of fragmentary heritage protection, targeted at the cultural products recording and mu-seumification, does not ensure the preservation of its viability. Drawing on international documents (the 2003 UNESCO Convention), works on game theory, folklore studies, and ethnography, the system-forming role of the live-bearer as an integrator of the verbal, game-based, and material codes of tradition is substantiated. Functional links between legend, game, and craft are identified. The ambivalence of arts and crafts, balancing between the internal needs of the community and the external souvenir market, is revealed. The principles of an ecosystem approach to cultural policy are formulated.

title: Claude Perrault’s Architectural Views as an Anticipation of the Romantic Artistic Worldview
title_original: Claude Perrault’s Architectural Views as an Anticipation of the Romantic Artistic Worldview
summary: The article examines the features of Claude Perrault’s architectural theory, a French architect of the 17th-century, in terms of anticipating the romantic artistic worldview, which is characterized by individualism and freedom of creativity as opposed to the universality, rational statics, and formality of classicism. C. Perrault’s theoretical views on architecture are characterized as judgments that did not reach the level of development of the aesthetic positions of the leading theorists of the Romantic era; however, it is possible to identify their se-mantic potential. C. Perrault’s conceptual provisions are explored in their cultural and intellectual context, which is necessary for correct interpretation. The anticipation of the romantic artistic worldview is manifested in C. Perrault’s attitude towards Gothic architecture, in the division of architecture into “positive” and “arbitrary”, as well as in the possibility of combining opposites in an architectural object.

title: Methods of Representing the Symbolic Meanings in Mo Yan’s Novel “Thirteen Steps”
title_original: Methods of Representing the Symbolic Meanings in Mo Yan’s Novel “Thirteen Steps”
summary: This article is dedicated to the exploration of the symbolics of Mo Yan’s novel “Thirteen Steps” (1989) received a worldwide recognition as a classic of Chinese literature. Using this work as an example, the authors of the published work demonstrate that when analyzing a statement in a high-context culture (E. Hall), such as Chi-nese one, it is necessary to consider the influence of the cultural and historical context associated with tradi-tions. This context may include the symbolic meanings of colour, animal and plant images, names and titles, geographical features and cardinal directions, natural objects and phenomena, numbers, body parts, food, household items, clothing and footwear, quotes, reminiscences, etc. The aim of the study, the results of which are presented in the publication, was to highlight the ways of representation of the information, that has a sym-bolic nature, in high-context Chinese culture as exemplified in Mo Yan’s novel “Thirteen Steps”. It is empha-sized that without considering the cultural and historical context of a statement in cultures such as Chinese one, its meaning may be either incompletely perceived, or distorted, or lost altogether. An analysis of the symbolics of Mo Yan’s novel “Thirteen Steps” taking into account the cultural and historical context revealed the writer’s genuine innovation in both the content and form of his work.
